modules.name: AbortBreaking
modules.summary: Allows you to stop breaking a block without losing the mining progress you have already accumulated. It works by cancelling the client's block-breaking cancel event, so when you release or interrupt mining the progress is retained instead of being reset. This lets you resume breaking the same block later from where you left off.
useCases: Mine a hard block partway, stop to do something else, then resume without restarting the progress.
Interrupt breaking to fight or react to a threat without wasting the mining time already spent.

modules.name: Aimbot
modules.summary: Aimbot (aliases AimAssist, AutoAim) automatically turns your view toward nearby entities, smoothing the rotation so it looks more natural. It selects targets by how close they are to your crosshair (within Range), can lock onto an entity you have hit for a set duration, and respects a whitelist that never aims at manually-listed names or auto-detected teammates. Unlike KillAura it only moves your aim (you still attack manually) and applies its own smoothing and per-axis control.
useCases: Get aim assistance while still attacking manually, useful where full KillAura is too obvious.
Lock onto a chosen enemy in a crowd and keep tracking them even as they strafe behind you.
Avoid friendly fire by whitelisting clan members via scoreboard team, name color, or tab prefix.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum distance (blocks) at which entities are targeted. Default 4.2, range 1-8.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target selection sub-group (priority Direction by default, range driven by the Range setting). Includes FOV (float, default 180, 0-180), HurtTime (int, default 10, 0-10), and Priority (multiEnum ordering such as Type/Direction/Distance/Health). Determines which entity within range is aimed at.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) drawing a marker on the current target with the shared Mode choice (Legacy/Circle/Image/GlowingCircle/Ghost/Hearts/Text/Arrow) and per-mode color, size and height settings.

settings.name: Whitelist
settings.description: Sub-group of entities Aimbot must never aim at (affects only Aimbot). Usernames (textList, empty by default; exact names you type are always skipped), AutoTeam (boolean, default false; automatically whitelist detected teammates), AutoTeamSources (multiEnum, default ScoreboardTeam; which signals count as a teammate: ScoreboardTeam, NameColor matching display-name color, Prefix matching the tab/nametag clan prefix), Notify (boolean, default true; announce auto-whitelisted entities once).

settings.name: AimPoint
settings.description: Point-tracker sub-group choosing which spot on the target hitbox to aim at, with ExemptBoxParts (multiEnum), ExemptBestHitVector (toggleable), Gaussian randomization (toggleable), Lazy (toggleable), and Delay (toggleable) processors.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be true for Aimbot to aim, from the KillAura requirement set (Click, Weapon, EmptyHand, VanillaName, NotBreaking). None selected by default, so it aims whenever a target is present and no screen is open.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Rotation-smoothing mode used to move your view to the target. Choices: Interpolation, Sigmoid, Linear (each with their own internal speed/factor settings). Controls how fast and how human-like the aim snaps onto targets.

settings.name: Axis
settings.description: Which rotation axes Aimbot is allowed to control: Horizontal (yaw) and Vertical (pitch). Both enabled by default; disabling one leaves that axis under your own control.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Open-screen situations in which the in-world aim is still applied: Screen (any GUI open) and Container (inventory/container open). None selected by default, meaning aiming is suppressed while those screens are open unless added here.

settings.name: LockTarget
settings.description: If enabled (default false), once you hit an entity Aimbot keeps aiming at that exact target for the lock duration instead of switching to whoever is closest to your crosshair. The lock is sticky and ignores FOV/range while it lasts.

settings.name: LockDuration
settings.description: How long (seconds) a target lock is held after a hit. Default 1, range 0.1-10. The lock releases early if the entity dies, despawns, or stops being attackable.

modules.name: AirJump
modules.summary: AirJump lets you jump while in mid-air. Depending on the selected mode it allows continuous free jumping in the air, a single extra double-jump after leaving the ground, or a ghost-block mode that creates a temporary solid block beneath you while holding jump so you can jump off air. The double-jump resets each time you touch the ground.
useCases: Gain extra vertical movement or reach ledges by jumping while airborne.
Use DoubleJump to get one controlled mid-air jump per ground contact, which can look more legitimate.
Use GhostBlock to effectively stand on air below you while holding the jump key.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the air-jump behavior. JumpFreely (default) allows unlimited mid-air jumps. DoubleJump allows a single extra jump in the air that resets when you land on the ground. GhostBlock makes the block shape below you solid (a full block) while the jump key is held and the position is below your feet, letting you jump off air.

modules.name: AirPlace
modules.summary: AirPlace lets you place blocks (and certain placeable items) in midair where you would normally need an adjacent block to place against. When you look at empty air and try to use a placeable item, the module performs the placement at the targeted position and cancels the vanilla interaction. It can optionally render a preview box at the target spot, place inside liquids, and use a custom fixed placement range adjustable by scrolling.
useCases: Quickly bridge or build floating structures without scaffolding by placing blocks directly in the air.
Place spawn eggs, armor stands, or firework rockets in midair where no supporting block exists.
Use CustomRange with scroll adjustment to fine-tune exactly how far from you blocks get placed.

settings.name: Preview
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (default enabled). When on, renders a box at the position where the block would be air-placed so you can see the target before placing.

settings.name: OutlineOnly
settings.description: Inside Preview (default false). When true the preview is drawn as an outline only (transparent fill); when false the box is filled with the Color.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Inside Preview. The fill color of the preview box (default a translucent blue, RGBA 69,119,255,104).

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Inside Preview. The outline color of the preview box (default white).

settings.name: PlaceInLiquid
settings.description: When enabled (default false), allows air-placing into fluid (water/lava) source positions as well as air, provided the LiquidPlace module is not running.

settings.name: CustomRange
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, instead of placing at the exact block you look at, AirPlace projects the placement to a fixed distance along your look direction defined by Range.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Inside CustomRange. The distance (default 3.0, range 1.0..4.5) from your eyes along your view direction at which the block is placed when CustomRange is active.

settings.name: ScrollAdjust
settings.description: Inside CustomRange. Toggleable sub-group (default enabled) that lets you change Range by scrolling the mouse wheel while a modifier key is held.

settings.name: Modifier
settings.description: Inside CustomRange > ScrollAdjust. The key that must be held to allow scroll-adjusting the range (default Left Alt). If set to none/unknown, scrolling always adjusts.

settings.name: Sensitivity
settings.description: Inside CustomRange > ScrollAdjust. Multiplier (default 0.5, range 0.1..1.0) applied to each scroll notch when changing the Range value.

modules.name: Anchor
modules.summary: Anchor pulls your player into nearby safe holes (1x1 enclosed spots) to keep you protected. It searches tracked holes within range below you, picks the closest valid one, and steers your movement toward its center, centering you once you are inside. The module is a HOLD bind (active only while the key is held), disables on quit, and stops acting while elytra flying, spectating, or swimming.
useCases: Drop into a safe bedrock/obsidian hole quickly during crystal PvP to avoid explosion damage.
Auto-center yourself inside a hole so you cannot be knocked or bumped out of it.

settings.name: MaxDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance (default 4, range 0.1 to 6) to a hole for it to be considered a target. Larger values let Anchor pull you toward holes that are farther away; it also defines the horizontal/vertical search radius for tracked holes.

settings.name: HorizontalSpeed
settings.description: Horizontal pull speed toward the target hole (default 0.3, range 0 to 10). The actual limit is the greater of this value and your current horizontal movement. If set to 0, Anchor does not actively pull you horizontally but will cancel horizontal movement when your bounding box is already over the hole (to stop you sliding off).

settings.name: VerticalSpeed
settings.description: Vertical pull speed toward the target hole (default 0.1, range 0 to 10). The actual limit is the greater of this value and your current vertical movement. If set to 0, vertical movement is left unmodified.

modules.name: Animations
modules.summary: Animations customizes first-person view-model item animations. It lets you reposition, rescale and re-rotate the main-hand and off-hand held items, adjust the swing speed, change the equip (item switch) offset behavior, and choose the sword-blocking animation used together with SwordBlock. It also includes an optional air-walking arm animation. All adjustments are purely visual and affect only your own view model.
useCases: Tweaking the position/scale/rotation of your held item for a custom first-person look.
Getting an old-school 1.7-style blocking animation when using the SwordBlock module.
Speeding up or slowing down your hand swing animation, or making the walk animation play while airborne.

settings.name: MainHand
settings.description: Toggle for the main-hand item-transform group (disabled by default). When enabled, the X/Y/scale/rotation child offsets below are applied to the main-hand view model.

settings.name: ItemScale
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Additional scale offset applied to the main-hand item model (default 0, range -5.0 to 5.0). Positive values enlarge the held item, negative values shrink it.

settings.name: X
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Horizontal position offset of the main-hand item (default 0, range -5.0 to 5.0).

settings.name: Y
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Vertical position offset of the main-hand item (default 0, range -5.0 to 5.0).

settings.name: PositiveRotationX
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Rotation offset of the main-hand item around the X axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: PositiveRotationY
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Rotation offset of the main-hand item around the Y axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: PositiveRotationZ
settings.description: Child of MainHand. Rotation offset of the main-hand item around the Z axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: OffHand
settings.description: Toggle for the off-hand item-transform group (disabled by default). When enabled, the X/Y/scale/rotation child offsets below are applied to the off-hand view model.

settings.name: ItemScale
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Additional scale offset applied to the off-hand item model (default 0, range -5.0 to 5.0).

settings.name: X
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Horizontal position offset of the off-hand item (default 0, range -1.0 to 1.0).

settings.name: Y
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Vertical position offset of the off-hand item (default 0, range -1.0 to 1.0).

settings.name: PositiveRotationX
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Rotation offset of the off-hand item around the X axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: PositiveRotationY
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Rotation offset of the off-hand item around the Y axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: PositiveRotationZ
settings.description: Child of OffHand. Rotation offset of the off-hand item around the Z axis in degrees (default 0, range -50 to 50).

settings.name: SwingDuration
settings.description: How many ticks the hand-swing animation lasts (default 6, range 1-20). Lower values make the swing animation faster, higher values make it slower.

settings.name: BlockingAnimation
settings.description: Selects which sword-blocking animation to use (only applied when the SwordBlock module is active). Options are '1.7' (default, mimics the classic 1.7 blocking animation) and 'Pushdown' (a pushdown-style animation similar to LiquidBounce Legacy). Each option has its own sub-settings.

settings.name: Y
settings.description: Child of the BlockingAnimation '1.7' choice. Vertical translation applied to the item during 1.7-style blocking (default 0.1, range 0.05 to 0.3). Raises or lowers the blocked item.

settings.name: SwingScale
settings.description: Child of the BlockingAnimation '1.7' choice. Scales the swing progress used in the 1.7 blocking offset (default 0.9, range 0.1 to 1.0). Lower values dampen the swing motion during blocking.

settings.name: EquipOffset
settings.description: Toggle for the equip-offset group (enabled by default). When enabled, it modifies the item equip (switch) animation, with the Ignore child controlling when that offset is suppressed.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Child of EquipOffset. Multi-select of conditions under which the equip offset animation is ignored/suppressed. Options: Blocking, Place, and Amount. By default Blocking and Place are selected, meaning the equip offset is not applied while blocking or while placing, and (if Amount is added) when only the item stack amount changes.

settings.name: AirWalker
settings.description: When enabled (default off), the walk/stride arm animation is also applied while you are in the air, by forcing a small stride force based on your horizontal movement. Purely a visual animation effect.

modules.name: AntiAFK
modules.summary: Keeps you from being kicked for inactivity by automatically performing small movements and interactions while you are away. It offers three behavior modes selectable via the Mode option: a simple 'Old' mode, a 'RandomInteraction' mode that performs randomized actions, and a fully configurable 'Custom' mode. Depending on the chosen mode it will rotate, swing, jump, move, and/or change direction so the server registers you as active.
useCases: Staying connected on servers that kick AFK players (e.g. to hold a queue spot or keep a session alive).
Idling on an anti-AFK protected farm or minigame lobby without manual input.
Avoiding AFK detection on servers that watch for repeated identical movement by using the RandomInteraction mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the anti-AFK behavior. Choices are 'Old', 'RandomInteraction' (the default active choice), and 'Custom'. Each choice exposes its own sub-settings (only the active choice's settings apply).

settings.name: Interaction
settings.description: RandomInteraction mode: the set of random actions that may be performed each cycle. Available actions are Jump, SwingHand, ChangeSlot, Yaw (random yaw turn between -180 and 180 degrees), Pitch (random pitch change between -5 and +5 degrees, clamped to -90..90), and RandomDirection (random movement input). Defaults to Yaw, Pitch and SwingHand enabled. One enabled action is picked at random per cycle.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: RandomInteraction mode: the random wait, in ticks, between performed interactions. Default range 4..7, configurable within 0..20 ticks. A random value within this range is chosen each cycle.

settings.name: Rotate
settings.description: Custom mode: toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that makes the player periodically rotate. When enabled it adjusts the server rotation by the configured Angle with a small random pitch jitter.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate: when true (default), rotations are still applied even while an inventory/screen is open. Disabling it suppresses rotation while a GUI is open.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate: nested rotation-engine sub-group (RotationsValueGroup) controlling how the rotation is applied. Its child settings are AngleSmooth (rotation smoothing mode), MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset (see below).

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate > Rotations: chooses how the rotation interpolates toward its target. Available modes include Linear, Sigmoid and Acceleration. Controls how smoothly/quickly the view snaps to the new rotation.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate > Rotations: how movement direction is corrected relative to the silent rotation. Defaults to SILENT (rotation is applied server-side only without turning the actual camera).

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate > Rotations: angular difference (default 2, range 1..180 degrees) below which the rotation is considered reached and may begin resetting back to the player's normal rotation.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate > Rotations: number of ticks (default 5, range 1..30) without a new rotation target before the rotation resets back to normal.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate: ticks to wait before each rotation update. Default 5, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: Angle
settings.description: Custom mode > Rotate: amount (in degrees) the yaw is offset on each rotation cycle. Default 1, range -180..180.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Custom mode: toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that periodically swings the main hand while you are not already swinging.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Custom mode > Swing: ticks to wait before each hand swing. Default 5, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: Jump
settings.description: Custom mode: when true (default), the player jumps each cycle while standing on the ground.

settings.name: Move
settings.description: Custom mode: when true (default), the forward movement key is held down so the player keeps walking forward.

modules.name: AntiBlind
modules.summary: Removes or reduces screen effects and overlays that obstruct your view, and lets you selectively keep certain renders. Via the DoRender multi-select you choose which effects/overlays remain enabled; anything not selected is suppressed (e.g. blinding, darkness, nausea, pumpkin blur, portal/wall/spyglass overlays, fog, fire, particles). It also includes a separate low-fire mode that shrinks the first-person flame overlay and an adjustable fire overlay opacity. Aliased as 'NoRender'.
useCases: Removing the blindness/darkness/nausea screen effects that opponents inflict during combat.
Clearing view-blocking overlays like the carved-pumpkin blur, portal overlay, or fire while burning.
Keeping useful renders (armor, beacon beams, etc.) while disabling distracting ones.

settings.name: LowFire
settings.description: Toggle for the LowFire group (default disabled). When on, the first-person fire overlay is shrunk and shifted (the classic 'low fire' pack effect) so flames cover less of the screen while burning, rather than just being made transparent.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: LowFire group. Vertical scale of the first-person fire overlay; smaller values shrink the flames. Default 0.5, range 0.1..1.

settings.name: Offset
settings.description: LowFire group. Vertical offset that shifts the fire overlay up or down. Default 0, range -1..1.

settings.name: DoRender
settings.description: The set of screen effects, overlays and renders that remain ENABLED; any option not in this set is suppressed by the module. Available options: Blinding, Darkness, Nausea, Armor, MobInSpawner, EnchantTableBook, EatParticles, BlockBreakParticles, BlockBreakOverlay, Title, PumpkinBlur, LiquidsFog, PowderSnowFog, FloatingItems, MapContents, MapMarkers, PortalOverlay, WallOverlay, FallingBlocks, BeaconBeams, SkylightUpdates, GuiBackground, SpyglassOverlay, SignText, InvisibleEntities, BossBars, ExplosionParticles, WorldBorder. Defaults to enabling: Armor, MobInSpawner, EnchantTableBook, EatParticles, BlockBreakParticles, BlockBreakOverlay, Title, MapContents, MapMarkers, FallingBlocks, BeaconBeams, SkylightUpdates, GuiBackground, SpyglassOverlay, SignText, InvisibleEntities, BossBars, ExplosionParticles, WorldBorder (so things like Blinding, Darkness, Nausea, PumpkinBlur, fog and overlays are removed by default).

settings.name: FireOpacity
settings.description: Opacity of the first-person fire overlay as a percentage. Default 100, range 0..100 (%). At 0 the fire overlay is fully invisible; the value is applied as a multiplier (FireOpacity/100) while the module runs.

modules.name: AntiBot
modules.summary: AntiBot detects fake/NPC players spawned by servers or anticheats and tells other client modules (such as combat features) to ignore them so they are not targeted or rendered as real players. It offers several detection modes, plus two always-on quick checks for entities not in the online-player list or missing from the tab list. Detection state is reset on disable and on world change.
useCases: Preventing combat modules (KillAura, etc.) from attacking server-spawned bots or NPCs.
Filtering out anticheat 'test' bots (e.g. Matrix, Intave, Horizon) used to bait cheats.
Using the Custom mode to build precise bot-detection rules tuned to a specific server.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the bot-detection algorithm. Choices: Custom (default), Matrix, IntaveHeavy, Horizon. Only the Custom mode exposes configurable sub-settings; the others are detection algorithms with no settings of their own.

settings.name: LiteralNPC
settings.description: If true, any player whose UUID is not present in the online-player list is treated as a bot. Default false.

settings.name: NotInTabList
settings.description: If true, any player missing from the listed (tab-list) players is treated as a bot. Default false.

settings.name: InvalidGround
settings.description: Custom mode toggle (default enabled). When on, flags entities that move while reporting onGround (impossible 'flying on ground' movement), accumulating violation points.

settings.name: VLToConsiderAsBot
settings.description: InvalidGround sub-setting: number of accumulated flags before the entity is considered a bot. Default 10, range 1..50.

settings.name: Conditions
settings.description: Custom mode multi-select of extra bot conditions. Available: Duplicate (same name different UUID), NoGameMode (no game mode in player info), IllegalPitch (|pitch|>90), FakeEntityID (entity id outside 0..1,000,000,000), NeedHit (never been attacked by you), IllegalHealth (health above your max), Swung (never swung), Critted (never critted), Attributes (never sent attribute updates), IllegalScale (scale attribute != 1.0). Default selection: NoGameMode, IllegalPitch, FakeEntityID.

settings.name: AlwaysInRadius
settings.description: Custom mode toggle (default disabled). When on, any player who has never been seen outside the configured radius is treated as a bot (server bots that always stay near you).

settings.name: AlwaysInRadiusRange
settings.description: AlwaysInRadius sub-setting: radius in blocks used for the always-in-radius check. Default 20, range 5..30.

settings.name: Age
settings.description: Custom mode toggle (default disabled). When on, players younger than the minimum tick age are treated as bots.

settings.name: Minimum
settings.description: Age sub-setting: minimum entity age in ticks; entities with a lower tickCount are flagged. Default 20, range 0..120.

settings.name: Armor
settings.description: Custom mode toggle (default disabled). When on, a player is flagged as a bot if their equipped armor does not match the allowed armor sets selected per slot below.

settings.name: Helmet
settings.description: Armor sub-setting: allowed helmet types. Options include Nothing, Leather, Chain, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Netherite, TurtleScute, Pumpkin, Skull. Default: Nothing. Empty selection skips this slot.

settings.name: Chestplate
settings.description: Armor sub-setting: allowed chestplate types. Options include Nothing, Leather, Chain, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Netherite, Elytra. Default: Nothing. Empty selection skips this slot.

settings.name: Leggings
settings.description: Armor sub-setting: allowed leggings types. Options: Nothing, Leather, Chain, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Netherite. Default: Nothing. Empty selection skips this slot.

settings.name: Boots
settings.description: Armor sub-setting: allowed boots types. Options: Nothing, Leather, Chain, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Netherite. Default: Nothing. Empty selection skips this slot.

settings.name: Name
settings.description: Custom mode toggle (default enabled). When on, players whose name length is outside the allowed range or whose characters fail the selected character validators are treated as bots.

settings.name: Length
settings.description: Name sub-setting: allowed name length range. Default 3..16, allowed 1..32. Names outside this range are flagged.

settings.name: ValidateChars
settings.description: Name sub-setting: character sets a valid name may use. Options: Vanilla (0-9, a-z, A-Z, underscore), Cyrillic, CJKUnifiedIdeographs. Default: Vanilla. A name is flagged if it contains characters disallowed by any selected validator.

modules.name: AntiBounce
modules.summary: AntiBounce prevents you from bouncing off bouncy blocks such as slime blocks and beds. It works entirely through an entity mixin and has no configurable settings; simply enabling it stops the bounce behavior.
useCases: Landing on slime blocks or beds without being thrown back into the air.
Maintaining stable, predictable movement when traversing areas with bouncy blocks.

modules.name: AntiCheatDetect
modules.summary: AntiCheatDetect attempts to identify which anti-cheat the current server is running and reports its guess to you in chat. It checks when enabled and again once the ServerObserver has gathered enough transaction data, using the server's IP to guess the anti-cheat; if no guess can be made it stays silent. The module has no configurable options and is excluded from auto-config exports.
useCases: Find out what anti-cheat a server uses so you can pick appropriate settings/bypasses.
Confirm an anti-cheat guess after the client has collected enough server transactions.

modules.name: AntiExploit
modules.summary: AntiExploit protects you against malicious server packets and known crash/lag exploits by limiting or cancelling abusive data. It can clamp absurd explosion strengths and particle amounts/speeds, block the forced demo screen, ignore protocol-mismatch kicks, and optionally fix a scoreboard rendering exploit. When it intervenes it can notify you in the client about the detected exploit or crash attempt.
useCases: Stay protected on untrusted servers that may try to crash or lag your client with malformed explosion or particle packets.
Avoid being kicked by servers that exploit protocol checks, and prevent forced demo-mode screens.
Get notified whenever the client blocks a suspected crash attempt so you know the server is misbehaving.

settings.name: Limit
settings.description: Which abusive values to clamp/limit. Options: ExplosionStrength (cap explosion power), ParticlesAmount (cap number of particles), ParticlesSpeed (cap particle speed). Default: none selected (no limiting applied unless chosen).

settings.name: CancelDemo
settings.description: When enabled (default true), blocks the server from forcing the Minecraft demo screen onto you.

settings.name: IgnoreProtocolKick
settings.description: When enabled (default true), ignores kick attempts that exploit protocol-version mismatches, preventing you from being disconnected.

settings.name: Notify
settings.description: When enabled (default true), shows a client notification whenever an exploit is blocked; crash attempts are shown as ERROR severity, other detections as INFO.

settings.name: VFPScoreboardFix
settings.description: When enabled (default false), applies a fix for a scoreboard-related exploit (implemented via the scoreboard mixin), typically relevant when using ViaFabricPlus on older protocols.

modules.name: AntiHunger
modules.summary: AntiHunger reduces or stops hunger/exhaustion from draining by spoofing your server-side state, though it will flag many anti-cheats. It works two ways: by preventing the server from seeing you sprint (sprinting causes exhaustion), and by keeping you reported as not on the ground (KeepFloating), since travel exhaustion is only applied while grounded. When it suppresses a sprint or block-break that would normally not be possible, it shows an informational notification (rate limited to once every 500ms) and performs a small jump to recover. The floating trick is skipped while in a vehicle, while actively breaking a block, and while in or under water.
useCases: Travelling long distances on foot without losing hunger on servers with weak anti-cheat.
Conserving food while exploring or grinding by preventing exhaustion buildup.

settings.name: NoSprint
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that cancels hunger loss by forcing the player to not sprint server-side, suppressing both network and input sprint sources. Child setting WhileSwimming: boolean, default false, which when enabled also keeps the no-sprint behavior active while you are swimming (otherwise no-sprint is disabled during swimming).

settings.name: KeepFloating
settings.description: Default true. Makes the player report as not on the ground when standing still and not falling, by rewriting outgoing movement packets to onGround=false, which prevents travel-based hunger exhaustion. It is automatically skipped when you are a passenger in a vehicle, currently breaking a block, or in/under/touching water to avoid breaking those interactions.

modules.name: AntiLevitation
modules.summary: AntiLevitation cancels the movement effects of the Levitation and Slow Falling status effects via a mixin hook into the player's travel/status-effect handling. With it enabled, those effects no longer alter your vertical movement, so you fall and move normally despite them. It has no configurable settings.
useCases: Avoiding being lifted helplessly upward when hit with Levitation (e.g., from shulkers or potions).
Falling normally instead of drifting slowly when affected by Slow Falling.

modules.name: AntiReducedDebugInfo
modules.summary: AntiReducedDebugInfo defeats the server's ability to hide extended debug information (the reduced debug info flag normally sent by some servers). When enabled it lets you see the full F3 debug screen and other extended debug details that the server tried to restrict. The module has no configurable options and simply works while active.
useCases: Viewing full coordinates and debug data on servers that force reduced debug info.
Restoring the complete F3 debug overlay for navigation or troubleshooting on restricted servers.

modules.name: AntiStaff
modules.summary: AntiStaff warns you when known server staff members are present or watching you. When you join or connect to a server it downloads that server's staff list from LiquidBounce's CDN (keyed by the server's root domain), and then watches incoming player-info packets for any staff names, alerting you in chat and via a notification when one is detected. It can also optionally mark staff members in the tab list. It only acts on per-server staff lists that exist on the CDN; if no list is found it notifies you accordingly.
useCases: Get an early warning when a server moderator or admin joins or starts spectating you so you can stop using risky modules.
Quickly identify staff members in the tab list on supported servers.

settings.name: ShowInTabList
settings.description: When enabled (default true), players identified as staff for the current server are flagged/highlighted in the tab list. Disabling it keeps the chat/notification alerts but stops the tab-list marking.

modules.name: AntiVoid
modules.summary: AntiVoid protects you from falling into the void by simulating your future movement for the next several ticks and detecting when you are likely to fall past the configured void level. When a fall into the void is predicted and no collision is found beneath you, it takes a rescue action determined by the selected mode (placing a ghost block, faking a position flag, or queuing/cancelling blink packets). It will not act in exempt situations such as when dead/dying or when Fly is running, and shows a notification when a rescue is performed.
useCases: Preventing accidental void deaths when bridging, fighting, or moving near map edges on void-floor maps.
Using the GhostBlock mode to silently catch yourself on a fake collision block when about to drop into the void.
Using the Blink mode to lag back to a previous safe position before falling, or Flag mode to nudge yourself upward when caught falling.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the rescue mechanism: GhostBlock (default), Flag, or Blink. Determines how the module attempts to save you when a void fall is predicted.

settings.name: VoidLevel
settings.description: The Y height treated as the start of the void. Default 0, range -256 to 0. Collision checks extend down to this level; falling with no collision above it triggers rescue.

settings.name: FallDistance
settings.description: Child of the Flag mode. The minimum fall distance the player must have accumulated before the Flag rescue triggers. Default 0.5, range 0.0 to 6.0.

settings.name: Height
settings.description: Child of the Flag mode. How far (in blocks) the player is moved/nudged upward when the Flag rescue triggers. Default 0.42, range 0.01 to 10.0.

settings.name: Silent
settings.description: Child of the Flag mode. When enabled, the upward correction is applied silently by modifying the outgoing network movement packet's Y instead of directly teleporting the player. Default false.

modules.name: ArmorDurability
modules.summary: ArmorDurability renders the remaining durability of each piece of nearby players' armor as a floating number next to the matching body part (helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots). It reads durability from the full ItemStack the server sends for entity equipment, so no resource pack or Optifine is needed. Numbers are positioned at each armor piece's approximate height and pushed slightly to the side so they do not block your view. Only players within range that are not spectators (and, depending on settings, not friends or teammates) are shown.
useCases: See at a glance which enemy armor pieces are nearly broken so you can focus attacks where they will break gear fastest.
Decide whether to keep fighting or retreat by reading opponents' overall armor condition in real time.
Keep the overlay focused on real threats by hiding durability for friends and scoreboard teammates.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum distance (in blocks) from you within which a player's armor durability numbers are drawn. Players farther than this are skipped. Default 32, range 4 to 64 blocks.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Render scale (size multiplier) of the durability text. Larger values make the numbers bigger on screen. Default 1, range 0.25 to 4.

settings.name: SideOffset
settings.description: Horizontal screen offset (in pixels) applied to the numbers so they sit beside the body instead of directly on top of it. 0 places them right on each piece; positive/negative values shift them right/left. Default 10, range -40 to 40.

settings.name: RoundToTens
settings.description: When enabled (default true), durability values are rounded to the nearest 10 (e.g. 340, 210), matching the look of armor-durability resource packs. When disabled, the exact remaining durability is shown.

settings.name: HideFull
settings.description: When enabled (default false), armor pieces that are at full durability are not shown, so only damaged pieces display a number. When disabled, full-durability pieces are shown too.

settings.name: ColorByDurability
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the number color is determined by the piece's remaining durability ratio, ramping from green (full) through yellow to red (nearly broken). When disabled, the fixed Color setting is used instead.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: The fixed text color used for the durability numbers when ColorByDurability is disabled. Default white. Has no effect while ColorByDurability is enabled.

settings.name: IgnoreFriends
settings.description: When enabled (default true), players marked as friends are skipped and their armor durability is not rendered, keeping the overlay focused on enemies.

settings.name: IgnoreTeammates
settings.description: When enabled (default true), players on your scoreboard team (allies) are skipped and their armor durability is not rendered.

modules.name: Aspect
modules.summary: Aspect changes the rendered aspect ratio of the game by scaling it according to a percentage. The single Ratio setting acts as a multiplier (percentage divided by 100) applied to the view, letting you stretch or compress the rendered image.
useCases: Stretch the game view to a wider or taller aspect for a different visual perspective.
Exaggerate the rendered ratio for cosmetic or experimental effects.

settings.name: Ratio
settings.description: The aspect ratio as a percentage, default 100% (no change), range 1 to 300. Internally divided by 100 to produce the multiplier applied to the view, so 200 doubles the ratio scaling.

modules.name: AutoAccount
modules.summary: AutoAccount automatically logs in or registers on servers that use authentication plugins (e.g. AuthMe-style /login and /register prompts). It watches chosen message sources (chat, title, subtitle) for prompts matching configurable regexes and then, after a randomized delay, sends the corresponding login or register command with your configured password. It runs even before the world is fully loaded (as long as the client isn't destructed/hidden) so it can react to early authentication prompts.
useCases: Automatically authenticate on offline-mode servers that require /login or /register on every join.
Register a new account on first join, then auto-login on subsequent joins, using a fixed password.

settings.name: Password
settings.description: The password sent with the login command (and twice for registration). Default 'a1b2c3d4'. This value is excluded from auto-config exports to avoid leaking your password.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Randomized delay (in ticks) waited after the connection is ready before sending the login/register command; a random value within the range is chosen each time. Default 3..5, range 0..50 ticks.

settings.name: RegisterCommand
settings.description: The command name used for registration (sent as '<RegisterCommand> <password> <password>'). Default 'register'.

settings.name: LoginCommand
settings.description: The command name used for logging in (sent as '<LoginCommand> <password>'). Default 'login'.

settings.name: RegisterRegex
settings.description: Regular expression matched against incoming messages to detect a registration prompt; when it matches, the register command is sent. Default pattern '/register'.

settings.name: LoginRegex
settings.description: Regular expression matched against incoming messages to detect a login prompt; when it matches, the login command is sent. Default pattern '/login'.

settings.name: MessageSource
settings.description: Which message channels are scanned for login/register prompts. Options are Chat, Title and Subtitle (multiple can be selected; cannot be set to none).

modules.name: AutoArmor
modules.summary: AutoArmor automatically equips the best available armor pieces from your inventory and hotbar, evaluating them by protection value. It schedules inventory actions under configurable constraints, can use hotbar right-clicks or inventory shift-clicks, and will throw out a worn piece if there's no inventory space to swap it. An optional SaveArmor feature swaps out armor whose durability drops below a threshold (optionally opening the inventory automatically) to keep you protected. It does not run in spectator mode and won't touch an equipped Elytra.
useCases: Automatically gear up with the strongest armor you pick up during a fight.
Swap out near-broken armor before it breaks so you stay protected (SaveArmor).
Keep optimal armor equipped on Kit-PvP or anarchy servers without manual inventory management.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Constraints group (PlayerInventoryConstraints). Ticks to wait before starting an inventory action. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Constraints group. Ticks to wait between inventory clicks. Default 2..4, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Constraints group. Ticks to wait before closing the inventory after actions complete. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Constraints group. Percentage chance to deliberately misclick to mimic human behavior. Default 0..0 (never), range 0..100 (%).

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Constraints group. Conditions that must be satisfied before inventory actions run. Options: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, and InventoryOpen (only require actions while the inventory is actually open). Default: none selected.

settings.name: Hotbar
settings.description: Toggleable UseHotbar group, default enabled. When on, the module may equip armor by right-clicking hotbar items (faster); when off it only uses inventory moves. Contains CanSwapArmor.

settings.name: CanSwapArmor
settings.description: UseHotbar group. Default false. When enabled, allows the hotbar method to use the MC 1.19.4+ armor-swap behavior to replace an already-equipped armor piece via the hotbar.

settings.name: SaveArmor
settings.description: Toggleable SaveArmor group, default enabled. Replaces armor pieces whose durability falls to or below DurabilityThreshold, and can auto-open the inventory to do so. Contains DurabilityThreshold and AutoOpenInventory.

settings.name: DurabilityThreshold
settings.description: SaveArmor group. Durability value at or below which an equipped armor piece is considered worth replacing. Default 24, range 0..100. When SaveArmor is off, no durability filtering is applied to candidate armor.

settings.name: AutoOpenInventory
settings.description: SaveArmor group. Default true. When enabled, the module will automatically open your inventory (closing other screens if needed) to perform the armor swap when the inventory constraints require an open inventory.

modules.name: AutoBow
modules.summary: AutoBow automatically aims at and shoots bows, crossbows, and tridents. It tracks the best enemy, computes the correct projectile angle (accounting for gravity/drop), and releases the shot once the weapon is charged enough and your aim is on target. It also offers an optional fast-charge exploit that spams movement packets to charge a bow faster than vanilla allows.
useCases: Reliably landing bow shots on moving targets in PvP without manually leading the arrow's arc.
Auto-releasing a fully charged bow or a pre-charged crossbow the instant your aim lines up with an enemy.
Charging your bow faster on vanilla servers to fire more arrows in a fight (FastCharge).

settings.name: AutoShoot
settings.description: Toggle for the auto-shoot sub-feature (enabled by default). When on, AutoBow will automatically release the bow/crossbow/trident once charge and aim conditions are met.

settings.name: Charged
settings.description: Minimum number of ticks a bow must be drawn before AutoShoot releases it. Default 15, range 3..20 ticks. Higher values wait for a more powerful shot; lower values fire sooner.

settings.name: ChargedRandom
settings.description: A float range (in ticks) of extra random charge time added on top of Charged, sampled via a Gaussian distribution to humanize timing. Default 0.0..0.0 (no randomization), range -10.0..10.0 ticks.

settings.name: DelayBetweenShots
settings.description: Minimum delay enforced between consecutive shots, in seconds. Default 0.0, range 0.0..5.0 s. Increase to slow down firing rate / appear more legit.

settings.name: AimThreshold
settings.description: Maximum allowed angular difference (in degrees) between your server rotation and the target rotation for AutoShoot to release. Default 1.5, range 1.0..4.0 degrees. Only used when relying on the BowAimbot's target; a larger value shoots even with looser aim.

settings.name: RequiresHypotheticalHit
settings.description: When enabled (default false), AutoShoot only fires if a simulated arrow fired along your current rotation is predicted to actually hit an attackable entity (it simulates up to 40 ticks of arrow flight against nearby targets). Replaces the aim-difference check with a true trajectory hit-test.

settings.name: UsePrechargedCrossbow
settings.description: When enabled (default false), AutoShoot will fire an already-charged crossbow held in either hand even if you are not currently using/drawing it.

settings.name: BowAimbot
settings.description: Toggle for the aimbot sub-feature (enabled by default). When on, AutoBow tracks the best enemy and silently sets your rotation to the calculated projectile angle so arrows land on the target.

settings.name: ThroughWalls
settings.description: Part of BowAimbot. When enabled (default true), the angle calculator will aim at targets even if there is no clear line of sight; when disabled it uses a verified-hit calculator that requires the shot to actually reach the enemy unobstructed.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: The target-selection group used by BowAimbot to pick which enemy to shoot, containing the FOV, HurtTime, and Priority settings below.

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Field-of-view cone (in degrees) within which an entity must lie relative to your crosshair to be considered a valid target. Default 180 (any direction), range 0..180.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Maximum allowed hurt-time of a candidate target; entities whose hurtTime exceeds this are skipped (so you can avoid re-targeting an entity that was just hit). Default 10, range 0..10.

settings.name: Priority
settings.description: Ordered set of criteria used to sort and choose targets. Options: Type (players first), Health (lowest health first), Distance (closest first), Direction (closest to crosshair first), HurtTime (lowest hurt-time first), Age (oldest entity first). Defaults to Type plus Distance; cannot be empty.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Group configuring how BowAimbot moves your view to the calculated angle (the dynamic rotation engine).

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Selects the rotation-smoothing algorithm used to turn toward the target. Available modes include Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration (and combat-only Interpolation/AI variants, not used here). Default is the first mode (Linear). Each mode exposes its own turn-speed settings, e.g. Linear's HorizontalTurnSpeed and VerticalTurnSpeed (float ranges, default 180..180, range 0..180 degrees/tick).

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Controls how silent rotations are reconciled with your movement input. Defaults to SILENT (rotations are server-side only and do not visibly move your camera).

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Angle difference (degrees) below which the rotation is considered to have reached its target before it starts resetting back. Default 2, range 1..180.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Number of ticks with no new rotation target before your rotation is released/reset. Default 5, range 1..30 ticks.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggle for the visual marker drawn on the currently selected target (enabled by default).

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Visual appearance of the target marker. World modes: Legacy (flat box), Circle, Image, GlowingCircle, Ghost, Hearts (orbiting hearts showing health); GUI modes: Text2D (on-screen text label) and Arrow. Defaults to the GlowingCircle appearance. Each appearance has its own sub-settings such as Color, Size/Radius, HeightMode (Feet/Top/Relative/Health/Animated) and, for Text2D, an editable Text list.

settings.name: FastCharge
settings.description: Toggle for the fast-charge exploit (disabled by default). When on, it spams movement packets while drawing a bow to charge it faster than vanilla. Intended for vanilla servers; most anti-cheats patch this.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Part of FastCharge. Number of extra movement packets sent per tick to speed up bow charging. Default 20, range 3..20; higher charges faster.

settings.name: NotInTheAir
settings.description: Part of FastCharge. When enabled (default true), fast-charging is suppressed while you are not on the ground (in the air), to reduce detection.

settings.name: NotDuringMove
settings.description: Part of FastCharge. When enabled (default false), fast-charging is suppressed while you are moving.

settings.name: NotDuringRegeneration
settings.description: Part of FastCharge. When enabled (default false), fast-charging is suppressed while you have the Regeneration effect.

settings.name: PacketType
settings.description: Part of FastCharge. Which movement packet type to spam: OnGroundOnly, PositionAndOnGround, LookAndOnGround, or Full. Default Full (sends full position+rotation packets).

modules.name: AutoBreak
modules.summary: Automatically breaks the block you are looking at without needing to hold the attack button. While enabled, whenever the attack keybind would be checked and your crosshair targets a solid (non-air) block, it keeps the attack input pressed and issues the initial click so block-breaking continues. It only acts when the attack cooldown (miss time) has elapsed.
useCases: Continuously mining or clearing blocks while looking at them, without holding left-click.
Breaking a targeted block (e.g. obsidian or a wall) hands-free during other tasks.

modules.name: AutoBuff
modules.summary: AutoBuff automatically uses or throws beneficial consumables to keep you topped up in combat, bundling several sub-features: Soup, Head, Pot (splash/lingering potions), Drink (drinkable potions) and Gapple (golden apples). Each tick it runs the first enabled feature whose conditions are met (for example swapping to and eating a golden apple when your health drops). It can silently auto-swap to the right hotbar slot, optionally avoid acting during combat, and a Refill sub-feature can move valid consumables from your inventory into the hotbar. Known aliases: AutoPot, AutoGapple, AutoSoup.
useCases: Automatically eat golden apples or drink/throw healing potions when your health gets low during PvP.
Keep soup-based health topped up on Soup-PvP servers, automatically dropping the empty bowl afterward.
Maintain buff status effects (strength, speed, regen, etc.) by auto-using or splashing the matching potions when they run out.

settings.name: AutoSwap
settings.description: Toggle for the AutoSwap group (default enabled). When on, the module silently swaps your selected hotbar slot to the best item for the situation, uses it, then swaps back; when off, it will only use a buff item if it is already your selected slot.

settings.name: DelayIn
settings.description: Default 1..1, range 0-20 ticks. Randomized delay to wait after swapping to the buff item before using it. Higher values look more human but slow reactions.

settings.name: DelayOut
settings.description: Default 1..1, range 0-20 ticks. Randomized delay to wait after using the item before swapping back to your previous slot.

settings.name: Refill
settings.description: Toggle for the Refill group (default enabled). When on, the module moves valid consumables from your main inventory into empty hotbar/offhand slots so AutoBuff always has items available; when off, no refilling occurs.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: Inventory-action constraints sub-group of Refill controlling how/when the refill clicks happen. Children: StartDelay (range, default 1..2 ticks, 0-20) delay before starting inventory actions; ClickDelay (range, default 2..4 ticks, 0-20) delay between clicks; CloseDelay (range, default 1..2 ticks, 0-20) delay before closing; MissChance (range, default 0..0 %, 0-100) chance to deliberately mis-click; Requires (multiEnum) conditions that must hold for actions to run, chosen from NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat and InventoryOpen (default none selected).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine sub-group shared by features that need a rotation change (such as Pot throwing). Children: RotationTiming (enum, default Normal; options Normal, OnTick, OnUse) controls when the throw rotation is applied relative to the use; MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent); ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1-180); TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1-30 ticks); AngleSmooth (choices) selecting the view-smoothing algorithm.

settings.name: CombatPauseTime
settings.description: Default 0, range 0-40 ticks. How long combat is paused for whenever a buff feature acts. 0 disables the pause.

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, AutoBuff does nothing while you are considered in combat, so it only buffs when you are out of a fight.

settings.name: Soup
settings.description: Toggle for the Soup feature (default enabled). When on and your health is low, the module uses mushroom stew to heal. It is health-based, eating soup when your effective health drops to or below the configured Health percentage.

settings.name: Health (Soup)
settings.description: Default 40, range 1-100 (%HP). The health percentage at or below which Soup will be used. Lower values wait until you are more hurt.

settings.name: ConsiderAbsorption (Soup)
settings.description: Default true. When on, absorption hearts are counted toward your effective health when deciding whether the Health threshold has been reached; when off, only normal health is considered.

settings.name: DropAfterUse
settings.description: Toggle for the Soup DropAfterUse group (default enabled). When on, the module drops the (now empty) bowl after drinking soup; when off, the bowl is kept.

settings.name: AssumeEmptyBowl
settings.description: Default true. When on, the module assumes the item becomes an empty bowl immediately and drops it without verifying; when off, it only drops the slot if it actually contains a bowl (and is not the offhand).

settings.name: Wait
settings.description: Default 1..2, range 1-20 ticks. Randomized delay between using the soup and dropping the empty bowl.

settings.name: Head
settings.description: Toggle for the Head feature (default enabled). When on and health is low, the module uses a player head (a server-specific healing/absorption consumable) to heal. It is health-based with the same Health/ConsiderAbsorption thresholds, plus its own cooldown and absorption cap.

settings.name: Health (Head)
settings.description: Default 40, range 1-100 (%HP). Health percentage at or below which the Head is used.

settings.name: ConsiderAbsorption (Head)
settings.description: Default true. Whether absorption hearts count toward effective health for the Head health check.

settings.name: MaxAbsorption
settings.description: Default 1, range 0-8. The Head is only used while your current absorption amount is at or below this value, preventing wasting heads when you already have plenty of absorption.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Default 0, range 0-120 (s). Minimum time that must elapse between Head uses. 0 means no enforced cooldown.

settings.name: Pot
settings.description: Toggle for the Pot feature (default enabled). When on, the module throws beneficial splash (and optionally lingering) potions at your feet to apply their effects, choosing potions whose effect you are missing. It will avoid throwing when it would benefit nearby enemies, when standing in a lingering cloud, when not close enough to the ground, or when a splash potion is already nearby.

settings.name: TillGroundDistance
settings.description: Default 2, range 1-5. Maximum distance to the ground (in blocks) at which the module is allowed to throw a potion, ensuring the splash lands near your feet rather than being wasted in mid-air.

settings.name: DoNotBenefitOthers
settings.description: Default true. When on, the module will not throw a potion if a nearby enemy (within ~16 blocks) would also gain the beneficial effect; friendly/team players nearby do not block the throw.

settings.name: AllowLingering
settings.description: Default false. When on, lingering potions are also considered valid for throwing; when off, only splash potions are used.

settings.name: Potions
settings.description: Sub-group of the Pot feature listing the supported potion effects, each its own toggleable entry (all enabled by default): Health (Instant Health), Regen (Regeneration), Strength, Speed, FireResistance, JumpBoost, and WaterBreathing. A potion type is only thrown if its entry is enabled and you currently lack that effect. The Health and Regen entries are additionally health-based and each have their own Health (int, default 40, range 1-100 %HP) threshold, so they are only thrown when your health is at or below that percentage.

settings.name: Drink
settings.description: Toggle for the Drink feature (default enabled). When on, the module drinks (holds use on) beneficial drinkable potions to apply a missing effect, selecting potions whose effect you do not currently have.

settings.name: Potions (Drink)
settings.description: Sub-group of the Drink feature listing supported drinkable potion effects, each a toggleable entry (all enabled by default): Health (Instant Health), Regen (Regeneration), Strength, Speed, FireResistance, JumpBoost, WaterBreathing. An effect is only drunk if its entry is enabled and you lack the effect; Health and Regen each have their own Health (int, default 40, range 1-100 %HP) threshold gating use by your current health.

settings.name: Gapple
settings.description: Toggle for the Gapple feature (default enabled). When on and health is low, the module eats a golden apple (and optionally an enchanted golden apple) to heal/buff. It is health-based using the shared Health/ConsiderAbsorption thresholds.

settings.name: Health (Gapple)
settings.description: Default 40, range 1-100 (%HP). Health percentage at or below which a golden apple is eaten.

settings.name: ConsiderAbsorption (Gapple)
settings.description: Default true. Whether absorption hearts count toward effective health for the Gapple health check.

settings.name: Enchanted
settings.description: Default true. When on, enchanted golden apples are also accepted as valid items to eat; when off, only normal golden apples are used.

modules.name: AutoBuild
modules.summary: AutoBuild automatically constructs structures using the shared block placer, with a selectable mode. The Portal mode locates the best nearby spot, builds a nether portal frame out of obsidian, then ignites it with flint and steel and disables itself; the Platform mode builds a flat square platform of a chosen block beneath you. Changing the mode disables the module. It is also known by the aliases Platform and AutoPortal.
useCases: Instantly build and light a nether portal from obsidian and flint and steel.
Quickly place a safe platform of obsidian (or another block) beneath you, e.g. to escape voids or bridge gaps.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the build mode: Portal (default) builds and ignites a nether portal, or Platform builds a square platform below you. Switching modes disables the module.

settings.name: DisableOnYChange
settings.description: Platform mode setting (default true). Disables the module when your Y coordinate changes from where building started.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Platform mode setting. Whitelist/Blacklist (default Whitelist) controlling which block from the Blocks list is used to build the platform.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Platform mode setting. The block(s) allowed for the platform, default obsidian. Combined with Filter to pick the hotbar slot.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Platform mode setting. The platform radius around your position, 1-6, default 3 (the platform spans Size blocks out in each horizontal direction).

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Placer sub-tree (Placing). Maximum reach distance for placements, 1.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Through-wall / facing-away reach, 0.0-6.0, default 4.5. 0 disables facing-away faces.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Tick range between placement actions, 0-40 ticks, default 1..2.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Swing/animation mode used when placing, default DoNotHide.

settings.name: ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Placer (Placing), default true. On raytrace failure, construct a center hit result so placement still works; more reliable but rotations can be slightly off and placement may go slightly out of range.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Ticks to sneak when placing on an interactable block, 0-10 ticks, default 1..1.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Conditions to ignore while placing: OpenInventory and UsingItem. Default none.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Ticks before the silently-selected slot is reset, 0-40 ticks, default 4..6.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Normal vs None rotation mode (default Normal) for aiming at placements.

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Placer RotationMode child (default false). Sends the action on post-move for a slight timing edge; may flag post-rotation anti-cheat checks.

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: Placer RotationMode child (default false). Instantly sends the action ignoring packet order; may flag anti-cheats and can make PostMove irrelevant.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: Placer Normal rotation mode child (default true). Allows rotating/placing while an inventory screen is open.

settings.name: SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Placer None rotation mode child (default false). Sends a standalone rotation packet before placement when in None mode.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations, under Normal mode). Chooses the rotation smoothing algorithm (e.g. Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration).

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). Movement correction relative to server rotation, default Silent.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). Angle difference (1-180, default 2) below which the rotation is considered reached.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). Ticks the rotation is held before resetting, 1-30 ticks, default 5.

settings.name: Support
settings.description: Placer Support sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Places helper blocks so unsupported structure positions become placeable.

settings.name: Depth
settings.description: Support child. Maximum support-path search depth (Manhattan distance), 1-12, default 4.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Support child. Minimum time between support-path searches, 0-1000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Support child. Whitelist/Blacklist (default Blacklist) for which blocks may be used as support blocks.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Support child. Block list used with the Support Filter to choose support blocks.

settings.name: DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Placer crystal-destroyer sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Attacks end crystals that would block placements.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Reach for attacking crystals, 1.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Through-wall reach for attacking crystals, 0.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Minimum time between crystal attacks, 0-1000 ms, default 0.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Swing/animation mode used when attacking crystals, default DoNotHide.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Normal vs None rotation mode (default Normal) with the same PostMove/Instant and Normal (Rotations, IgnoreOpenInventory) / None (SendRotationPacket) sub-options as the main placer.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Placer PlacementRenderer sub-group (disabled by default). Renders boxes at positions queued to be placed. Contains the rendering settings below.

settings.name: PlacedRendering
settings.description: Placer PlacementRenderer sub-group (enabled by default). Renders boxes at positions just placed (not kept). Contains the same rendering settings as TargetRendering.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child (default true). Clumps/culls adjacent placement boxes for cleaner rendering.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Box size at animation start, 0.0-2.0, default 1.0.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing for the start-size animation, default Linear.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Box size at animation end, 0.0-2.0, default 0.8.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing for the end-size animation, default Linear.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing for the fade-in, default Linear.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing for the fade-out, default Linear.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fade-in duration, 0-5000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fade-out duration, 0-5000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fill color of placement boxes, default green low alpha.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Outline color of placement boxes, default green fully opaque.

modules.name: AutoChatGame
modules.summary: AutoChatGame automatically solves chat-game riddles and questions by sending them to an OpenAI-compatible API and posting the AI's answer back into chat. It listens only to server game messages, waits for a configurable trigger sentence, buffers the following lines into a single question, and asks the configured model for a short answer. It also auto-types 'gg' when it detects a 'Show some love by typing' message. The module requires a valid OpenAI key and will disable itself with a warning if none is set.
useCases: Winning server chat mini-games (trivia, math, unscramble, first-to-type) automatically.
Hands-free 'gg' replies and quick answers on minigame servers that run periodic chat games.

settings.name: BaseUrl
settings.description: Text field for the API base URL. Defaults to the built-in OpenAI base URL. Change it to point at a different OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

settings.name: OpenAiKey
settings.description: Text field for your OpenAI API key. Empty by default; if left blank the module prints a warning and disables itself on enable.

settings.name: Model
settings.description: Text field for the model name used for completions. Defaults to 'gpt-4o-mini', which the author notes is sufficient for the chat game.

settings.name: ReactionTime
settings.description: Integer range (in ms) for the random delay before sending an answer or 'gg', simulating human reaction time. Default 1000..5000, allowed 0..10000; a random value in the range is picked each time.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Cooldown in minutes after answering before the module will answer again, preventing duplicate answers to the same tagged round. Default 2, range 0..60.

settings.name: BufferTime
settings.description: Time in ms after the trigger sentence during which incoming game messages are collected into the question buffer. Default 200, range 0..500. Larger values capture multi-line questions but increase latency.

settings.name: TriggerSentence
settings.description: Text the module looks for in a game message to start capturing a question. Default 'Chat Game'.

settings.name: IncludeTrigger
settings.description: If true (default), the message containing the trigger sentence is itself added to the question buffer; if false, that line is skipped and only subsequent lines are buffered.

settings.name: ServerName
settings.description: Text inserted into the prompt's {SERVER_NAME} placeholder to give the AI context about the server. Default 'Minecraft'.

settings.name: AnswerTemplate
settings.description: Format string applied to the AI answer before sending. Default '%s' (sends the raw answer). If the formatted result starts with '/', it is sent as a command instead of a chat message.

settings.name: Prompt
settings.description: Text field holding the system prompt sent to the AI, pre-filled with an optimized default that instructs the AI to answer chat-game questions tersely. The {SERVER_NAME} placeholder is replaced with the ServerName value. Editing is discouraged; line breaks may break the JSON format.

modules.name: AutoClicker
modules.summary: AutoClicker automatically clicks for you while you hold down (or, optionally, without holding) the attack and/or use mouse buttons. It uses a humanized click scheduler that simulates how Minecraft processes per-tick clicks, with configurable CPS, click patterns and cooldown handling. The attack side can be restricted by target type, weapon type and critical-hit logic, while the use side can ignore certain held items, blocks and situations. It is also known by the alias TriggerBot.
useCases: Maintain a high, randomized click rate in PvP without manually spamming the attack button.
Use it as a trigger bot that only attacks when your crosshair is on an enemy and you are holding the right weapon.
Auto-place blocks or auto-use items by enabling the Use side while ignoring items/blocks you do not want it to spam.

settings.name: Attack
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling automatic left-click / attacking. When disabled, no automatic attacking occurs.

settings.name: CPS
settings.description: Attack clicker: clicks-per-second range (default 5..8, range 1..max 60, unit clicks). The scheduler randomly varies clicks within this range. Changing it refills the click pattern.

settings.name: Technique
settings.description: Attack clicker click pattern. Options: Stabilized (default), Efficient, Spamming, DoubleClick, Drag, Butterfly, NormalDistribution. Each shapes the timing/distribution of clicks differently to mimic various clicking styles.

settings.name: AttackCooldown
settings.description: Attack clicker only (present because the key is the attack key), default true. When enabled, respects Minecraft's miss cooldown so it will not click again while in the post-miss attack cooldown, helping bypass anti-cheats that detect ignoring this cooldown.

settings.name: Minimum
settings.description: ItemCooldown sub-group of the attack clicker. Minimum attack-strength cooldown progress required before a click counts, chosen randomly within the range (default 1.0..1.0, range 0.0..2.0). 1.0 means waiting for a fully-charged attack; lower values allow clicking before the cooldown fully recharges.

settings.name: RequiresNoInput
settings.description: Attack side, default false. When enabled, attacking is automated even without holding the attack button (full auto). When disabled, you must hold the button.

settings.name: DelayOnBroken
settings.description: Attack side, default true. When enabled, the clicker pauses for about 300ms after finishing breaking a block, preventing an unwanted attack immediately after mining.

settings.name: Objective
settings.description: Attack side. Restricts what your crosshair must be on for the clicker to fire. Options: Enemy (only entities that should be attacked), Entity (any entity), Block (only blocks), Any (default, no restriction).

settings.name: OnItemUse
settings.description: Attack side. Behavior when you are using an item while the clicker wants to attack. Options: Wait (default, waits until item use finishes then waits DelayPostStopUse), Stop (releases the item being used then waits DelayPostStopUse), Ignore (attacks anyway).

settings.name: Weapon
settings.description: Attack side. The clicker only attacks when the item in your main hand matches one of the selected weapon types (default ANY). Cannot be set to none.

settings.name: Criticals
settings.description: Attack side. Critical-hit selection mode (default Smart) that controls whether/when the clicker waits to land critical hits and whether it should stop sprinting for criticals. It gates clicks on entities until a critical hit condition is satisfied.

settings.name: DelayPostStopUse
settings.description: Attack side. Extra ticks to wait after item use has stopped/finished (per OnItemUse) before resuming clicking. Default 0, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: Use
settings.description: Toggleable group (disabled by default) controlling automatic right-click / item use. When enabled, the module auto-uses the use key under the configured conditions.

settings.name: CPS
settings.description: Use clicker: clicks-per-second range for the use/right-click scheduler (default 5..8, range 1..60, unit clicks). Separate from the attack clicker's CPS.

settings.name: Technique
settings.description: Use clicker click pattern (default Stabilized; same options as the attack clicker). Shapes the timing of automatic right-clicks.

settings.name: HoldingItemsForIgnore
settings.description: Use side. List of items that, when held in the main or off hand, cause the use clicker to do nothing. Defaults include Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, Ender Pearl, Ender Eye and Player Head, so it will not accidentally spam these.

settings.name: BlocksForIgnore
settings.description: Use side. List of blocks the use clicker will not right-click. Defaults to all doors, fence gates and trapdoors so it does not spam-toggle them.

settings.name: DelayStart
settings.description: Use side, default false. When enabled, the use clicker waits 2 ticks before its first click after you start holding/triggering use.

settings.name: OnlyBlock
settings.description: Use side, default false. When enabled, the use clicker only acts when the item in your main or off hand is a placeable block item.

settings.name: RequiresNoInput
settings.description: Use side, default false. When enabled, item use is automated without holding the use button (full auto right-click); when disabled you must hold the button.

modules.name: AutoConfig
modules.summary: AutoConfig automatically loads a matching saved settings configuration for the server you connect to, so the right modules/settings are applied per server. When you join a server it intercepts the connection, looks up known online configs whose server address matches the server's root domain (preferring the shortest-named, most general config), loads it, then proceeds with the connection. It shows notifications for success, failure, missing configs, or blacklisted servers, and skips a small built-in blacklist of anticheat test servers (poke.sexy, loyisa.cn, anticheat-test.com). It is enabled by default and ignores the normal in-game running requirement.
useCases: Automatically apply a server-specific config (e.g. a tuned Hypixel setup) every time you connect, without manually loading it.
Trigger an immediate config load for the server you are already on by toggling the module while connected.

modules.name: AutoCrafter
modules.summary: AutoCrafter automatically crafts a configured list of items using the vanilla recipe book while a supported crafting/smelting menu is open and its recipe book tab is open. For each target item it finds a craftable recipe (avoiding crafting loops such as ingot to block to ingot), places the recipe and takes the result, merging it into your inventory. It can craft full stacks, process items sequentially or all in one tick, and choose what to do when the inventory is full.
useCases: Mass-craft building blocks (e.g. deepslate variants) automatically when standing at a crafting table with the recipe book open.
Auto-smelt ores/foods at a furnace, blast furnace or smoker by selecting those containers and target outputs.
Bulk-process a queue of items in order, automatically stopping, closing, or throwing items when your inventory fills up.

settings.name: ItemsToCraft
settings.description: Ordered list of items the module will attempt to craft/produce. Defaults to Polished Deepslate, Deepslate Bricks and Deepslate Tiles. Later items in the list are treated as ingredients to avoid crafting loops.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Randomized delay (in ticks) between craft actions. Default 2..3, range 1..20 ticks.

settings.name: StackCrafting
settings.description: When enabled, places recipes for a full stack at once rather than a single item. Default true.

settings.name: SequentialCrafting
settings.description: When enabled, only one item from the list is processed per tick handler pass (sequential). When disabled, the module continues through the list in one pass (except for furnace-type menus, which are always sequential). Default true.

settings.name: OnFull
settings.description: Action taken when the result cannot be merged because your inventory is full. Disable turns the module off; CloseScreen closes the container; Wait waits and retries; Throw drops the result item. Default Wait.

settings.name: AllowedContainers
settings.description: Which recipe-book menus AutoCrafter is allowed to operate in: Inventory (2x2 crafting), CraftingTable, Furnace, BlastFurnace, Smoker. Default selects only CraftingTable.

modules.name: AutoDisable
modules.summary: AutoDisable automatically turns off a chosen set of modules whenever a configured trigger event occurs (such as getting flagged, dying, switching worlds, or disconnecting).
