The list of modules it manages is edited through the AutoDisable command rather than purely from the settings panel, and by default it pre-fills the list with Fly, Speed, NoClip and KillAura. When any of the selected trigger events fires, every still-enabled module in its list is disabled and a notification is shown explaining the reason.
useCases: Automatically disable risky combat or movement cheats the moment an anticheat flag (server position correction) is received, to reduce the chance of a ban.
Have modules switch off on death so you don't keep running cheats after respawning.
Cleanly disable active modules when changing worlds or disconnecting so you start fresh next session.

settings.name: Modules
settings.description: A registry list of client-module names that AutoDisable will turn off when a trigger fires. It is populated/edited via the AutoDisable command and the add/remove helpers; by default it contains Fly, Speed, NoClip and KillAura. Adding or removing module names changes which modules get disabled on the configured events.

settings.name: On
settings.description: Selects which event(s) trigger the auto-disable. Choices are Flag (a ClientboundPlayerPositionPacket / server teleport, treated as an anticheat flag), Death, WorldChange, and Disconnect. Multiple can be enabled at once; at least one must remain selected (it cannot be set to none).

modules.name: AutoDodge
modules.summary: AutoDodge automatically evades incoming arrows, spectral arrows, and returning tridents by simulating their flight paths against a simulated version of your player. When a projectile is predicted to hit you, it computes an evasion plan and overrides your movement input (and optionally your yaw and a jump) to step out of the way. It will not act while Blink is running, while MurderMystery disallows arrow dodging, or under the configured ignore conditions.
useCases: Automatically sidestep enemy bow shots in PvP without manual reaction.
Dodge skeleton arrows or trident throws while focusing on melee combat.

settings.name: AllowRotationChange
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off). When enabled, AutoDodge is allowed to change your yaw/rotation as part of the dodge plan, enabling more effective evasions that require turning.

settings.name: AllowJump
settings.description: Child of AllowRotationChange (default on). When enabled and the dodge plan calls for it, AutoDodge will jump (only while on the ground) to evade the projectile.

settings.name: AllowTimer
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off). When enabled, AutoDodge may use game timer manipulation to help dodge when the plan requests it.

settings.name: TimerSpeed
settings.description: Child of AllowTimer (default 2.0, range 1.0 to 10.0, suffix x). The timer/game-speed multiplier requested during a timer-assisted dodge. Higher values speed up the client tick rate to move out of the way faster.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Multi-select of situations in which AutoDodge should still run normally; if an option is NOT selected, AutoDodge is suppressed in that situation. Options: OpenInventory (when an inventory/container screen is open), UsingItem (while using/eating/charging an item), and UsingScaffold (while the Scaffold module is running).

modules.name: AutoF5
modules.summary: AutoF5 automatically switches the camera into third-person back view (the F5 perspective) whenever you open a container inventory, so you can see your character while browsing chests and other GUIs. It only triggers for container screens (AbstractContainerScreen) and only when the optional screen-type and screen-title filters both validate the open screen. When the filters do not match, the normal first-person view is kept.
useCases: Automatically rotate to third-person while looting chests so you can keep an eye on your surroundings.
Restrict the auto-perspective to only specific container types (e.g. chests, shulker boxes) using the filters.

settings.name: CheckScreenHandlerType
settings.description: Toggle for the screen-handler-type filter group (enabled by default). When enabled, AutoF5 only activates if the open container's menu type passes the Types/Filter check below; when disabled, the menu type is not considered.

settings.name: Types
settings.description: The list of container menu types this filter matches. Defaults to GENERIC_9x3, GENERIC_9x6 and SHULKER_BOX. Combined with Filter to whitelist or blacklist which container handler types trigger AutoF5.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whether the Types list is a whitelist or blacklist (default WHITELIST). WHITELIST means only the listed menu types activate AutoF5; BLACKLIST means every type except the listed ones activates it.

settings.name: CheckScreenTitle
settings.description: Toggle for the screen-title filter group (enabled by default, also known as CheckTitle). When enabled, AutoF5 only activates if the open screen's title passes the Titles/Custom/Filter check; when disabled, the title is not considered.

settings.name: Titles
settings.description: Predefined container title keys to match against the screen title. Defaults to Chest, LargeChest, ShulkerBox, Barrel and ChestMinecart. Other selectable titles include Beacon, BlastFurnace, BrewingStand, Dispenser, Dropper, EnderChest, Furnace, Hopper, Smoker and HopperMinecart.

settings.name: Custom
settings.description: A list of custom title strings to additionally match (empty by default). A screen counts as matching if its title equals one of the predefined Titles or appears in this custom list.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whether the title match is treated as a whitelist or blacklist (default WHITELIST). WHITELIST means only matching titles activate AutoF5; BLACKLIST inverts it so matching titles are excluded.

modules.name: AutoFarm
modules.summary: AutoFarm automatically harvests, replants and fertilizes crops for you. It scans loaded chunks for farmable blocks, aims at the nearest valid target through the rotation engine, and then either breaks ready crops (preferring a Fortune tool), uses/harvests right-click crops, replants seeds/nether wart/cocoa on suitable blocks, or applies bone meal. It prefers harvesting over planting, can auto-walk to farm targets and dropped items, visualizes targets and paths, and can disable itself when your inventory is full.
useCases: Fully automate a wheat/carrot/potato/beetroot/nether wart/cocoa farm: break ready crops and replant them.
Speed up crop growth automatically by applying bone meal to fertilizable plants.
Walk the player automatically between farm blocks and pick up dropped produce while farming.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum reach distance for interacting with and searching farm blocks, 1.0-6.0, default 5.0.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Reach distance for targeting blocks through walls, 0.0-6.0, default 0. It is clamped to never exceed Range.

settings.name: InteractDelay
settings.description: Ticks to wait after fully breaking/interacting with a block, 1-15 ticks, default 2..3 (random value each time).

settings.name: DisableOnFullInventory
settings.description: When true (default false), disables the module and shows a notification when your inventory has no free space.

settings.name: AutoPlant
settings.description: Toggle for the auto-replant sub-group (enabled by default; alias AutoPlace). When enabled, replants seeds, nether wart and cocoa on suitable farm blocks. Contains a SwapBackDelay child.

settings.name: SwapBackDelay
settings.description: AutoPlant child. Ticks before the silently-selected planting slot is reset, 1-20 ticks, default 1..2.

settings.name: AutoUseBoneMeal
settings.description: Toggle for the bone meal sub-group (default false). When enabled, applies bone meal to fertilizable crops. Contains UseDelay and SwapBackDelay children.

settings.name: UseDelay
settings.description: AutoUseBoneMeal child. Random cooldown between bone meal uses, 0-20000 ms, default 20..200 (a fresh random value is chosen after each use).

settings.name: SwapBackDelay
settings.description: AutoUseBoneMeal child. Ticks before the silently-selected bone meal slot is reset, 1-20 ticks, default 1..2.

settings.name: UseFortune
settings.description: When true (default), silently swaps to the hotbar item with the highest Fortune enchantment (level >= 1) before breaking crops to increase drops.

settings.name: AutoWalk
settings.description: Navigation sub-group toggle (default false). Automatically walks the player toward farm targets and, optionally, dropped items. Contains MinimumDistance, ToPlant, Auto, and the ToItems sub-group.

settings.name: MinimumDistance
settings.description: AutoWalk child. How close the player should get to the target before stopping, 1.0-4.0, default 2.0.

settings.name: ToPlant
settings.description: AutoWalk child (default true; alias ToPlace). When enabled, also walks to farmland/soul sand blocks that need replanting (only if you have plantable items); otherwise only walks to harvestable blocks.

settings.name: Auto
settings.description: AutoWalk child. Movement assists to enable while navigating: Jump (auto-jump over obstacles), Swim (auto-swim/jump in water) and Sprint. Default none selected.

settings.name: ToItems
settings.description: AutoWalk child sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Also walks toward dropped item entities to pick them up (skipped when the inventory is full). Contains Range, Items and Filter children.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: ToItems child. Maximum distance to consider walking to a dropped item, 8.0-64.0, default 20.0.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: ToItems child. The item list used with the ToItems Filter to decide which dropped items to walk to (empty by default).

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: ToItems child. Whitelist/Blacklist (default Blacklist) applied to the Items list to control which dropped items are picked up.

settings.name: Visualize
settings.description: Visualizer sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Renders the farm targets and auto-walk path. Contains the Path and Blocks sub-groups.

settings.name: Path
settings.description: Visualize child sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Draws a line from the player to the current auto-walk target (only when AutoWalk is running). Contains PathColor.

settings.name: PathColor
settings.description: Path child. Color of the auto-walk path line, default green (36,237,0,255).

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Visualize child sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Draws boxes on tracked farm blocks. Contains Outline, ReadyColor, PlaceColor, Range, Rainbow, PlaceTargets and the CurrentTarget sub-group.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Blocks child (default true). Draws an outline around the rendered farm-block boxes.

settings.name: ReadyColor
settings.description: Blocks child. Color used for blocks ready to harvest, default green (36,237,0,255).

settings.name: PlaceColor
settings.description: Blocks child. Color used to highlight the plantable sides of placeable blocks, default light green (191,245,66,100).

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Blocks child. Maximum horizontal distance from the player at which farm blocks are rendered, 10-128, default 50.

settings.name: Rainbow
settings.description: Blocks child (default false). When enabled, animates the harvest/base box color through a rainbow instead of using ReadyColor.

settings.name: PlaceTargets
settings.description: Blocks child. Selects which plantable block types (Farmland, SoulSand, JungleLogs) have their placeable sides highlighted.

settings.name: CurrentTarget
settings.description: Blocks child sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Highlights the block currently being targeted. Contains Color and Rainbow children.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: CurrentTarget child. Color of the current-target box, default blue (66,120,245,255).

settings.name: Rainbow
settings.description: CurrentTarget child (default false). When enabled, animates the current-target box color through a rainbow instead of using Color.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Rotations sub-tree. Chooses the rotation smoothing algorithm (e.g. Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration) used when aiming at farm blocks.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Rotations sub-tree. Movement correction relative to the server rotation, default Silent.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Rotations sub-tree. Angle difference (1-180, default 2) below which the rotation is considered reached.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Rotations sub-tree. Ticks the rotation is held before resetting to your own aim, 1-30 ticks, default 5.

modules.name: AutoFish
modules.summary: AutoFish automatically catches fish for you while a fishing rod is held in either hand. It listens for the fishing bobber splash sound and, when heard near your hook, reels the rod in after a short randomized delay. It can optionally recast the rod after a catch and auto-cast it when no hook is active, and it can verify that the trigger sound originates close to your hook to avoid false triggers.
useCases: AFK fishing farms: leave the rod in hand and let the module catch and recast automatically.
Reliable fishing on servers with nearby players where many splash sounds occur, by restricting triggers to sounds close to your own hook.
Hands-free continuous fishing by enabling AutoCastRod so the rod is thrown again whenever no hook is in the water.

settings.name: ReelDelay
settings.description: Randomized delay (in ticks) after a catch is detected before reeling the rod in. Default 5..8, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: RecastRod
settings.description: Toggleable group: when enabled, the rod is recast after reeling in a catch. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Randomized delay (in ticks) after reeling in before recasting the rod. Default 15..20, range 10..30 ticks. (Inside the RecastRod group.)

settings.name: AutoCastRod
settings.description: Toggleable group: when enabled, casts the rod automatically whenever no fishing hook is active. Disabled by default.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Randomized delay (in ticks) before auto-casting the rod when no hook is active. Default 15..20, range 0..30 ticks. (Inside the AutoCastRod group.)

settings.name: Sounds
settings.description: List of sound events that trigger the reel/pull. Defaults to the fishing bobber splash sound; additional custom server sounds can be added so non-vanilla catch sounds also trigger AutoFish.

settings.name: SoundDistance
settings.description: Toggleable group: when enabled, only triggers a catch if the trigger sound is played close to your fishing hook, preventing false triggers from sounds elsewhere. Enabled by default.

settings.name: MaxDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance (in blocks) between your hook and the trigger sound for the catch to register. Default 1.0, range 0.0..10.0 blocks. (Inside the SoundDistance group.)

modules.name: AutoLeave
modules.summary: AutoLeave automatically disconnects you from the server when your health drops below a configured threshold, helping you avoid death. It continuously checks your health and, once the condition has held for the configured delay, triggers a kick/leave using the chosen Kick mode and then disables itself. It ignores the check in creative mode, in singleplayer, or while holding a Totem of Undying (death-protection item) in either hand.
useCases: Combat-log to safety when low on health during PvP to avoid losing your items.
Auto-disconnect at a health buffer so you never die to chip damage on a server.

settings.name: Health
settings.description: Health threshold (in HP) at or above which you are considered safe. Default 8, range 0..20. When your health is below this value (and you have no death protection), the leave is triggered.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Number of ticks the low-health condition must persist before leaving. Default 0..0 (immediate), range 0..60 ticks. A random value in the range is used each time; if the condition stops being met the counter resets.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: How to leave the server, using the Kick module's modes. Default Quit (clean disconnect). Other options: InvalidPacket, SelfHurt, IllegalChat, IllegalSwitchitem, IllegalInteract, which force a server kick via malformed/illegal packets.

modules.name: AutoMobHeal
modules.summary: AutoMobHeal automatically heals nearby vanilla-healable mobs by silently selecting the correct repair or feeding item and interacting with the mob, exactly as the vanilla game would. It scans rendered entities within range that you have line of sight to, picks the closest valid target whose health is at or below the configured threshold, and uses the appropriate item (iron ingots for iron golems, mob-specific foods for animals). Each supported mob type is its own toggleable group with its own health threshold and item preferences, and the module respects sneak-interactions and avoids wasting over-healing items when configured. It is also known by the alias AutoGolemRepair.
useCases: Keep an iron golem repaired during a raid or farm by feeding it iron ingots automatically.
Automatically feed and heal tamed wolves, cats, horses, llamas, camels or nautili so your pets/mounts stay alive.
Maintain a mob farm or village defense without manually managing healing items.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum distance to a mob to heal it, 1.0-6.0, default 4.5. Effective range is clamped to the player's actual entity interaction range.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Ticks to wait after a successful heal interaction before the next one, 0-40 ticks, default 4..4 (a random value in the range is used).

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Ticks before the silently-selected hotbar slot is reset back to your original slot, 0-20 ticks, default 2.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: Swing/animation mode used when interacting with the mob, default DoNotHide.

settings.name: IronGolem
settings.description: Toggle for healing iron golems (enabled by default). Uses the closest iron ingot in the offhand/hotbar to repair the golem. Contains a HealthThreshold child.

settings.name: Wolf
settings.description: Toggle for healing wolves (enabled by default). Only heals tamed wolves, feeding any item in the wolf-food tag (heals 2x the food's nutrition). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: Cat
settings.description: Toggle for healing cats (enabled by default). Only heals cats you own, feeding any item in the cat-food tag (heals 1x nutrition). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: HorseFamily
settings.description: Toggle for healing horses and donkeys/mules (enabled by default; excludes llamas, camels, zombie and skeleton horses). Feeds sugar (1), wheat (2), apple (3), carrot (3) or hay block (20), with optional golden items. Contains HealthThreshold, NoWaste and the three golden-food toggles below.

settings.name: AllowGoldenCarrot
settings.description: HorseFamily child (default false). When enabled, allows feeding golden carrots (heals 4) to horses.

settings.name: AllowGoldenApple
settings.description: HorseFamily child (default false). When enabled, allows feeding golden apples (heals 10) to horses.

settings.name: AllowEnchantedGoldenApple
settings.description: HorseFamily child (default false). When enabled, allows feeding enchanted golden apples (heals 10) to horses.

settings.name: ZombieHorse
settings.description: Toggle for healing zombie horses (enabled by default). Feeds red mushrooms (heals 3). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: Llama
settings.description: Toggle for healing llamas (enabled by default). Feeds wheat (heals 2) or hay block (heals 10). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: Camel
settings.description: Toggle for healing camels (enabled by default; excludes camel husks). Feeds cactus (heals 2). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: CamelHusk
settings.description: Toggle for healing camel husks (enabled by default). Feeds rabbit's foot (heals 2). Contains HealthThreshold and NoWaste children.

settings.name: Nautilus
settings.description: Toggle for healing nautili (enabled by default; only tamed, non-baby). Feeds raw/cooked fish (heals 2x nutrition) and optionally fish buckets. Prefers non-bucket food. Contains HealthThreshold, NoWaste and AllowBucketFood children.

settings.name: AllowBucketFood
settings.description: Nautilus child (default false). When enabled, allows using fish buckets (cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish buckets) as healing food in addition to normal fish.

settings.name: HealthThreshold
settings.description: Shared child of every heal-target group. The mob is only healed when its health is at or below this percentage of its max health, 1-100%, default 75%. Higher values heal mobs earlier (at higher health).

settings.name: NoWaste
settings.description: Shared child of every food-based heal-target group (default true). When enabled, avoids picking food whose heal amount exceeds the mob's missing health, so over-healing items are not wasted; the module otherwise prefers the food that best matches the missing health.

modules.name: AutoPearl
modules.summary: AutoPearl detects ender pearls thrown by other players, simulates the pearl's trajectory to find its landing point, and automatically aims and throws your own pearl to land at the same spot. It hooks the pearl-spawn packet, computes the destination, and if limits are satisfied queues a rotation and uses a pearl from your hotbar or offhand. It can pause combat briefly while throwing and optionally rotate silently to the calculated angle before throwing.
useCases: Following an enemy's pearl to the same destination in PvP (combo/escape tracking).
Automatically matching a specific target's pearl landing spot when used with KillAura's target.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which thrown pearls trigger the module. Trigger (default): reacts to any pearl whose owner should be attacked (or owner-less pearls). Target: only reacts to a pearl thrown by KillAura's current target.

settings.name: Limits
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that gates throwing on distance and angle constraints. When disabled, no limit checks are applied.

settings.name: Angle
settings.description: Limits sub-setting: maximum crosshair-to-pearl angle (degrees) for the module to react. Default 180 (no restriction), range 0..180. Lower values only react to pearls roughly in front of you.

settings.name: MinDistance
settings.description: Limits sub-setting ('MinDistance'): minimum distance in meters from you to the pearl's destination required to act; if the destination is closer than this, the module skips it. Default 8.0, range 0.0..10.0.

settings.name: DestinationDistance
settings.description: Limits sub-setting ('DestinationDistance'): maximum allowed distance in meters between the enemy pearl's landing point and your own simulated pearl's landing point for the throw to be considered accurate. Default 8.0, range 0.0..30.0.

settings.name: Rotate
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled). When enabled, the module silently rotates toward the calculated throw angle and only throws once the server rotation is within ~1 degree of the target; when disabled it throws without rotating.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine sub-group inside Rotate that configures how rotations are performed (contains AngleSmooth, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold, TicksUntilReset below).

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Rotations setting: smoothing algorithm used when turning toward the target. Choices (non-combat variant): Linear (default), Sigmoid, Acceleration. Each choice exposes its own speed/curve settings.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Rotations setting: how rotations interact with movement. Defaults to Silent (server-side rotation without changing visible aim).

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Rotations setting: angular difference (degrees) below which the rotation is considered reached and reset can begin. Default 2, range 1..180.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Rotations setting: number of ticks to keep the rotation before resetting to normal aim. Default 5, range 1..30.

settings.name: CombatPauseTime
settings.description: How long (in ticks) combat is paused for while AutoPearl operates. Default 0 (no pause), range 0..40.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Random delay range (in ticks) before the hotbar slot is reset after using the pearl. Default 0..0 (no delay), allowed 0..40; a random value in range is used.

modules.name: AutoQueue
modules.summary: AutoQueue (also known as AutoPlay) automatically re-queues you into games on supported servers so you can chain matches without manual interaction. It works through selectable server presets: a built-in Hypixel SkyWars preset that sends a /play command while paper is in your hotbar, a GommeHD.net Duels preset that interacts with the Duels NPC and re-queues on win/loss, and a fully Custom preset where you define your own trigger (what signals a finished game) and action (how to re-queue). It can be configured to pause itself while certain screens are open so it does not fire while you are in a menu.
useCases: Endlessly farm SkyWars or Duels matches AFK-style by auto-rejoining queues after each game.
On Hypixel SkyWars, automatically run the /play solo command whenever you return to the lobby.
Build a custom auto-requeue routine for any server by matching a title/chat/item/tab trigger and firing a chat command or item use.

settings.name: Presets
settings.description: Selects which server preset/behavior to use. Options: HypixelSW (default), GommeDuels, Custom. Each preset exposes its own sub-settings (below).

settings.name: Pause
settings.description: Conditions under which AutoQueue suspends itself (no triggers/actions fire). Options: ClickGuiOpen (the LiquidBounce ClickGUI is open), ChatScreenOpen (the chat input screen is open), ContainerScreenOpen (any container/inventory GUI is open), PauseScreenOpen (the game pause menu is open). Default: none selected.

settings.name: GameMode
settings.description: HypixelSW preset only. Which SkyWars solo mode to join. Options: Normal (sends 'play solo_normal', default) or Insane (sends 'play solo_insane'). The join command is only sent while paper is present in your hotbar.

settings.name: WinMessage
settings.description: GommeDuels preset only. Text chat message automatically sent ~2 seconds after winning a match. Default: 'GG, nice try'.

settings.name: LoseMessage
settings.description: GommeDuels preset only. Text chat message automatically sent ~2 seconds after losing a match. Default: 'GG, bist wohl besser als ich!'.

settings.name: ControlKillAura
settings.description: GommeDuels preset only. When enabled (default true), AutoQueue disables KillAura outside of an active match and re-enables it once a match starts.

settings.name: Trigger
settings.description: Custom preset only. Selects what event marks a finished game and should start the next queue. Options: Title, Subtitle, Message, Item, TabHeader, TabFooter (each with its own settings below). Default: first option (Title).

settings.name: Keywords
settings.description: Custom preset, Title trigger: list of substrings searched in the on-screen title; if any appears, the trigger fires. Defaults: 'Win', '胜利'. (The Subtitle trigger has its own Keywords list defaulting to '恭喜'; the Message trigger has its own Keywords list defaulting to 'Новая игра', '游戏结束'.)

settings.name: ChatTypes
settings.description: Custom preset, Message trigger only. Which chat message types are scanned for the keywords. Default: GAME_MESSAGE; at least one type must remain selected (cannot be none).

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Custom preset, Item trigger and UseItem action. Chooses how the relevant item is identified: 'Name' (match by display name) or 'Item' (match by item type). For the Item trigger, the trigger fires when a matching item is found in your offhand or hotbar.

settings.name: Names
settings.description: Sub-setting of the 'Name' identification mode. List of name strings to match against an item's display name. Default: 'Paper'.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Sub-setting of the 'Name' identification mode. String match mode applied to the name list (e.g. Equals/Contains). Default: EQUALS.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: Sub-setting of the 'Item' identification mode. Set of item types to match. Default: Paper.

settings.name: Text
settings.description: Custom preset, TabHeader/TabFooter triggers. Substring searched in the tab-list header (TabHeader) or footer (TabFooter); the trigger fires when present. Default: 'Duels'.

settings.name: Action
settings.description: Custom preset only. Selects what AutoQueue does to re-queue once the trigger fires. Options: Chat (send chat messages/commands) or UseItem (select and use a matching item). Default: first option (Chat).

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Custom preset, Chat action. Random delay (in ms, range 0..5000) before sending the first message. Default: 0..0 (no delay).

settings.name: MessageDelay
settings.description: Custom preset, Chat action. Random delay (in ms, range 0..5000) between sending subsequent messages. Default: 0..0 (no delay).

settings.name: Messages
settings.description: Custom preset, Chat action. The list of chat messages/commands sent in order to re-queue. Default: '/play solo_normal'.

settings.name: WaitUntilWorldChange
settings.description: Custom preset only. When enabled (default true), after firing the action AutoQueue waits until a world change is detected (i.e. you are actually moved into a new game) before continuing its loop.

settings.name: Control
settings.description: Custom preset only. Toggleable group (default enabled) that automatically toggles other modules off while you are in a queue and back on once you leave. Contains the child toggles below.

settings.name: KillAura
settings.description: Child of the Custom preset's Control group. When enabled (default true), KillAura is disabled while in queue and re-enabled when you leave the queue.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Child of the Custom preset's Control group. When enabled (default false), the Speed module is disabled while in queue and re-enabled when you leave the queue.

modules.name: AutoRespawn
modules.summary: Automatically respawns your character after death. When the death screen appears, it triggers a respawn and closes the screen, optionally after a configurable delay (since the respawn button is not clickable for the first ~20 ticks on the death screen).
useCases: Instantly returning to the world after dying without manually clicking respawn.
Re-entering combat or a farm quickly after death by minimizing downtime on the death screen.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Ticks to wait after the death screen appears before respawning. Default 0 (respawn immediately), range 0..20 ticks. Useful because the respawn button is not clickable for roughly 20 ticks after death.

modules.name: AutoRod
modules.summary: AutoRod automatically uses a fishing rod against nearby enemies for combat utility (knockback/disruption). When a valid target is within the configured range and visible, it silently aims the rod (either with a straight/linear point or with proper projectile gravity), casts the rod, and then pulls it back when the hook lands on the entity, stops moving, the timeout expires, or the target leaves range. It picks the closest valid target and respects a set of safety requirements (own health, target health, nearby enemy count, currently held item, other active modules).
useCases: Automatically knock back or interrupt opponents in PvP without manually timing rod casts.
Disrupt enemies who are eating, drawing a bow, or running away by reeling them with the rod.
Keep distance in crystal/sword fights by reliably landing rod hits at range.

settings.name: GravityType
settings.description: How the aim point is computed. Linear (default) aims in a straight line at a tracked point on the target; Projectile uses the fishing rod's trajectory/gravity so the cast arcs correctly toward the target at longer ranges.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Distance band (in blocks) at which a target is considered valid for casting. Default 3.5-5, adjustable within 2-10. Targets must be at least the start distance and at most the end distance (plus ScanExtraRange) away.

settings.name: ScanExtraRange
settings.description: Extra range randomly added on top of the max Range each cast to vary detection distance. Default 0-0 (disabled), adjustable 0-5. A random value in this band is chosen on each use.

settings.name: MaxEnemiesNearby
settings.description: Maximum number of valid targets that may be nearby for AutoRod to act. Default 1, range 0-10; 0 means no limit. If more enemies than this are tracked, AutoRod will not cast.

settings.name: MinHealth
settings.description: Minimum own health required to use the rod. Default 10, range 1-20. Below this health AutoRod stays inactive to avoid risky plays.

settings.name: MinTargetHealth
settings.description: Minimum actual health a target must have to be roded. Default 4, range 1-20. Targets weaker than this are skipped.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be true to act, chosen from KillAura-style requirements (Click, Weapon, EmptyHand, VanillaName, NotBreaking). Default is all of these except EmptyHand. Click = attack key held/recently pressed; Weapon = holding a weapon; EmptyHand = empty main hand; VanillaName = item has no custom name; NotBreaking = not currently breaking a block.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Situations in which AutoRod is suppressed: OpenInventory (inventory or a container screen open), UsingItem (currently using an item), HoldingConsumable (holding food/potion in main or off hand). None selected by default.

settings.name: HoldingItemsForIgnore
settings.description: List of items that, when held in the main hand, prevent AutoRod from acting. Defaults to Bow, Crossbow, Trident, Fire Charge, Ender Pearl. Editable item list.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target selection sub-group (shared TargetTracker, default priority Distance). Contains: FOV (float, default 180, 0-180; only target entities within this view angle), HurtTime (int, default 10, 0-10; only target entities whose hurt-time is at or below this so you do not re-target invulnerable entities), Priority (multiEnum ordering of selection criteria such as Type, Distance, Health, Direction, HurtTime, Age; default Type then Distance).

settings.name: AimPoint
settings.description: Point-tracker sub-group controlling which spot on the target's hitbox is aimed at. Contains ExemptBoxParts (multiEnum of box regions to never aim at), ExemptBestHitVector (toggleable group to avoid always aiming the closest point), Gaussian (toggleable randomization processor), Lazy (toggleable processor that holds the point until a threshold is exceeded), and Delay (toggleable processor that delays the point by a number of ticks).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Silent-rotation engine sub-group. Contains AngleSmooth (choices of rotation smoothing modes such as Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration with their own speed settings), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent; how movement is corrected to the rotation), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, 1-180; angle within which the rotation is considered reached and reset begins), and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, 1-30 ticks; how long to keep the rotation before snapping back).

settings.name: AimOffThreshold
settings.description: Maximum allowed angle (degrees) between your server rotation and the target rotation before AutoRod is allowed to cast. Default 5, range 2-10. Larger values cast even when not yet precisely aimed.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: How the arm swing is sent when using the rod. Default DoNotHide (swing normally visible).

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that draws a marker on the current target. Offers a Mode choice (Legacy box, Circle, Image, GlowingCircle, Ghost, Hearts, plus GUI Text/Arrow), each with their own color, size, height-mode and related appearance settings.

settings.name: HitTimeout
settings.description: Maximum ticks to wait after casting before forcibly pulling the rod back in. Default 30, range 5-200 ticks.

settings.name: PullOnOutOfRange
settings.description: If enabled (default true), the rod is reeled in immediately when the target moves out of the configured range band.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Ticks before the silently-selected rod slot is restored to your previous slot after the pull. Default 0-0, range 0-20 ticks; a random value in the band is used.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Ticks to wait between rod uses. Default 4-8, range 1-50 ticks; a random value in the band is picked each cycle to vary timing.

modules.name: AutoShoot
modules.summary: AutoShoot automatically aims at and throws projectiles (eggs/snowballs by default, or a custom item set) at the nearest visible enemy. It is designed for projectile-based minigames such as Hypixel QuakeCraft, Cytooxien Lasertag, and Paintball, and replaces the older AutoBalls module with more accurate aiming. It pre-aims using simulated next-tick rotations, selects the throwable slot automatically, and only fires once your rotation is close enough to the target.
useCases: Automatically hit enemies in projectile minigames like QuakeCraft, Lasertag, or Paintball.
Throw eggs or snowballs at the nearest opponent without manual aiming.
Use a custom whitelist/blacklist of throwable items for non-standard game modes.

settings.name: ThrowableType
settings.description: Chooses which projectile category to use: EggAndSnowball (finds the closest egg or snowball, default) or Custom (uses a configurable item filter). Determines how the module locates a throwable slot.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Child of the Custom throwable type. Whether the Items list is treated as a Whitelist (default) or Blacklist when deciding which held items count as throwables.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: Child of the Custom throwable type. The set of items used with the Filter to determine valid throwables. Defaults to Egg and Snowball.

settings.name: GravityType
settings.description: How aiming compensates for projectile drop: Auto (default; picks Projectile for eggs/snowballs and Linear for other items), Linear (aim straight at the target's hitbox, no gravity compensation), or Projectile (compute a ballistic arc using the generic trajectory). Affects accuracy depending on the projectile type.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Target acquisition distance range (in blocks) used by the target tracker. Default 3.0 to 6.0, configurable within 1.0 to 256.0. Enemies within this range may be selected and shot at.

settings.name: AimOffThreshold
settings.description: Maximum allowed angular difference (in degrees) between your current server rotation and the required aim before the module is allowed to throw. Default 2.0, range 0.5 to 10.0. Lower values require more precise aim before firing.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: Controls the arm-swing animation when throwing. Default DO_NOT_HIDE (shows a normal swing); other options change or hide how the swing is sent.

settings.name: SelectSlotAutomatically
settings.description: When enabled (default), the module silently switches to the hotbar slot containing the throwable so it can shoot. When disabled, it only shoots if the throwable is already the held item.

settings.name: TicksUntilSlotReset
settings.description: Number of ticks after a silent slot selection before the server-side slot is reset back. Default 1, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: ConsiderInventory
settings.description: When enabled (default), the module accounts for an open inventory: it will not throw while the inventory is open and factors inventory state into rotation handling. Disabling lets it act regardless of inventory state.

settings.name: RequiresKillAura
settings.description: When enabled, AutoShoot only operates while the KillAura module is running; otherwise it pauses and resets its target. Default off.

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: When enabled, the module stops shooting while the CombatManager reports you are in melee combat. Default off.

settings.name: ConstantLag
settings.description: Boolean flag (default off) exposed by the module that, when enabled, applies constant-lag behavior used by related logic. Default off.

modules.name: AutoShop
modules.summary: AutoShop automatically buys items in a BedWars shop based on a per-server configuration that defines item categories, slots, prices and purchase conditions. When a recognized shop GUI is open, it walks through the configured shopping list, switches categories, clicks to buy each needed item while it can afford it, and respects per-item limits (blocks, tools, armor, tiered items, etc.). It supports two purchase modes (Normal, one click verified at a time; Quick, rapid clicking by simulation) and can automatically close the shop after buying.
useCases: Instantly restock your BedWars loadout (blocks, tools, potions) on supported servers when you open the shop.
Use the Quick purchase mode for the fastest possible buying when you need to rush back into the fight.
Auto-close the shop after a buy run so you are immediately back in control of your character.

settings.name: Config
settings.description: Selects which built-in server shop configuration to load (defines trader titles, categories, slots, prices and conditions). Options: PikaNetwork (default), BlocksMC, CubeCraft, TeamHoly, FunnyMC, Dexland. Changing it reloads the corresponding shop layout.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Random delay (in ticks, range 0..10) to wait after the shop opens before the first click. Default: 1..2.

settings.name: PurchaseMode
settings.description: Selects the buying strategy: Normal (default; buys one item per click and waits to confirm the item was received before continuing) or Quick (clicks rapidly based on a purchase simulation). Each mode has its own sub-settings below.

settings.name: ExtraDelay
settings.description: Normal purchase mode only. Extra random delay (in ticks, range 0..10) waited after each successful item purchase. Default: 2..3.

settings.name: Action
settings.description: Normal purchase mode only. The container click action used to buy: PickUp (default, normal left-click pickup) or Throw. Determines how the buy click is sent to the server.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Quick purchase mode only. Random delay (in milliseconds, range 0..150) between the rapid buy clicks. Default: 50..70.

settings.name: WaitForItems
settings.description: Quick purchase mode only. When enabled (default true), the mode only treats armor items as pending/expected-later; this affects how it tracks which purchased items will arrive after the shop closes.

settings.name: ExtraCategorySwitchDelay
settings.description: Random extra delay (in ticks, range 0..10) waited after switching the shop's item category. Default: 3..4.

settings.name: AutoClose
settings.description: When enabled (default true), automatically closes the shop GUI after at least one purchase has been made.

modules.name: AutoTool
modules.summary: AutoTool automatically switches to the best tool in your hotbar (and optionally your full inventory) for whatever block you are breaking. When you start breaking a block it picks the fastest applicable tool and silently selects it, restoring your previously held item after a configurable delay. It supports a dynamic best-tool search or a fixed hotbar slot, block filtering, a silk-touch protection handler, and conditional gating (sneaking, combat, proximity to a bed).
useCases: Mine efficiently while building or PvP-ing without manually swapping to the right pickaxe, axe, or shovel.
During bed-defense, only swap tools when near your bed (RequireNearBed) so combat hotbar slots stay intact otherwise.
Force a silk-touch tool on blocks like ender chests or glowstone via the SilkTouchHandler so you collect them intact.

settings.name: ToolSelector
settings.description: Chooses how the tool is selected. 'Dynamic' (default) searches for the objectively best/fastest tool for the block; 'Static' always uses a fixed hotbar slot.

settings.name: IgnoreDurability
settings.description: Dynamic mode only. When false (default), tools that are nearly broken are avoided when choosing the best tool; when true, durability is ignored and the fastest tool is used regardless of how damaged it is.

settings.name: ConsiderInventory
settings.description: Dynamic mode toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, the best-tool search also looks through your main inventory, not just the hotbar, and will swap a tool from the inventory into the hotbar to use it (governed by the Constraints and SwapPreviousDelay below).

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Inside ConsiderInventory > Constraints. Random tick range (default 1..2, range 0..20) to wait before beginning an inventory swap action.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Inside ConsiderInventory > Constraints. Random tick range (default 2..4, range 0..20) between inventory clicks when moving the tool.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Inside ConsiderInventory > Constraints. Random tick range (default 1..2, range 0..20) to wait before closing the inventory after the swap.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Inside ConsiderInventory > Constraints. Percentage chance (default 0..0, range 0..100) to intentionally misclick during the inventory action to look more human.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Inside ConsiderInventory > Constraints. Conditions that must be met before an inventory swap is allowed: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat (OpenInventory is excluded for this generic constraint set). Default none selected.

settings.name: Slot
settings.description: Static mode only. The fixed hotbar slot (default 0, range 0..8) that AutoTool selects whenever you break a filtered block.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Determines how the Blocks list is interpreted for whether AutoTool acts on a block: BLACKLIST (default) means act on all blocks except those listed; WHITELIST means act only on listed blocks.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The block list used together with Filter to decide which blocks AutoTool selects a tool for. Empty by default.

settings.name: SilkTouchHandler
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, forces tool selection to prefer (or avoid) a Silk Touch tool for the configured blocks, so blocks that need silk touch are mined intact.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Inside SilkTouchHandler. How its block list is interpreted: WHITELIST (default) means the silk-touch rule applies only to the listed blocks; BLACKLIST inverts this.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Inside SilkTouchHandler. Blocks for which a Silk Touch tool is required; defaults to Ender Chest, Glowstone, Sea Lantern, and Turtle Egg.

settings.name: SwapPreviousDelay
settings.description: How many ticks (default 20, range 1..100) AutoTool keeps the chosen tool selected before silently restoring your previously held slot. Also used as the swap-restore delay for inventory swaps.

settings.name: RequireSneaking
settings.description: When enabled (default false), AutoTool only switches tools while you are sneaking; otherwise it does nothing.

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: When enabled (default false), AutoTool will not switch tools while the client considers you to be in combat, preventing tool swaps from interrupting fights.

settings.name: RequireNearBed
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, AutoTool only operates when a tracked bed is within the configured Distance, otherwise it stays inactive.

settings.name: Distance
settings.description: Inside RequireNearBed. Maximum distance (default 10.0, range 3.0..50.0) from your eyes to a bed within which AutoTool is allowed to switch tools.

modules.name: AutoTrap
modules.summary: AutoTrap (aliases Ignite and AutoWeb) automatically traps nearby enemies by placing blocks/items on or around them: it ignites them with lava buckets or flint and steel, and/or boxes them in with cobwebs. It tracks targets within range, simulates their movement to predict where the trap should go, then rotates toward the placement spot and places when timing is favorable. Placement timing can wait for ongoing combat (KillAura) hit windows so it does not interfere with attacks, and it respects a configurable cooldown between placements.
useCases: Setting enemies on fire automatically during PvP to apply continuous fire damage (Ignite).
Webbing opponents in place to immobilize them for easier hits or to stop them escaping (AutoWeb).

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Float range (default 3.0-4.5, bounds 2.0-6.0) defining the minimum and maximum distance at which entities are considered valid trap targets. Wider ranges trap from farther away but may be less legitimate.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Cooldown in ticks (default 20, range 0-400) the module waits after a successful placement before placing again. Higher values slow trapping down; 0 places as fast as possible.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: When true (default), the module keeps trapping even while a container/inventory screen is open and does not force rotations to account for the open inventory. When false, it pauses while a container screen is open and considers the inventory for rotations.

settings.name: Ignite
settings.description: Toggle for the ignition trap planner (enabled by default). When on, the module places lava (lava bucket) or fire (flint and steel) on enemies that are not already on fire, predicting their position. Requires a lava bucket or flint and steel in the hotbar/offhand.

settings.name: AutoWeb
settings.description: Toggle for the cobweb trap planner (enabled by default). When on, the module places cobwebs at predicted enemy positions to slow/immobilize them. Requires cobwebs in the hotbar/offhand. AutoWeb is attempted before Ignite when both are enabled.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target-selection sub-group controlling which entities are chosen as trap targets. Contains FOV, HurtTime and Priority below, and uses the module's Range for distance filtering.

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Field-of-view limit in degrees (default 180, range 0-180) within which a target must lie relative to your crosshair to be selected. 180 means any direction; lower values only trap targets in front of you.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Maximum hurt-time (invulnerability ticks after being damaged) a target may have to still be valid (default 10, range 0-10). Lower values skip recently-hit entities.

settings.name: Priority
settings.description: Ordered set of criteria used to rank candidate targets (default includes Type and Health; cannot be none). Options: Type (players first), Health (lowest health first), Distance (closest first), Direction (closest to crosshair first), HurtTime (lowest hurt time first), Age (oldest entity first). Reorder to change which enemy is trapped first.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Dynamic rotation engine sub-group used to aim at placement spots. Contains AngleSmooth (mode selector), MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset below.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Selects how rotations are smoothed toward the target. Available modes include Linear, Sigmoid, and Acceleration (each with their own turn-speed settings). Smoother modes look more human but reach the target more slowly.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: How player movement is reconciled with silent server-side rotations (default Silent). Controls whether your visual look direction or strafing is corrected to match the rotation sent to the server.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Angular difference in degrees (default 2.0, range 1-180) below which the rotation is considered to have reached its target before it can reset back to normal.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Number of ticks (default 5, range 1-30) the rotation lingers on the last target before snapping back to the player's normal aim.

modules.name: AutoWalk
modules.summary: Automatically makes you walk forward continuously while enabled by forcing the forward movement input on. It overrides normal movement input at critical priority so you keep moving forward without holding the key.
useCases: Traveling long distances in a straight line without holding the forward key.
Keeping forward motion while AFK or while focusing on other actions.

modules.name: AutoWeapon
modules.summary: AutoWeapon automatically silently switches to the best weapon in your hotbar when you attack or target an entity, then switches back to your original slot after a delay. It can prefer a weapon type (sword by default for attack speed), automatically pick an axe to break a shield-blocking target, and automatically pick a mace when a smash attack is possible. The slot switch is silent and is synced so the attack uses the chosen weapon, after which it reverts.
useCases: Always hit with your strongest weapon in PvP without manually switching hotbar slots.
Automatically swap to an axe to stun an opponent who is blocking with a shield.
Automatically swap to a mace for a falling smash attack when conditions allow.

settings.name: Preferred
settings.description: The weapon type(s) to prefer when no special case applies (default Sword). If left empty, no weapon type is preferred, which is useful when you only want the AutoShieldBreak or AutoMace behavior.

settings.name: AutoShieldBreak
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, if the target is blocking with a shield (and on versions newer than 1.8), the module selects an axe to stun the shield instead of the preferred weapon.

settings.name: AutoMace
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, whenever a mace smash attack is possible (e.g. you are falling, or MaceKill is active), the module selects a mace, since a mace smash cannot be blocked by a shield.

settings.name: SwitchBack
settings.description: Number of ticks after the silent switch before reverting to your originally selected slot. Default 20, range 1..300 ticks. Higher values keep the weapon selected longer.

settings.name: ChangeOn
settings.description: When the weapon switch should occur. Options: OnAttack (default, switch at the moment you attack an entity) and OnTarget (switch when an entity becomes your target/crosshair target). OnAttack also enables attack-speed correction for the swapped weapon.

modules.name: AutoWindCharge
modules.summary: AutoWindCharge automatically uses a Wind Charge to boost you upward while you hold the jump key. It predicts your collision with the ground 7 ticks ahead and triggers a Wind Charge just before landing so you launch much higher. It searches your offhand and hotbar for a Wind Charge item and uses it, optionally rotating toward the correct direction first. It can also perform a horizontal boost when a configured key is held.
useCases: Quickly gaining height while parkouring or escaping by holding jump and letting the module fire a Wind Charge at the optimal moment.
Launching yourself horizontally for fast travel by holding the configured horizontal-boost key while jumping.
Chaining vertical boosts in PvP or movement situations without manually timing the Wind Charge throw.

settings.name: HorizontalBoost
settings.description: Toggle for the horizontal-boost sub-feature (enabled by default). When enabled and its boost key is held, the module aims with a shallower pitch so the Wind Charge propels you more horizontally instead of straight up.

settings.name: Pitch
settings.description: Child of HorizontalBoost. The pitch angle (in degrees) used when performing a horizontal boost. Default 70, range 0 to 90. Lower values aim more horizontally; higher values aim closer to straight down for a more vertical launch.

settings.name: Key
settings.description: Child of HorizontalBoost. The keybind that must be held to activate the horizontal boost. Defaults to Left Control. While held, the module switches from the default vertical pitch (90) to the configured Pitch value.

settings.name: Rotate
settings.description: Toggle for the rotation sub-feature (enabled by default). When enabled, the module rotates toward the throw direction (server-side via the rotation engine) and only uses the Wind Charge once the server rotation is within 1 degree of the target.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Child of Rotate. A nested rotation-engine value group controlling how rotations are applied when aiming the Wind Charge. Contains the sub-settings below.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Child of Rotations. Selects the angle-smoothing algorithm used to turn toward the target (Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration). Determines how the rotation speed/curve is applied while aiming.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Child of Rotations. Controls how player movement is corrected relative to the silent server rotation (default Silent). Affects whether movement direction follows the visual or the silent rotation.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Child of Rotations. The angular difference (degrees) at which the rotation is considered close enough to begin resetting. Default 2, range 1 to 180.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Child of Rotations. Number of ticks to keep the rotation before resetting back to normal. Default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks.

settings.name: CombatPauseTime
settings.description: How long (in ticks) combat is paused while the module rotates to use the Wind Charge. Default 0, range 0 to 40. A higher value prevents combat modules from interfering during the boost.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Random delay range (in ticks) before resetting/switching back the hotbar slot after using the Wind Charge. Default 0 to 0, range 0 to 40 ticks. A random value within this range is chosen each use.

modules.name: AvoidHazards
modules.summary: AvoidHazards keeps you from walking into blocks and fluids that can hurt or trap you, such as cacti, fire, lava, cobwebs, ladders and magma. It works in two ways: a Shape mode that overrides the collision shape of selected hazard blocks so your physics treat them as solid (or as a low cap) and you bump off of them, and an Input mode that simulates your next couple of movement ticks and rewrites your movement input toward a safe direction before you actually step into a hazard. You choose which hazard types it should protect against. Note that the cobweb option conflicts with NoWeb and cannot be used together with it.
useCases: Surviving PvP or parkour on maps littered with cacti, fire, or lava without manually steering around every hazard.
Preventing accidental falls into lava or trapping yourself in cobwebs while sprinting through dangerous terrain.
Avoiding stepping on pressure plates (traps) or climbing onto unwanted ladders during fast movement.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how hazards are avoided. 'Shape' (default) rewrites the collision shape of hazard blocks so you collide with them as if solid (full cube for most hazards, or a low 4-block-high cap for pressure plates and magma), making you physically unable to walk into them. 'Input' instead simulates your upcoming movement (about 2 ticks ahead) and steers your directional input toward a safe alternative before you enter a hazard.

settings.name: Avoid
settings.description: Multi-select list of which hazard types to avoid. Options: Cacti, BerryBush, Fire, Cobwebs, Ladders, PressurePlates, MagmaBlocks, Lava, WitherRose, PowderSnow. Only the selected hazards are protected against; enabling Cobwebs makes this module incompatible with NoWeb (NoWeb will force-disable AvoidHazards).

modules.name: Backtrack
modules.summary: Backtrack holds back (blinks) incoming packets from a target enemy so that the enemy's hitbox lags behind its real position on your screen, letting you hit the enemy where it used to be a fraction of a second ago. It only delays packets for a tracked target within a configured distance range and time window, and intelligently flushes the queue when the real position becomes closer than the lagged position (so you don't lose legitimate hits) or on teleports, death and disconnects. An optional ESP renders the lagged/backtracked hitbox of the target.
useCases: Landing hits in melee/KillAura fights by attacking the enemy's delayed (backtracked) position, effectively increasing your reach window.
Gaining an advantage against players who strafe quickly, since their on-screen hitbox stays where it was for a short delay.
Pairing with combat modules so you only backtrack the enemy you are currently attacking (Attack mode) or any enemy in range (Range mode).

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Float distance range (default 1-3, bounds 0-10 blocks) within which a target may be backtracked. The target must be within this boxed distance for packet holding to start/continue.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Integer millisecond range (default 100-150, bounds 0-1000 ms) for how long incoming packets from the target are held before being flushed. A random value in this range is chosen as the current delay; larger values cause the enemy's lagged hitbox to fall further behind.

settings.name: NextBacktrackDelay
settings.description: Integer millisecond range (default 0-10, bounds 0-2000 ms) of cooldown enforced after a backtrack session ends before the next one may begin. A random value in this range is waited.

settings.name: TrackingBuffer
settings.description: Time in milliseconds (default 500, range 0-2000) that the target keeps being tracked/backtracked after it leaves the Range, before tracking is dropped. Higher values keep backtracking active briefly even when the enemy steps out of range.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Percent chance (default 50%, range 0-100) that backtracking actually activates on a given attack/target. A random roll is re-evaluated each attack; lower values make backtracking trigger less often (more legit).

settings.name: PauseOnHurtTime
settings.description: Toggleable group (default disabled). When enabled, backtracking is paused while the target's hurtTime is at or above the configured HurtTime, i.e. while the enemy is in its hurt-animation cooldown.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Child of PauseOnHurtTime (default 3, range 0-10). The target hurtTime threshold at or above which backtracking is paused while PauseOnHurtTime is enabled.

settings.name: TargetMode
settings.description: Selects how the backtrack target is chosen (default Attack). Attack: backtracks only the entity you actually attack via combat. Range: continuously backtracks any enemy found within Range each game tick.

settings.name: LastAttackTimeToWork
settings.description: Time window in milliseconds (default 1000, range 0-5000) since your last attack during which backtracking is allowed to operate. If you haven't attacked within this window, backtracking stops, keeping it tied to active combat.

settings.name: Esp
settings.description: Selects how the backtracked (lagged) target position is visualized. Options are Box, Model, Wireframe and None (default selection is the third entry, Wireframe). This is purely visual and not always included in configs.

modules.name: BedDefender
modules.summary: BedDefender protects beds (typically your own in Bedwars-style modes) by automatically placing blocks over them to cover exposed faces, layering protection up to a configurable depth. It searches for nearby bed blocks, determines via the SelfBed mode which beds should be defended, computes the open positions around each bed in priority order (closest layer first, then nearest to your eyes), and feeds them to the shared BlockPlacer engine to place the hardest/best available blocks. It picks blocks from your hotbar/offhand, preferring full blocks (and optionally chests), sorting by block hardness so the toughest material is used.
useCases: Automatically wall up and protect your own bed in Bedwars so opponents must mine through extra layers before they can break it.
Keep a defensive block layer maintained over a bed even after enemies partially break it, since the module re-searches and refills exposed spots.
Use SelfBed color/spawn/manual tracking to only defend the bed that belongs to you and ignore enemy beds.

settings.name: MaxLayers
settings.description: How many block layers deep BedDefender will build around the bed. Default 1, range 1..5. Higher values create thicker, harder-to-break protection but require more blocks and reach.

settings.name: AllowChests
settings.description: If enabled, chests are also considered valid defending blocks (in addition to full blocks). Default false. Useful because chests are hard to break/blast in some modes.

settings.name: SelfBed
settings.description: Selects how the module decides which bed counts as the one to defend. Options: None (defends every bed, ignoring ownership), Color, SpawnLocation, and Manual (default selected index 0 = None).

settings.name: SelfBed > Color > Slots
settings.description: Armor equipment slots whose dye color is compared against the bed's color to identify your bed. Defaults to HEAD; can select any humanoid armor slots; cannot be none. Only present under the Color SelfBed mode.

settings.name: SelfBed > Color > Loose
settings.description: If enabled, color matching is approximate by snapping the armor color to the closest dye color rather than requiring an exact match. Default false. Loosening helps when armor tints don't exactly equal the bed dye color.

settings.name: SelfBed > SpawnLocation > BedDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance from your tracked spawn point within which a bed is treated as yours. Default 24.0, range 16.0..48.0. The spawn point is captured from server position packets that move you far (>16 blocks).

settings.name: SelfBed > Manual > Track
settings.description: Keybind that records the nearest bed (within 16 blocks) as the tracked bed to defend. Default Numpad Plus.

settings.name: SelfBed > Manual > Untrack
settings.description: Keybind that clears the currently tracked bed so it is no longer defended. Default Numpad Minus.

settings.name: RequiresSneak
settings.description: If enabled, the module only places defending blocks while you are sneaking (shift). Default false. Useful to make defending manual/intentional.

settings.name: Place
settings.description: The shared BlockPlacer sub-group that performs the actual block placement (placement priority is NOT_IMPORTANT, support placements disabled for this module). It contains the placement settings below.

settings.name: Place > Range
settings.description: Maximum reach used to place blocks. Default 4.5, range 1..6.

settings.name: Place > WallRange
settings.description: Reach allowed for placements considered to be through/behind walls (faces pointing away). Default 4.5, range 0..6. 0 disables placing on away-facing faces.

settings.name: Place > Cooldown
settings.description: Random tick delay between placement actions, picked from this range. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0..40. Higher values place slower and look more legit.

settings.name: Place > Swing
settings.description: How the hand swing is shown when placing. Default DO_NOT_HIDE (visible swing).

settings.name: Place > ConstructFailResult
settings.description: If a raytrace to the target fails, a center hit result is synthesized so the placement still happens. Default true. Improves reliability on most servers at the cost of slightly less accurate rotations/range.

settings.name: Place > Sneak
settings.description: Number of ticks to keep sneaking when placing onto an interactable block (so its GUI/action isn't triggered). Default 1..1 ticks, range 0..10.

settings.name: Place > Ignore
settings.description: Conditions under which placement is still allowed: OpenInventory (place even with a container screen open) and UsingItem (place even while using an item). By default none are checked, so an open container or item use blocks placement.

settings.name: Place > SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Ticks after a silent hotbar slot selection before the slot is reset, picked from this range. Default 4..6 ticks, range 0..40.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode
settings.description: How the player rotates to place blocks. Normal performs server-visible rotations (one placement per tick); None skips real rotation for faster multi-placement (and can optionally send a rotation packet).

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > PostMove
settings.description: Shared rotation-mode option: if enabled, the placement is executed after the movement packet rather than before. Default false.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > Normal > Rotations
settings.description: The dynamic rotation engine sub-group (AngleSmooth mode, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold, TicksUntilReset) used to smoothly aim toward placement targets in Normal mode.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > None > SendRotationPacket
settings.description: In None rotation mode, if enabled a rotation move packet is sent to face the placement before placing. Default false.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > None > Placements
settings.description: How many blocks may be placed per operation/tick in None rotation mode (labeled b/o). Default 1, range 1..10. Higher values place multiple blocks at once.

settings.name: Place > Support
settings.description: Toggleable support feature that builds helper blocks so target positions become placeable. Disabled for BedDefender (support placements are not allowed for this module).

settings.name: Place > Support > Depth
settings.description: Maximum search/path depth for the support pathfinder. Default 4, range 1..12.

settings.name: Place > Support > Delay
settings.description: Minimum delay between support-path searches. Default 500 ms, range 0..1000.

settings.name: Place > Support > Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/Blacklist mode controlling which blocks may be used as support material. Default BLACKLIST.

settings.name: Place > Support > Blocks
settings.description: The block set used together with Filter to decide which items count as support (helper) blocks.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Toggleable feature that attacks end crystals blocking placement positions. Enabled by default within the placer.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > Range
settings.description: Reach for attacking crystals. Default 4.5, range 1..6.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > WallRange
settings.description: Through-wall reach for attacking crystals. Default 4.5, range 0..6.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > Delay
settings.description: Delay between crystal attacks. Default 0 ms, range 0..1000.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > SwingMode
settings.description: How the swing is shown when attacking crystals. Default DO_NOT_HIDE.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > RotationMode
settings.description: Normal or None rotation handling when aiming at crystals (Normal uses the dynamic rotation engine at high priority).

settings.name: Place > TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable PlacementRenderer that draws boxes at positions queued to be placed. Disabled by default for this placer.

settings.name: Place > PlacedRendering
settings.description: Toggleable PlacementRenderer that draws boxes at positions just placed (does not keep them). Enabled by default.

modules.name: BedPlates
modules.summary: BedPlates renders a floating, screen-space overlay above every nearby bed showing the bed itself and the protective blocks surrounding it, layer by layer. Each surrounding block is drawn as an item icon with its count, and the bed icon shows the distance in meters. It is built for bed-defense game modes (e.g. Bed Wars) so you can instantly judge how well-protected a bed is and which tools you need to break it. Beds are sorted by distance and the closest ones are shown first up to a configurable maximum.
useCases: Quickly assess how many and what kind of blocks protect enemy beds in Bed Wars before committing to a rush.
See at a glance whether you are holding the correct tool to mine a bed's defenses (unbreakable-without-tool blocks are highlighted red).
Filter out your own bed so the overlay only highlights enemy beds worth attacking.

settings.name: BackgroundColor
settings.description: The color (and alpha) of the rectangular background drawn behind each bed plate. Defaults to the client default background color.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: When enabled (default false), draws an outline around each bed plate tinted with the bed's wool/map color; when disabled the outline is transparent.

settings.name: MaxLayers
settings.description: How many concentric defensive layers around the bed to scan and display, from 1 to 5 (default 5). Changing it triggers a full rescan of beds. Lower values show only the innermost protection.

settings.name: ShowBed
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the bed's own item icon is shown as the first entry in the plate (with the distance label); when disabled only the surrounding blocks are listed.

settings.name: TextShadow
settings.description: When enabled (default true), text such as layer numerals and block counts is drawn with a drop shadow for readability.

settings.name: RenderOffset
settings.description: A 3D world-space offset added to the bed position before projecting it to the screen, letting you nudge the plate up/down or sideways. The in-world locate button is disabled for this value.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: A distance-to-scale curve controlling how big the plate is drawn based on camera distance. X axis is Distance (0..200), Y axis is Scale (0.25..4); default keeps a constant scale of 1 across all distances. If the computed scale is below 0.01 the plate is skipped.

settings.name: MaxCount
settings.description: The maximum number of beds to render at once, from 1 to 64 (default 8). Beds are sorted by distance so the nearest ones are drawn first.

settings.name: HighlightUnbreakable
settings.description: When enabled (default true), surrounding blocks that require a correct tool to drop and for which you currently have no matching tool in your hotbar are tinted red, signalling you cannot mine them efficiently.

settings.name: Compact
settings.description: When enabled (default true), surrounding blocks are collapsed into a compact list (using compact surrounding blocks) and no per-block layer Roman numeral is drawn; when disabled the full block list is shown with layer numerals (I..VIII).

settings.name: PreventOverlap
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the renderer offsets overlapping plates so multiple nearby beds do not visually stack on top of each other.

settings.name: FilterMode
settings.description: Selects how the surrounding blocks are filtered before display. Choices are Predefined (default) and Custom.

settings.name: Predefined
settings.description: FilterMode choice (default). Shows all non-air blocks that are redstone-conductive (solid) plus a built-in whitelist of meaningful non-solid blocks (ladders, water, glass, stained glass). It has no further settings.

settings.name: Custom
settings.description: FilterMode choice that lets you define exactly which blocks count, via its own Blocks list and Filter mode.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Child of the Custom filter mode: a user-editable set of blocks (empty by default) used together with the Filter setting to whitelist or blacklist which surrounding blocks are shown.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Child of the Custom filter mode: whether the Blocks set acts as a BLACKLIST (default, hide listed blocks) or WHITELIST (only show listed blocks).

settings.name: IgnoreSelfBed
settings.description: Selects how the module decides which bed is your own so it can be skipped from rendering. Choices are None (default), Color, SpawnLocation and Manual.

settings.name: None
settings.description: IgnoreSelfBed choice (default): no bed is ever treated as your own, so all beds are shown. Has no settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: IgnoreSelfBed choice that treats a bed as yours when its color matches the dye color of your worn armor.

settings.name: Slots
settings.description: Child of the Color self-bed mode: which armor equipment slots to compare against the bed color (default HEAD; cannot be empty). The bed is considered yours if any selected slot's armor color matches.

settings.name: Loose
settings.description: Child of the Color self-bed mode: when enabled (default false), the armor color is matched to its closest dye color before comparing, allowing approximate matches; when disabled an exact color match is required.

settings.name: SpawnLocation
settings.description: IgnoreSelfBed choice that treats beds within a distance of your detected spawn/teleport location as your own.

settings.name: BedDistance
settings.description: Child of the SpawnLocation self-bed mode: the radius (16.0..48.0, default 24.0) around the tracked spawn point within which a bed is considered yours.

settings.name: Manual
settings.description: IgnoreSelfBed choice that lets you manually mark/unmark a bed near you with hotkeys.

settings.name: Track
settings.description: Child of the Manual self-bed mode: the key (default numpad +) that records the nearest bed within 16 blocks as your own.

settings.name: Untrack
settings.description: Child of the Manual self-bed mode: the key (default numpad -) that clears the currently tracked self-bed position.

settings.name: IgnoreAdjacent
settings.description: When enabled (default false), a bed is skipped if another tracked bed is directly adjacent to it (Manhattan distance <= 1), reducing clutter from double-counted bed parts.

modules.name: BetterChat
modules.summary: BetterChat adds quality-of-life improvements to the in-game chat. Through a multi-select feature list it can give the chat an unlimited message buffer, prevent the server from clearing your chat, keep the chat usable on the death screen, and convert your sent text to full-width Unicode. It can also automatically append a prefix and/or suffix to your messages, auto-translate incoming messages of selected chat types, and let you copy chat lines to the clipboard (Shift + left click) or re-insert them into the chat box (right click).
