It also has an AntiSpam sub-feature and is aliased as 'AntiSpam'.
useCases: Keeping a large/infinite scrollback of chat and stopping servers from wiping your chat history.
Automatically translating foreign-language chat messages into your language for selected chat types.
Quickly copying a received chat line to your clipboard or appending a personalized signature to your own messages.

settings.name: Features
settings.description: Multi-select toggle set of core chat features. Options: Infinite (unlimited chat message buffer), AntiClear (ignore server attempts to clear chat), KeepAfterDeath (allow opening/using chat on the death screen), ForceUnicodeChat (convert sent ASCII characters to full-width Unicode). Defaults enabled: Infinite, AntiClear, KeepAfterDeath.

settings.name: AutoTranslate
settings.description: Multi-select set of incoming chat types (ChatReceiveEvent.ChatType values) to auto-translate. For each selected type, received messages are stripped of color codes and translated via the global auto-translate settings, with the translation shown in chat. Empty by default (nothing translated).

settings.name: AppendPrefix
settings.description: Toggleable group (default OFF). When enabled, the configured Prefix is prepended to every message you send.

settings.name: Prefix
settings.description: Text prepended to your outgoing messages when AppendPrefix is enabled. Default is '> '.

settings.name: AppendSuffix
settings.description: Toggleable group (default OFF). When enabled, the configured Suffix is appended to every message you send.

settings.name: Suffix
settings.description: Text appended to your outgoing messages when AppendSuffix is enabled. Default is a stylized ' | LiquidBounce' suffix written in special Unicode mathematical characters.

settings.name: AntiSpam
settings.description: Toggleable AntiSpam sub-group attached to the module (added via tree). It groups anti-spam handling for incoming chat; settings beyond its toggle are defined in the AntiSpam sub-tree.

settings.name: Copy
settings.description: Toggleable group (default ON) enabling chat-line copy interactions: Shift + left click copies the clicked chat line's text to the clipboard, and right click re-inserts that line's text into the chat input box.

settings.name: Notify
settings.description: Child of the Copy group (default true). When enabled, shows a success notification ('The line is copied') after copying a chat line to the clipboard.

settings.name: Highlight
settings.description: Child of the Copy group (default true). When enabled, the chat line under the cursor is visually highlighted to indicate it can be copied/interacted with.

modules.name: BetterInventory
modules.summary: Adds quality-of-life rendering features to inventory and container screens. It can highlight the most recently clicked slot, draw a textual cooldown progress indicator on items that are on cooldown, and preview the contents of container items (such as shulker boxes or bundles) by rendering their inner stacks as a floating list. Each feature is an independent toggleable group.
useCases: Tracking which slot you last clicked while moving items around quickly.
Seeing exact item cooldown progress (percent, ticks, or seconds) directly on hotbar/inventory items.
Previewing the contents of shulker boxes or bundles without opening them.

settings.name: HighlightClicked
settings.description: Toggle for the HighlightClicked group (default enabled). When on, the slot you last clicked is visually highlighted using the selected mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: HighlightClicked group. How the last-clicked slot is highlighted. Choices: Border (draws a colored border around the slot, default selected) and Texture (overlays the vanilla hotbar selection texture over the slot).

settings.name: Color
settings.description: HighlightClicked > Border mode. Color of the border drawn around the last-clicked slot. Default green.

settings.name: TextCooldownProgress
settings.description: Toggle for the TextCooldownProgress group (default enabled). When on, items currently on cooldown show a centered text indicator of their remaining cooldown.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: TextCooldownProgress group. Format of the cooldown text. Options: Percentage (e.g. '37%', default), DurationTicks (remaining ticks), DurationSeconds (remaining seconds, e.g. '2s' or '1.4s').

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: TextCooldownProgress group. Scale of the cooldown progress text. Default 1.0, range 0.25..4.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: TextCooldownProgress group. Color of the cooldown progress text. Default white.

settings.name: ContainerItemView
settings.description: Toggle for the ContainerItemView group (default enabled). When on, hovering a container item (one with stored contents) renders a preview of its inner item stacks.

settings.name: SkipEmptyStack
settings.description: ContainerItemView group. When enabled, only non-empty inner stacks are shown in the preview; when disabled, all slots (including empty) are shown. Default false.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: ContainerItemView group. Scale of the container contents preview. Default 1.0, range 0.25..4.

settings.name: RelativeToMouse
settings.description: ContainerItemView group. When enabled, the preview is positioned relative to the mouse cursor; when disabled it uses fixed offsets only. Default true.

settings.name: RenderOffsetX
settings.description: ContainerItemView group. Horizontal offset of the contents preview. Default 150.0, range -4096..4096.

settings.name: RenderOffsetY
settings.description: ContainerItemView group. Vertical offset of the contents preview. Default 0.0, range -4096..4096.

modules.name: BetterTab
modules.summary: BetterTab enhances the in-game player list (tab overlay) with custom sorting, configurable size, player highlighting, accurate latency display, player hiding and game-mode display. You can sort players by ping, name length, alphabetically and more, color-code yourself/friends/others, and show exact ping values in milliseconds. It works purely on the client's tab rendering.
useCases: Sort the tab list by ping to quickly spot lag, or alphabetically to find a specific player.
Highlight yourself, friends and other players with distinct colors to read the player list at a glance.
Show the exact millisecond latency for each player instead of the vanilla connection-bars icon.

settings.name: Sorting
settings.description: How players are ordered in the tab list. Options: Vanilla (default, server order), Ping, NameLength, DisplayNameLength, Alphabetical, ReverseAlphabetical, None.

settings.name: Visibility
settings.description: Which tab-list elements are shown. Options: Header (default on), Footer (default on), NameOnly. Controls whether the server header/footer text and name-only mode are displayed.

settings.name: TabSize
settings.description: (Limits group) Maximum number of players shown in the tab list. Default 80, range 1..1000.

settings.name: ColumnHeight
settings.description: (Limits group) Number of player rows per column before wrapping to a new column. Default 20, range 1..100.

settings.name: Highlight
settings.description: Toggle for the Highlight group (default enabled). When on, colored backgrounds are drawn behind player entries based on the sub-groups below.

settings.name: Self
settings.description: (Highlight group) Toggle for highlighting your own entry. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Color (Self)
settings.description: (Highlight > Self) The highlight color drawn behind your own entry. Default green RGBA(50,193,50,80).

settings.name: Friends
settings.description: (Highlight group) Toggle for highlighting friends' entries. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Color (Friends)
settings.description: (Highlight > Friends) The highlight color drawn behind friends' entries. Default blue RGBA(16,89,203,80).

settings.name: Others
settings.description: (Highlight group) Toggle for highlighting other players' entries. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Color (Others)
settings.description: (Highlight > Others) The highlight color drawn behind other players' entries. Default dark gray RGBA(35,35,35,80).

settings.name: FilterBy (Others)
settings.description: (Highlight > Others > Filter) Which name to test against the regex list for the Others highlight: DisplayName and/or PlayerName.

settings.name: Names (Others)
settings.description: (Highlight > Others > Filter) A list of regex patterns; players whose chosen name matches are affected. Empty by default.

settings.name: AccurateLatency
settings.description: Toggle for showing each player's exact ping value instead of the vanilla bars. Enabled by default.

settings.name: AppendMSSuffix
settings.description: (AccurateLatency group) When enabled (default true), appends an 'ms' suffix to the displayed latency number.

settings.name: PlayerHider
settings.description: Toggle for the PlayerHider group (default disabled). When on, players matching the filter below are removed from the tab list.

settings.name: FilterBy (PlayerHider)
settings.description: (PlayerHider > Filter) Which name to test against the regex list when hiding players: DisplayName and/or PlayerName.

settings.name: Names (PlayerHider)
settings.description: (PlayerHider > Filter) A list of regex patterns; matching players are hidden from the tab list. Empty by default.

settings.name: ShowGameMode
settings.description: When enabled (default true), shows each player's game mode in the tab list.

modules.name: BetterTitle
modules.summary: BetterTitle enhances on-screen title and subtitle messages, currently providing an optional automatic translation feature. When AutoTranslate is enabled, the text of incoming title/subtitle popups is sent through the client's global auto-translate service and the result can be shown in chat and/or substituted directly into the title display. It deliberately updates the title text without resetting the title display timer.
useCases: Automatically translate foreign-language title and subtitle announcements on international servers so you can read them.
Show translated titles in chat for a persistent record while still keeping the original on-screen popup.

settings.name: AutoTranslate
settings.description: Toggle for the AutoTranslate sub-feature (default off / disabled group). When enabled, title and subtitle text is passed through the global auto-translate service and the translation is displayed according to the child settings below.

settings.name: Components
settings.description: Which title components to translate: Title and/or Subtitle. By default both entries are available; only the selected types will be translated and acted upon.

settings.name: ShowIn
settings.description: Where the translation result is displayed. 'Chat' prints the translated text to chat prefixed with the component name; 'Message' replaces the actual on-screen title/subtitle text with the white translated text. Defaults to Chat.

modules.name: Blink
modules.summary: Blink suspends (queues) packets before they are sent to or received from the server, effectively freezing your character on the server side while you keep moving locally; releasing/disabling the module flushes the queued packets at once. You choose which packet directions (outgoing/incoming) to delay, and can spawn a dummy clone at your start position. It can auto-disable on certain actions (ambush), automatically reset after a number of ticks, and integrates with AutoDodge to flush packets to evade incoming arrows.
useCases: Freeze your server-side position to 'teleport' (blink) to a new location when disabled, catching opponents off guard.
Use Ambush to appear stationary until you attack or interact, then instantly resume.
Combine with AutoDodge to flush queued packets at the right moment to dodge arrows.

settings.name: Directions
settings.description: Which packet transfer directions (TransferOrigin: outgoing and/or incoming) are blinked/queued. Defaults to OUTGOING; cannot be set to none. Only packets matching these directions are delayed and later flushed.

settings.name: Dummy
settings.description: When enabled (default false), spawns a fake clone (RemotePlayer) at your starting position when the module is enabled, showing where the server still thinks you are. The clone is removed on disable.

settings.name: Ambush
settings.description: When enabled (default false), the module auto-disables (flushing packets) as soon as you send an attack, interact, or spectator action packet, so combat actions are not held back.

settings.name: AutoDisable
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the module disables itself after an AutoReset is triggered.

settings.name: AutoReset
settings.description: Toggle for the AutoReset value group (disabled by default). When enabled, the module automatically performs a reset action after a set number of movement ticks have passed.

settings.name: ResetAfter
settings.description: Child of the AutoReset group. Number of player movement ticks to wait before performing the reset action. Default 100, range 1..1000.

settings.name: ResetAction
settings.description: Child of the AutoReset group. Action taken when AutoReset fires: 'Reset' (cancel/discard queued packets, default) or 'Blink' (flush queued packets in the configured directions and snap the dummy clone to your position).

modules.name: BlockBounce
modules.summary: BlockBounce lets you bounce higher off bouncy blocks. When you jump while standing on a slime block, bed, or honey block, it adds extra upward motion to the jump. The bounce only triggers when the block directly beneath the player is one of these bouncy block types.
useCases: Reach greater heights when jumping off slime blocks or beds.
Gain a movement boost in parkour or bouncy-block environments.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Extra upward motion added to the jump when standing on a bouncy block (slime block, bed, or honey block). Default 0.42, range 0.2 to 2.0. Higher values produce a higher bounce.

modules.name: BlockESP
modules.summary: BlockESP highlights chosen block types through walls so you can locate them from a distance. It continuously scans loaded chunks for matching blocks and renders them either as filled boxes (optionally with outlines) or with a glowing outline effect. Colors can be static, rainbow, derived from the block's map color, and the highlight can fade out with distance; adjacent shapes may optionally be merged for cleaner visuals.
useCases: Find beds and dragon eggs (the defaults) through terrain in Bed Wars or similar modes.
Locate ores, chests or any custom block type behind walls or underground.
Highlight specific structures with a static or rainbow color for easier orientation.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: How tracked blocks are rendered: Box (default, filled boxes with optional outlines) or Glow (a glowing outline around the blocks).

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Child of the Box mode: when enabled (default true), draws line outlines around the highlighted boxes in addition to the faces; disabling it clears outline render state and shows only faces.

settings.name: Targets
settings.description: The set of block types to highlight. Defaults to all beds (blocks ending in _BED) and the dragon egg. Changing it restarts the module's tracking so the new selection takes effect immediately.

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: How the highlight color is determined: Map (default, uses each block's map color), Static (a fixed color, default RGBA 255,179,72,50) or Rainbow (animated rainbow).

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of the Static color mode: the fixed color and alpha used for all highlighted blocks (default RGBA 255,179,72,50).

settings.name: NearStart
settings.description: Child of the DistanceFade group: the distance (0..512, default 0) at which near fade begins; clamped to not exceed NearEnd. Controls fading of the highlight close to the camera.

settings.name: NearEnd
settings.description: Child of the DistanceFade group: the distance (0..512, default 0) at which near fade ends; clamped between NearStart and FarStart. Blocks become fully visible beyond this distance.

settings.name: FarStart
settings.description: Child of the DistanceFade group: the distance (0..512, default 512) at which far fade begins; clamped between NearEnd and FarEnd. Beyond this the highlight starts fading out.

settings.name: FarEnd
settings.description: Child of the DistanceFade group: the distance (0..512, default 512) at which the highlight fully fades to invisible; never less than FarStart.

settings.name: MergeAdjacent
settings.description: When enabled (default false), adjacent matching block shapes are merged into single combined shapes for cleaner rendering and fewer outlines; changing it forces a re-render.

modules.name: BlockIn
modules.summary: BlockIn builds a protective shell of blocks around you, encasing your position to shield against attacks. On enable it records your standing position, computes the surrounding positions (the block below, the ring of blocks around you at body height, and the block above your head) and queues them in the placer. It auto-disables (with a 'filled' notification) once the shell is complete and aborts (with an error notification) if you move out of your starting position. The module is disabled automatically on quitting the world.
useCases: Instantly wall yourself in during PvP or anchor/crystal fights to block incoming hits.
Quickly encase yourself in obsidian or other blocks to survive a burst of damage while you heal or plan.
Use a randomized or top-to-bottom placement order to make the encasing pattern less predictable.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Inside Placer. Maximum placement reach (default 4.5, range 1..6) to a block face in line of sight.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Inside Placer. Reach used for placements through walls / without direct line of sight (default 4.5, range 0..6). 0 disables placing through walls.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Inside Placer. Random tick delay (default 1..2, range 0..40) inserted between placements after an action runs.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Inside Placer. Hand-swing behavior when placing (default DO_NOT_HIDE), controlling whether/how the swing animation is shown to the server.

settings.name: ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Inside Placer (default true). When a raytrace to the target fails, constructs a center-based hit result so the placement still happens; more reliable on most servers but rotations may be slightly off and placement can occur slightly out of range.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: Inside Placer. Random number of ticks (default 1..1, range 0..10) to sneak when placing against an interactable block, preventing accidental block activation.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Inside Placer. Conditions under which the placer keeps working that would normally pause it: OpenInventory (keep placing with an inventory screen open) and UsingItem (keep placing while using an item). Default none selected.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Inside Placer. Random tick range (default 4..6, range 0..40) the silently-selected block slot is held before restoring your previous slot.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Inside Placer. How the player rotates toward placements: 'Normal' performs realistic server-side rotations (one placement per tick), 'None' places without proper rotation (optionally just sending a rotation packet) and can do multiple placements per tick.

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Inside Placer > RotationMode (both Normal and None, default false). When enabled the placement action is executed after the movement packet (post-move) rather than before.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Inside Placer > RotationMode 'Normal'. A sub-tree of rotation-behavior settings (such as turn speed/interpolation, fixed/aiming options) controlling how smoothly and convincingly the player turns toward each placement.

settings.name: SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Inside Placer > RotationMode 'None' (default false). When enabled, sends a rotation packet matching the placement target even though the client doesn't visibly rotate.

settings.name: Placements
settings.description: Inside Placer > RotationMode 'None'. Number of blocks placed per operation/tick (default 1, range 1..10, unit b/o). Higher values place faster but less legitimately.

settings.name: Support
settings.description: Inside Placer. Toggleable sub-group (default enabled) that places extra 'helper' blocks so that otherwise unsupported target positions become placeable, pathing helper blocks via a shortest-path search.

settings.name: Depth
settings.description: Inside Placer > Support. Maximum search depth / Manhattan distance (default 4, range 1..12) for the support-block path.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Inside Placer > Support. Minimum time in milliseconds (default 500, range 0..1000) between support-path searches.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Inside Placer > Support. How the support Blocks list is interpreted (default BLACKLIST): which blocks may be used as helper/support blocks.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Inside Placer > Support. The block list (with Filter) defining which blocks are usable as support/helper blocks. Empty by default.

settings.name: DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Inside Placer. Toggleable sub-group (default enabled) that attacks end crystals blocking a target placement spot, as long as the explosion wouldn't kill you.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals. Reach for hitting a blocking crystal in line of sight (default 4.5, range 1..6).

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals. Reach for hitting a crystal through walls (default 4.5, range 0..6).

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals. Minimum delay in milliseconds (default 0, range 0..1000) between crystal attacks.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals. Hand-swing behavior when attacking the crystal (default DO_NOT_HIDE).

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals. Rotation behavior for aiming at the crystal: Normal (real rotations) or None.

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Inside Placer > DestroyCrystals > RotationMode (default false). Executes the crystal attack after the movement packet when enabled.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Inside Placer. Toggleable renderer sub-group (default disabled) drawing boxes at positions queued to be placed.

settings.name: PlacedRendering
settings.description: Inside Placer. Toggleable renderer sub-group (default enabled) drawing boxes at positions that were just placed (boxes are not kept).

settings.name: AutoDisable
settings.description: When enabled (default true), BlockIn turns itself off and shows a 'filled' notification once the protective shell is complete; when off it keeps re-filling.

settings.name: PlaceOrder
settings.description: Order in which the surrounding positions are placed: Normal (default, fixed ring order), Random (shuffled), BottomTop (ascending Y), or TopBottom (descending Y).

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: How the Blocks list is interpreted when choosing which hotbar/offhand blocks BlockIn may place with (default BLACKLIST).

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The block list (with Filter) restricting which held blocks BlockIn uses to build the shell. Empty by default; harder blocks are preferred for shell positions and softer blocks for non-shell positions.

modules.name: BlockOutline
modules.summary: BlockOutline replaces Minecraft's default block-highlight outline with a customizable colored box. You can fill and outline the targeted block, optionally only highlight the face you are looking at, and choose custom fill/outline colors. An optional slide animation smoothly interpolates the highlight as your target moves from one block to another. It correctly handles non-cube block shapes by drawing the actual collision shape.
useCases: Giving the block selection box a clearer, custom color so it stands out.
Highlighting only the face you are looking at (useful for precise placement/mining alignment).
Adding a smooth sliding transition to the block outline as you move your crosshair between blocks.

settings.name: SideOnly
settings.description: When enabled (default), only the face of the block you are looking at is highlighted (a flat plane) instead of the whole block box. When off, the entire block box is drawn.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: The fill color (RGBA) of the block highlight. Default is a blue tint (68,117,255) with alpha 70 (semi-transparent).

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: The outline/edge color (RGBA) of the block highlight. Default is the same blue tint (68,117,255) with alpha 150 (more opaque than the fill).

settings.name: Slide
settings.description: Toggle for the slide-animation group (enabled by default). When enabled, the highlight smoothly interpolates (slides) from the previously targeted block box to the new one instead of jumping instantly. Child settings control timing and easing.

settings.name: Time
settings.description: Child of Slide. Duration in milliseconds of the slide animation between block targets (default 150, range 1-1000). Higher values make the highlight slide more slowly.

settings.name: Easing
settings.description: Child of Slide. The easing function used to interpolate the slide animation (default LINEAR). Changing it alters the acceleration/feel of the sliding transition.

modules.name: BlockTrap
modules.summary: BlockTrap traps a nearby enemy by surrounding their hitbox with blocks, boxing them in so they cannot move or escape. It tracks the best target (by default the one closest to your crosshair within range), computes the placement positions around the target's bounding box, optionally adds extra blocks above the head or below the feet, and queues them to the shared BlockPlacer engine in a chosen order. With Instant enabled it can re-place broken blocks the moment a block update packet arrives.
useCases: Box an opponent inside blocks during PvP so they can't run, then attack them freely.
Place double layers above an enemy's head to stop them from towering up to escape.
Cage a player on the floor (with Below double-placement) so they can't mine straight down to flee.

settings.name: DoublePlace
settings.description: Adds a second layer of blocks at chosen edges. Above places two blocks above the target's head (preventing them from mining the cap and towering up); Below places an extra layer beneath them (requires Floor in PlaceAt). Default none selected.

settings.name: PlaceAt
settings.description: Which edge planes around the target are filled. Legs allows placing next to their legs; Floor allows placing next to the floor. Default has both entries available; disabling one filters out the corresponding layer (legs layer at lowestY+1, floor layer at lowestY).

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: If enabled, broken trap blocks are replaced instantly when a block-update packet arrives. Default true. Requires the placer's rotation mode to be None to function.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/Blacklist mode controlling which blocks (from the Blocks list) are eligible to be placed as trap material. Default BLACKLIST (use anything except the listed blocks).

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The set of blocks used together with Filter to decide which items in your hotbar are used to build the trap.

settings.name: PlacePriority
settings.description: Order in which queued trap positions are placed. Closest/Furthest sort by distance to you (default Furthest), Highest/Lowest sort by Y. Changing this changes which side of the cage is built first.

settings.name: Place
settings.description: The shared BlockPlacer sub-group (priority NORMAL) that performs the placements, containing the placement settings below.

settings.name: Place > Range
settings.description: Maximum reach used to place blocks. Default 4.5, range 1..6.

settings.name: Place > WallRange
settings.description: Reach for placements on away-facing/through-wall faces. Default 4.5, range 0..6 (0 disables).

settings.name: Place > Cooldown
settings.description: Random tick delay between placements. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0..40.

settings.name: Place > Swing
settings.description: Hand swing visibility when placing. Default DO_NOT_HIDE.

settings.name: Place > ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Synthesizes a center hit result when raytrace fails, improving placement reliability. Default true.

settings.name: Place > Sneak
settings.description: Ticks to sneak when placing on an interactable block to avoid triggering it. Default 1..1, range 0..10.

settings.name: Place > Ignore
settings.description: OpenInventory and UsingItem; when checked, placement continues even with a container open or while using an item. Default none.

settings.name: Place > SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Ticks before a silent slot selection resets. Default 4..6, range 0..40.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode
settings.description: Normal (server-visible rotation, one placement/tick) or None (no real rotation, faster multi-placement; required for Instant).

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > PostMove
settings.description: Run placement after the movement packet instead of before. Default false.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > Normal > Rotations
settings.description: Dynamic rotation engine sub-group (AngleSmooth, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold, TicksUntilReset) used in Normal mode.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > None > SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Send a rotation packet before placing in None mode. Default false.

settings.name: Place > RotationMode > None > Placements
settings.description: Blocks placed per operation in None mode (b/o). Default 1, range 1..10.

settings.name: Place > Support
settings.description: Toggleable support feature placing helper blocks so trap positions become placeable. Enabled by default (support placements are allowed for BlockTrap).

settings.name: Place > Support > Depth
settings.description: Support pathfinding depth. Default 4, range 1..12.

settings.name: Place > Support > Delay
settings.description: Minimum delay between support searches. Default 500 ms, range 0..1000.

settings.name: Place > Support > Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/Blacklist for support block material. Default BLACKLIST.

settings.name: Place > Support > Blocks
settings.description: Block set used with the support Filter to choose helper materials.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Toggleable feature attacking end crystals blocking placements. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > Range
settings.description: Reach to attack crystals. Default 4.5, range 1..6.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > WallRange
settings.description: Through-wall reach to attack crystals. Default 4.5, range 0..6.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > Delay
settings.description: Delay between crystal attacks. Default 0 ms, range 0..1000.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > SwingMode
settings.description: Swing visibility when attacking crystals. Default DO_NOT_HIDE.

settings.name: Place > DestroyCrystals > RotationMode
settings.description: Normal or None rotation handling for crystal attacks.

settings.name: Place > TargetRendering
settings.description: PlacementRenderer drawing queued-to-place positions. Disabled by default.

settings.name: Place > PlacedRendering
settings.description: PlacementRenderer drawing just-placed positions (not kept). Enabled by default.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: The TargetTracker sub-group selecting which entity to trap. Default priority Direction (closest to crosshair). Contains the settings below.

settings.name: Target > Range
settings.description: Maximum distance at which an entity can be selected as the trap target. Default 4.0, range 1..6 (this is the FloatValueProvider range supplied to the tracker).

settings.name: Target > FOV
settings.description: Maximum crosshair angle to the entity for it to be a valid target. Default 180, range 0..180 (180 = no angle restriction).

settings.name: Target > HurtTime
settings.description: Maximum allowed hurt time of the entity to be targeted. Default 10, range 0..10.

settings.name: Target > Priority
settings.description: Ordered priority criteria for choosing among valid targets (Type, Health, Distance, Direction, HurtTime, Age). Defaults to Type plus the module default (Direction); cannot be none.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable TargetRenderer that visually highlights the current trap target. Enabled by default; offers multiple appearance modes (Legacy box, Circle, Image, GlowingCircle, Ghost, Hearts, 2D Text, Arrow) each with their own color/size/height sub-options.

modules.name: BlockWalk
modules.summary: BlockWalk lets you walk on top of blocks that normally do not have a full collision box, treating them as solid full blocks. It works by intercepting the collision shape of configured block types and replacing it with a full cube shape. By default it targets cobweb and snow (layers), so you can stand on or traverse them as if they were solid ground.
useCases: Walk across or stand on top of snow layers and cobwebs without sinking in or being slowed.
Add other normally non-solid blocks to the list to create reliable footing on them.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: A sorted set of block types whose collision shape is replaced with a full block so you can walk on them. Defaults to Cobweb and Snow. Any block added here will be treated as a solid full cube for collision purposes.

modules.name: BookBot
modules.summary: BookBot automatically fills and signs writable books, enabling mass book creation or book spam. It repeatedly finds an empty writable book in your inventory, swaps it into your hand if needed, fills it with generated content split across pages, and signs it. Content can be random characters or read from a file, with a configurable delay between books; the module disables itself when no empty book remains and turns off on quit.
useCases: Mass-producing filled/signed books for spam or stress testing.
Writing the contents of a text file into one or more in-game books automatically.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: Inventory-action constraint sub-group (PlayerInventoryConstraints) controlling timing and requirements for the inventory swaps used to grab books (contains StartDelay, ClickDelay, CloseDelay, MissChance, Requires below).

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Constraints setting: delay range in ticks before starting an inventory action. Default 1..2, allowed 0..20.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Constraints setting: delay range in ticks between inventory clicks. Default 2..4, allowed 0..20.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Constraints setting: delay range in ticks before closing the inventory. Default 1..2, allowed 0..20.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Constraints setting: percentage chance range to deliberately misclick during inventory actions. Default 0..0, allowed 0..100.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Constraints setting: conditions that must hold before performing inventory actions. Options: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, InventoryOpen. Default: none selected (no requirements).

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the content generation mode. Choices: Random (default) and File. Each mode shares a Pages setting and has its own extra options.

settings.name: Pages
settings.description: Shared generation setting (present in both Random and File modes): number of pages to fill per book. Default 50, range 0..100.

settings.name: AsciiOnly
settings.description: Random mode setting: if true, restrict generated characters to printable ASCII (0x21..0x7E); if false (default), use a wide Unicode range (0x0800..0x10FFFF).

settings.name: AllowSpace
settings.description: Random mode setting: if true (default), whitespace characters may appear in generated text; if false, whitespace is filtered out.

settings.name: Cyclic
settings.description: File mode setting: if true (default), the source file's code points are repeated cyclically to fill all pages; if false, generation stops when the file's content is exhausted.

settings.name: Source
settings.description: File mode setting: file picker for the source text file (read as UTF-8, up to 64 MiB of code points). Empty or unreadable files produce no content.

settings.name: Sign
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled). When enabled, the book is signed with the generated title; when disabled, the book is written but left unsigned.

settings.name: Name
settings.description: Sign sub-setting: title template for the signed book. Default 'Generated book #%count%', where %count% is replaced by the current book counter.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Time in seconds to wait between writing successive books. Default 0.5, range 0..20.

modules.name: Breadcrumbs
modules.summary: Breadcrumbs (alias PlayerTrails) leaves a visible trail behind players, marking the path they have walked. Each tick it records a player's position and connects the recorded points into a continuous line or a vertical ribbon (depending on the Height setting). The trail can be limited to your own player or shown for every player in the world, and trail segments can expire and fade out over time.
useCases: Visualize your own movement path to review jumps, strafes, or parkour routes.
Track where other players have moved across the map in multiplayer.
Create a stylized rainbow ribbon trail for recordings or visual flair.

settings.name: OnlyOwn
settings.description: When enabled (default true) only your own player leaves a trail; trails for all other players are removed. When disabled, trails are drawn for every player currently in the world.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: The RGBA color of the trail. Default is a translucent blue (RGBA 70, 119, 255, 120). The alpha component sets the base opacity of the trail. Ignored when Rainbow is enabled.

settings.name: Rainbow
settings.description: When enabled (default false), the trail cycles through a rainbow color animation instead of using the fixed Color value.

settings.name: Height
settings.description: The vertical height of the trail ribbon, default 0.5, range 0 to 2. At 0 the trail is drawn as a flat line; any value above 0 extrudes it upward into a filled vertical quad of that height in blocks.

settings.name: Temporary
settings.description: Toggle for the Temporary value group (enabled by default). When enabled, trail points expire after a set time so the trail has a limited length; when disabled, trail points persist indefinitely and the trail keeps growing.

settings.name: Alive
settings.description: Child of the Temporary group. How long each trail point remains visible in milliseconds before it is removed, default 900, range 10 to 10000. Higher values produce longer-lasting, longer trails.

settings.name: Fade
settings.description: Child of the Temporary group (default true). When enabled, older trail points gradually fade toward transparent as they approach their expiration time (alpha scales from full down to zero based on remaining lifetime). Only has an effect while the Temporary group is enabled.

modules.name: CameraClip
modules.summary: CameraClip lets the third-person camera pass through walls and blocks instead of being pushed in, so you keep a clear view even when standing against terrain. It exposes a configurable camera distance, an optional smooth animation when the camera moves out, and an optional scroll-to-adjust feature that lets you change the camera distance with the mouse wheel while holding a modifier key.
useCases: Keep a clean, unobstructed third-person view when standing near or inside walls.
Use the scroll-adjust feature to zoom the third-person camera in and out on the fly.
Combine with FreeLook to dynamically pan the camera distance during gameplay.

settings.name: CameraDistance
settings.description: The third-person camera distance from the player, in blocks. Default 4, range 1 to 48. Larger values move the camera further back.

settings.name: Animation
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling smooth interpolation of the camera distance when switching out of first person. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Animation: interpolation speed/amount used to lerp the camera toward its target distance. Default 0.6, range 0.1 to 1. Higher values reach the target faster.

settings.name: Easing
settings.description: Animation: easing function applied to the camera distance interpolation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: ScrollAdjust
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling adjustment of the camera distance with the mouse scroll wheel. Enabled by default. Scrolling is only applied while the (optional) modifier key is held and the relevant view/FreeLook conditions are met.

settings.name: Modifier
settings.description: ScrollAdjust: the key that must be held for scroll-adjust to take effect. Default Left Control. If set to unbound, scrolling adjusts the distance without any modifier.

settings.name: Sensitivity
settings.description: ScrollAdjust: how much each scroll notch changes the camera distance. Default 0.3, range 0.1 to 2.

settings.name: RememberScrolled
settings.description: ScrollAdjust: if true, the distance you scrolled to is saved back into CameraDistance when scrolling is reset (e.g. on releasing the modifier or returning to first person). Default false.

settings.name: RequireFreeLook
settings.description: ScrollAdjust: if true, scroll-adjust only works while the FreeLook module is active. Default false.

modules.name: Chams
modules.summary: Chams provides custom render pipelines/render types that draw entities so they remain visible through walls and other obstructions. It defines translucent, cutout, and no-cull entity render types with a relaxed depth/stencil configuration so entity models are not hidden behind solid geometry. This module exposes no user-configurable settings; its behavior is driven entirely by the custom render pipelines it installs.
useCases: Seeing players or mobs through walls and terrain so targets are never lost behind cover.
Tracking opponents in combat even when they break line of sight.

modules.name: ChestCleaner
modules.summary: ChestCleaner (also aliased ContainerCleaner) automatically throws out unwanted items from an open container such as a chest, shulker box, or barrel. When a matching container screen is open, it scans the container slots and drops every item that passes the configured filter against the items list. If no matching items remain, it can automatically close the container. Item interactions respect inventory action constraints (delays and requirements).
useCases: Quickly clearing junk items out of looted chests during raids or sorting runs without manually dragging each stack out.
Keeping only desired items by using a whitelist/blacklist to drop everything that matches the list.
Restricting cleaning to specific container types or titles (e.g., only chests and shulkers) to avoid touching the wrong inventories.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whether the Items list acts as a Whitelist (only listed items are dropped) or a Blacklist (everything except listed items is dropped). Default Whitelist.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: The list of item types used together with the Filter to decide which items in the container are thrown out. Empty by default.

settings.name: AutoClose
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the container screen is automatically closed once there are no more matching items left to drop.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: Nested value group of inventory action constraints controlling timing and requirements for the throw/close actions. Contains the sub-settings below.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Child of Constraints. Random delay range (ticks) before the first inventory action begins. Default 1 to 2, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Child of Constraints. Random delay range (ticks) between individual click/throw actions. Default 2 to 4, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Child of Constraints. Random delay range (ticks) before closing the screen. Default 1 to 2, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Child of Constraints. Random chance range (percent) to deliberately miss an inventory action to look more human. Default 0 to 0, range 0 to 100%.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Child of Constraints. Conditions that must all be met before inventory actions run. Options: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, and InventoryOpen (player-inventory variant). None selected by default.

settings.name: CheckScreenHandlerType
settings.description: Toggle (enabled by default) for restricting cleaning to specific container menu types. When enabled, the container's menu type must pass the Types filter for the module to act.

settings.name: Types
settings.description: Child of CheckScreenHandlerType. The list of allowed container menu types. Defaults to GENERIC_9x3, GENERIC_9x6, and SHULKER_BOX.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Child of CheckScreenHandlerType. Whether the Types list is a Whitelist (only those menu types allowed) or Blacklist. Default Whitelist.

settings.name: CheckScreenTitle
settings.description: Toggle (enabled by default, alias CheckTitle) for restricting cleaning by the container's screen title. When enabled, the title must match the configured set/custom titles.

settings.name: Titles
settings.description: Child of CheckScreenTitle. Set of recognized container titles to match against (Barrel, Beacon, BlastFurnace, BrewingStand, Chest, LargeChest, Dispenser, Dropper, EnderChest, Furnace, Hopper, ShulkerBox, Smoker, ChestMinecart, HopperMinecart). Defaults to Chest, LargeChest, ShulkerBox, Barrel, and ChestMinecart.

settings.name: Custom
settings.description: Child of CheckScreenTitle. Additional custom title strings to match exactly against the container's title. Empty by default.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Child of CheckScreenTitle. Whether matched titles are treated as a Whitelist (only matching titles allowed) or Blacklist (matching titles excluded). Default Whitelist.

modules.name: ChestStealer
modules.summary: ChestStealer automatically pulls all items out of an open container (chest, shulker box, barrel, etc.) into your inventory, scheduling the clicks in a configurable, server-friendly way. It can decide which slots to take and in what order, optionally cooperate with InventoryCleaner to only grab useful items and discard junk, quick-swap chest items directly into hotbar slots, and automatically close the screen when finished. It also bundles an optional ChestAura sub-feature that opens nearby chests for you and a SilentScreen sub-feature that hides the container GUI while still letting it be stolen.
useCases: Instantly loot chests in scenarios like Skywars/loot games where speed of grabbing gear matters.
Automatically empty a row of storage chests by combining it with ChestAura so chests are opened and stolen hands-free.
Loot only valuable items (and throw away junk to make room) by running it together with InventoryCleaner.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: A value group bundling the timing and condition rules applied to every scheduled inventory action (shared by all inventory-interacting modules). Contains StartDelay, ClickDelay, CloseDelay, MissChance and Requires (documented as separate entries below).

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Random delay (in ticks) inserted before the first interaction with the container. Default range 1..2, selectable within 0..20 ticks. Higher values look more human but slow stealing.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Random delay (in ticks) between individual clicks while stealing. Default range 2..4, selectable within 0..20 ticks. Larger values are safer against anticheats but slower.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Random delay (in ticks) before the container screen is closed. Default range 1..2, selectable within 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Chance (in percent) to deliberately 'miss' a scheduled action to mimic human error. Default range 0..0 (never miss), selectable within 0..100%.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be satisfied before any inventory action runs. Options: NoMovement (not moving/jumping), NoRotation (server rotation unchanged), NotUsingItem, NotBreaking (not breaking a block), NotDuringCombat. Default: none selected. Adding requirements makes interaction pause until the situation is safe.

settings.name: AutoClose
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the container screen is automatically closed once all targeted items have been taken. Disable to keep the screen open after stealing.

settings.name: SelectionMode
settings.description: Determines the order in which container slots are stolen. Options: Distance (default), Index, Random. Each mode has its own sub-settings.

settings.name: StartItem
settings.description: Distance mode only. Chooses which slot the nearest-neighbor ordering starts from. Options: Default (first slot, default), Random (random slot), MaxSlot (highest container slot index), MinSlot (lowest container slot index).

settings.name: RandomFactor
settings.description: Distance mode only. Random multiplier applied to slot-to-slot distances to add jitter to the steal order. Default 1.0..1.0 (no randomization), selectable within 0.25..2.0. A wider range makes the path less optimal/more human-like.

settings.name: Order
settings.description: Index mode only. Sorts the slots to steal by their container index. Options: Ascending (default) or Descending.

settings.name: MoveMode
settings.description: How items are physically moved out of the container. QUICK_MOVE (default) shift-clicks items across; DRAG_AND_DROP picks up and places stacks manually, merging into matching/empty slots. DragAndDrop can be more reliable for partial merges but uses more clicks.

settings.name: QuickSwaps
settings.description: When enabled (default true), eligible items (e.g. swords) are swapped directly from the chest into hotbar slots using a swap action instead of normal pickups, since some servers dislike shift-click moves. Empty target slots are swapped directly, useful hotbar items are first moved to an empty inventory slot, and useless hotbar items are thrown (offhand items are swapped instead of thrown to look legit).

settings.name: OnFull
settings.description: What to do when your inventory is full but more useful items remain. Options: NONE (do nothing, stop) or THROW (default, drop a junk item from your inventory to make room). PutBack is defined but disabled in code.

settings.name: CheckScreenHandlerType
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that restricts stealing to specific container menu types. Contains the Types list and Filter sub-settings. When disabled, all container types are accepted.

settings.name: Types
settings.description: Registry list of allowed/blocked container menu types under CheckScreenHandlerType. Defaults include GENERIC_9x3, GENERIC_9x6 and SHULKER_BOX. Combined with the Filter setting to decide which menus may be stolen.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Under CheckScreenHandlerType: WHITELIST (default, only listed Types are stolen) or BLACKLIST (listed Types are excluded).

settings.name: CheckScreenTitle
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default, alias CheckTitle) that restricts stealing to containers whose GUI title matches a set of titles. Contains Titles, Custom and Filter sub-settings. When disabled, any title is accepted.

settings.name: Titles
settings.description: Under CheckScreenTitle: the set of known container titles to match (by translation key). Defaults: Chest, LargeChest, ShulkerBox, Barrel, ChestMinecart. Other options include Beacon, BlastFurnace, BrewingStand, Dispenser, Dropper, EnderChest, Furnace, Hopper, Smoker, HopperMinecart.

settings.name: Custom
settings.description: Under CheckScreenTitle: a list of custom literal title strings to also match. Default empty. Useful for servers with renamed container GUIs.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Under CheckScreenTitle: WHITELIST (default, only containers with matching titles are stolen) or BLACKLIST (matching titles are excluded).

settings.name: Aura
settings.description: Toggleable sub-feature (ChestAura, enabled by default) that automatically finds and opens nearby storage blocks within range and line of sight so they can be stolen, then moves on to the next. Contains the settings below.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Aura: maximum reach (in blocks) for interacting with a storage block. Default 3.0, range 1.0..6.0.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Aura: maximum reach (in blocks) for interacting with storage blocks through walls. Default 0.0 (no through-wall interaction), range 0.0..6.0; clamped to never exceed Range.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Aura: delay (in ticks) between interactions with successive storage blocks. Default 5, range 1..80.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: Aura: how the hand swing is sent when interacting. Default DO_NOT_HIDE (swing normally visible).

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: Aura: when enabled (default true), the aura clears its target and stops interacting while you are in combat.

settings.name: TrackManualInteractions
settings.description: Aura: when enabled (default true), chests you open manually are recorded as already-interacted so the aura won't reopen them.

settings.name: PauseOn
settings.description: Aura: conditions under which the aura is paused. Options: Combat (while in combat) and UsingItem (while using an item). Default: none selected.

settings.name: AwaitContainer
settings.description: Aura: toggleable group (enabled by default) that makes the aura wait and confirm a container screen actually opened after interacting, retrying if not. Contains Timeout and MaxRetries.

settings.name: Timeout
settings.description: Aura/AwaitContainer: how long (in ticks) to wait for the container screen to appear after an interaction before retrying. Default 10, range 1..80.

settings.name: MaxRetries
settings.description: Aura/AwaitContainer: maximum number of interaction retries for a block before giving up and marking it as done. Default 4, range 1..10.

settings.name: ValidStorageBlocks
settings.description: Aura: the set of block types treated as storage and targeted by the aura. Defaults to all blocks ending in CHEST, SHULKER_BOX, BARREL, FURNACE plus brewing stand, dispenser and hopper.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Aura: dynamic rotation-engine value group controlling how the player turns to aim at the chest. Contains AngleSmooth (mode selection of how rotations are smoothed, default first/Linear-style with Sigmoid and Acceleration alternatives), MovementCorrection (default Silent, how rotations relate to movement), ResetThreshold (default 2.0, range 1.0..180.0 degrees, the angular difference at which the rotation is considered done) and TicksUntilReset (default 5, range 1..30 ticks, how long before rotations snap back).

settings.name: SilentScreen
settings.description: Toggleable sub-feature (disabled by default) that hides the container GUI while a stealable container is open so you keep playing normally; the chest can still be stolen in the background. Contains the settings below.

settings.name: UnlockCursor
settings.description: SilentScreen: when enabled (default false), frees the mouse cursor while the screen is silently hidden.

settings.name: DrawInventoryTag
settings.description: SilentScreen: toggleable group (enabled by default) that renders a floating preview of the hidden container's contents in the world at the chest's location. Contains Background, Scale, RenderOffset and ShowTitle. This is a render-only feature and is excluded from config publication.

settings.name: Background
settings.description: SilentScreen/DrawInventoryTag: the background style used behind the rendered item-stack list preview.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: SilentScreen/DrawInventoryTag: scale of the rendered preview. Default 1.5, range 0.25..4.0.

settings.name: RenderOffset
settings.description: SilentScreen/DrawInventoryTag: a 3D offset added to the chest's center when positioning the preview in the world. Default zero offset (locate button disabled).

settings.name: ShowTitle
settings.description: SilentScreen/DrawInventoryTag: when enabled (default false), also draws the container's title above the previewed items.

modules.name: ClickGUI
modules.summary: ClickGUI opens LiquidBounce's main graphical menu for toggling and configuring modules. It is bound to Right Shift by default and, rather than being a persistent on/off feature, simply opens the configuration screen when activated. It can optionally cache a standalone browser-backed screen for faster reopening and offers a snap-to-grid system for arranging panels. It also exposes the integrated browser settings once the browser is ready.
useCases: Open the in-game menu to enable, disable, and configure modules without using chat commands.
Arrange ClickGUI panels neatly using grid snapping for a tidy layout.
Speed up reopening the menu by caching the standalone screen instead of rebuilding it each time.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Overall scale (zoom level) of the ClickGUI interface. Larger values make the menu and its elements bigger. Default 1, range 0.5 to 2. Changing it fires a scale-change event that resizes the GUI live.

settings.name: SearchBarAutoFocus
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the ClickGUI search bar automatically receives keyboard focus when the menu opens, so you can start typing a module name immediately.

settings.name: Snapping
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that makes ClickGUI panels snap to a grid when moved, for aligned positioning. Its 'Enabled' toggle turns snapping on/off; contains the nested GridSize setting.

settings.name: GridSize
settings.description: Size of the snapping grid cells in pixels; panels snap to multiples of this value when Snapping is enabled. Default 10, range 1 to 100 px.

settings.name: Cache
settings.description: When enabled (default true), ClickGUI uses a cached standalone screen so the menu reopens faster and persists across world changes. When disabled, the cached screen is closed and the menu is rebuilt each time it opens.

settings.name: Browser
settings.description: Browser settings (ScreenManager.browserSettings) are attached to this module once the integrated browser is ready, exposing the browser-related configuration used to render the ClickGUI. The specific options come from the shared browser settings group.

modules.name: ClickTp
modules.summary: ClickTp lets you teleport onto a block you are looking at by abusing a movement-validation flaw in the Vulcan AntiCheat. While enabled, the block under your crosshair (within Range) is highlighted green if it is a valid landing spot or red if not. Pressing the pick-block key (default middle mouse) triggers the teleport: your client position is moved onto the target, a series of fake jumps with forced collision are performed, and outgoing packets are queued (blinked) to mask the move. It only works against Vulcan, shows chat/notification feedback on start, and reports success or failure after a short delay.
useCases: Instantly relocating to a block you can see (e.g. up onto a ledge or platform) on a server protected by Vulcan AntiCheat.
Bypassing terrain or distance to reach a suitable standing spot without walking.
Quickly repositioning during gameplay by aiming at a target block and pressing pick-block.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum distance (in blocks) the crosshair raytrace will search for a target block to teleport to. Default 60, range 10 to 500. Higher values let you teleport to farther blocks.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Number of ticks to wait after a completed teleport before another can be performed. Default 20, range 0 to 120. Higher values throttle how often you can teleport.

settings.name: LagAfter
settings.description: Number of ticks the module keeps lagging/queuing packets (and applying alternating movement) after the jump sequence, to settle the teleport. Default 40, range 0 to 120.

settings.name: Jumps
settings.description: How many forced ground jumps with simulated downward collision are performed as part of the teleport sequence. Default 3, range 1 to 10.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Number of ticks to wait after setting the new position and before beginning the jump sequence. Default 5, range 0 to 20.

modules.name: Clip
modules.summary: Clip lets you teleport (clip) through nearby blocks by moving, sneaking, or jumping into them. In Fancy mode it continuously scans the direction you are pressing for a valid air pocket on the other side of a wall and snaps you there, showing on-screen arrows for available vertical clip directions. In Old mode, simply enabling it performs a single one-shot positional offset and then turns itself back off.
useCases: Phasing through a wall, floor, or ceiling to reach an otherwise blocked area.
Quickly clipping down through blocks (sneak) or up through them (jump) in Fancy mode while exploring.
Performing a single scripted teleport offset with Old mode for a fixed horizontal/vertical jump.

settings.name: Choice
settings.description: Selects the clip implementation: Fancy (default; continuous, direction-aware clipping that finds a safe air pocket) or Old (one-shot fixed offset that disables itself afterward).

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Fancy mode. Maximum number of blocks to clip horizontally in your movement direction when walking into a wall. Default 0, range 0..6; 0 disables horizontal clipping.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Fancy mode. Maximum number of blocks to clip vertically when sneaking (down) or jumping (up). Default 5, range 0..6; 0 disables vertical clipping.

settings.name: RequiresStandOn
settings.description: Fancy mode. When enabled (default true), the destination is only accepted if there is a solid block to stand on below it (except when clipping upward), preventing you from clipping into a fall.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Old mode. Horizontal distance (relative to your facing yaw) to offset your position when the module is enabled. Default 0, range -10..10.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Old mode. Vertical distance to offset your position when the module is enabled. Default 5, range -10..10.

settings.name: ResetVelocity
settings.description: Old mode. When enabled (default true), your motion is zeroed after the offset so you do not keep moving/falling after the clip.

modules.name: CombineMobs
modules.summary: CombineMobs hides entities of the same type that are crammed together in the same block position and instead renders a single representative entity, optionally annotated with a count of how many were merged. It groups by entity type (and separately for baby variants), which dramatically reduces visual clutter and lag from large stacks of mobs. By default it only combines true mobs, but it can be extended to also combine armor stands and minecarts.
useCases: Reducing lag and screen clutter on anarchy servers like 2b2t where spawn is packed with huge numbers of chickens or other crammed entities.
Cleaning up the view in farms or grinders where many identical mobs pile into the same block.
Optionally collapsing large clusters of armor stands or minecarts into a single rendered object.

settings.name: CombineArmorStands
settings.description: When enabled, armor stands crammed together are also combined into a single rendered entity. Default false; when off, armor stands are never combined regardless of how many overlap.

settings.name: CombineMinecarts
settings.description: When enabled, minecarts (AbstractMinecart) crammed together are also combined into a single rendered entity. Default false; when off, minecarts are never combined.

modules.name: Criticals
modules.summary: Criticals automatically lands critical hits whenever you attack an entity, increasing your melee damage. It exposes several modes (Packet, NoGround, Jump, Blink, Timer, plus None) that achieve crits in different ways, and it includes logic that decides when to stop sprinting since sprinting normally cancels a critical hit. Optional client-side visual particles can be shown to make hits look like crits even when the conditions differ.
useCases: Boost melee damage in PvP by ensuring nearly every attack is a critical hit.
Pair with KillAura or manual combat to maximize burst damage during fights.
Force critical-hit particle visuals (e.g. for legit-looking hits or to fake crits) via the Visuals group.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how critical hits are performed. Options are None, Packet, NoGround, Jump, Blink, and Timer. Default is index 1 (Packet). Each mode uses a different technique (e.g. sending packets, faking off-ground state, micro-jumping, blinking, or manipulating the timer) to satisfy the game's critical-hit requirements when attacking.

settings.name: WhenSprinting
settings.description: Toggle for the WhenSprinting sub-group (default off). When enabled, the module manages sprinting around attacks so that a critical hit can occur even while you would normally be sprinting; it only acts when a critical hit would be possible and an enemy is within the configured range.

settings.name: StopSprinting
settings.description: Child of WhenSprinting. Chooses how sprinting is stopped to allow a crit: None (do not stop sprinting), Legit (cancels sprint on movement/input ticks), OnNetwork (cancels sprint on network/input), or OnAttack (sends a stop-sprinting packet right when attacking). Default is Legit.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Child of WhenSprinting. Maximum distance (in blocks) at which an enemy must be present for the WhenSprinting logic to activate. Default 4.0, range 0.0 to 10.0.

settings.name: Visuals
settings.description: Toggle for the Visuals sub-group (default off). When enabled, the module spawns client-side critical-hit particle effects on the entity you attack.

settings.name: Fake
settings.description: Child of Visuals (default off). When enabled, critical particles are shown on every attack regardless of whether an actual critical hit would occur; when disabled, particles only appear when a real critical hit would happen.

settings.name: Critical
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Number of normal critical-hit particle bursts to spawn on the target per attack. Default 1, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: Magic
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Number of magic (enchantment-style) critical particle bursts to spawn on the target per attack. Default 0, range 0 to 20.

modules.name: Crosshair
modules.summary: Crosshair replaces the vanilla crosshair with a custom one rendered at screen center, offering a Circle style or a CS2-style four-line style. Both styles support a configurable color (single or dual color with an animated spin) and can dynamically expand based on your attack cooldown so the crosshair opens up after attacking and tightens as the cooldown recovers.
useCases: Use a CS2-style crosshair for cleaner aim feedback in PvP.
Display a dynamic crosshair that visualizes your attack cooldown/charge.
Customize crosshair color, size, and animation to your preference.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the crosshair style. Options: Circle (a ring) and CS2 (four lines with a center gap). Default is the first option, Circle.

settings.name: ShowInThirdPerson
settings.description: Whether the custom crosshair is also drawn while in third person view. Default true. (Shared by both crosshair modes.)

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Circle mode: the inner-to-outer radius range of the ring (start = inner radius, end = outer radius). Default 3 to 5, selectable within 0 to 25.

settings.name: DynamicRadiusMultiplier
settings.description: Circle mode: how much the ring radius expands based on attack cooldown. Default 1.0, range 0 to 5. The extra radius scales with (1 - attack strength), so the ring is largest right after an attack. A value of 0 disables the dynamic expansion.

settings.name: Length
settings.description: CS2 mode: length of each of the four crosshair lines. Default 5, range 1 to 20.

settings.name: Thickness
settings.description: CS2 mode: thickness of the crosshair lines. Default 1, range 0.5 to 5.

settings.name: Gap
settings.description: CS2 mode: gap between the center and the start of each line. Default 2, range 0 to 10.

settings.name: DynamicMultiplier
settings.description: CS2 mode: how much the center gap widens based on attack cooldown. Default 1.0, range 0 to 10. The extra gap scales with (1 - attack strength); 0 disables the dynamic expansion.

settings.name: Sync
settings.description: Color: if true (default), the second color is ignored and only the first color is used (no gradient blending between two colors).

settings.name: FirstColor
settings.description: Color: the primary crosshair color. Default blue (RGBA 0,0,255,255).

settings.name: SecondColor
settings.description: Color: the secondary color blended with the first when Sync is off. Default blue (RGBA 0,0,255,255).

settings.name: SpinSpeed
settings.description: Color: speed of the animated color spin/cycling along the crosshair. Default 4, range -10 to 10. Negative values reverse the animation direction; 0 disables the time-based animation.

modules.name: CrystalAura
modules.summary: CrystalAura (alias AutoCrystal) automatically places and detonates end crystals to deal heavy explosion damage to enemies while protecting you and your friends. It evaluates candidate positions for self/enemy/friend damage (with optional self-position and target-position prediction), places crystals on obsidian/bedrock and immediately breaks them, and can build its own obsidian bases. A flexible trigger system decides when calculations run (on tick, on packets such as crystal spawn/destroy, explosion sound, entity movement, etc.), and the work can be run off the render thread for performance. The module disables itself on quit.
useCases: Win crystal-PvP fights on Anarchy/SMP servers by auto-placing and popping crystals on opponents.
Burst down enemies that come into range while automatically avoiding self-kills via damage limits and anti-suicide.
Set up obsidian bases and instantly detonate placed crystals using ID prediction for very fast combos.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target selection sub-group with a built-in Range value (float, default 4.5, 1-12 blocks) plus the shared FOV, HurtTime and Priority selection settings. Determines which enemy the aura focuses for damage calculations.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: How the client rotates when placing/breaking crystals. Normal (default) sends silent server-side rotations toward the crystal; NoRotation skips rotating and instead raytraces from the current view.

settings.name: Place
settings.description: Toggleable sub-module (enabled by default) that places crystals. Settings: Swing (enum, default DoNotHide), Switch (enum slot-switch behavior Silent/Normal/None, default Silent), 1_12_2 (boolean, default false; legacy placement protocol), Delay (int ms between placements, default 0, 0-1000), Range (float, default 4.5, 1-6), WallsRange (float through-walls reach, default 4.5, 0-6), OnlyAbove (boolean, default false; only place on the top face), Sequenced (boolean, default false), NotFacingAway (boolean, default false; only without OnlyAbove), Jitter (boolean, default false; randomize rotations, only without OnlyAbove), and a TargetRendering placement renderer sub-group for highlighting the place spot.

settings.name: Destroy
settings.description: Toggleable sub-module (enabled by default) that breaks/detonates crystals. Settings: Swing (enum, default DoNotHide), Delay (int ms, default 0, 0-1000), Range (float, default 4.5, 1-6), WallsRange (float, default 4.5, 0-6), PrioritizeVisibleFaces (boolean, default false; prefer visible faces, may slow the aura).

settings.name: Damage
settings.description: Damage-evaluation sub-group. Settings: MaxSelfDamage (float, default 2, 0-10; never place/break if it would deal more than this to you), MaxFriendDamage (float, default 1, 0-10; limit damage to friends; 10 disables the friend check), MinEnemyDamage (float, default 5, 0-10; require at least this much damage to the target), AntiSuicide (boolean, default true; never do an action that would kill you), Efficient (boolean, default true; only act when enemy damage exceeds self damage), Terrain (boolean, default true; exclude blocks that would be blown away from exposure/damage calculation).

settings.name: Triggers
settings.description: Sub-group deciding when the aura recalculates. NotWhileUsingItem (boolean, default false; pause while using an item to avoid multi-action flags), Off-Thread (boolean, default true; run calculations on a background thread). Per-event toggles: Tick (default on), BlockChange (default on), ClientBlockBreak (default on), CrystalSpawn (default on), CrystalDestroy (default on), ExplodeSound (default on), EntityMove (default on), SelfMove (default off). Each toggle enables triggering place/break logic when that event occurs.

settings.name: Predict
settings.description: Container group holding Self and Target prediction. Each is a toggleable PredictFeature (both enabled by default) used to simulate future positions for damage and placement validity.

settings.name: Self
settings.description: Self-prediction sub-feature (toggleable, default enabled) under Predict. PlaceTicks (int, default 2, 0-20; ticks ahead to simulate your position when placing), BreakTicks (int, default 1, 0-20), BasePlaceTicks (int, default 4, 0-20), CalculationMode (choices Both/PredictOnly; Both combines current and predicted damage via a Logic operator And/Or, default And), CheckIntersect (boolean, default true; skip placements your predicted body would block).

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target-prediction sub-feature (toggleable, default enabled) under Predict, mirroring Self: PlaceTicks (default 2), BreakTicks (default 1), BasePlaceTicks (default 4), CalculationMode (Both/PredictOnly with Logic And/Or), CheckIntersect (default true) but applied to the enemy's predicted position.

settings.name: IDPredict
settings.description: Toggleable sub-module (default off) that sends a break/attack packet immediately after placing by guessing the new crystal's entity ID. OffsetRange (range of ID offsets to attack, default 1-2, 1-100), SwingAlways (boolean, default false; swing before each attack instead of once), and a Rotate toggleable group (default on) with a Back option (boolean, default false) that sends an extra rotation packet toward the crystal and optionally rotates back afterward.

settings.name: SetDead
settings.description: Toggleable sub-module (default on) that removes a hit crystal from the world instantly instead of waiting for the server remove packet, allowing faster follow-up placements. ConfirmTime (int, default 150, 10-2000 ms): if no remove confirmation arrives within this time the crystal is restored to the world.

settings.name: BasePlace
settings.description: Toggleable sub-module (default on) that builds improved obsidian/bedrock bases to place crystals on. Settings: CalcDelay (int ms before a new calculation, default 120, 0-1000), TimeOut (int ms after which the placer clears, default 240, 0-5000), PlatformOnly (boolean, default false; only place directly below the enemy), OnlyAboveSelf (boolean, default false; only place at/above your Y to not help the enemy), Terrain (boolean, default true; exclude terrain for base placements, only effective if Damage>Terrain is on), MinAdvantage (float, default 2, 0.1-10; minimum damage advantage required to base place), and a SimulateMovement toggleable group.

settings.name: SimulateMovement
settings.description: Toggleable group (default on) under BasePlace that simulates your movement so the aura will not trap itself in placements. Ticks (int, default 3, 1-20; how many ticks to simulate), Error (float, default 0.1, 0-2; how much the bounding box grows per simulated tick), ErrorStep (float, default 0.05, 0-1; per-tick error growth), DownError (boolean, default false; also extend the box downward), AntiPlatformSimulate (boolean, default true; exclude Y levels you might enter to avoid helping enemies).

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that draws a marker on the current crystal target. Provides the shared Mode choice (Legacy/Circle/Image/GlowingCircle/Ghost/Hearts/Text/Arrow) with per-mode color, size, height-mode and appearance options.

modules.name: CrystalView
modules.summary: CrystalView tweaks how End Crystal models are rendered, letting you resize, reposition, spin, and bounce the crystal model. It hooks the crystal model and renderer via mixins to apply these visual changes. It is purely cosmetic/visibility-oriented and affects how crystals appear in the world.
useCases: Shrink crystals so they obstruct your view less during crystal PvP.
Lower or raise the crystal model to better judge its actual position/hitbox.
Disable spinning or bouncing animations for a cleaner, more readable view of crystals.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Scale factor applied to the crystal model. Default 0.3, range 0.1..1.5. Lower values shrink the crystal, higher values enlarge it.

settings.name: YTranslate
settings.description: Vertical offset applied to the crystal model. Default -0.5, range -2..2. Negative moves the model down, positive moves it up.

settings.name: SpinSpeed
settings.description: Rotation speed of the crystal model. Default 0 (no spin), range 0..5. Higher values make the crystal spin faster.

settings.name: Bounce
settings.description: Amount of vertical bobbing/bounce animation applied to the crystal model. Default 0.25, range -1..1. 0 removes the bounce; sign inverts the direction of the bob.

modules.name: CustomAmbience
modules.summary: CustomAmbience (alias FogChanger) overrides the visual ambience of the game world. It can force a specific weather type and time of day, modify precipitation rendering, customize or disable fog, override the lightmap (world lighting/tint), and set a custom sky color.
