Each major effect is an independently toggleable group, letting you mix and match overrides to craft a custom atmosphere.
useCases: Force constant daytime or a specific time of day regardless of the server's clock.
Remove or recolor fog to improve visibility or for aesthetic recordings.
Apply a custom world lighting tint or sky color for a stylized look.

settings.name: Weather
settings.description: Forces the world weather. Options: NoChange, Sunny, Rainy, Snowy (default), Thunder. Overrides the server-reported weather while the module is active.

settings.name: Time
settings.description: Forces the world time of day. Options: NoChange, Dawn (23041 ticks), Day (1000), Noon (6000), Dusk (12610), Night (default, 13000), MidNight (18000). Overrides the world clock used for lighting/sky while active.

settings.name: ModifyPrecipitation
settings.description: Toggle for the precipitation override group (enabled by default). When enabled, the module modifies how rain/snow precipitation is rendered.

settings.name: Gradient
settings.description: Child of ModifyPrecipitation. Controls the precipitation gradient/intensity, default 0.7, range 0.1 to 1. Higher values increase the precipitation effect.

settings.name: Fog
settings.description: Toggle for the fog override group (enabled by default). When enabled, the module rewrites the game's fog parameters and background clear color according to the settings below.

settings.name: DisableWorldFog
settings.description: Child of the Fog group (default false). When enabled, removes world fog entirely.

settings.name: FogColorOverride
settings.description: Toggle for a nested group inside Fog (disabled by default). When enabled, overrides the fog color with the Color value below.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of FogColorOverride. The fog color used when FogColorOverride is enabled. Default translucent blue (RGBA 47, 128, 255, 201).

settings.name: BackgroundColor
settings.description: Child of the Fog group. The background/clear color of the scene, default translucent blue (RGBA 47, 128, 255, 201). When its alpha is 0 the original background color is kept; otherwise this color replaces it.

settings.name: Environmental
settings.description: Child of the Fog group. Float range controlling the environmental fog start and end distances, default 0 to 1024, allowed range -16 to 2048. The start and end values are written directly to the fog data.

settings.name: RenderDistance
settings.description: Child of the Fog group. Float range controlling the render-distance fog start and end, default 230 to 256, allowed range 0 to 1024. Controls where distance fog begins and fully obscures.

settings.name: SkyEnd
settings.description: Child of the Fog group. The sky fog end distance, default 256, range 0 to 1024.

settings.name: CloudEnd
settings.description: Child of the Fog group. The cloud fog end distance, default 20480 (clamped by the slider range), range 0 to 4096.

settings.name: CustomLightmap
settings.description: Toggle for the lightmap override group (disabled by default). When enabled, the module overrides the world lighting/lightmap using the selected editor Mode below.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Child of CustomLightmap. Selects the lightmap editing mode: SingleColor (index 0, default) clears the entire lightmap to a single flat color, or Custom which tints individual lighting channels.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of the SingleColor lightmap mode. The flat color the lightmap texture is cleared to. Default BLUE.

settings.name: BlockLightTint
settings.description: Child of the Custom lightmap mode. Tint applied to block light. Default white with alpha 0; when transparent (alpha 0) it is ignored and the original value is kept, otherwise the RGB is applied.

settings.name: SkyLightColor
settings.description: Child of the Custom lightmap mode. Color applied to sky light. Default blue with alpha 0; ignored while transparent, otherwise applied.

settings.name: AmbientColor
settings.description: Child of the Custom lightmap mode. Color applied to ambient light. Default blue with alpha 0; ignored while transparent, otherwise applied.

settings.name: NightVisionColor
settings.description: Child of the Custom lightmap mode. Color applied to the night vision tint. Default white with alpha 0; ignored while transparent, otherwise applied.

settings.name: SkyColor
settings.description: Toggle for the sky color override group (disabled by default). When enabled, overrides the sky color with the Color value below.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of the SkyColor group. The custom sky color used when SkyColor is enabled. Default BLUE.

modules.name: Damage
modules.summary: Damage instantly deals a configurable amount of self-damage to your own player by exploiting movement-packet handling on certain anti-cheats. You pick an exploit mode and a target HP amount, then enabling the module fires the exploit once. It self-disables behavior is driven by disableActivation, so it acts as a one-shot trigger rather than a persistent toggle.
useCases: Reducing your own health to a target value (e.g. for crystal/anchor PvP setups or testing) without taking real combat damage.
Triggering health-based effects or testing how a server's anti-cheat reacts to self-damage exploits.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Which self-damage exploit to use. NCP (default) spams paired up/down position packets to accumulate fall damage; AAC sets your downward delta movement to 5*Damage; Verus sends a vertical position spike sequence (noted to give ~2 flags). Choose the mode matching the server's anti-cheat.

settings.name: Damage
settings.description: Amount of self-damage to apply, expressed in HP (suffix "HP"). Default 1, range 0..20. The value scales the exploit (e.g. NCP repeats its packet loop 65*Damage times, AAC multiplies downward velocity by Damage).

modules.name: DamageParticles
modules.summary: Displays floating damage/health-change numbers above entities whenever their health changes. When an entity takes damage, heals, dies, or is healed to full, a colored number showing the magnitude of the change pops up, drifts (by default upward) and scales over its lifetime before fading out. Health changes can be detected either every game tick or from server health-update packets.
useCases: Seeing exactly how much damage you deal to opponents in combat.
Monitoring when enemies heal or are restored to full health.
Tracking incoming damage to nearby mobs/players for situational awareness.

settings.name: TimeToLive
settings.description: How long each damage number stays on screen before being removed. Default 3, range 0.5..5.0 (seconds). Also used as the basis for the lifetime progress that drives scale and displacement transitions.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Base text scale of the damage numbers. Default 2, range 0.25..4. The displayed size is this value multiplied by the ScaleTransition value over the particle's life.

settings.name: ScaleTransition
settings.description: Easing curve that animates the number's scale over its lifetime. Default QUAD_OUT. Controls how the text grows/shrinks as it ages.

settings.name: Displacement
settings.description: World-space movement vector applied to a particle over its lifetime. Default (0, 1.5, 0), i.e. it rises 1.5 blocks upward. Change to make numbers drift in a different direction/amount.

settings.name: DisplacementTransition
settings.description: Easing curve that animates how the displacement is applied over the particle's lifetime. Default QUAD_OUT. Controls the motion profile of the rising/drifting number.

settings.name: TrackMode
settings.description: How health changes are detected. OnTick (default) polls every entity's health each game tick; OnUpdate reacts to server entity health-update events instead.

settings.name: Damage
settings.description: Colors group. Color used for numbers when an entity loses health (takes damage). Default red.

settings.name: Death
settings.description: Colors group. Color used when an entity's health change brings it to 0 or below (death). Default red.

settings.name: Heal
settings.description: Colors group. Color used when an entity gains health below its maximum (heal). Default green.

settings.name: MaxHealth
settings.description: Colors group. Color used when an entity gains health up to its maximum. Default green.

modules.name: DankBobbing
modules.summary: DankBobbing exaggerates the view-bobbing animation that occurs while you walk, making your camera bob far more dramatically than normal. It is purely a cosmetic, client-side visual effect and has no impact on gameplay or other players. The strength of the effect scales directly with a single multiplier setting.
useCases: Adding an over-the-top, comedic walking animation to your view for fun or recording content.
Demonstrating or showing off a stylized first-person camera effect.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Multiplier that controls how strong the view-bobbing effect is. Default is 5, with a range of 1 to 50. Higher values produce a more extreme, exaggerated bobbing motion.

modules.name: Debug
modules.summary: Debug is a developer/diagnostic render module that visualizes internal client state. It can render captured debug parameters as an on-screen text overlay (grouped by owner with how long ago each value was captured) and draw debug geometry (lines, boxes, triangles, points) in the world. It also includes optional tools to render a simulated future path of the local player and to plot a sample curve overlay. Captured parameters expire after a configurable time, and the parameter overlay hides while the player list key is held.
useCases: Inspect live internal values (rotations, parameters) that modules report while developing or troubleshooting.
Visualize hitboxes, lines, and other debug geometry rendered by other features.
Preview the simulated future movement path of your player for testing prediction logic.

settings.name: Parameters
settings.description: Whether to render captured debug parameters as the on-screen 'Debugging' text overlay. Default true. Toggling clears the stored parameter captures.

settings.name: Geometry
settings.description: Whether to render debug geometry (lines, boxes, triangles, points) in the world. Default true. Toggling clears the stored geometry.

settings.name: Expires
settings.description: How long (suffix 'secs') a captured debug parameter remains before it is removed from the overlay. Default 5, range 1..30.

settings.name: SimulatedPlayer
settings.description: Toggle for the SimulatedPlayer value group (disabled by default). When enabled, it simulates the local player's movement and draws a blue line strip showing the predicted future positions.

settings.name: TicksToPredict
settings.description: Child of the SimulatedPlayer group. Number of ticks into the future to simulate and render. Default 20, range 5..100. Higher values show a longer predicted path.

settings.name: Graph
settings.description: Toggle for the Graph value group (disabled by default). When enabled, draws a sample 'Graph' curve overlay on screen, plotting the configured curve and its control points.

settings.name: Curve
settings.description: Child of the Graph group. The editable curve that is plotted by the Graph overlay, with an X axis ('X Axis', range 0..180) and Y axis ('Y Axis', range 40..120). Editing the control points changes the plotted shape.

modules.name: DebugRecorder
modules.summary: DebugRecorder is a developer/tester tool that captures gameplay and packet data into JSON files for debugging and machine-learning data collection. The active recording mode is chosen via the Mode setting; while enabled it accumulates samples, and when disabled it writes them to a timestamped JSON file under the client's debug-recorder/<mode> folder (showing a clickable path in chat) or reports that nothing was recorded. The module automatically disables on quit and is excluded from auto-config exports.
useCases: Collect combat or aim data sets for training/analyzing LiquidBounce's deep-learning aim models.
Record CPS (click) timing or entity/box debug data to investigate behavior or bugs.
Practice and record hit-target training samples using the CombatTrainer mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which data recorder is active. Choices: Combat, CombatTrainer, Generic (default), CPS, Aim, and Box. Each mode records a different dataset; only the Combat mode exposes additional settings (see below).

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Combat mode (Target sub-group). Maximum field-of-view angle (degrees) from your crosshair within which an entity is considered a valid target. Default 180, range 0..180.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Combat mode (Target sub-group). Maximum allowed hurt-time of an entity for it to be treated as a valid target; entities with a higher hurt time are ignored. Default 10, range 0..10.

settings.name: Priority
settings.description: Combat mode (Target sub-group). Ordered priorities used to sort/choose targets. Options: Type, Health, Distance, Direction, HurtTime, Age. Default prioritizes Type then Direction (the recorder's default priority); cannot be set to none.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Combat mode (Target sub-group). Distance (in blocks) at which entities begin being tracked as combat targets for recording. Default 10, range 7..12.

modules.name: Derp
modules.summary: Derp makes your character appear to look around erratically by overriding your sent yaw (horizontal) and pitch (vertical) rotations through the rotation engine. The yaw and pitch behaviors are each chosen independently from a set of modes (static, offset, random, jitter, spin for yaw; static, offset, random for pitch). It uses the standard silent rotation system so the visual effect is sent to the server, and it can optionally avoid clamping the pitch or pause while you sprint.
useCases: Making it look as if you are confused or 'derping around' to other players for fun.
Spinning your head continuously (Spin yaw mode) as a visual gag.
Randomizing your view direction to obscure where you are actually looking.

settings.name: Yaw
settings.description: Selects how the horizontal (yaw) rotation is generated. Options are Static, Offset, Random, Jitter, and Spin. Default is Random.

settings.name: Yaw
settings.description: Child of the Static yaw mode. The fixed yaw angle to face, in degrees. Default 0, range -180 to 180.

settings.name: Offset
settings.description: Child of the Offset yaw mode. Angle in degrees added to your actual yaw to compute the sent yaw. Default 0, range -180 to 180.

settings.name: ForwardTicks
settings.description: Child of the Jitter yaw mode. Number of ticks the yaw stays facing your actual forward direction before jittering. Default 2, range 0 to 100 ticks.

settings.name: BackwardTicks
settings.description: Child of the Jitter yaw mode. Number of ticks the yaw is flipped 180 degrees (facing backward) during each jitter cycle. Default 2, range 0 to 100 ticks.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Child of the Spin yaw mode. Degrees the yaw advances each tick, producing continuous spinning. Default 50, range -70 to 70 degrees per tick; negative values spin the opposite direction.

settings.name: Pitch
settings.description: Selects how the vertical (pitch) rotation is generated. Options are Static, Offset, and Random. Default is Random.

settings.name: Pitch
settings.description: Child of the Static pitch mode. The fixed pitch angle, in degrees. Default -90 (looking straight up), range -180 to 180.

settings.name: Offset
settings.description: Child of the Offset pitch mode. Angle in degrees added to your actual pitch to compute the sent pitch. Default 0, range -180 to 180.

settings.name: SafePitch
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the resulting pitch is clamped to the normal -90 to 90 range so it stays within legal/realistic values; the Random pitch mode also only picks from -90 to 90. When disabled, pitch may go beyond normal limits (down to -180 / up to 180).

settings.name: NotDuringSprint
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the derp rotations are not applied while you are sprinting or holding the sprint key, so sprinting behaves normally. Disable to keep derping even while sprinting.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Shared rotation-engine configuration group used to smooth and send the derp rotations. Contains AngleSmooth (the smoothing mode that controls how quickly rotations move toward the target), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent, controlling how movement is corrected relative to the fake rotation), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1 to 180, the angular difference below which rotations are considered reached) and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks, how long before rotations reset back to normal).

modules.name: Disabler
modules.summary: Disabler bundles a collection of per-target sub-disablers, each crafted to defeat a specific anti-cheat or server (Grim, Vulcan, AAC, Verus, Hypixel, Mineland, Miniblox, CubeCraft and more). Each sub-disabler is an independent toggleable group that is off by default, so you enable only the one matching the server you are on. When the module is enabled (outside of auto-config loading) it prints an informational chat message. The individual disablers manipulate packets, sprinting, teleports and movement timing to disrupt the targeted anti-cheat's checks.
useCases: Enabling the matching sub-disabler (e.g. Hypixel or Verus) so other cheats can bypass that server's anti-cheat.
Disrupting a specific anti-cheat's movement or combat checks on the server you are playing on.

settings.name: GrimSpectate
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting Grim's spectate check (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: VulcanScaffold
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler aimed at Vulcan's scaffold checks (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: VulcanRiptide
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler aimed at Vulcan's riptide checks (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: AAC1.9.10
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting AdvancedAntiCheat 1.9.10 (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: SpigotSpam
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler that abuses Spigot packet spam (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: VanillaSpeed
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler (off by default) that splits movement into many extra move packets to gain speed. Child setting PacketType: enum choosing the move packet variant, default ON_GROUND_ONLY (alternative POSITION_AND_ON_GROUND; rotating packets are noted as not working). Child setting DistancePerPacket: float, default 10, range 1 to 20, controlling how much travelled distance each extra packet represents (lower values send more packets per move).

settings.name: SwingOrder
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler that manipulates the arm-swing packet order (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: LiveOverflow
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting the LiveOverflow anti-cheat setup (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: MinelandFly
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler enabling flight bypass on Mineland (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: VerusCombat
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler (off by default) that ignores/falsifies transaction (ping) packets to bypass Verus combat checks. Child setting WaitUntilCombat: boolean, default true, which delays activating the bypass until you have actually attacked an entity, reducing detection risk before combat.

settings.name: VerusExperimental
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler (off by default) built by referencing Verus source, originally aimed at BlocksMC, that uses fake-lag/blink packet queuing and packet rewriting to evade checks. Child settings: WorldChangeWait (int, default 15000, range 0 to 30000 ms) how long to pause the bypass after changing worlds; DelayEndTime (int, default 14000, range 0 to 30000 ms) the flush/queue end timing for fake lag; DelayBeginTime (int, default 13800, range 0 to 30000 ms) the move-packet queue begin timing; Scaffold14E (boolean, default true) re-sends block-place packets with a centered hit result to bypass the scaffold 14E check. It contains two nested toggleable groups: NoAction (off by default) with child Sprinting (boolean, default true) that cancels sprint start/stop command packets; and VoidTP (off by default) with children VoidTPDelay (int, default 1000, range 0 to 30000 ms) the minimum delay between void-teleport attempts and WaitForGround (boolean, default true) which only performs the void teleport while on the ground.

settings.name: VerusScaffoldG
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting Verus's scaffold-G check (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: Hypixel
settings.description: Toggleable Hypixel motion disabler (off by default). Child setting NotWithStar: boolean, default true, which disables the bypass while a Nether Star is present in your hotbar (avoiding interference in modes where the star is used).

settings.name: HypixelScaffold
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting Hypixel's scaffold check (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: Miniblox
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting the Miniblox server's anti-cheat (off by default). Has no further child settings.

settings.name: CubeCraft
settings.description: Toggleable sub-disabler targeting the CubeCraft server's anti-cheat (off by default). Has no further child settings.

modules.name: DroneControl
modules.summary: DroneControl opens a dedicated control screen that lets you manually pick a target position and time bow shots like piloting a drone, while the client computes and applies the correct projectile launch angle for a fully-drawn bow (BOW_FULL_PULL trajectory) toward the chosen target. Each game tick it aims at the current target using the configurable rotation engine, holds the bow drawn, and releases the shot when you trigger it. Closing the module also closes its screen.
useCases: Precisely lobbing fully-charged bow shots at a manually selected target/position via the drone-style control screen.
Calculating and applying the exact bow launch angle so arrows land on a target without manual aiming.
Timing and releasing charged bow shots on command while the client maintains the firing rotation.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine value group controlling how the computed aim angle is applied to the player. It contains the AngleSmooth mode selection plus MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset described below.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Selects how rotations are smoothed toward the target angle (default Linear). Available modes are Linear, Sigmoid and Acceleration. Each mode has its own sub-settings (see below).

settings.name: HorizontalTurnSpeed
settings.description: Linear/Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 180-180, bounds 0-180 degrees). Maximum yaw (horizontal) turn speed per tick; a random value in the range is used when actively turning. Lower values make horizontal aiming slower and more human-like.

settings.name: VerticalTurnSpeed
settings.description: Linear/Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 180-180, bounds 0-180 degrees). Maximum pitch (vertical) turn speed per tick. Lower values slow vertical aiming.

settings.name: Steepness
settings.description: Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 10, range 0-20). Steepness of the sigmoid curve that scales turn speed by the remaining angle difference; higher values make the speed transition sharper.

settings.name: Midpoint
settings.description: Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 0.3, range 0-1). Midpoint of the sigmoid curve (relative to a 120-degree scale) where turn speed reaches half of its maximum.

settings.name: YawAcceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth child (default 20-25, bounds 1-180). Per-tick yaw acceleration range applied when accelerating the turn toward the target.

settings.name: PitchAcceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth child (default 20-25, bounds 1-180). Per-tick pitch acceleration range applied when turning.

settings.name: DynamicAccel
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, acceleration is adjusted by distance to the target and uses separate crosshair acceleration values when looking at the target.

settings.name: CoefDistance
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default -1.393, range -2 to 2). Coefficient multiplied by target distance to add a distance-based offset to the acceleration range.

settings.name: YawCrosshairAccel
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default 17-20, bounds 1-180). Yaw acceleration used when DynamicAccel is on and the crosshair is already on the target.

settings.name: PitchCrosshairAccel
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default 17-20, bounds 1-180). Pitch acceleration used when DynamicAccel is on and the crosshair is already on the target.

settings.name: AccelerationError
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default enabled). When enabled, adds randomized error proportional to the computed acceleration to make rotations look less robotic.

settings.name: YawAccelError
settings.description: AccelerationError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of yaw error applied proportionally to acceleration.

settings.name: PitchAccelError
settings.description: AccelerationError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of pitch error applied proportionally to acceleration.

settings.name: ConstantError
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default enabled). When enabled, adds a fixed randomized error to each turn regardless of acceleration.

settings.name: YawConstantError
settings.description: ConstantError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of the constant yaw error added each tick.

settings.name: PitchConstantError
settings.description: ConstantError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of the constant pitch error added each tick.

settings.name: SigmoidDeceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, applies a sigmoid-based deceleration factor as the rotation nears the target, slowing the approach.

settings.name: Steepness
settings.description: SigmoidDeceleration child (default 10, range 0-20). Steepness of the deceleration sigmoid curve.

settings.name: Midpoint
settings.description: SigmoidDeceleration child (default 0.3, range 0-1). Midpoint of the deceleration sigmoid curve.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Rotations child (default Silent). Controls how the applied rotation interacts with movement input, e.g. silent rotations versus moving relative to the rotation.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Rotations child (default 2, range 1-180 degrees). Angle threshold below which the rotation is considered reached, allowing the rotation to reset.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Rotations child (default 5, range 1-30 ticks). Number of ticks after the target is reached before the rotation resets back to normal movement.

modules.name: Dupe
modules.summary: Dupe attempts to duplicate items by exploiting a known server-side bug, selecting an exploit implementation from the Exploit choice list. It refuses to run in singleplayer or while in creative mode, printing an error chat message instead. The currently bundled exploit (Paper-1.20.4) abuses an oversized book-edit packet on Paper 1.20.4 through 1.21.1: it requires a Writable Book in your hotbar, throws out all other items, then sends a crafted book edit. The module disables itself on quit, does not auto-activate, and is excluded from auto configs because dupes are rare and situational.
useCases: Duplicating valuable items on a vulnerable Paper 1.20.4-1.21.1 server that has not patched the book-edit dupe.
Testing whether a server is susceptible to the Paper book dupe exploit.

settings.name: Exploit
settings.description: Selects which dupe exploit implementation to use. Only one option is currently available, Paper-1.20.4, which performs the Paper 1.20.4-1.21.1 book-edit duplication. The active exploit is run when the module is enabled.

modules.name: Eagle
modules.summary: Eagle (also called FastBridge, BridgeAssistant or LegitScaffold) is a legit bridging assistant that automatically sneaks when you approach the edge of a block, letting you bridge/build over gaps faster and more safely without falling. It only triggers when you are close to an edge (within a randomized edge distance) and not flying, and it can be gated behind movement/look conditions so it only activates when you are actually bridging. It transparently overrides your sneak input, and re-randomizes the edge distance between uses for a more human-like pattern.
useCases: Safely bridge across voids in SkyWars/BedWars without manually timing your sneak at each block edge.
Restrict auto-sneak to only when you are holding blocks and moving forward, so it does not interfere with normal walking.
Limit eagle behavior to a specific look-pitch range so it only kicks in while you are looking down to bridge.

settings.name: EdgeDistance
settings.description: Random distance (in blocks, range 0.01..1.3) from a block edge at which auto-sneak engages; a value is picked from this range and refreshed after each sneak cycle. Larger values sneak earlier/farther from the edge. Default: 0.4..0.6.

settings.name: Conditional
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that restricts when eagle is allowed to sneak. When disabled, eagle always applies its edge logic; when enabled, the Conditions and Pitch sub-settings must be satisfied. Contains the child settings below.

settings.name: Conditions
settings.description: Child of Conditional. The movement/state conditions that must all be met for eagle to act. Options: Left, Right, Forwards, Backwards (directional input), HoldingBlocks (a placeable block in main or off hand), OnGround, Sneak (you are pressing sneak). Default: OnGround. Selecting Sneak also makes eagle take over sneak control (capture) behavior.

settings.name: Pitch
settings.description: Child of Conditional. Allowed look-pitch range (range -90..90); eagle only activates while your vertical look angle falls within it. Default: -90..90 (any pitch).

modules.name: EasyPearl
modules.summary: EasyPearl helps you throw ender pearls exactly where you are looking. When you hold an ender pearl and press the use key, it calculates the projectile angle needed to land the pearl at the block you are aiming at, rotates the server-side view to that angle, and then throws the pearl once the rotation is aligned. It renders a colored box highlight on the targeted block (green when the spot is reachable, red when it is not). If ReachableCheck is on and you aim at a block that is out of pearl range, it cancels the throw and warns you in chat.
useCases: Pearl precisely onto a distant block, ledge, or rooftop without manually guessing the throw arc.
Avoid wasting pearls by getting a chat warning and highlight feedback when a target spot is out of reach.
Quickly escape or reposition in PvP by aiming at a safe landing spot and letting the module handle the throwing angle.

settings.name: AimOffThreshold
settings.description: Maximum allowed angular difference (in degrees) between your current server rotation and the calculated pearl-throw rotation before the module considers the aim 'done' and releases the pearl. Lower values demand more precise alignment before throwing; higher values throw sooner with looser aim. Default 2, range 0.5 to 10.

settings.name: ReachableCheck
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the module verifies the targeted block is within pearl throwing range before throwing. If you are looking at a block that is too far to reach (and the look is not a miss), the throw is cancelled and a 'not in reach' warning is shown in chat. Disabling it lets the throw attempt proceed regardless of reachability.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Value group configuring the dynamic rotation engine used to aim toward the pearl target. Contains the nested settings below (AngleSmooth, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold, TicksUntilReset).

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Chooses how rotation toward the pearl target is smoothed/animated. Available modes here are Linear, Sigmoid, and Acceleration (combat-specific modes are not included for this module). The selected mode controls how quickly and naturally the view turns toward the throw angle. Default is the first mode (Linear).

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Controls how your movement is reconciled with the silent rotation engine (e.g. keeping movement direction consistent with the server-side rotation). Default is SILENT for this module.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Angular distance (in degrees) at which the rotation is considered far enough off-target to allow resetting back to the player's normal view. Default 2, range 1 to 180.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Number of ticks the rotation stays locked toward the target before it is allowed to reset to the player's real look direction. Default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks.

modules.name: ElytraFly
modules.summary: Makes elytra gliding far easier to control by letting you steer, set custom speeds, start/stop flight instantly and optionally avoid using durability. While wearing an elytra (and not in creative, not affected by Levitation, not riding a vehicle, and the elytra not about to break) it can auto-start fall-flying when you jump and auto-stop when you sneak on the ground. It offers several flight modes (Static, Vanilla, Boost, Firework, Pitch40Infinite) each with their own physics, plus a shared speed control and a durability exploit that rapidly re-starts gliding to avoid wearing out the elytra.
useCases: Flying smoothly and controllably with an elytra without needing fireworks, using custom vertical/horizontal speeds.
Preserving elytra durability indefinitely with the DurabilityExploit or Pitch40Infinite mode.
Auto-launching into flight on jump and instantly stopping on sneak for quick takeoffs and landings.

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: Selects which instant transitions are active. 'Start' makes the player begin fall-flying immediately when jumping in the air with vertical motion; 'Stop' makes the player instantly stop gliding when sneaking while on the ground. Default selection is Stop only.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Toggle for the Speed value group (enabled by default). When enabled, the module overrides flight speed using the Vertical and Horizontal values; when disabled, flight uses the active mode's default movement without the custom speed override.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Vertical flight speed applied when holding jump (up) or sneak (down) while the Speed group is enabled. Default 0.5, range 0.0 to 5.0. Higher values climb/descend faster.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Horizontal strafing speed applied while moving and the Speed group is enabled. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 8.0. Higher values fly forward faster.

settings.name: NotInFluid
settings.description: When enabled (default false), the module forces you to stop fall-flying while you are in liquid, preventing elytra flight underwater.

settings.name: DurabilityExploit
settings.description: When enabled (default false), repeatedly re-sends the start-fall-flying action so the player constantly switches between falling and gliding, which avoids consuming elytra durability. Some anti-cheats detect this when moving.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the active ElytraFly flight algorithm. Options: Static (default), Vanilla, Boost, Firework, Pitch40Infinite. Each mode changes how speed, lift and direction are computed.

settings.name: DurabilityExploitNotWhileNoMove
settings.description: Static mode option (default false). When enabled, the durability exploit only runs while the player is not moving, which can avoid detection by anti-cheats that only flag the exploit during movement.

settings.name: Glide
settings.description: Static mode toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled, adds a slow constant glide effect while you are not actively moving, which can prevent 'flying is not enabled' kicks on some servers.

settings.name: Vertical (Glide)
settings.description: Static mode Glide group: downward glide speed applied while idling and gliding. Default 0.01, range 0.0 to 1.0. Higher values descend faster during the glide.

settings.name: Horizontal (Glide)
settings.description: Static mode Glide group: horizontal glide speed applied along the current movement direction while idling. Default 0.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Speed (Boost)
settings.description: Boost mode: target maximum boost acceleration / top speed factor. Default 0.9, range 0.5 to 2.0. Higher values reach a higher boosted flight speed.

settings.name: Acceleration
settings.description: Boost mode: how quickly the boost ramps up toward the Speed target (and how fast it decays). Default 0.01, range 0.005 to 0.05. Higher values accelerate more aggressively.

settings.name: AutoBoost
settings.description: Boost mode (default true). When enabled, automatically boosts when looking sufficiently upward (pitch below about -10) and not near the ground, without needing to hold jump.

settings.name: VerticalControl
settings.description: Boost mode: scales how much vertical speed is applied when holding jump/sneak. Default 0.8, range 0.2 to 1.0. Higher values give stronger climb/descent control.

settings.name: SmartGroundBehavior
settings.description: Boost mode (default true). When enabled, detects nearby ground below and adjusts flight (boosts horizontal speed, reduces vertical) to avoid crashing into the ground; when disabled, no ground proximity adjustments are made.

settings.name: GroundDistance
settings.description: Boost mode: how far below the player (in blocks) the ground check looks when SmartGroundBehavior is on. Default 3.0, range 1.5 to 7.0. Larger values react to the ground from further away.

settings.name: DiveMechanics
settings.description: Boost mode (default true). When enabled, looking down builds up dive speed and pulling back up converts it into a forward/upward boost, emulating real elytra dive momentum.

settings.name: DiveAcceleration
settings.description: Boost mode: how quickly dive speed builds up while looking downward. Default 0.05, range 0.01 to 0.1. Higher values gain dive speed faster.

settings.name: DiveEfficiency
settings.description: Boost mode: how efficiently accumulated dive speed converts into a pull-up boost when leveling out or looking up. Default 0.8, range 0.4 to 1.5. Higher values give a stronger pull-up boost.

settings.name: ConsiderInventory
settings.description: Firework mode toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled, the module may pull firework rockets from the main inventory (not just hotbar/offhand) using the configured inventory constraints; when disabled, only hotbar and offhand slots are searched.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Firework mode ConsiderInventory constraints: random tick delay before starting an inventory action. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Firework mode ConsiderInventory constraints: random tick delay between inventory clicks. Default 2..4 ticks, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Firework mode ConsiderInventory constraints: random tick delay before closing the inventory. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Firework mode ConsiderInventory constraints: chance (percent) to deliberately misclick a slot to look more human. Default 0..0, range 0 to 100.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Firework mode ConsiderInventory constraints: conditions that must be met before inventory actions run, chosen from NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat and InventoryOpen. Default none selected.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Firework mode: tick delay between automatic firework uses, chosen randomly from this range. Default 20..20, range 0 to 300 ticks.

settings.name: MinSpeed
settings.description: Pitch40Infinite mode: speed (in km/h) below which the pitch oscillation flips to climbing. Default 25, range 10 to 70.

settings.name: MaxSpeed
settings.description: Pitch40Infinite mode: speed (in km/h) above which the pitch oscillation flips to diving. Default 150, range 50 to 170.

settings.name: MaxHeight
settings.description: Pitch40Infinite mode: altitude at or above which the mode forces a climb to maintain infinite flight. Default 200, range 50 to 360. A warning is shown when flying below this height.

settings.name: PitchIncrement
settings.description: Pitch40Infinite mode: how many degrees the pitch is adjusted each tick (clamped between -40 and 40) to alternate diving and climbing. Default 3, range 1 to 10.

modules.name: ElytraRecast
modules.summary: ElytraRecast automatically re-triggers elytra flight (fall flying) while you hold the jump key. It only fires when conditions are valid: you are not creative-flying, not riding an entity, not on a climbable block, not in water, not under Levitation, are wearing an elytra that will not break from the next damage, and the jump key is held. When those conditions are met it sends the server the start-fall-flying action so flight resumes.
useCases: Quickly restart elytra gliding after touching the ground or stalling, just by holding jump.
Maintain continuous elytra flight during travel without manually re-deploying the elytra each time.

modules.name: ElytraSwap
modules.summary: ElytraSwap quickly swaps the item in your chestplate slot between a chestplate and an elytra (and vice versa) using a scheduled sequence of inventory clicks. When enabled it searches your hotbar, main inventory, and offhand: if the chest slot is empty it equips an elytra, if you are wearing an elytra it swaps in a found chestplate, and if you are wearing a chestplate it swaps in a found elytra. It only acts once and then disables itself automatically, and it also disables when you leave the world.
useCases: Instantly put on an elytra to take off, then swap back to a chestplate for combat with a single toggle.
Bind it to a key to react quickly during PvP or movement situations where you need to switch between flight and protection.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Random delay (range of ticks) waited before beginning the swap click sequence. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0..20. Inherited from the inventory Constraints group.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Random delay (range of ticks) between individual inventory clicks during the swap. Default 2..4 ticks, range 0..20. Inherited from Constraints.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Random delay (range of ticks) waited before closing the inventory after the swap. Default 1..2 ticks, range 0..20. Inherited from Constraints.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Chance (percentage range) to intentionally perform a 'miss' click to mimic human behavior. Default 0..0 (no misses), range 0..100. Inherited from Constraints.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be satisfied before the swap inventory actions run. Options include NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, and InventoryOpen (the player-inventory variant allows requiring the inventory to be open). Defaults to none selected. Enabling these makes the swap wait until the chosen conditions are met.

modules.name: ElytraTarget
modules.summary: ElytraTarget makes you follow and chase a combat target while gliding with an Elytra, and is designed to work together with KillAura. It only operates while you are fall-flying: it selects the first valid line-of-sight target, rotates toward it with fast adaptive aim, optionally auto-fires fireworks to keep speed, and can nudge you upward to avoid collisions. It resets its target when disabled.
useCases: Chase down a flying or fleeing player while gliding on an Elytra and stay locked onto them.
Maintain elytra speed automatically during a chase by auto-using fireworks.
Pair with KillAura so you keep attacking a target while flying after it.

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Part of the Target sub-group (TargetTracker). Maximum angle (degrees) between your crosshair and an entity for it to be a valid target. Default 180 (any direction), range 0..180.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Part of the Target sub-group. Only targets whose hurtTime is at or below this value are considered. Default 10, range 0..10.

settings.name: Priority
settings.description: Part of the Target sub-group. Ordered set of criteria used to sort/choose the best target. Defaults to Type plus Health. Available: Type (players first), Health (lowest first), Distance (closest first), Direction (closest to crosshair), HurtTime (lowest first), Age (oldest first). Cannot be empty.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that draws a visual indicator on the current target. Contains the Mode appearance selector and its per-appearance options.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Target-rendering appearance. Default index 3 (GlowingCircle). World appearances: Legacy, Circle, Image, GlowingCircle, Ghost, Hearts; GUI appearances: Text2D, Arrow. Each exposes its own settings (colors, sizes, height mode, etc.).

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Ghost appearance color (default blue); also used as the base color in Legacy, Hearts, Text2D and Arrow appearances. Controls the tint of the chosen indicator.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Ghost particle size (default 0.5, range 0.4..0.7); also a size control in Legacy (0.5, 0.1..2), Hearts (0.15, 0.05..1) and Arrow (1.5, 0.5..20). Scales the rendered indicator.

settings.name: Length
settings.description: Ghost appearance: number of trailing particles/segments. Default 25, range 15..40.

settings.name: Height
settings.description: Legacy appearance box height. Default 0.1, range 0.02..2. Also the value used by the Relative height mode (default 0.5, range -0.5..1.5).

settings.name: ExtraYOffset
settings.description: Legacy appearance: extra vertical offset above the entity. Default 0.1, range 0..1.

settings.name: Source
settings.description: Image appearance texture source. Default index 0 (Custom). Choose Custom to supply your own texture or Builtin to use a bundled marker (Marker1/Marker2).

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Image appearance 2D scale (Vector2f), default (1,1). Stretches the marker image horizontally/vertically. (Text2D also has a Scale float, default 1, range 0.01..10.)

settings.name: ColorModulator
settings.description: Image appearance: color tint applied to the marker texture. Default white.

settings.name: Curve
settings.description: Image appearance Rotate animation curve mapping Progress (0..1) to Degrees (-180..180). Controls how the marker image rotates over time.

settings.name: HeightMode
settings.description: Used by Image, Circle, GlowingCircle and Text2D appearances. Determines the vertical placement of the indicator: Feet, Top, Relative, Health, or Animated, each with its own sub-options.

settings.name: Offset
settings.description: Feet height mode and Top height mode offset. Default 0, range -1..1. Adjusts the indicator height relative to the entity feet/top.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Animated height mode bobbing speed (default 0.18, range 0.01..1). Also the Hearts orbit speed (default 35, range -360..360 deg/s). Controls animation rate.

settings.name: HeightMultiplier
settings.description: Animated height mode: amplitude multiplier of the bobbing motion. Default 0.4, range 0.1..1.

settings.name: HeightOffset
settings.description: Animated height mode: base vertical offset of the bobbing motion. Default 1.3, range 0..2.

settings.name: GlowOffset
settings.description: Animated height mode: phase offset used for the glow height calculation. Default -1, range -3.1..3.1.

settings.name: Radius
settings.description: Circle and GlowingCircle outer radius. Default 0.85, range 0.1..2. Also Hearts orbit radius (default 0.5, range 0.1..1).

settings.name: InnerRadius
settings.description: Circle appearance inner radius for the gradient. Default 0, range 0..2; clamped to not exceed Radius.

settings.name: OuterColor
settings.description: Circle/GlowingCircle outer gradient color. Default LiquidBounce blue with alpha 100.

settings.name: InnerColor
settings.description: Circle appearance inner gradient color. Default LiquidBounce blue with alpha 100.

settings.name: Color (Circle/GlowingCircle outline)
settings.description: Circle and GlowingCircle outline color. Default opaque 0x007CFF (blue).

settings.name: GlowColor
settings.description: GlowingCircle glow color. Default LiquidBounce color with alpha 0 (transparent fade).

settings.name: GlowHeight
settings.description: GlowingCircle glow vertical extent (used unless the height mode provides its own glow height). Default 0.3, range -1..1.

settings.name: DynamicCount
settings.description: Hearts appearance. Default true. When enabled the number of hearts reflects the target's actual health; when disabled a fixed HeartCount is shown.

settings.name: HeartCount
settings.description: Hearts appearance: fixed number of hearts when DynamicCount is off. Default 10, range 1..32.

settings.name: YOffset
settings.description: Hearts appearance vertical offset. Default 0.1, range -1..3.

settings.name: SqueezeStrength
settings.description: Hearts orbit: how strongly hearts squeeze inward on damage. Default 0.25, range 0..1.

settings.name: SqueezeSpeed
settings.description: Hearts orbit: speed of the damage squeeze animation. Default 2, range 1..4.

settings.name: CanBeCovered
settings.description: Hearts appearance. Default false. When false hearts render without depth testing (always visible through blocks); when true they can be occluded by geometry.

settings.name: Scale (Text2D)
settings.description: Text2D appearance text scale. Default 1, range 0.01..10.

settings.name: Shadow
settings.description: Text2D appearance: whether the text is drawn with a drop shadow. Default true.

settings.name: Text
settings.description: Text2D appearance: list of text lines to display over the target. Default a single line 'TARGET'.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Arrow appearance outline color. Default transparent.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: ElytraRotationProcessor value group holding the aim/rotation settings used to look at the target. Contains Sharp, IgnoreKillAuraRotation, Look, AutoDistance, RotateAt and the Prediction sub-group.

settings.name: Sharp
settings.description: Rotations group. Default false. When enabled, rotation speed (yaw and pitch) is multiplied by 1.5 for sharper, snappier aiming.

settings.name: IgnoreKillAuraRotation
settings.description: Rotations group. Default true. When enabled, ElytraTarget's own fast rotations take precedence over KillAura's rotations so flying aim isn't fought by KillAura.

settings.name: Look
settings.description: Rotations group. Default false. When enabled, uses CHANGE_LOOK movement correction (your visible head actually turns); when disabled uses STRICT (silent) rotation.

settings.name: AutoDistance
settings.description: Rotations group. Default true. When enabled, automatically adjusts the aim point to keep an ideal distance (about 10 blocks) from the target while chasing.

settings.name: RotateAt
settings.description: Rotations group. Which part of the target to aim at. Default Eyes. Determines the reference point used for rotation/prediction.

settings.name: Prediction
settings.description: Toggleable Prediction sub-group of Rotations (default enabled). Predicts the target's future position so your aim leads a moving target. Contains Mode, GlidingOnly and Multiplier.

settings.name: Mode (Prediction)
settings.description: Prediction group. Default Simple (extrapolate along velocity). WithGravity additionally accounts for gravity drop in the prediction.

settings.name: GlidingOnly
settings.description: Prediction group. Default true. When enabled, movement prediction is applied only when the target is fall-flying (gliding); otherwise the raw position is used.

settings.name: Multiplier
settings.description: Prediction group. Float range scaling how far ahead the target's motion is projected. Default 1.8..2.0, range 0.5..3.0. A random value in the range is used per calculation; higher leads the target more.

settings.name: AutoFirework
settings.description: Toggleable AutoFirework sub-group (default enabled). Automatically uses firework rockets to maintain elytra speed while chasing. Only active when a target exists. Contains UseMode, ExtraDistance, SlotResetDelay, SyncCooldownWithKillAura and Cooldown.

settings.name: UseMode
settings.description: AutoFirework group. How fireworks are used. Default Normal (swap to the slot and use it). Packet sends a use-item packet directly (optionally switching held slot silently).

settings.name: ExtraDistance
settings.description: AutoFirework group. Distance threshold (meters) beyond which the longer cooldown is used; within it the shorter cooldown is used to fire more often. Default 50, range 5..100 (m).

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: AutoFirework group. Ticks to wait before switching the held slot back after using a firework. Default 0..0, range 0..20 ticks (random value per use).

settings.name: SyncCooldownWithKillAura
settings.description: AutoFirework group. Default false. When enabled, firework usage is timed around KillAura's attack ticks so it doesn't interfere with KillAura clicks.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: AutoFirework group. Tick cooldown range between firework uses. Default 8..10, range 1..50 ticks. The first value is used when close to the target and the last value when farther than ExtraDistance.

settings.name: Safe
settings.description: Module-level. Default true. When enabled, if your predicted movement would collide with the world the module pushes you slightly upward (0.1 blocks) to avoid crashing into blocks while gliding.

settings.name: AlwaysGlide
settings.description: Module-level. Default false. When enabled (and a target exists, the module is running, and you are not in flying mode), allows continuous gliding behavior toward the target.

modules.name: EntityControl
modules.summary: Lets you steer rideable entities (such as pigs, horses or other mounts) even without a saddle, and can enforce client-side assumptions about the mount. Through its Enforce option it can make the client treat the mount as saddled and/or apply a jump-strength value, enabling control the server would normally restrict. The module exposes a single multi-select option and otherwise has no other settings.
useCases: Riding and directing a mount that has no saddle equipped.
Forcing jump strength so a ridden entity can jump when it normally would not.

settings.name: Enforce
settings.description: Multi-select of client-side enforcements for ridden entities. 'Saddled' makes the client treat the mount as if it has a saddle so you can control it; 'JumpStrength' enforces a jump-strength value so the mount can jump. Both are off by default; enable the ones you need.

modules.name: ESP
modules.summary: ESP highlights living entities so you can see targets through walls. It offers several render modes (Glow, Box, 2D, Legacy2D) and a configurable color system that can tint entities by distance, health, a static color, or a rainbow, with special colors for invisible players and friends. Entities are only rendered up to a configurable maximum distance, and hurt entities flash red.
useCases: Track players and mobs through walls and terrain in combat or exploration.
Quickly distinguish friends (green), invisible players (orange), and damaged targets (red) at a glance.
Use the 2D mode with a health bar to monitor opponents' remaining health during fights.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the ESP render style. Options: Box (3D bounding box), 2D (screen-space rectangle with outline/health bar), Legacy2D (old-style flat marker), and Glow (entity glow outline). Default is Glow. Glow requires true sight to render entities through walls.

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: Selects how entity colors are computed. Options: Distance (HSB color from distance), Health (red-to-green by health), Static (fixed color), Rainbow (animated rainbow). Default is the first option, Distance.

settings.name: Saturation
settings.description: Distance color mode: HSB saturation of the computed color. Default 1.0, range 0 to 1. Lower values wash the color toward gray.

settings.name: Brightness
settings.description: Distance color mode: HSB brightness of the computed color. Default 1.0, range 0 to 1. Lower values darken the color.

settings.name: Hue
settings.description: Distance color mode: a curve mapping entity distance (0 to 200) to hue (0 to 360 degrees). Default points (0,0), (100,120), (200,120). Lets you control which color represents near vs far entities.

settings.name: Alpha
settings.description: Distance color mode: opacity of the color, 0 to 1, default 1.0. (Only present because this color mode is used without a fixed alpha here.)

settings.name: Alpha
settings.description: Health color mode: opacity of the health-based color, 0 to 255, default 255.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Static color mode: the fixed color applied to all entities. Default white with alpha 100.

settings.name: Invisible
settings.description: Color used to highlight invisible entities. Default orange. Invisible entities are always shown in this color regardless of the color mode.

settings.name: Friends
settings.description: Color used to highlight players recognized as friends. Default green. Only applied when its alpha is greater than 0; otherwise friends fall through to the normal color logic.

settings.name: MaximumDistance
settings.description: The maximum distance (in blocks) at which entities are rendered by ESP. Default 128, range 1 to 512. Entities farther than this are not drawn.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Box mode: whether to draw an outline around each 3D box in addition to the filled box. Default true.

settings.name: MergeIntersecting
settings.description: Box mode: if true, overlapping entity boxes are merged into combined shapes. Default false.

settings.name: Expand
settings.description: Box-based modes (Box and 2D): how much to inflate each entity's bounding box, in blocks. Default 0.05, range 0 to 0.5. Larger values make boxes slightly bigger than the entity.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: 2D mode: toggleable group enabling the colored outline around the screen-space rectangle. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Thickness
settings.description: 2D mode > Outline: line thickness of the rectangle outline, in pixels. Default 1, range 1 to 9.

settings.name: Corner
settings.description: 2D mode: toggleable group that, when enabled, draws only the corners of the rectangle instead of full edges. Disabled by default.

settings.name: Gap
settings.description: 2D mode > Corner: percentage of each edge left empty in the middle when corner mode is on. Default 50, range 1 to 100 (percent). Higher values leave smaller corner brackets.

settings.name: Border
settings.description: 2D mode: toggleable group that draws a black border/shadow around the outline and health bar for contrast. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Thickness
settings.description: 2D mode > Border: thickness of the black border drawn around the outline, in pixels. Default 1, range 1 to 9.

settings.name: Fill
settings.description: 2D mode: whether to fill the rectangle with a translucent version of the entity color. Default true.

settings.name: HealthBar
settings.description: 2D mode: toggleable group that draws a vertical health bar beside each entity, colored red-to-green by remaining health. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Spacing
settings.description: 2D mode > HealthBar: horizontal spacing between the health bar and the entity rectangle, in pixels. Default 2, range 0 to 32.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Legacy2D mode: scale of the flat marker drawn at the entity. Default 0.1, range 0.02 to 0.3.

settings.name: YOffset
settings.description: Legacy2D mode: vertical offset applied to the marker's position, in blocks. Default 0, range -1 to 1.

settings.name: BackgroundAlpha
settings.description: Legacy2D mode: opacity of the marker's black background. Default 150, range 0 to 255.

modules.name: ExtendedFirework
modules.summary: Extends (amplifies) the velocity boost you receive while flying with elytra and using a firework rocket. When boosting, the module multiplies the rocket's added velocity by a configurable per-axis vector, letting you travel faster or further per firework. The effect is applied through a mixin hook on the firework rocket entity, so it only matters while you are actively gliding and boosting.
useCases: Travel long distances faster on a survival or anarchy server using elytra and fireworks.
Gain extra forward/vertical thrust per rocket to climb or cover ground with fewer fireworks.
Fine-tune your boost profile per axis with the Custom mode when the default feels too strong or too weak.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how the firework velocity multiplier is determined. Choose between 'Normal' (a fixed preset multiplier of x=0.1, y=1.65, z=0.5) and 'Custom' (a user-editable multiplier vector). Defaults to Normal.

settings.name: VelocityMultiplier
settings.description: Only available in the 'Custom' mode. A 3D vector (x, y, z) by which the firework's added boost velocity is multiplied. Higher values produce a stronger boost along that axis. Defaults to the Normal preset (0.1, 1.65, 0.5). The locate button is disabled for this value.

modules.name: Extinguish
modules.summary: Automatically extinguishes you when you catch fire by silently aiming at the ground and placing water from a water bucket, then it can pick the water back up with an empty bucket. It simulates your future positions to find a frame where you are on the ground before planning the water placement, rotates with normal-life priority, and respects a configurable cooldown between actions. It does nothing in dimensions where water evaporates (e.g. the Nether) and skips acting if you have Fire Resistance.
useCases: Surviving accidental fire (lava splash, flint and steel, fire aspect) in survival or PvP by instantly self-dousing with water.
Recovering your water bucket after extinguishing by automatically picking the placed water back up.
Avoiding fire damage during travel while keeping the water placement disabled during active combat (via NotDuringCombat).

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Minimum time, in seconds, to wait between extinguish placements. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 20.0. The timer is started after a successful placement before another extinguish can occur.

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: When true (default), the module will not place water (or pick it up) while you are considered in combat by the CombatManager, preventing it from interfering during fights.

settings.name: Pickup
settings.description: Toggle for the Pickup feature group (enabled by default). When enabled, after placing water the module will use an empty bucket to pick the water back up within the configured time window.

settings.name: PickupSpan
settings.description: Time window, in seconds, during which a previously placed water source is eligible to be picked back up. Default 0.1 to 10.0, range 0.0 to 20.0. The start bound is the earliest delay before pickup, the end bound is when the record expires.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Standard rotation engine value-group controlling how the silent aim toward the placement target behaves. Contains AngleSmooth (choices: Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1 to 180) for the angle difference under which rotations reset, and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks) for how long to hold a rotation before returning to normal.

modules.name: FakeLag
modules.summary: FakeLag holds back (blinks) your outgoing packets to simulate lag, making your character appear to teleport/rubberband on the enemy's screen and harder to hit. It flushes the held packets after a randomized delay, or immediately on certain triggers such as taking damage, knockback, explosions, attacks/interactions, or teleports. In Dynamic mode it only lags when an enemy is near and when your real position is not safer than your lagged position; in Constant mode it lags continuously. It integrates with AutoDodge (to evade arrows by flushing) and AutoShoot, and disables itself in water, while dead, in menus, or while consuming items.
useCases: Making yourself hard to hit in PvP by desyncing your position so enemies attack where you no longer are.
Dynamically lagging only when enemies are close and it is positionally advantageous, to reduce obvious rubberbanding.
Combining with AutoDodge so held packets can be flushed in a way that avoids incoming arrows.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Float distance range (default 2-5, bounds 0-10 blocks) used to detect a nearby enemy and to gather entities for the Dynamic-mode positional check. Lagging in Dynamic mode requires an enemy within this range.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Integer millisecond range (default 300-600, bounds 0-1000 ms) for how long outgoing packets are held before being flushed. A random value in the range is chosen each cycle; higher values produce more pronounced lag.

settings.name: RecoilTime
settings.description: Cooldown in milliseconds (default 250, range 0-1000) after a forced flush during which the module will not start holding packets again, preventing immediate re-lag after a flush trigger.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Lag behavior (default Dynamic). Constant: always queues/holds outgoing packets. Dynamic: only holds packets when an enemy is nearby and your held (server) position is not closer to enemies than your current position, and not while intersecting an enemy.

settings.name: FlushOn
settings.description: Set of packet categories that immediately flush the held queue (reset the lag) when sent. EntityInteract: interact/attack/spectator/swing packets. BlockInteract: use-item-on/sign-update packets. Action: player-action packets. Enabling a category makes those actions break the lag so they are not delayed.

modules.name: FastBreak
modules.summary: FastBreak lets you break blocks faster than vanilla by removing the destroy delay and forcing the block-break progress to complete once it passes a configurable threshold. Each game tick it zeroes the interaction destroy delay and, if your break progress exceeds BreakDamage, snaps it to fully broken. It can optionally only act when holding a mining tool, and offers an anti-cheat bypass mode aimed at Grim. When disabled, it restores the vanilla destroy delay.
useCases: Mining or clearing blocks more quickly in survival/creative-style play.
Breaking through obstacles faster during PvP or bridging on servers where it is tolerated.

settings.name: BreakDamage
settings.description: Break-progress threshold (default 0.8, range 0.1-1.0). Once your destroy progress on a block exceeds this fraction, the block is instantly set to fully broken. Lower values break sooner/faster but are more obvious; higher values are closer to vanilla.

settings.name: OnlyTool
settings.description: When true, FastBreak only speeds up breaking while a proper mining tool is in your main hand (default false). When false, it accelerates breaking with any held item.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Behavior mode selector (default None). None applies only the basic speed-up. AbortAnother is an anti-cheat bypass (tested against Grim 2.3.48) that, whenever a stop-destroy packet is sent, also sends an abort-destroy packet for the block directly above, helping evade certain break checks. Has no further sub-settings.

modules.name: FastExp
modules.summary: FastExp automatically repairs your Mending-enchanted armor (and the item in your other hand) by rapidly throwing experience bottles from your hotbar or offhand. It is a hold-to-activate module (active only while its bind is held) and disables itself when you quit. While an inventory screen is open it pauses throwing but keeps the repair process alive so you can refill bottles. With the NoWaste safeguard it estimates how many bottles are actually required to fully repair your gear and stops once that target is met, avoiding wasted XP.
useCases: Quickly top up the durability of Mending armor and tools mid-fight or between rounds without manually spamming experience bottles.
Maintain near-full gear on Kit-PvP or practice servers by holding the bind whenever you have spare experience bottles.
Repair only when truly needed (NoWaste) so you don't burn through your bottle stockpile after every couple of hits.

settings.name: Rotate
settings.description: Toggle for the Rotate group (default enabled). When on, the module rotates your view downward (pitch toward 90 degrees) before throwing bottles so the orbs spawn at your feet; when off, bottles are thrown at a fixed 90-degree pitch without changing your actual look rotation.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine sub-group used by the Rotate feature, controlling how the look-down rotation is applied. Children: MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent) selects how movement is corrected relative to the server rotation; ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1-180) the angular distance at which the rotation is considered to need resetting; TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1-30 ticks) how long the rotation is held before snapping back; AngleSmooth (choices) selects the smoothing algorithm (Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration) that controls how gradually the view turns.

settings.name: NoWaste
settings.description: Toggle for the NoWaste group (default enabled). When on, the module calculates how many experience bottles are needed to fully repair your Mending gear and only throws that many, preventing wasted experience; when off, it throws bottles continuously as long as a bottle is available.

settings.name: MinDurabilityToStartRepair
settings.description: Default 64, range 0-2048. Repairing only begins once at least one Mending item has remaining durability less than or equal to this value. Raising it makes the module start repairing sooner (at less damage); lowering it waits until gear is more damaged.

settings.name: MaxDurabilityToContinueRepair
settings.description: Default 85, range 1-100 (%). Once a repair cycle is underway, the module keeps throwing bottles to finish the job only while at least one item is still at or below this percentage of max durability. This prevents the module from restarting a full repair after just a few hits.

settings.name: ThrowMode
settings.description: Selects how fast bottles are thrown. Default is Normal. Normal mode throws roughly one bottle every few ticks; Fast mode throws multiple bottles per tick for much quicker repairs.

settings.name: TicksPerItem
settings.description: Setting of the Normal throw mode. Default 2.0-3.0, range 0.5-10.0 ticks. The randomized number of ticks to wait between each thrown bottle; the module throws one bottle per this many ticks. Lower values throw faster.

settings.name: ItemsPerTick
settings.description: Setting of the Fast throw mode. Default 3.0-5.0, range 0.5-16.0. The randomized number of bottles thrown each tick. Higher values repair faster but are more obvious.

settings.name: CombatPauseTime
settings.description: Default 0, range 0-40 ticks. How long combat (e.g. auto-attack modules) is paused for whenever the module throws bottles. 0 means combat is not paused.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Default 0..0, range 0-40 ticks. Randomized delay before the silently-selected hotbar slot is reset back after each bottle use. Higher values keep the bottle slot selected longer per throw.

modules.name: FastPlace
modules.summary: Removes or reduces the right-click use cooldown so you can place blocks and use projectile items much faster than vanilla allows. It hooks the item-use cooldown event and overrides the cooldown with a configurable (randomized) tick value, but only for the item categories you select and only after an optional start delay since you began holding the use key.
useCases: Placing blocks faster than the vanilla 4-tick cooldown when building or bridging.
Spamming projectile items (e.g. snowballs, eggs, ender pearls) at a higher rate.
Limiting the speed boost to only blocks or only projectiles, and adding a start delay so the first taps feel legitimate.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: The use cooldown (in ticks) that replaces the vanilla cooldown; a random value in this range is chosen each time. Default 0 to 0 (no cooldown, maximum speed), range 0 to 4 ticks. Higher values throttle the placement speed.

settings.name: ApplyTo
settings.description: Which item types the faster cooldown applies to. Options Projectiles (items implementing ProjectileItem) and Blocks (BlockItem). The override only triggers if the main-hand or off-hand item matches a selected category.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Time (in milliseconds) the use key must have been held before the faster cooldown kicks in. Default 0 (immediate), range 0 to 1000. Prevents the very first uses from being sped up.

modules.name: FastUse
modules.summary: FastUse (alias FastEat) speeds up item usage on legacy servers by manipulating the client tick/timer and sending extra movement packets so the server simulates the eating/using process faster. It offers three modes: Immediate (timer boost plus many use packets, then release), ItemUseTime (waits a configurable number of use ticks before bursting packets), and Crossbow (rapidly loads crossbows via offhand swaps). It only accelerates consumable items currently being used, and can be conditionally disabled in situations that would look suspicious.
useCases: Eat golden apples or food almost instantly during PvP on 1.8-style legacy servers.
Drink potions faster to recover health/effects without standing still as long.
Rapidly load and fire a crossbow using the Crossbow mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the acceleration strategy: Immediate (default), ItemUseTime, or Crossbow. Each mode has its own sub-settings.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Immediate mode: number of ticks to wait after starting to use the item before bursting packets. Default 0, range 0..10 ticks. The timer boost is reset after 1 + Delay ticks.

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: Immediate mode: client timer speed multiplier requested while using the item. Default 1.0 (no change), range 0.1..5.0. Higher values speed up the use animation/processing.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Immediate mode: number of movement packets sent per tick, i.e. how many times the server simulates the eating process each tick. Default 20, range 1..35 packets. Higher is faster but more detectable.

settings.name: ConsumeTime
settings.description: ItemUseTime mode: number of ticks the item must already have been used before the packet burst and release fire. Default 15, range 0..20. Lower finishes sooner.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: ItemUseTime mode: number of movement packets sent per tick once ConsumeTime is reached. Default 20, range 1..35 packets.

settings.name: TickCooldown
settings.description: Crossbow mode: interval in ticks between the offhand-swap reload cycles while holding a crossbow. Default 1, range 1..20. Acts every tick where tickCount is divisible by this value.

settings.name: Conditions
settings.description: Situations in which acceleration is disabled (if any condition is met, FastUse does not accelerate). Options: NotInTheAir (disable while not on ground), NotDuringMove (disable while moving), NotDuringRegeneration (disable while you have the Regeneration effect). Default: NotInTheAir selected.

settings.name: StopInput
settings.description: When enabled (default false), movement input is zeroed out while the use key is held, keeping you stationary during item use.

settings.name: PacketType
settings.description: The type of movement packet sent to simulate faster usage. Default FULL (position+rotation+onGround), which best mimics vanilla 1.17+ clients and tends to bypass timer checks. Other MovePacketType values send less data.

modules.name: FlagCheck
modules.summary: FlagCheck alerts you when the server appears to flag or correct your movement, helping detect anti-cheat reactions. It watches for server-sent position packets and classifies them as a lagback or, if the forced rotation change is large (>=90 degrees on yaw or pitch), a force-rotate, and can also alert on invalid attribute states (being alive with zero health or zero hunger). Alerts can be shown in chat and/or as notifications and include a running flag count. It can render a wireframe outline at the position the server set you back to, and can periodically reset the flag counter. The module is aliased as 'FlagDetect'.
useCases: Detecting when an anti-cheat lags you back or force-rotates your view so you can react.
Visually seeing where the server set your player back to via a wireframe outline.
Spotting invalid health/hunger states that may indicate desync or anti-cheat behavior.

settings.name: ChatMessage
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, flag alerts (lagback, force-rotate, invalid) are printed to chat.

settings.name: Notification
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, flag alerts are shown as pop-up notifications (INFO severity).

settings.name: InvalidAttributes
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, raises an 'invalid' alert each tick the player is alive but has health <= 0 and/or food level <= 0, listing the offending attribute(s).

settings.name: ResetFlags
settings.description: Toggleable group (default ON). When enabled, the running flag counter is automatically reset to zero on an interval.

settings.name: After
settings.description: Child of ResetFlags. Interval in seconds after which the flag count is reset to zero. Default 30, range 1..300.

settings.name: Render
settings.description: Toggleable group (default ON). When enabled, draws a wireframe player outline at the position/rotation the server set you back to when a flag occurs, fading out over time.

settings.name: NotInFirstPerson
