settings.description: Child of Render (default true). When enabled, the wireframe setback render is suppressed while in first-person camera view (only shown in third person).

settings.name: Alive
settings.description: Child of Render. Duration in milliseconds the wireframe is shown at full opacity before fading. Default 1000, range 0..3000.

settings.name: FadeOut
settings.description: Child of Render. Easing curve controlling how the wireframe fades out after the Alive duration. Default QUAD_OUT.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: Child of Render. Duration in milliseconds over which the wireframe fades out. Default 500, range 0..2000.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of Render. Fill color of the setback wireframe player. Default a darker red with alpha 100.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Outline color of the setback wireframe player. Default a darker red.

modules.name: Fly
modules.summary: Fly lets the player move freely through the air, ignoring normal gravity and movement constraints. It offers a large list of flight modes, ranging from generic ones (Vanilla, Creative, Jetpack, Enderpearl, AirWalk, Explosion, Fireball) to many anti-cheat- and server-specific bypasses (Vulcan, Grim, Spartan, Sentinel, Verus, NCP, Hypixel, Hycraft). It can optionally apply a visual stride effect for smoother movement animation and can automatically disable itself when the server sets the player back.
useCases: Flying around a map to scout or travel quickly when the server or game mode permits creative-style flight.
Bypassing a specific anti-cheat (e.g. Vulcan, Grim, Hypixel) by selecting the matching specialized fly mode.
Auto-disabling flight on setback detection to reduce the chance of repeated flags or kicks.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the active flight algorithm. Defaults to Vanilla. Available choices include generic modes (Vanilla, Creative, Jetpack, Enderpearl, AirWalk, Explosion, Fireball), anti-cheat-specific modes (Vulcan277, Vulcan286, Vulcan286MC18, Vulcan286Teleport, Grim2859V, Grim2373Jan15, Spartan524), and server/version-specific modes (Sentinel20thApr, Sentinel27thJan, Sentinel10thMar, Sentinel26thDec, VerusB3896Damage, VerusB3869Flat, NcpClip, Hypixel, HypixelFlat, HycraftDamage). Each mode tailors flight behavior to bypass a particular environment.

settings.name: Visuals
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling client-side flight visuals. When enabled its child settings apply.

settings.name: Stride
settings.description: Child of Visuals (default true). When on, applies a stride/walking animation force equal to the smaller of 0.1 and the player's current horizontal movement speed, making the flying animation look like normal walking instead of standing still.

settings.name: DisableOnSetback
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, Fly automatically turns itself off and shows a 'setback detected' error in chat the moment the server sends a position-correction (setback) packet, helping avoid getting dragged back or flagged repeatedly.

modules.name: FreeCam
modules.summary: FreeCam detaches the camera from the player so you can fly the view freely around the world while your body stays in place. Movement keys steer the camera (with jump/sneak moving it up/down), and it can optionally let you interact with blocks from the camera's perspective, navigate toward what the camera is looking at, and teleport the camera with a middle click. It automatically disables on world change and on quit, and can be configured to auto-cancel on events such as taking damage or moving. Rotation behavior while looking at targets is governed by the shared Rotations engine.
useCases: Scouting around corners, over walls, or behind your player without moving your real position.
Interacting with blocks that are behind walls or out of normal reach using the camera-interact feature.
Inspecting your surroundings or bases from angles your body cannot physically reach.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Movement speed multiplier of the free camera. Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 2.0; higher values move the camera faster per input tick.

settings.name: AllowCameraInteract
settings.description: Toggle for the camera-interaction sub-feature (a toggleable group, enabled by default). When on, raycasts/interactions originate from the camera position instead of the player, letting you interact with blocks behind the player or walls (similar to GhostBlock).

settings.name: LookAt
settings.description: Child of AllowCameraInteract (default true). When enabled, the player's rotation is aimed at the camera's crosshair target so interactions line up with where the camera is pointing.

settings.name: CancelOn
settings.description: Selects which events automatically disable FreeCam. Options: Damage (health decreases), Teleport (server position packet received), Move (horizontal player movement detected), Liquid (player is in liquid). Default selection is empty (no auto-cancel triggers); enabling entries makes FreeCam turn itself off when those conditions occur.

settings.name: Navigation
settings.description: Toggle for the Navigation sub-feature (disabled by default). When enabled and its hold key is pressed, the player walks toward the position the camera is looking at, using directional input and the auto-actions below.

settings.name: Auto
settings.description: Child of Navigation. Selects automatic movement assists while navigating: Jump (auto-jump on horizontal collision and allow auto-jump), Swim (auto-jump/swim while in water), Sprint (auto-sprint while moving). Default none selected.

settings.name: Key
settings.description: Child of Navigation. The key that must be held to make the player navigate toward the camera's look position. Default Left Control; if unset, navigation never activates.

settings.name: MidClickCameraTeleport
settings.description: When enabled (default false), pressing the middle mouse button teleports the free camera toward the block it is looking at (interpolated to 90% to avoid teleporting into a block).

settings.name: KeepSneaking
settings.description: When enabled (default false), forces the player to keep sneaking while FreeCam is active, so the body stays crouched even though sneak input is redirected to camera movement.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Shared rotation-engine value group controlling how the player's rotation is moved toward look/navigation targets. Contains: AngleSmooth (choices of smoothing modes: Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration; default the first mode), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent; how rotations interact with movement), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1-180 degrees; angle difference under which rotation resets), and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1-30 ticks; how long before rotation snaps back after target is gone).

modules.name: FreeLook
modules.summary: FreeLook lets you rotate the third-person camera independently of your character's facing direction. While the bind is held it switches to a third-person perspective and decouples mouse movement from your in-game rotation, so you can look around without turning your body. The module is bound as a hold action and disables itself on quit. Camera sensitivity can be boosted and the pitch (up/down) clamp can be removed for a full 360-degree free camera.
useCases: Look behind or around yourself while continuing to move and aim forward.
Get a free-rotating third-person camera for screenshots or scouting.
Spin the camera fully vertically by disabling the pitch limit.

settings.name: Perspective
settings.description: Which third-person perspective FreeLook uses while active: Back (default, camera behind the player) or Front (camera in front, which produces an inverted view). Front sets the view as inverted.

settings.name: SenseBoost
settings.description: Multiplier applied to mouse movement when rotating the free camera, default 1, range 0.1 to 2. Higher values make the camera turn faster relative to mouse movement.

settings.name: NoPitchLimit
settings.description: When enabled (default true), removes the vertical pitch clamp so the camera can rotate beyond straight up/down. When disabled, camera pitch is clamped between -90 and 90 degrees like the normal view.

modules.name: Freeze
modules.summary: Freeze halts your own movement and tick processing client-side while keeping (or selectively withholding) network communication, effectively acting like a timer-at-zero so the server does not register that you have stopped. It offers Stationary (freezes movement but keeps packets flowing, with rotation spoofing to bypass duplicate-rotation checks), Queue (queues outgoing/incoming packets like artificial lag), and Cancel (drops the selected packets entirely) modes. It can disable itself when the server sets your position back (a flag), optionally show a notification, and optionally 'balance' the missed ticks by fast-forwarding the player when disabled (rendering the predicted path while frozen). The module disables automatically when you quit.
useCases: Faking a freeze or lag-out in PvP so opponents misjudge your position while you remain in control.
Holding your client position without the server knowing you stopped, e.g. to set up a sudden move or pearl.
Building up queued/missed movement ticks and then 'warping' forward by releasing them when disabling.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the freeze technique. Default is Stationary. Options: Queue (queues the selected packets as fake lag), Cancel (drops the selected packets), Stationary (cancels only movement ticks while keeping network communication intact).

settings.name: DisableOnFlag
settings.description: When enabled, the module turns itself off if the server sends a position correction (ClientboundPlayerPositionPacket), i.e. when you get flagged/set back. Default true.

settings.name: Notification
settings.description: When enabled, shows an info notification when the module disables itself due to a server flag. Default false.

settings.name: BalanceWarp
settings.description: When enabled, on disable the module replays all the ticks that were withheld while frozen (fast-forwarding the player) to 'balance' the missed movement, and while frozen renders the predicted future path as a blue line. Default false.

settings.name: Origin
settings.description: Queue and Cancel modes only. Multi-select of which packet transfer direction is affected; for Queue the matching packets are queued, for Cancel they are dropped. Default includes Outgoing.

settings.name: CancelC0B
settings.description: Stationary mode only. When enabled, cancels outgoing Pong packets (C0B) to bypass Grim's BadPacketsR and Matrix7's timer check. Default true.

modules.name: Fucker
modules.summary: Fucker (aliases BedBreaker and IdNuker) automatically destroys or uses selected blocks around you, defaulting to beds and dragon eggs. It searches for target blocks in range, rotates toward them and breaks them, and can also tunnel through surrounding blocks to reach a protected target by computing the cheapest path of blocks to break. It integrates with PacketMine, AutoTool and KillAura priorities, can skip your own bed via the SelfBed detector, and renders the current target. An Entrance sub-feature treats targets that already have an opening as directly reachable (useful on Hypixel/CubeCraft).
useCases: Breaking enemy beds quickly in Bedwars (BedBreaker), including digging through obsidian/wool surroundings to reach them.
Destroying or using dragon eggs and other configured blocks automatically.
Auto-using selected interactable blocks when Action is set to Use.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum reach in blocks (default 5.0, range 1.0-6.0) for finding and breaking visible target blocks.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Maximum reach in blocks for targets behind walls / not directly visible (default 0.0, range 0.0-6.0). It is automatically clamped to never exceed Range. 0 disables through-wall breaking.

settings.name: Entrance
settings.description: Toggle (default off) for the Entrance sub-feature. When enabled, if a target block already has an open (non-occluded) side it is treated as reachable at full Range instead of WallRange, breaking it as if normally visible. Useful on Hypixel and CubeCraft.

settings.name: BreakFree
settings.description: Child of Entrance (default true). When the target has no entrance, breaks the weakest neighboring block of the target to open an entrance to it.

settings.name: Surroundings
settings.description: When true (default), the module will tunnel through surrounding blocks, computing the cheapest path of blocks to break in order to expose a protected target. When false, only directly reachable targets are broken.

settings.name: Targets
settings.description: The set of block types the module will target. Defaults to all beds (blocks ending in _BED) plus the dragon egg. Add or remove blocks to control what gets destroyed/used.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Delay in ticks (default 0, range 0-20) inserted when switching targets and after a Use action. Higher values slow down repeated actions and target switches.

settings.name: Action
settings.description: What to do with the target block (default Destroy). Destroy breaks the block; Use right-clicks/uses it (and swings the hand) instead of breaking.

settings.name: ForceImmediateBreak
settings.description: When true, forces the block to break immediately rather than via normal progressive breaking (default false). Only applies to the Destroy action.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: When true (default), continues targeting/breaking while a container screen is open and ignores the inventory for rotations. When false, it pauses while a container screen is open and considers the inventory when rotating.

settings.name: IgnoreUsingItem
settings.description: When true (default), keeps updating targets even while you are using an item (e.g. eating, drawing a bow). When false, it stops targeting while you are using an item.

settings.name: PrioritizeOverKillAura
settings.description: When true, Fucker's rotations take higher priority than KillAura's (default false), so breaking is favored over attacking. When false, KillAura keeps rotation priority.

settings.name: ChestAsFullBlock
settings.description: When true, treats chests as full cube blocks when computing surrounding break paths (default false). Useful so the pathing can target chest faces reliably even though chests have a smaller hitbox.

settings.name: SelfBed
settings.description: Mode selector that determines which beds are considered your own and therefore skipped (default None). Modes: None (treat no bed as self), Color (match bed color to your armor), SpawnLocation (beds near your tracked spawn point), Manual (manually tracked bed via keys).

settings.name: Slots
settings.description: Child of SelfBed Color mode (default Head; cannot be none). The armor slots whose dye color is compared against bed color to identify your own bed.

settings.name: Loose
settings.description: Child of SelfBed Color mode (default false). When true, matches armor color to the closest dye color rather than requiring an exact color match, making self-bed detection more lenient.

settings.name: BedDistance
settings.description: Child of SelfBed SpawnLocation mode (default 24.0, range 16.0-48.0). Beds within this distance of your tracked spawn location are treated as your own and skipped.

settings.name: Track
settings.description: Child of SelfBed Manual mode (default numpad +). Pressing this key tracks the nearest bed around you as your own bed.

settings.name: Untrack
settings.description: Child of SelfBed Manual mode (default numpad -). Pressing this key clears the manually tracked self-bed position.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Dynamic rotation engine sub-group used to aim at the target block. Contains AngleSmooth, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Selects how rotations are smoothed toward the target block (e.g. Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration). Smoother modes appear more human but turn more slowly.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: How player movement is reconciled with silent rotations (default Silent).

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Angular difference in degrees (default 2.0, range 1-180) at which the rotation is considered to have reached its target before resetting.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Ticks (default 5, range 1-30) the rotation stays on target before snapping back to normal aim.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggle (enabled by default) for rendering a box around the current target block (default color red, alpha 90). Contains the placement-renderer animation/color settings below.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering. When true, merges adjacent rendered boxes/culling for cleaner rendering.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default 1.0, range 0-2). Box size at the start of the fade-in animation.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default Linear). Easing curve applied to the start-size animation.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default 0.8, range 0-2). Box size at the end of the animation.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default Linear). Easing curve applied to the end-size animation.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default Linear). Easing curve for the box fade-in.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default Linear). Easing curve for the box fade-out.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default 500 ms, range 0-5000). Duration of the appear/fade-in animation.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering (default 500 ms, range 0-5000). Duration of the disappear/fade-out animation.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering. Fill color of the target box (default red, alpha 90).

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Child of TargetRendering. Outline color of the target box (default red, full alpha).

modules.name: FullBright
modules.summary: FullBright lets you see clearly in dark areas using one of two selectable modes. The Gamma mode gradually raises the game's brightness/gamma toward a configurable target each tick, while the NightVision mode continually applies the Night Vision status effect (and removes it when disabled). Only the chosen mode's behavior is active at a time.
useCases: Exploring caves, mineshafts, or the Nether without placing torches or fumbling in the dark.
Improving visibility at night or in dark structures during PvP or building.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the brightness method. Options: Gamma (default) which ramps up the in-game gamma toward a target, and NightVision which applies the Night Vision effect. Only one mode is active at a time.

settings.name: Brightness
settings.description: Child of the Gamma mode. The target gamma level the module ramps toward each tick (increments by 0.1 per tick until reached). Default 15, range 1 to 15; higher values produce a brighter, more washed-out but more visible scene.

modules.name: GhostHand
modules.summary: GhostHand lets you interact with certain blocks through walls and other obstructions, bypassing the normal line-of-sight requirement. It is restricted to a configurable set of container-type blocks rather than every block. In practice, you can open a chest or shulker box even when it is hidden behind another block.
useCases: Open chests, ender chests, or shulker boxes that are walled off or otherwise blocked from direct line of sight.
Access containers on servers with flawed reach/interaction checks without needing to break the blocks in front of them.

settings.name: TargetedBlocks
settings.description: The set of block types you are allowed to interact with through walls. Defaults to chests, ender chests, trapped chests, plain shulker boxes, and all dyed (colored) shulker box variants. Only blocks in this list will be reachable through obstructions; add or remove entries to control which containers GhostHand applies to.

modules.name: GUICloser
modules.summary: GUICloser automatically closes container GUIs (chests, shops, vote menus, etc.) whose title matches one of your configured patterns the instant the server tries to open them. When a container screen opens, its title is tested against your filter list using regular expressions; if it matches, the screen is prevented from appearing. This is useful for blocking spammy or unwanted server-side menus.
useCases: Block annoying vote or advertisement GUIs that servers force open on join.
Prevent specific shop or menu screens from interrupting you while playing.
Identify the exact titles of GUIs you want to block by enabling PrintScreenTitle and copying the printed title.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: How a filter pattern is compared against the container title. 'Matches' (default) requires the regex to match the entire title string, while 'Contains' closes the screen if the regex matches anywhere within the title.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: The list of regular expressions tested against container titles; any match closes the screen. Defaults to a single pattern '^Vote$'. Add patterns for the titles of GUIs you want to auto-close.

settings.name: PrintScreenTitle
settings.description: When enabled (default false), any container screen whose title does NOT match the filter prints its exact title to chat as a clickable/copyable message, so you can capture titles to add to the Filter list.

modules.name: HandDerp
modules.summary: HandDerp repeatedly switches your main hand (left/right handedness) by sending updated client-information packets to the server, making your held item appear to flip sides. Switching can be triggered either on a fixed tick delay or every time you swing your arm. An optional Silent mode cancels the server entity-data updates so the swap is hidden from how others see your held-item metadata. When the module is disabled it automatically restores your original main hand.
useCases: Making your held item rapidly flip between left and right hands as a visual gag.
Switching hands on every swing for an animated effect while attacking or using items.
Using Silent mode to change handedness without broadcasting the entity-data change.

settings.name: Silent
settings.description: When enabled (default false), incoming entity-data packets that reflect your main-hand setting are cancelled, hiding the hand swap from that metadata channel. When disabled the swaps are sent normally.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects what triggers a hand switch. Options are Delay (switch on a timer) and Swing (switch on each arm swing). Default is Delay.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Child of the Delay mode. Number of ticks to wait between each automatic hand switch. Default 1, range 0 to 20 ticks. Lower values switch faster.

modules.name: Hats
modules.summary: Hats renders a decorative cosmetic shape floating above the head of you and (optionally) your friends. You pick one of several visual modes (Cone, Halo, Orbs, Flower, Star, Image), each with its own shape, color and animation settings, and a shared height-offset animation controls how high the hat hovers and how it bobs over time. Each mode can react to damage by flashing red, follow the player's rotation, and be shown or hidden in first person.
useCases: Add a personalized cosmetic hat above your own head for style.
Display hats above friends so you can spot teammates at a glance.
Use the animated HeightOffset to make the hat gently bob up and down.

settings.name: HeightOffset
settings.description: An animated value group controlling how high above the head the hat floats over time. Combines the Height curve below with the Period and Symmetric timing settings to produce a looping vertical animation.

settings.name: Height
settings.description: A curve mapping animation Progress (0..1) to vertical Offset (0..2). Default control points keep a flat offset of about 0.2 (Vector2f(0,0.2) and Vector2f(1,0.2)); editing the curve changes how the hat's height varies across the animation cycle.

settings.name: Period
settings.description: Duration in milliseconds of one HeightOffset animation cycle (default 1000, range 10..20000). Larger values make the height animation slower.

settings.name: Symmetric
settings.description: When enabled (default), the height animation plays forward then back over a doubled period for a smooth ping-pong motion; when disabled it loops one-directionally over the period.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which hat shape is rendered. Options are Cone, Halo, Orbs, Flower, Star and Image (default Cone). Each mode exposes its own settings plus the shared per-mode options below.

settings.name: FollowRotation
settings.description: Shared per-mode option. When enabled, the hat rotates to follow the wearer's body/head rotation; disabled by default so the hat keeps a fixed world orientation.

settings.name: EquipmentOffset
settings.description: Shared per-mode value group holding the armor offset adjustment used when the wearer has a helmet equipped.

settings.name: ArmorOffset
settings.description: Shared per-mode option (inside EquipmentOffset). Additional vertical offset (default 0.1, range 0..1) applied to raise the hat when the wearer has a head/helmet item, so the hat does not clip into worn armor. Has no effect when no helmet is worn.

settings.name: ShowDamage
settings.description: Shared per-mode option (enabled by default). When on, the hat flashes red while the wearer is taking damage (hurt time active); when off the hat keeps its normal colors during damage.

settings.name: FriendsOptions
settings.description: Shared per-mode value group controlling whether and how far away hats are drawn on friends.

settings.name: ViewOnFriend
settings.description: Shared per-mode option (inside FriendsOptions, enabled by default). When enabled, hats are also rendered above players marked as friends; when disabled, only your own hat is shown.

settings.name: Distance
settings.description: Shared per-mode option (inside FriendsOptions). Maximum distance in blocks (default 64, range 8..512) within which friends' hats are rendered. Friends farther than this are not drawn.

settings.name: FirstPersonView
settings.description: Shared per-mode option (enabled by default). When enabled, your own hat is still rendered while you are in first-person view; when disabled it only appears in third person (or when FreeLook is active).

settings.name: HatSettings (Cone)
settings.description: Cone mode shape settings group containing the Peak height of the cone.

settings.name: Peak
settings.description: Cone mode. Height of the cone's tip above its base (default 0.3, range 0.01..2). Higher values make a taller, sharper cone.

settings.name: RadiusSettings
settings.description: Cone mode sub-group containing the cone's outer radius.

settings.name: OuterRadius
settings.description: Cone mode (inside RadiusSettings). Radius of the cone's circular base (default 0.6, range 0.1..2). Larger values widen the cone.

settings.name: Radius (Halo)
settings.description: Halo mode. Outer radius of the halo ring/torus (default 0.3, range 0.1..2). Larger values make a wider halo.

settings.name: Thickness (Halo)
settings.description: Halo mode. Tube thickness (inner radius) of the halo ring (default 0.05, range 0.01..1). Larger values make a fatter ring.

settings.name: color (Orbs)
settings.description: Orbs mode. Color of the orbiting orbs (default semi-transparent blue, RGBA 0,0,255,125). When the wearer is hurt the orbs flash red while keeping this color's alpha.

settings.name: Radius (Orbs)
settings.description: Orbs mode. Orbit radius of the orbs around the head (default 0.5, range 0..2). Larger values spread the orbs farther out.

settings.name: Speed (Orbs)
settings.description: Orbs mode. Speed at which the orbs travel around their orbit (default 0.5, range 0.1..10). Higher values spin the orbs faster.

settings.name: OrbsSize
settings.description: Orbs mode. Size of each individual orb (default 0.1, range 0.01..0.5). Larger values make bigger orbs.

settings.name: OrbsCount
settings.description: Orbs mode. Number of orbs in the ring (default 6, range 1..12).

settings.name: Wave
settings.description: Orbs mode toggleable sub-group (enabled by default). When enabled, the orbs bob up and down in a sine wave; when disabled they stay at a constant height.

settings.name: WaveHeight
settings.description: Orbs mode (inside Wave). Vertical amplitude of the orb wave motion (default 0.1, range 0.01..1). Larger values make orbs rise and fall more.

settings.name: WaveSpeed
settings.description: Orbs mode (inside Wave). Speed of the up/down wave oscillation (default 2.0, range 0.1..10). Higher values make the orbs bob faster.

settings.name: SpinSpeed (Orbs)
settings.description: Orbs mode. Rotation speed of each orb's own rhombus shape (default 2, range -10..10). Negative values reverse the spin direction; 0 disables spinning.

settings.name: HatSettings (Flower)
settings.description: Flower mode shape settings group containing radius, thickness, sharpness, petal count and spin speed.

settings.name: Radius (Flower)
settings.description: Flower mode. Outer radius of the flower (default 0.3, range 0.1..2). Larger values make a bigger flower.

settings.name: Thickness (Flower)
settings.description: Flower mode. Tube thickness of the flower outline (default 0.05, range 0.01..1). Larger values make thicker petals.

settings.name: Sharpness (Flower)
settings.description: Flower mode. Controls how pronounced/pointed the petals are (default 0.6, range 0.1..0.9). Lower values produce sharper, more defined petals.

settings.name: PetalCount
settings.description: Flower mode. Number of petals on the flower (default 5, range 5..15).

settings.name: SpinSpeed (Flower)
settings.description: Flower mode. Rotation speed of the whole flower (default 1, range -10..10). Negative values spin the other way; 0 keeps it still.

settings.name: HatSettings (Star)
settings.description: Star mode shape settings group containing radius, thickness, sharpness, points count and spin speed.

settings.name: Radius (Star)
settings.description: Star mode. Outer radius of the star (default 0.3, range 0.1..2). Larger values make a bigger star.

settings.name: Thickness (Star)
settings.description: Star mode. Tube thickness of the star outline (default 0.05, range 0.01..1). Larger values make thicker arms.

settings.name: Sharpness (Star)
settings.description: Star mode. Controls how pointed the star's arms are (default 0.6, range 0.1..0.7). Affects how deep the notches between points cut in.

settings.name: PointsCount
settings.description: Star mode. Number of points on the star (default 5, range 5..15).

settings.name: SpinSpeed (Star)
settings.description: Star mode. Rotation speed of the whole star (default 1, range -10..10). Negative values reverse spin direction; 0 disables spinning.

settings.name: Image
settings.description: Image mode. A file picker for the texture/image used as the hat (errors loading the file are printed to chat). The selected image is drawn as a flat textured quad above the head.

settings.name: ColorModulator
settings.description: Image mode. Color tint multiplied onto the image (default white = no tint). Use this to recolor or fade (via alpha) the image hat.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Image mode. A 2D scale (X,Y) applied to the image quad (default 1,1). Increasing a component stretches the image along that axis.

settings.name: SpinSpeed (Image)
settings.description: Image mode. Rotation speed of the image around its vertical axis (default 1, range -10..10). Negative values reverse direction; 0 keeps it static.

settings.name: Colors
settings.description: Shared color group used by the Cone, Halo, Flower and Star modes (not Orbs or Image). Holds SyncColors, FirstColor, SecondColor and a SpinSpeed that animates a color gradient around the shape.

settings.name: SyncColors
settings.description: Inside Colors (Cone/Halo/Flower/Star). When enabled (default), only FirstColor is used for the whole shape; when disabled, the shape blends between FirstColor and SecondColor.

settings.name: FirstColor
settings.description: Inside Colors (Cone/Halo/Flower/Star). Primary color of the hat (default semi-transparent blue, RGBA 0,0,255,125). Its alpha is also used for the red flash when ShowDamage triggers.

settings.name: SecondColor
settings.description: Inside Colors (Cone/Halo/Flower/Star). Secondary color blended with FirstColor when SyncColors is disabled (default semi-transparent blue, RGBA 0,0,255,125). Ignored while SyncColors is on.

settings.name: SpinSpeed (Colors)
settings.description: Inside Colors (Cone/Halo/Flower/Star). Speed at which the color gradient animates around the shape over time (default 1, range 0..10). 0 freezes the gradient in place.

modules.name: HighJump
modules.summary: HighJump increases the upward velocity applied when you jump, letting you reach greater heights than vanilla. The jump strength is controlled by a single Motion value, and a Mode chooses how the boost is applied to bypass different anti-cheats. The Vulcan mode additionally delays a velocity reset and can optionally glide you back down to look more legitimate.
useCases: Jumping onto blocks or ledges that are normally too high to reach in survival.
Bypassing servers protected by Vulcan anti-cheat using the dedicated Vulcan mode (still flags slightly per the code notes).
Gaining extra vertical reach in parkour or escape situations.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the jump-boost method; defaults to Vanilla. Vanilla simply sets your jump motion to the configured Motion value. Vulcan is tuned to bypass Vulcan anti-cheat (tested on 2.7.5): it boosts the jump, then after 100 ticks zeroes your vertical movement and can glide you down.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: The upward velocity applied to your jump. Default 0.8, range 0.2..10. Higher values make you jump significantly higher; applies to both Vanilla and Vulcan modes (vanilla jump motion is ~0.42).

settings.name: Glide
settings.description: Sub-option of the Vulcan mode. Default false (off). When enabled, after the boosted jump peaks the module forces a controlled descent: while falling it nudges your vertical velocity downward (-0.155 every other tick while falling, otherwise -0.1) until you land, producing a smoother, less suspicious fall.

modules.name: Hitbox
modules.summary: Hitbox enlarges the collision/attack hitbox of other entities so they are easier to hit. It expands the targetable bounding box of entities that should be attacked by the configured size margin. This makes landing attacks easier when your aim is slightly off.
useCases: Make hitting fast-moving or strafing opponents easier in PvP by widening their effective hitbox.
Compensate for high ping or imprecise aim so attacks register more reliably.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: How much to expand the hitbox margin of attackable entities, in blocks added to each side. Default 0.1, range 0.0..1.0. Higher values make entities much easier to hit but are more obvious/detectable.

settings.name: ApplyToDebugHitbox
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, the enlarged margin is also applied to the debug hitbox rendering (the F3+B outline), so the visible box matches the expanded hitbox.

settings.name: ApplyToComponent
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, the enlarged margin is applied to the item AttackRange hitbox margin component, affecting attack-range based hit detection for items that define one.

modules.name: HitFX
modules.summary: HitFX adds custom visual particle effects and custom sounds when you land hits on living entities. When you attack an entity it remembers it as the last target, and when a vanilla hit/hurt sound for that nearby target arrives it spawns the chosen particles on the target and can replace the vanilla hit sound with a custom one. It can also play a separate self sound when you hit. Sounds are picked randomly from the selected sound sets each hit.
useCases: Make combat feel more satisfying or comedic with custom hit particles (blood, fire, hearts, etc.) and meme sound effects.
Get clearer visual/audible feedback confirming that your attacks actually connected with a target.

settings.name: Particle
settings.description: Multi-select of which particle effect(s) to spawn on the target when you hit it. Options: Blood (redstone block break effect above the target), Fire (lava), Heart, Water (falling water), Smoke, Magic (enchanted hit), Crits (crit particles). A random one of the selected types is used per particle spawned. Defaults to Fire. If nothing is selected, no particles are shown.

settings.name: ParticleAmount
settings.description: Integer range for how many particle effects to spawn per hit; a random value within the range is chosen each hit. Default range is 1..1 and the allowed bounds are 1..20.

settings.name: OtherSound
settings.description: Multi-select of custom sound sets to play (and which replace the vanilla hit sound) when the hit sound for your target is detected near it. Options come from the HitFX sound registry (e.g. Hit, Orb, Bonk, Boykisser, Bring, Glass, Click, Meow, Moan, MagicSquash, NYA, Pop, Soft, Squash, Tung, UWU). A random sound from the selected sets is used each hit. Defaults to Pop. If a custom sound is chosen, the original vanilla hit sound event is cancelled and replaced.

settings.name: SelfSound
settings.description: Multi-select of custom sound sets used for the self sound exposed to other client features when you hit. Same option list as OtherSound (the HitFX sound registry). A random sound from the selected sets is used. Defaults to Boykisser.

modules.name: HoleESP
modules.summary: HoleESP detects and highlights safe spots ('holes') used in Crystal PvP and renders them within a configurable scan range. It distinguishes hole sizes (1x1, 1x1 bedrock-only, 1x2, and 2x2) and color-codes each type. Holes can be drawn either as full boxes or as a glowing plane on the floor, and their visibility fades with distance from you.
useCases: Crystal PvP: quickly finding safe 1x1 holes to stand in and avoid crystal damage.
Identifying bedrock-only holes that cannot be mined/broken, versus regular holes.
Scouting nearby safe spots within a controlled range while moving around an arena.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how holes are rendered. Options are 'Box' (draws a full 3D box around each hole) and 'GlowingPlane' (default; draws a plane on the bottom of the hole plus an upward gradient glow). Each mode has its own sub-settings.

settings.name: HorizontalScanDistance
settings.description: Maximum horizontal distance (in blocks) from the player within which holes are detected and rendered (default 32, range 4-128). Larger values find more distant holes at greater performance cost.

settings.name: VerticalScanDistance
settings.description: Maximum vertical distance (in blocks) from the player within which holes are detected and rendered (default 8, range 4-128). Larger values detect holes further above/below you.

settings.name: DistanceFade
settings.description: Controls how strongly hole rendering fades out with distance (default 0.3, range 0.0-1.0). A value of 0 disables fading (holes are always fully opaque); higher values make distant holes fade based on how close they are to the scan-range edge.

settings.name: 1x1Bedrock
settings.description: Color used for 1x1 holes that are surrounded only by bedrock (cannot be mined). Default is a green tint (full alpha 0x19c15c).

settings.name: 1x1
settings.description: Color used for standard 1x1 holes. Default is a red tint (full alpha 0xf7381b).

settings.name: 1x2
settings.description: Color used for 1x2 holes. Default is a cyan/blue tint (full alpha 0x35bacc).

settings.name: 2x2
settings.description: Color used for 2x2 holes. Default is a yellow tint (full alpha 0xf7cf1b).

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Child of the 'Box' mode. When enabled (default), an outline is drawn around each hole's box in addition to the fill. When off, only the filled box is drawn.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Child of the 'GlowingPlane' mode. When enabled (default), an outline is drawn around the bottom plane of each hole. When off, only the filled plane and glow are drawn.

settings.name: GlowHeight
settings.description: Child of the 'GlowingPlane' mode. The height of the upward fading glow gradient rising from the hole's floor, as a fraction of the block height (default 0.7, range 0.0-1.0). Higher values make the glow rise taller before fading to transparent.

modules.name: HoleFiller
modules.summary: HoleFiller automatically fills nearby holes (1x1, 2x1, 2x2 safe spots) with blocks such as obsidian, using a configurable block placer. In its default 'Smart' mode it only fills holes that enemies are about to step into (optionally checking their movement direction), prioritizing the most relevant holes and respecting how many fill blocks you actually have. It can avoid filling the hole you yourself want to enter and can be limited to only act while you stand in a hole.
useCases: Trap opponents in crystal/anchor PvP by filling the safe hole they are running toward so they take explosion damage.
Defend your own hole position by only filling holes while you are inside one (OnlyWhenSelfInHole).
Quickly cap exposed holes around you with obsidian without manually placing each block.

settings.name: Features
settings.description: Set of behavior flags. Smart: only fill holes entities are about to enter (otherwise fill all holes) - enabled by default. PreventSelfFill: don't fill the hole you intend to enter (allowed only if the hole is above you, doesn't intersect your fill area, or you're already in a hole) - enabled by default. OnlyWhenSelfInHole: only operate while you are in a hole - off by default. CheckMovement: in Smart mode, skip holes that lie more than 30 degrees away from the entity's velocity direction - enabled by default. Only1x1: only fill 1x1 holes, ignoring 2x2 and 2x1 holes - off by default.

settings.name: Area
settings.description: The cubic area (default 2, range 1..5) around each entity's feet that is scanned for holes to fill.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: How the Blocks list is interpreted when picking a fill block from your hotbar/offhand (default WHITELIST): only listed blocks are used for filling.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The blocks used to fill holes; defaults to just Obsidian.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Inside Placing. Maximum placement reach (default 4.5, range 1..6) for filling a hole in line of sight.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Inside Placing. Reach for filling through walls (default 4.5, range 0..6). 0 disables through-wall fills.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Inside Placing. Random tick delay (default 1..2, range 0..40) between placements after an action.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Inside Placing. Hand-swing behavior when placing (default DO_NOT_HIDE).

settings.name: ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Inside Placing (default true). Builds a center-based hit result when raytracing fails, making fills more reliable at the cost of slightly less accurate rotations/range.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: Inside Placing. Random ticks (default 1..1, range 0..10) to sneak when placing against an interactable block to avoid activating it.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Inside Placing. Conditions to keep placing through: OpenInventory and UsingItem. Default none.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Inside Placing. Random ticks (default 4..6, range 0..40) the fill-block slot is held before restoring the previous slot.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Inside Placing. Rotation behavior toward fills: Normal (realistic, one placement/tick) or None (no/packet-only rotation, multiple per tick).

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Inside Placing > RotationMode (both modes, default false). Executes the placement after the movement packet when enabled.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Inside Placing > RotationMode 'Normal'. Sub-tree controlling how the player turns toward each fill (turn speed/interpolation and related aiming options).

settings.name: SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Inside Placing > RotationMode 'None' (default false). Sends a matching rotation packet without visibly rotating.

settings.name: Placements
settings.description: Inside Placing > RotationMode 'None'. Blocks placed per operation/tick (default 1, range 1..10, unit b/o).

settings.name: DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Inside Placing. Toggleable sub-group (default enabled) that breaks end crystals blocking a fill position, unless the explosion would kill you.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals. Reach for hitting a blocking crystal in sight (default 4.5, range 1..6).

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals. Reach for hitting a crystal through walls (default 4.5, range 0..6).

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals. Minimum milliseconds between crystal attacks (default 0, range 0..1000).

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals. Hand-swing behavior when attacking the crystal (default DO_NOT_HIDE).

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals. Rotation behavior for aiming at the crystal: Normal or None.

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Inside Placing > DestroyCrystals > RotationMode (default false). Executes the crystal attack after the movement packet when enabled.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Inside Placing. Toggleable renderer (default disabled) drawing boxes at hole positions queued to be filled.

settings.name: PlacedRendering
settings.description: Inside Placing. Toggleable renderer (default enabled) briefly drawing boxes at positions that were just filled.

modules.name: HUD
modules.summary: HUD is the client's in-game dashboard overlay, rendering the theme-based interface (arraylist, watermark, tab GUI elements, and additional native components such as the minimap). It is enabled by default and opens a browser-backed overlay while you are in-game and not hiding the client appearance. It also manages theme settings and additional HUD components, and can apply a blur background effect.
useCases: Display the standard LiquidBounce on-screen interface (enabled modules, watermark, etc.) while playing.
Add and configure extra HUD elements like the in-game minimap.
Toggle the background blur effect or switch/configure HUD themes to customize the look of the overlay.

settings.name: Blur
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling the background blur effect behind HUD elements. When enabled, a blur is applied (except when the vanilla HUD is hidden and no screen is open).

settings.name: AlphaBlendRange
settings.description: Child of the Blur group. Float range defining the alpha range over which the transition from not-blurred to blurred is blended. Default 0.0..0.75 within allowed bounds 0.0..1.0.

settings.name: SpaceSeperatedNames
settings.description: When enabled, player/entity names are rendered with spaces separating characters (fires a name-formatting change event when toggled). Default true.

settings.name: Themes
settings.description: Container group that holds the configuration sub-trees of the loaded HUD themes; its contents are populated dynamically from the available themes, so the available settings depend on the active theme(s).

settings.name: AdditionalComponents
settings.description: Container group for extra native HUD components added to the overlay. By default it contains the Minimap component described below.

settings.name: Minimap
settings.description: Toggleable native HUD component (enabled by default) that renders an in-game minimap of the surrounding chunks. Contains the alignment, sizing, texture, entity, and extra-element settings below.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Minimap alignment: horizontal anchor on screen. Options Left, Center, CenterTranslated, Right. Defaults to Left for the minimap.

settings.name: HorizontalOffset
settings.description: Minimap alignment: horizontal pixel offset from the chosen horizontal anchor. Range -1000..1000; defaults to 7 for the minimap.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Minimap alignment: vertical anchor on screen. Options Top, Center, CenterTranslated, Bottom. Defaults to Top for the minimap.

settings.name: VerticalOffset
settings.description: Minimap alignment: vertical pixel offset from the chosen vertical anchor. Range -1000..1000; defaults to 180 for the minimap.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Pixel size (width and height) of the square minimap. Default 96, range 1..256.

settings.name: ViewDistance
settings.description: How many chunks of radius the minimap shows / zoom level; larger values zoom out to show more area. Default 3.0, range 1.0..8.0.

settings.name: FixedDirection
settings.description: When enabled, the minimap stays fixed (north-up) instead of rotating with the player's yaw. Default false (map rotates with the player).

settings.name: Texture
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that draws the rendered chunk/terrain texture on the minimap. Disabling it leaves the minimap without the map background; enabling it subscribes the chunk scanner to keep the map updated.

settings.name: VertexColor
settings.description: Child of the Texture group. Tint color applied to the minimap terrain texture vertices. Default white.

settings.name: Entity
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that draws entities (from the ESP rendered-entities set, colored by ESP) as markers on the minimap.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Child of the Entity group. Scale multiplier for the size of entity markers on the minimap. Default 1.0, range 0.25..4.0.

settings.name: OutOfBounds
settings.description: Child of the Entity group. Controls drawing edge markers for entities outside the visible minimap area. None = no out-of-bounds markers; All = draw edge markers for all out-of-range entities. Default None.

settings.name: Compass
settings.description: Toggleable extra-element group (disabled by default) that renders a compass item icon on the minimap (uses a compass from your inventory if present, otherwise a default compass).

settings.name: Placement
settings.description: Child of the Compass element. Corner of the minimap where the compass icon is drawn: TopLeft, TopRight, BottomLeft, BottomRight. Default TopLeft.

settings.name: Clock
settings.description: Toggleable extra-element group (disabled by default) that renders a clock item icon on the minimap (uses a clock from your inventory if present, otherwise a default clock).

settings.name: Placement
settings.description: Child of the Clock element. Corner of the minimap where the clock icon is drawn: TopLeft, TopRight, BottomLeft, BottomRight. Default TopLeft.

modules.name: InventoryCleaner
modules.summary: InventoryCleaner (also called InventoryManager) automatically tidies your inventory by throwing away useless items, merging stacks to save space, and sorting preferred items into chosen hotbar/offhand slots. You assign each of the nine hotbar slots (and the offhand) a desired item category, and set maximum amounts for blocks, arrows, throwables and food so excess gets discarded. It respects inventory-interaction constraints (timing, no-movement/rotation requirements, etc.) and leaves armor and the offhand alone when AutoArmor/AutoTotem are managing them.
useCases: Keep a consistent hotbar layout (weapon, bow, tools, food, blocks) automatically as you pick up loot.
Automatically drop surplus blocks/arrows/food above your set caps so your inventory stays clean during a game.
Merge fragmented item stacks together to free up inventory space without manual shuffling.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Constraints sub-tree. Random delay (in ticks, range 0..20) before starting an inventory interaction. Default: 1..2.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Constraints sub-tree. Random delay (in ticks, range 0..20) between individual inventory clicks. Default: 2..4.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Constraints sub-tree. Random delay (in ticks, range 0..20) before closing the inventory after actions. Default: 1..2.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Constraints sub-tree. Chance (in percent, range 0..100) to intentionally miss/misclick for a more human-like pattern. Default: 0..0 (never miss).

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Constraints sub-tree. Conditions that must be met before any inventory action runs. Options: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, InventoryOpen (perform actions only with the inventory actually open). Default: none selected.

settings.name: MaximumBlocks
settings.description: Maximum number of building blocks to keep; excess blocks are thrown out. Default: 512, range 0..2500.

settings.name: MaximumArrows
settings.description: Maximum number of arrows to keep; excess arrows are thrown out. Default: 128, range 0..2500.

settings.name: MaximumThrowables
settings.description: Maximum number of throwable items to keep; excess are thrown out. Default: 64, range 0..600.

settings.name: MaximumFoodPoints
settings.description: Maximum total food value to keep; food beyond this is thrown out. Default: 200, range 0..2000.

settings.name: Greedy
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the cleaner is more aggressive about satisfying slot targets, keeping/sorting items that fulfill a slot's desired category even when supply is limited.

settings.name: OffHandItem
settings.description: Desired item category for the off-hand slot. Default: Shield. (Ignored if AutoTotem/Offhand module is operating, which locks the off-hand.) Choose Ignore to leave the slot's current contents untouched, or None for no preference.

settings.name: SlotItem-1
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 1. Default: Weapon. Selectable categories include Sword, Weapon, Spear, Mace, Bow, Crossbow, Axe, Pickaxe, Shovel, Hoe, Rod, Shield, Water, Lava, Milk, Pearl, Gapple, Food, Potion, Block, Throwables, Ignore, None.

settings.name: SlotItem-2
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 2. Default: Bow. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-3
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 3. Default: Pickaxe. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-4
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 4. Default: Axe. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-5
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 5. Default: None. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-6
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 6. Default: Potion. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-7
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 7. Default: Food. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-8
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 8. Default: Block. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

settings.name: SlotItem-9
settings.description: Desired item category for hotbar slot 9. Default: Block. Same category options as SlotItem-1.

modules.name: InventoryMove
modules.summary: Lets you keep walking, jumping and moving while an inventory or other screen is open, instead of vanilla freezing your movement. A Behavior setting controls how it interacts with anti-cheats: Normal (always move), Safe (blocks clicking while moving and closes the inventory), Undetectable (stops in real containers), or StopOnAction (delays container packets until you stop moving). Optional sub-features add sprint/sneak control while a screen is open, a timer speed-up, and a Blink mode that holds packets and auto-closes the inventory after a time limit.
useCases: Continuing to run away or strafe while managing your inventory or a chest during PvP.
Using Safe or StopOnAction behavior to move in inventories while reducing the chance of anti-cheat flags.
Combining with Blink to delay outgoing packets while sorting an inventory, then catch up.

settings.name: Behavior
settings.description: Controls how movement and clicks are handled while a screen is open. Normal (default): always allow movement input. Safe: disallows inventory clicks while a movement key is held and closes the inventory when you start moving server-side. Undetectable: stops movement input in real container screens. StopOnAction: delays container packets and zeroes movement input until you stop, sending the packets afterward.

settings.name: PassthroughSneak
settings.description: When enabled (default false), the sneak key is also forwarded while a screen is open so you can sneak in the inventory; when disabled, sneak input is ignored in screens.

settings.name: SprintControl
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled and a handled screen is open, it can force or suppress sprint on both the client and server side via the Client and Server settings.

settings.name: Client
settings.description: SprintControl: client-side sprint override applied during movement-tick/input. DoNotChange (default) leaves sprint as-is; ForceSprint forces client sprint while moving; ForceNoSprint disables client sprint.

settings.name: Server
settings.description: SprintControl: server-side sprint override applied to network/input sprint state. DoNotChange (default) leaves it as-is; ForceSprint forces server-perceived sprint while moving; ForceNoSprint makes the server think you are not sprinting.

settings.name: SneakControl
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled and a handled screen is open, it forces or suppresses sneak input via the Client setting.

settings.name: Client (SneakControl)
settings.description: SneakControl: sneak override. DoNotChange (default) leaves sneak as-is; ForceSneak forces sneaking; ForceNoSneak disables sneaking while a screen is open.

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled, requests a custom game timer speed while a container screen is open, speeding up or slowing down game time.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Timer: the game timer speed multiplier applied while a container screen is open. Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 2.0. Above 1.0 speeds up time, below 1.0 slows it.

settings.name: Blink
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (disabled by default). When enabled, while a container screen is open it queues non-container outgoing packets (fake-lag) and automatically closes the inventory after the configured time limit.

settings.name: MaximumTime
settings.description: Blink: the maximum time (in milliseconds) a container screen can stay open before the module force-closes it and flushes queued packets. Default 10000, range 0 to 30000.

modules.name: InventoryTracker
modules.summary: InventoryTracker records the items it sees other players use or equip and reconstructs an approximate inventory for them, viewable via the Invsee command. As remote players swap held items or change armor, those items are remembered and shown when you inspect that player, with a 'Last Seen' time added to each item's lore. It ignores bots detected by AntiBot. Optionally it can keep tracking players even after they leave your render distance.
useCases: Spy on what gear and items an opponent has been using before engaging in PvP.
Keep a record of a player's seen equipment even after they leave view, to inspect later with Invsee.

settings.name: SavePlayers
settings.description: When enabled, stores the (non-persistent) player object together with their UUID so you can look up the tracked inventories of players who are no longer in render distance. Default false. Toggling this clears the saved player map.

modules.name: ItemChams
modules.summary: ItemChams applies visual effects to the items held in your hands. It has two independent sub-features: a Lightmap effect that recolors and adds a layered glow to the held item's lighting (making items appear tinted and glowing), and a Shield tint that recolors the held shield. Each sub-feature can be toggled on or off separately and finely customized.
useCases: Make your held item glow and stand out with a custom colored chams/glow effect.
Recolor or tint your held shield, including making it translucent.

settings.name: Lightmap
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that recolors and adds a glowing layered effect to the held item's lightmap. When disabled the held item uses normal lighting.

settings.name: BlendColor
settings.description: Lightmap. Base color blended into the held item's lighting (default RGBA 0,64,255,186, a blue). Changing it tints the held item toward this color.

settings.name: Alpha
settings.description: Lightmap. Overall strength/opacity of the lightmap effect (default 95, range 1..255). Higher values make the tint and glow more intense.

settings.name: GlowColor
settings.description: Lightmap. Color of the additional glow layers around the item (default RGBA 0,64,255,15, a faint blue). Changing it recolors the glow halo.

settings.name: Layers
settings.description: Lightmap. Number of glow layers rendered (default 3, range 1..10). More layers create a thicker, more pronounced glow.

settings.name: LayerSize
settings.description: Lightmap. Size/spread of each glow layer (default 1.91, range 1..5). Larger values widen the glow.

settings.name: Falloff
settings.description: Lightmap. Controls how quickly the glow fades out toward its edges (default 6.83, range 0..20). Higher values make the glow fall off more sharply.

settings.name: Shield
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group (enabled by default) that tints the held shield. When disabled the shield keeps its normal coloring.

settings.name: TintMode
settings.description: Shield. How the Tint color is applied: Multiply (default) multiplies the tint with the shield's existing color, while Override replaces the shield's color entirely with the Tint.

settings.name: Tint
settings.description: Shield. The color used to tint the shield (default white). With Multiply white leaves the shield unchanged; lowering the alpha makes the shield translucent.

modules.name: ItemESP
modules.summary: ItemESP highlights dropped items (and optionally certain projectiles) through walls so you can find them easily. You can filter which items are shown, limit the render distance, and choose between Glow, Box and Legacy2D visual styles, with optional tracer lines from your camera to each item. It can also render collectible arrows and thrown tridents lying on the ground.
useCases: Locate valuable dropped items through walls and terrain after fights or in loot rooms.
Spot pickable arrows or thrown tridents to retrieve them.
Filter to only specific item types and draw tracers to find them quickly across a large area.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: How the Items list is applied to dropped items. BLACKLIST (default) shows all items except those listed; WHITELIST shows only listed items.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: The set of item types used by the filter. Empty by default.

settings.name: MaximumDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance (in blocks) at which items/arrows/tridents are rendered. Default 128, range 1..512.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: When enabled, draws a line from your camera to each rendered item. Default false.

settings.name: ShowArrows
settings.description: Toggle for the ShowArrows group (default enabled). When on, collectible arrows on the ground are rendered (only those with pickup allowed).

settings.name: RegularArrows
settings.description: (ShowArrows group) Whether plain arrows (no effect/color) are rendered. Default true.

settings.name: SpectralArrows
settings.description: (ShowArrows group) Whether spectral arrows are rendered. Default true.

settings.name: ArrowsWithEffects
settings.description: (ShowArrows group) Whether tipped/effect arrows (colored) are rendered. Default true.

settings.name: ShowTridents
settings.description: Whether thrown tridents lying on the ground are rendered. Default true.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: The visual rendering style. Options (index 0 default): Glow (entity glow outline), Box (3D box), Legacy2D (flat 2D marker). Each adds its own sub-settings.

settings.name: MergeIntersecting
settings.description: (Box mode) When enabled, overlapping item boxes are merged into a single box. Default false.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: (Legacy2D mode) Size of the flat 2D marker drawn at each item. Default 0.1, range 0.02..0.3.

settings.name: YOffset
settings.description: (Legacy2D mode) Vertical offset applied to the 2D marker position. Default 0, range -1..1.

settings.name: BackgroundAlpha
settings.description: (Legacy2D mode) Opacity of the marker's black background. Default 150, range 0..255.

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: How the ESP color is determined. Options (index 0 default): Static (a fixed color) or Rainbow (animated rainbow). Each adds its own sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: (ColorMode > Static) The fixed color used for the ESP. Default orange RGBA(255,179,72,255).

modules.name: ItemScroller
modules.summary: ItemScroller speeds up moving items in container/inventory screens. While the module is enabled, holding Shift and pressing (or holding) the left mouse button over a slot performs a quick-move (shift-click transfer) of that item automatically, with a small randomized delay between actions so transfers are not instantaneous. This makes it fast to drag-transfer many items across a chest or inventory by sweeping the cursor while holding Shift.
useCases: Rapidly emptying or filling a chest by holding Shift and sweeping the mouse over slots.
Quickly sorting or transferring stacks between inventory and a container without manual clicking on each slot.

settings.name: ClickMode
settings.description: Selects how the click on each slot is performed. The only available value is QuickMove (default), which issues a left-button QUICK_MOVE (shift-click style) transfer of the slot's item.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Integer tick range (default 2..3, allowed 0..20, in ticks) that randomizes the minimum wait between consecutive scroll transfers. A random value in this range is picked each action and multiplied by 50ms; lower values transfer items faster, higher values slow it down to look more human.

modules.name: ItemTags
modules.summary: ItemTags renders floating tags over dropped item entities in the world, showing each item's icon and stack count. Nearby item drops are clustered together by distance so a pile of items is shown as one combined tag, and identical items can be merged by item or by full component data. It can optionally peek inside dropped shulker boxes and display their contents, with an optional title.
useCases: See valuable item drops (e.g. from kills or broken blocks) at a glance and decide what to pick up.
Whitelist only certain items so the overlay shows only the loot you care about.
Inspect the contents of dropped shulker boxes without picking them up.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whether the Items set acts as a BLACKLIST (default, hide listed items) or WHITELIST (only show listed items) when deciding which dropped items get tags.

settings.name: Items
settings.description: The user-editable set of item types (empty by default) used together with Filter to control which dropped items are tagged.

settings.name: BackgroundColor
settings.description: The color and alpha of the rectangular background drawn behind each item tag (default client default background color).

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: A distance-to-scale curve controlling tag size by camera distance. X axis Distance (0..200), Y axis Scale (0.25..4); default keeps scale at 1. Items whose computed scale falls below 0.01 are not rendered.

settings.name: RenderOffset
settings.description: A 3D world-space offset added to the item position before projecting it to the screen, to nudge the tag. The in-world locate button is disabled.

settings.name: RowLength
settings.description: Maximum number of item icons drawn per row in a tag before wrapping, from 1 to 100 (default 100).

settings.name: PreventOverlap
settings.description: When enabled (default true), overlapping tags are nudged apart so multiple nearby item clusters do not visually stack.

settings.name: ClusterEntities
settings.description: A distance-to-radius curve defining how large the clustering radius is at a given distance, so farther items are grouped more aggressively. X axis Distance (0..200), Y axis Size (0.1..32); default points (0,2),(64,16),(128,16),(200,24). Item entities within this radius are merged into one tag.

settings.name: MergeMode
settings.description: How identical stacks within a cluster are combined: None (no merging, just sorted), ByItem (merge same item type summing counts) or ByComponents (default, merge only items with identical item and data components).

settings.name: Shulker
settings.description: Toggle for the Shulker group (default disabled). When enabled, dropped shulker boxes additionally show their internal contents as a second tag.

settings.name: MergeStacks
settings.description: Child of the Shulker group: when enabled (default true), the shulker's contents are merged using the current MergeMode before display; when disabled the raw stacks are shown.

settings.name: ShowTitle
settings.description: Child of the Shulker group: when enabled (default true), the shulker box's name is shown as a title above its contents tag.

modules.name: JumpEffect
modules.summary: JumpEffect spawns an expanding, fading gradient circle on the ground at your feet every time you jump. Each circle grows from zero to its configured radius following an easing curve over its lifetime, fading out as it does, with an optional animated hue shift. It is purely cosmetic and adds a visual flourish to your jumps.
useCases: Add a stylish visual effect under your character whenever you jump for screenshots or recordings.
Customize the client's look with colored, rainbow-shifting jump rings.
Make your movement more visually expressive during gameplay or showcases.

settings.name: EndRadius
settings.description: The float range defining the inner and outer target radius the circle expands to (start = inner radius, end = outer radius). Default 0.15 to 0.8, selectable within 0 to 3. Larger values produce a bigger ring.

settings.name: InnerColor
settings.description: The color used at the inner edge of the gradient circle. Default is green with alpha 0 (RGBA 0,255,4,0), i.e. transparent at the center so the ring blends out toward the middle.

settings.name: OuterColor
settings.description: The color used at the outer edge of the gradient circle. Default is semi-transparent green (RGBA 0,255,4,89).

settings.name: AnimCurve
settings.description: The easing function controlling how the circle's expansion and fade progress over its lifetime. Default QUAD_OUT (fast start, slowing toward the end). Changing it alters the pacing of the grow/fade animation.

settings.name: HueOffsetAnim
settings.description: Amount of hue shift (in degrees) applied to the colors over the course of the animation, scaled by progress. Default 63, range -360 to 360. A value of 0 disables hue shifting and keeps the static colors.

settings.name: Lifetime
settings.description: How long each spawned circle lives, in ticks, before it expires and disappears. Default 15, range 1 to 30. Higher values make rings last longer.

settings.name: CanBeCovered
settings.description: If true, the circle respects depth testing so blocks and terrain in front of it can hide it. If false (default), depth testing is disabled and the circle is always drawn on top, visible through obstructions.

modules.name: KeepSprint
modules.summary: KeepSprint prevents the normal sprint reset and knockback slowdown that occurs when you hit an entity, letting you retain more of your movement momentum after attacking. The amount of retained motion is configurable and can differ depending on whether you are currently in hurt (recently damaged) state. A chance setting controls how often the effect is applied.
useCases: Maintain sprint momentum after landing melee hits for stronger combos and positioning.
Tune retained knockback/motion separately for when you are being hit versus normal hits.
Randomize how often sprint is kept to appear less consistent.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Percentage of motion retained after a hit under normal conditions, chosen randomly within the range. Default 100% to 100%, configurable within 0% to 100%. Lower values retain less momentum.

settings.name: MotionWhenHurt
settings.description: Percentage of motion retained after a hit while you are within the hurt-time window, chosen randomly within the range. Default 100% to 100%, range 0% to 100%.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: The player hurtTime tick window during which MotionWhenHurt is used instead of Motion. Default 1 to 10, range 1 to 10.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Percentage chance that the keep-sprint motion is applied on a given hit; otherwise a default reduced motion (0.6) is used. Default 100%, range 0% to 100%.

modules.name: Kick
modules.summary: Kick forcibly disconnects you from the current server, using a chosen method ranging from a clean quit to sending intentionally malformed packets that cause the server to kick you. It refuses to run in singleplayer (showing an error) and acts as a one-shot trigger via disableActivation. Some modes can be detected or treated as cheating by servers.
useCases: Instantly leaving a server in an emergency without navigating the menus (Quit mode).
Forcing a server-side disconnect via a malformed packet to exploit kick/anti-cheat behavior or escape a stuck state.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: How to disconnect. Quit (default): cleanly leaves the world. InvalidPacket: sends a movement packet with NaN/Infinity coordinates. SelfHurt: sends an attack packet targeting yourself. IllegalChat: sends a malformed chat string with stray section signs. IllegalSwitchitem: sends an invalid held-item slot change (-1). IllegalInteract: sends a malformed interact packet. Only usable on multiplayer.

modules.name: KillAura
modules.summary: KillAura automatically attacks nearby enemies for you, handling target selection, silent rotations, click timing, range, criticals, sprint management and optional auto-blocking. It picks the best target in range, aims at the optimal point on its hitbox (optionally through walls), and attacks according to a configurable clicker while applying bypass options like raycast verification and crit selection. It also offers advanced helpers: an auto-block system, fail-swing to fake hits, a fight-bot that moves you in combat, failed-hit notifications and an on-screen range indicator.
useCases: Automatically fight one or many enemies in PvP without manually aiming and clicking.
Maintain critical hits, sprint resets and shield/auto-block handling for higher effective damage.
Use the fight bot to automatically strafe toward and around opponents, or follow a leader.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Attack/scan range sub-group. RangeIncrease (float, default 1, 0-5 blocks; added on top of your vanilla interaction range), ThroughWallsRange (float, default 3, 0-8 blocks; reach used for non-visible entities, capped at the normal range), ScanRangeIncrease (range, default 2-3, 0-7 blocks; extra distance used to pre-aim/scan for targets, randomized each attack).

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target selection sub-group (KillAura tracker). FOV (float, default 180, 0-180), HurtTime (int, default 10, 0-10), Priority (multiEnum selection ordering such as Type/Distance/Health/Direction), and IgnoreShield (boolean, default true; allow targeting enemies holding a shield that would otherwise block hits).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Combat rotation engine. AngleSmooth (choices: Linear, Sigmoid, Interpolation, Acceleration, AI — each with their own speed settings), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, 1-180), TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, 1-30 ticks), plus a ShortStop and a Fail rotation processor (toggleable) for legit-looking aiming. RotationTiming (enum, default Normal; Normal/Snap aim ahead of the click, OnTick rotates exactly on the attack tick). ThroughWalls (boolean, default false; allow aiming through walls when no direct line exists).

settings.name: AimPoint
settings.description: Point-tracker sub-group selecting the spot on the target hitbox to attack, with ExemptBoxParts (multiEnum), ExemptBestHitVector (toggleable), Gaussian (toggleable randomization), Lazy (toggleable), and Delay (toggleable) processors.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be true to attack, from the requirement set (Click, Weapon, EmptyHand, VanillaName, NotBreaking). None selected by default. Click = attack key held/recently pressed; Weapon = holding a weapon; EmptyHand = empty hand; VanillaName = no custom item name; NotBreaking = not breaking a block.

settings.name: Raycast
settings.description: How attacks are verified against your crosshair. None (TRACE_NONE) skips raycasting, Enemy (TRACE_ONLYENEMY) only redirects to entities that should be attacked, All (TRACE_ALL, default) lets any entity under the crosshair be hit. Affects legitimacy and which entity actually gets attacked.

settings.name: Criticals
settings.description: Critical-hit selection mode (from ModuleCriticals), default Smart. Controls whether KillAura waits for / forces critical-hit conditions and whether it stops sprinting to land crits.

settings.name: KeepSprint
settings.description: If enabled (default true), preserves sprint when attacking instead of having the hit reset it, unless crit selection requires stopping sprint.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: If enabled (default true), KillAura keeps running even while your inventory/container screen is open.

settings.name: SimulateInventoryClosing
settings.description: If enabled (default true), KillAura temporarily sends inventory-close/open packets around attacks so it can hit while an inventory is open without the server blocking the attack.

settings.name: TargetRendering
