settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) drawing a marker on the current target, with the shared Mode choice (Legacy/Circle/Image/GlowingCircle/Ghost/Hearts/Text/Arrow) and per-mode color/size/height settings.

settings.name: AutoBlocking
settings.description: Toggleable sub-feature (default off) that fakes/performs sword or shield blocking around attacks. BlockMode (enum Basic/Interact/Fake, default Interact), SimulateVanillaUse (boolean, default true), UnblockMode (enum StopUsingItem/ChangeSlot/SwapHand/None, default StopUsingItem), Reblock (range ticks, default 0-0, 0-3; delay before re-blocking after a hit), PauseOnUnblock (range ticks, default 0-0, 0-3; attack pause after unblocking), Chance (float %, default 100, 0-100; probability of blocking), Blink (int ticks, default 0, 0-10; how long blocking packets may be queued/blinked), PrioritizeBlocking (boolean, default true; lower CPS to keep blocking), OnScanRange (boolean, default true; start blocking when a target is within scan range), OnlyWhenInDanger (boolean, default false; only block when a target is aiming at you), AssumeShield (boolean, default false; assume a server shield in offhand on legacy protocols).

settings.name: FailSwing
settings.description: Toggleable sub-feature (default off) that swings to fake attacks when a target is just out of real reach. AdditionalRange (range, default 2.5-3, 0-10; extra range within which fail swings trigger, randomized per attack). NotifyWhenFail (choices None/Box/Sound, default Box) showing/hearing feedback for failed hits.

settings.name: NotifyWhenFail
settings.description: Feedback for failed (faked) hits, under FailSwing. None disables it; Box draws a fading box at the missed spot with Fade (int secs, default 4, 1-10), Color (color, default amber) and Rainbow (boolean, default false); Sound plays a click with Volume (float, default 50, 0-100) and Pitch (float, default 0.8, 0-2).

settings.name: FightBot
settings.description: Toggleable navigation sub-feature (default off) that moves you during combat (approach, strafe and run away on cooldown). OpponentRange (float desired distance to keep, default 3, 0.1-10), DangerousYaw (float degrees, default 55, 0-90; yaw difference considered dangerous when positioning), RunawayOnCooldown (boolean, default true; back off while your attack is on cooldown). Contains TargetFilter and Leader sub-groups plus inherited navigation settings.

settings.name: TargetFilter
settings.description: Sub-group under FightBot filtering which entity the bot engages. Range (float, default 50, 10-100; max distance the bot will pursue), VisibleOnly (boolean, default true; only fight entities with line of sight), NotWhenVoid (boolean, default true; ignore targets over a drop/void).

settings.name: Leader
settings.description: Toggleable group under FightBot (default off) to follow an ally. Username (text, empty by default; player name to follow), Radius (float, default 5, 2-10; how close to stay to the leader).

settings.name: RangeIndicator
settings.description: Toggleable sub-feature (default off) drawing range circles around you synced to KillAura's settings. ColorMode (enum Static/Rainbow/Distance, default Static), IdleColor / ActiveColor (colors for no-target vs target), Outline (boolean, default true) and OutlineColor, PulseAnimation (boolean, default false) with PulseSpeed (float, default 2, 0.5-5) and PulseIntensity (float, default 0.15, 0.05-0.5), FadeAnimation (boolean, default true) with FadeSpeed (float, default 0.1, 0.01-0.5), WallRangeColor / ScanRangeColor / OpponentRangeColor (colors for the extra circles, alpha 0 hides them), HideWhenDead (default true), HideWhenSpectator (default true), HideInVehicle (default false), RespectInventorySetting (boolean, default true; hide when inventory is open and IgnoreOpenInventory is off), CanBeCovered (boolean, default false; whether terrain can occlude the circles).

settings.name: AttackSpeed (Clicker)
settings.description: Click-scheduling sub-group governing CPS and click timing for attacks. Includes the attack click pattern/CPS settings plus an item-cooldown sub-group with IgnoreOnShieldBreak (boolean, default true), IgnoreOnMaceSmash (boolean, default true) and IgnoreWhenExitingRange (boolean, default true) which let attacks ignore the weapon cooldown in those situations.

modules.name: LiquidFiller
modules.summary: LiquidFiller automatically places blocks into liquid source blocks (water and/or lava) within reach, effectively filling or removing liquids around you. It scans for replaceable fluid source blocks in range, orders them, and queues them for the shared block placer to place a filler block (or optionally a sponge for water). When sponge mode is on, it finds a valid sponge placement adjacent to water that can absorb the source via the vanilla sponge absorption search. Placement is handled by the configurable Placer sub-system.
useCases: Quickly removing enemy water or lava around your base or bridge.
Filling water/lava source blocks with blocks while building or fighting in liquid.
Using sponges to clear large bodies of water automatically (UseSponge).

settings.name: PlaceIn
settings.description: Which liquid types to fill (default both Water and Lava; cannot be none). Water sources are filled using the normal filler block or a sponge (if UseSponge), lava sources are filled with the normal filler block only.

settings.name: PlaceOrder
settings.description: Order in which detected liquid positions are filled (default FurtherFirst). Options: Random, CloserFirst, FurtherFirst, BottomTop, TopBottom. Controls which sources get filled first when several are in range.

settings.name: UseSponge
settings.description: When true, uses sponges to absorb water targets instead of placing a normal block, finding a nearby valid sponge spot whose absorption reaches the target (default false). Lava is still filled with the normal block.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/blacklist mode (default Whitelist) determining how the Blocks list is interpreted when selecting which item/block to place as filler from your hotbar.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The set of blocks usable as filler material (defaults to all wool variants plus dirt, cobblestone, stone, netherrack, diorite, granite and andesite). Combined with Filter to decide which held block is used to fill liquids.

settings.name: Placer
settings.description: Block-placer sub-group that performs the actual placements. Contains Range, WallRange, Cooldown, Swing, ConstructFailResult, Sneak, Ignore, SlotResetDelay, RotationMode, Support, DestroyCrystals and the rendering sub-groups below. Note: support placements are disabled for LiquidFiller.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Child of Placer (default 4.5, range 1-6). Maximum reach for placing filler blocks; also drives the liquid scan range.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Child of Placer (default 4.5, range 0-6). Maximum reach for placing on targets behind walls; 0 disables through-wall placement.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Child of Placer (default 1-2 ticks, range 0-40). Random wait in ticks between placement actions; a value is chosen from this range after each placement.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Child of Placer (default DoNotHide). Controls how the hand swing animation is shown/hidden on placement.

settings.name: ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Child of Placer (default true). When the raytrace to a target fails, constructs a center hit result so placement still happens; improves reliability on most servers at the cost of less accurate rotations and slightly out-of-range placements.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: Child of Placer (default 1-1 ticks, range 0-10). How many ticks to sneak when placing on an interactable block so its GUI/action is not triggered.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Child of Placer. Conditions to ignore while placing: OpenInventory (place even with a container screen open) and UsingItem (place even while using an item).

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Child of Placer (default 4-6 ticks, range 0-40). How long the silently-selected hotbar slot is held before resetting after a placement.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Child of Placer. Selects how the player rotates to place: Normal (uses the rotation engine, has its own Rotations group, IgnoreOpenInventory, PostMove and Instant) or None (no rotation, with SendRotationPacket, PostMove and Instant).

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Child of the selected RotationMode (default false). Sends the action packet on post-move so packets are queued slightly earlier; not legit and may flag post-rotation anti-cheat checks.

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: Child of the selected RotationMode (default false). Sends the action instantly when possible, ignoring packet order; may flag some anti-cheats and can make PostMove irrelevant.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: Child of the Normal RotationMode (default true). When true, rotates/places without accounting for an open inventory screen.

settings.name: SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Child of the None RotationMode (default false). When true, sends a rotation packet to the server even though the client does not visibly rotate.

settings.name: Support
settings.description: Support sub-feature toggle of the Placer. For LiquidFiller this is force-disabled (allowSupportPlacements = false), so support placements are not performed even though the group exists.

settings.name: DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Child toggle of Placer (enabled by default). When a placement spot is blocked by an end crystal, this feature attacks/destroys the crystal so the block can be placed. Has its own Range, WallRange, Delay, SwingMode and RotationMode sub-settings, and avoids destroying crystals that would kill you.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Child of Placer (disabled by default). Renders boxes on positions queued to be filled, with the standard clump/animation/color sub-settings (Clump, StartSize/StartCurve, EndSize/EndCurve, FadeInCurve, FadeOutCurve, InTime, OutTime, Color, OutlineColor).

settings.name: PlacedRendering
settings.description: Child of Placer (enabled by default). Renders boxes on positions that were just filled (not kept), with the standard clump/animation/color sub-settings (Clump, StartSize/StartCurve, EndSize/EndCurve, FadeInCurve, FadeOutCurve, InTime, OutTime, Color, OutlineColor).

modules.name: LiquidPlace
modules.summary: LiquidPlace allows you to place blocks against liquids (water and lava) as if they were solid surfaces. When enabled it removes the vanilla restriction that normally prevents placing against fluid faces. It has no configurable options; it is purely on/off.
useCases: Bridge or build directly on top of or against water and lava without a solid block to click on.
Place blocks to seal off or cross liquid areas more quickly during building or PvP.

modules.name: LiquidWalk
modules.summary: LiquidWalk (aliases Jesus, WaterWalk) lets you walk on top of liquids as if the surface were solid, by making liquid blocks present a full collision shape when you are above the water. It offers multiple modes tuned to bypass specific anticheats, each handling jump suppression, packet spoofing, or timer manipulation differently. The walk-on-water behavior is generally suppressed while sneaking, when on fire, or after a large fall, letting you drop into the water when desired.
useCases: Crossing oceans, rivers, or lakes on foot without swimming or building bridges.
Walking on water on servers protected by NoCheatPlus, Verus, or Vulcan by picking the matching bypass mode.
Quickly traversing liquid terrain while sneaking to drop in when needed.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the LiquidWalk implementation/bypass. Default Vanilla. Options: Vanilla, NoCheatPlus, VerusB3901, Vulcan291. Each is tuned for a different server environment or anticheat.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Only in the Vulcan291 mode: the upward Y velocity (acting as a high-jump) applied each tick while inside water or a bubble column; the mode also briefly speeds up the game timer (1.125x) for extra speed. Default 0.8, range 0.2 to 1.4. Higher values bounce you higher off the water. Note this mode does not work on lava.

modules.name: LogoffSpot
modules.summary: LogoffSpot spawns a fake clone player entity at the exact position, rotation, inventory, and health of any player that logs off or otherwise leaves view, marking where they disappeared. The clone is removed automatically when its chunk unloads or when the real player reappears (re-joins). Attacks/interactions aimed at these fake entities are blocked so you do not accidentally swing at a ghost.
useCases: Keep track of where an opponent logged off in PvP so you can ambush them when they return.
Spot and remember logoff locations on anarchy or survival servers where players combat-log.

settings.name: SendInChat
settings.description: When enabled, prints chat notifications about logoff-spot events: when a player disappears (with their name and block coordinates), when their spot unloads, and when they reappear. Default true.

modules.name: LongJump
modules.summary: LongJump launches you a long horizontal distance in a single jump by exploiting specific anticheat weaknesses. It offers several anticheat-tailored modes (NoCheatPlus boost, NoCheatPlus bow, Vulcan, and a Matrix flag-based jump), each producing the boost in a different way. It can optionally auto-jump while you are moving on the ground and optionally disable itself after a successful long jump.
useCases: Crossing large gaps or voids in one jump on servers running a vulnerable anticheat.
Quickly escaping or repositioning in PvP by covering distance faster than a normal jump.
One-shot traversal where you enable the module, perform a single boosted jump, and let it auto-disable.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the long-jump technique, each tuned for a specific anticheat. Default is NoCheatPlusBoost. Options: NoCheatPlusBoost, NoCheatPlusBow, Vulcan289, Matrix-7.14.5-Flag.

settings.name: AutoJump
settings.description: When enabled, automatically jumps for you while you are on the ground and moving (except in the NoCheatPlusBow mode, which manages its own jump timing). Default false.

settings.name: DisableAfterFinished
settings.description: When enabled, the module turns itself off automatically once a boosted long jump has completed and you land or start flying. Default false.

settings.name: NCPBoost
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBoost mode only. Horizontal velocity multiplier applied on jump; higher values fling you further. Default 4.25, range 1 to 10.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBow mode only. Sub-group configuring the silent rotation engine used to aim the bow downward before launching. Contains AngleSmooth (rotation smoothing mode), MovementCorrection (how movement is corrected relative to the silent rotation, default Silent), ResetThreshold (angle difference in degrees below which rotation is considered reached, default 2, range 1 to 180) and TicksUntilReset (ticks before the rotation resets back to normal, default 5, range 1 to 30).

settings.name: Charged
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBow mode only. Number of item-use ticks the bow must be drawn before each arrow is released. Default 4, range 3 to 20.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBow mode only. Horizontal strafe speed applied to the jump after all arrows have been fired. Default 2.5, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: ArrowsToShoot
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBow mode only. How many arrows are fired downward to build up the boost before the launch jump occurs. Default 8, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: FallDistanceToJump
settings.description: NoCheatPlusBow mode only. The accumulated fall distance threshold at which an extra jump is triggered (fall distance is then reset) after the arrows have been shot. Default 0.42, range 0 to 2.

settings.name: BoostSpeed
settings.description: Matrix-7.14.5-Flag mode only. Horizontal strafe speed applied during the flag-triggered boost steps. Default 1.97, range 0.1 to 5.

settings.name: MotionY
settings.description: Matrix-7.14.5-Flag mode only. Upward (Y) velocity set on each boost step. Default 0.42, range 0.0 to 5.0.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Matrix-7.14.5-Flag mode only. Number of air ticks to wait after leaving the ground before starting the boost. Default 0, range 0 to 3.

modules.name: MaceKill
modules.summary: MaceKill makes the mace deal massive damage by faking fall height when you attack. When you hit an entity while holding a mace, it teleports (warps) your position upward by the computed safe height and back down so the server registers a large fall, multiplying the mace's smash damage. It exploits Paper/Spigot teleport handling for heights above 10 blocks and only activates while a mace is in your main hand.
useCases: One-shot or heavily damage opponents with a mace in PvP without actually needing to fall.
Maximize mace smash damage on servers that do not properly validate fake fall distance.

settings.name: FallHeight
settings.description: The maximum fake fall height (blocks) to apply when smashing with the mace. Default 22, range 1-170. MaceKill scans downward from this height to the highest value at which you would not collide with a block and uses that as the warp height, so larger values allow bigger (more damaging) fake falls where space permits.

modules.name: Macros
modules.summary: Macros lets you bind custom actions to keyboard keys so that pressing a key automatically performs chat/command input or item interactions. It provides five Chat macros and five Item macros, each independently configurable. When a bound key is pressed, the corresponding macro runs (subject to its trigger delay), sending the configured chat messages or using/placing the selected item.
useCases: Bind a key to instantly send a series of chat messages or commands (e.g. a kit request or greeting).
Bind a key to use a held item such as food, a bow or a potion, or to place a block on the spot you are looking at.
Automate repetitive in-game actions on PvP or minigame servers with a single keypress.

settings.name: Chat-1 / Chat-2 / Chat-3 / Chat-4 / Chat-5
settings.description: Each is a chat macro value group containing its own trigger, delays and message list. Five identical Chat macros are provided (Chat-1 through Chat-5).

settings.name: Item-1 / Item-2 / Item-3 / Item-4 / Item-5
settings.description: Each is an item-action macro value group containing its own trigger, delays, item pick mode, action and swing settings. Five identical Item macros are provided (Item-1 through Item-5).

settings.name: TriggerDelay
settings.description: Per-macro cooldown (in ms) enforced between consecutive activations of the same macro. A random value within this range is chosen each time. Default 0..0 (no cooldown), range 0..15000 ms. Present on every Chat and Item macro.

settings.name: Trigger
settings.description: The keyboard key that activates this macro when pressed. Present on every Chat and Item macro; unbound by default.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: (Chat macros only) Delay in ms applied after each message is sent before sending the next one. A random value within the range is used per message. Default 0..0, range 0..5000 ms.

settings.name: Messages
settings.description: (Chat macros only) The list of chat messages or commands to send in order when the macro is triggered. Empty by default.

settings.name: UseClientCommand
settings.description: (Chat macros only) When enabled, a message that begins with the client command prefix is executed as a LiquidBounce client command instead of being sent to the server chat. Default false.

settings.name: Action
settings.description: (Item macros only) What to do with the selected item. UseOnly (default) just uses the item in hand; PlaceOrUse performs a block placement/interaction against the block you are looking at.

settings.name: PickMode
settings.description: (Item macros only) Determines how the target item is identified. ByName selects an item by its name (default, index 0); ByItem selects a specific item type. The chosen sub-mode adds its own item-selection setting.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: (Item macros only) Controls the hand-swing animation when the item is used. Default DoNotHide (normal visible swing); other options hide or alter the swing.

settings.name: HoldTime
settings.description: (Item macros only) How long (in ticks) the chosen slot is silently selected before resetting, effectively how long the item is held/used. A random value within the range is used. Default 1..1, range 1..20 ticks.

modules.name: MiddleClickAction
modules.summary: MiddleClickAction lets you bind useful actions to the middle mouse button (the 'pick item' key). It offers two mutually exclusive modes selected via the Mode setting: a FriendClicker mode that adds or removes the player you are middle-clicking from your friends list, and a Pearl mode that selects and throws an ender pearl from your hotbar/offhand on middle click. The module is not included in auto-config exports.
useCases: Use FriendClicker to quickly add or remove a player as a friend by aiming at them and middle-clicking.
Use Pearl mode to throw ender pearls with the middle mouse button, with an automatic stop near vertical pitch to avoid wasting pearls when looking straight up.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which middle-click behavior is active. Choices are FriendClicker (default) and Pearl. Only the selected mode's settings apply.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Pearl mode. Number of ticks to keep the ender pearl slot silently selected before resetting back to your previous slot, also used as the delay when actually using the pearl. Default 1, range 0..10 ticks.

settings.name: StopOnSubmit
settings.description: Pearl mode. A pitch range (in degrees) within which the module will NOT throw a pearl; if your pitch falls inside this range the press is ignored. Default 85..90, adjustable within 60..90 degrees. Prevents accidental near-vertical pearl throws.

settings.name: PickUpRange
settings.description: FriendClicker mode. Maximum reach (in blocks) for detecting the player under your crosshair to toggle their friend status. Default 3.0, range 1..100.

modules.name: MobOwners
modules.summary: MobOwners shows which player owns a tamable entity (such as tamed wolves, cats and horses) and, optionally, projectiles. When you look at an applicable entity it resolves the owner's UUID and displays their name; if the owner is a player present in the world the scoreboard name is used, otherwise the name is looked up asynchronously from the Mojang API (showing Loading..., or an error/canceled message on failure). Resolved names are cached for the session.
useCases: Identify whose tamed pets (wolves, cats, horses) you are seeing on a server.
Enable Projectiles to also see which player shot a given arrow or other projectile.

settings.name: Projectiles
settings.description: When enabled, the owner name is also shown for projectiles (e.g. who shot an arrow), not just for tamable animals and horses. Disabled by default.

modules.name: MoreCarry
modules.summary: MoreCarry (alias XCarry) lets you keep items stored in your 2x2 crafting grid slots instead of having them dropped back when a container/inventory is closed. It works by cancelling the outgoing ServerboundContainerClosePacket, so the server never registers the close and items left in the crafting slots are not ejected. This effectively gives you extra carry slots. It only works on multiplayer servers.
useCases: Gaining extra inventory storage by stashing items in the crafting slots during multiplayer gameplay.
Carrying additional items beyond normal inventory capacity, for example before a fight or while transporting loot.

modules.name: MultiActions
modules.summary: MultiActions (also aliased as MultiTask) removes vanilla restrictions that normally prevent the client from doing two actions at the same time, allowing combined interactions like attacking while using an item. You pick which combined actions are permitted through a multi-select list; only the actions you enable are allowed, and other client features query this module to know whether the combination is permitted. With nothing selected it has no effect even while enabled.
useCases: Continuing to mine or place blocks while eating or drinking a potion.
Attacking enemies while keeping a shield or bow drawn (using an item).
Placing blocks while breaking another block for faster building or bridging.

settings.name: Actions
settings.description: Multi-select list of which simultaneous actions to allow. Options: PlacingWhileBreaking (place a block while breaking another), AttackingWhileUsing (attack entities while using/holding an item like a bow or shield), and BreakingWhileUsing (break blocks while using an item). Only the selected combinations are permitted; unselected ones behave like vanilla.

modules.name: MurderMystery
modules.summary: MurderMystery assists in the Murder Mystery minigame by detecting and color-coding players based on their role. It inspects equipment packets to identify who is holding a sword (murderer-like) or a bow (detective-like) and tags those players with colored ESP: detective-like players in blue and murderers in red. It also plays alert sounds (a villager hurt sound and a crossbow shoot sound) on relevant events, highlights dropped bows held by invisible armor stands with a box, and prevents you from targeting players who should not be attacked. The active game mode (Classic, Infection, or Assassination) determines how roles are assigned.
useCases: Quickly identify the murderer and detective in a Murder Mystery match.
Get audio and visual cues for bow pickups and dropped bows.
Avoid accidentally targeting innocent players via the built-in target filtering.

settings.name: SetTeamPrefix
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the module sets a colored team prefix on detected players matching their role (detective-like or murderer). When disabled, only the ESP coloring is applied and no team prefix is set.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the Murder Mystery game mode logic used to determine player roles. Options are Classic (default), Infection, and Assassination. Changing the mode resets the module's per-mode tracking state. None of the modes expose additional settings.

modules.name: NameCollector
modules.summary: NameCollector captures the names of all players currently online on the server and saves them to a text file. When enabled it immediately writes the names (one per line) to a timestamped .txt file inside a 'name-captures' folder in the LiquidBounce config directory, then disables itself (it cannot be left toggled on). If no players are found it shows an error notification instead.
useCases: Save a snapshot of everyone currently online for record-keeping, tracking, or later lookup.
Export player names from a server to a file for use with other tools or lists.

modules.name: NameProtect
modules.summary: NameProtect changes player names client-side so they are hidden from view, e.g. in screenshots or streams. By default it replaces your own username everywhere with a chosen placeholder and recolors it. It can optionally also obfuscate friends' names (replacing them with their alias or a default name) and all other players' names, each with its own color mode. Replacements are applied to both plain strings and formatted chat text, with caching for performance.
useCases: Hiding your own username in recordings, screenshots, or streams.
Anonymizing friends' names while keeping them distinguishable via aliases and a distinct color.
Masking every other player's name to fully anonymize the player list and chat.

settings.name: Replacement
settings.description: Text that your own username is replaced with everywhere it appears. Default 'You'.

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: Color applied to your replaced name. Choices: a static color (default, an orange-ish RGBA 255,179,72,50) and a rainbow color mode. The active choice exposes its own color settings (e.g. the static color picker).

settings.name: ObfuscateFriends
settings.description: Toggle (default enabled) for the friends sub-group. When enabled, each friend's name is replaced with their alias or a generated default name and recolored using the group's ColorMode.

settings.name: ColorMode (ObfuscateFriends)
settings.description: Color applied to replaced friend names. Choices: static color (default cyan RGB 0,241,255) and rainbow. The active choice exposes its color settings.

settings.name: ObfuscateOthers
settings.description: Toggle (default disabled) for the other-players sub-group. When enabled, every other online player's name (except yours) is replaced and recolored using the group's ColorMode.

settings.name: ColorMode (ObfuscateOthers)
settings.description: Color applied to replaced other-player names. Choices: static color (default gray RGB 71,71,71) and rainbow. The active choice exposes its color settings.

modules.name: Nametags
modules.summary: Replaces vanilla name tags with custom, more readable ones that scale with distance and can show extra information such as distance, ping, health, game mode and a bot marker, plus the entity's equipped items, item enchantments, and a highlight when an item is in use. It collects the entities that should be shown, computes a distance-based scale, and draws the tags as a screen overlay sorted from farthest to nearest. Tags below a tiny scale threshold are skipped, and the vanilla name tag is suppressed for entities the client renders.
useCases: Reading enemy info at a glance in combat (health, ping, distance) without relying on the small vanilla nametag.
Seeing what gear and enchantments other players are wearing above their heads.
Identifying bots, invisible players, and sneaking players via colored name highlighting.

settings.name: BorderWidth
settings.description: Width of the border drawn around the nametag background. Default 1, range 0..8. Set to 0 to remove the border.

settings.name: BackgroundRadius
settings.description: Corner rounding radius of the nametag's background rectangle. Default 2, range 0..16. Higher values give more rounded corners.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Distance-to-scale curve controlling how large nametags are at a given distance. X axis is Distance (0..200), Y axis is Scale (0.25..4); defaults to a flat curve of scale 1.0 from 0 to 200 blocks. Tags whose computed scale is at or below ~0.01 are not rendered.

settings.name: Parts
settings.description: Which text components appear in the nametag (cannot be empty; defaults to all enabled). Options: Distance (meters to the entity, hidden for yourself), Ping (player ping in ms, colored green/yellow/red by latency), Name (display name with team/tag coloring, baby prefix, and combined-mob count), Health (entity HP colored green/yellow/red, includes absorption), GameMode (player's game mode shorthand, colored), and BotMark (a red 'Bot' label for detected bots).

settings.name: Slots
settings.description: Part of the Equipment group. Which equipment slots are shown above the nametag. Defaults to all of MAINHAND, HEAD, CHEST, LEGS, FEET, OFFHAND enabled; can be set to none. Controls which worn/held items are displayed.

settings.name: SkipEmptySlot
settings.description: Equipment group. When enabled, empty equipment slots are omitted from the item row instead of being shown as blank. Default true.

settings.name: ShowInfo
settings.description: Equipment group. When enabled, item info (such as stack/durability details) is shown for the rendered equipment items. Default true.

settings.name: Enchantment
settings.description: Toggle for the Enchantment sub-group (default enabled). When on, abbreviated enchantment labels are drawn above each enchanted equipment item, colored by level (curse=red, level>=4 gold, 3 yellow, 2 green, else white).

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Enchantment group. Scale of the enchantment labels relative to the nametag font. Default 0.8, range 0.25..4.

settings.name: MaxCountPerItem
settings.description: Enchantment group. Maximum number of enchantment labels shown per item; if an item has more, the extra ones are collapsed into an ellipsis ('...') row. Default 4, range 1..16.

settings.name: BackgroundRadius
settings.description: Enchantment group. Corner rounding radius of each enchantment label's background, scaled by the label scale. Default 1.0, range 0..8.

settings.name: HighlightItemInUse
settings.description: Toggle for the HighlightItemInUse sub-group (default disabled). When on, the item an entity is currently using (e.g. eating, drawing a bow, blocking) is highlighted with a filled/outlined quad over its slot.

settings.name: FillColor
settings.description: HighlightItemInUse group. Fill color of the highlight quad drawn over the in-use item. Default red with alpha 100.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: HighlightItemInUse group. Outline color of the in-use item highlight quad. Default transparent (no visible outline).

modules.name: NewChunks
modules.summary: NewChunks highlights chunks that are likely newly generated versus already-loaded, drawing a colored plane over each tracked chunk. It listens to chunk and block-update packets: a chunk is initially marked as 'new' (not yet flagged old) when received, and is reclassified as 'old' when a non-source flowing fluid update is detected within it (a heuristic for already-explored/edited terrain). It can optionally smooth the coloring by blending toward the new color based on nearby old chunks, persist chunks after they are unloaded, and auto-place the render plane below the player.
useCases: Detect freshly generated terrain to find unexplored areas or potential bases/stashes on anarchy-style servers.
Distinguish player-modified/older chunks from untouched ones while traveling.
Keep a visual map of discovered chunks that persists even after they unload.

settings.name: RenderDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance (in chunks) from the player within which chunk planes are drawn. Default 32, range 4 to 128. Chunks farther than this (measured to their center) are skipped from rendering.

settings.name: RenderY
settings.description: The Y height at which the chunk highlight planes are drawn. Default 0.0, range -64.0 to 320.0. Ignored when AutoY is enabled.

settings.name: AutoY
settings.description: When enabled (default false), automatically draws the planes 100 blocks below the player's current Y position instead of using the fixed RenderY value.

settings.name: Smooth
settings.description: When enabled (default true), smooths the highlight coloring: old chunks surrounded by other old chunks are blended (interpolated) toward the new color based on a distance-weighted count of nearby old chunks, producing a gradient rather than hard color boundaries.

settings.name: Persist
settings.description: When enabled (default true), keeps tracked chunks in memory even after the server tells the client to unload them (forget chunk packets). When disabled, unloaded chunks are removed from the highlight set. Tracking is always cleared on world change.

settings.name: NewColor
settings.description: Color used to highlight chunks classified as new. Default semi-transparent green (RGBA 0,255,0,80).

settings.name: OldColor
settings.description: Color used to highlight chunks classified as old. Default semi-transparent red (RGBA 255,0,0,80). Also serves as the base color that is interpolated toward NewColor when Smooth blending applies.

modules.name: NoBlockInteract
modules.summary: NoBlockInteract lets you use an item (e.g. eat, draw a bow, throw a potion) while looking at an interactable block without triggering the block's interaction (such as opening a chest or door). When you aim at an interactable block while holding a usable item, the module briefly forces a sneak before the use, which causes Minecraft to use the item rather than activate the block. The sneak is applied for the movement input and the item use is started on the next game tick. This module has no configurable settings.
useCases: Eat, drink, or use items while standing in front of chests, doors, or other interactable blocks without accidentally opening them.
Throw potions or use a bow next to furnaces, buttons, or workstations without activating them.

modules.name: NoBob
modules.summary: NoBob disables the view bobbing effect, the slight up-and-down and side-to-side camera sway that normally occurs while walking. With it enabled the first-person view stays steady during movement. It has no configurable options.
useCases: Steady the camera for cleaner gameplay recordings or screenshots.
Reduce motion that some players find distracting or nauseating while moving.

modules.name: NoClip
modules.summary: NoClip lets you move freely through blocks by disabling the player's physics collision (noPhysics), zeroing fall distance, and forcing you off the ground each tick. You control flight with movement keys for horizontal motion and jump/sneak for vertical motion, all at a configurable speed. If you are riding a controlled vehicle, the no-clip and movement is applied to the vehicle instead (unless VehicleControl is active). It also watches for server position-correction (setback) packets and can auto-disable itself to avoid being flagged.
useCases: Flying through walls and floors to explore or bypass obstacles.
Phasing a boat or minecart you control through blocks when using OnlyInVehicle.
Escaping enclosed areas where normal movement is blocked.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Movement speed while no-clipping, applied to horizontal strafe motion and to the vertical motion when jump or sneak is held. Default 0.32, range 0.1 to 0.4. Higher values move you through blocks faster.

settings.name: OnlyInVehicle
settings.description: When enabled, NoClip only activates while you are in a controlled vehicle; if you are not in a vehicle the module pauses and restores normal physics. Default false.

settings.name: DisableOnSetback
settings.description: When enabled, the module automatically turns itself off (and prints an error message) if the server sends a player-position correction packet (a setback), which indicates the server rejected your movement. Default true. Disable to keep no-clipping despite setbacks.

modules.name: NoEntityInteract
modules.summary: NoEntityInteract skips entity interactions for the entity under your crosshair based on configurable entity-type and held-item filters. When your crosshair is on a matching entity (per the entity-type filter) and you are holding a matching item (per the holding-item filter), the interaction is suppressed, preventing accidental right-click interactions. By default it blocks interacting with villagers and armor stands, and only applies the held-item rule for empty hands plus utility items like shears, TNT, buckets, cobwebs and mining tools.
useCases: Avoid accidentally opening villager trade screens while fighting or moving near villages.
Stop accidentally rotating or equipping armor stands when interacting with blocks behind them.
Prevent unwanted right-click entity interactions while holding tools or buckets (e.g. when placing or breaking).

settings.name: EntityTypeFilter
settings.description: Default Blacklist. Determines how the EntityTypes list is interpreted: Blacklist suppresses interaction for entities of the listed types, Whitelist suppresses interaction only for entities NOT in the list (i.e. allows interaction with listed types).

settings.name: EntityTypes
settings.description: The list of entity types the filter applies to. Default contains Villager and Armor Stand. Add or remove entity types to control which entities are affected by the chosen EntityTypeFilter.

settings.name: HoldingItemFilter
settings.description: Default Whitelist. Determines how the HoldingItems list is interpreted: Whitelist suppresses interaction only when your main-hand item is in the list, Blacklist suppresses interaction for any item NOT in the list.

settings.name: HoldingItems
settings.description: The list of held items the filter applies to. Default includes empty hand (Air), Shears, TNT, Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, Cobweb, and all mining tools. Edit this list to control for which held items entity interaction is skipped.

modules.name: NoFall
modules.summary: NoFall protects you from taking fall damage using one of many selectable bypass modes tailored to different anticheats and servers (e.g. SpoofGround, Packet, MLG, Vulcan, Verus, Hypixel, Grim, etc.). It automatically disables itself in creative/spectator mode, while invulnerable or flying, and can be suppressed under user-chosen conditions such as while gliding with an elytra or holding a mace. The active mode is shown as the module tag.
useCases: Avoid fall damage when descending from heights or after being knocked off ledges in survival PvP.
Pick an anticheat-specific bypass mode (e.g. Vulcan, Verus, Grim, Hypixel) that works on your target server.
Allow normal fall damage in chosen situations, such as elytra gliding or mace combos, by enabling the Not conditions.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: The fall-damage bypass technique to use. Options include SpoofGround (default), SpoofLanding, NoGround, Packet, PacketJump, MLG, Mount, Rettungsplatform, Spartan524Flag, Vulcan, VulcanTP, Verus, ForceJump, Cancel, Blink, HypixelPacket, Hypixel, BlocksMC and Grim2371. The chosen mode is displayed as the module tag.

settings.name: Not
settings.description: Conditions under which NoFall is suppressed so you take normal fall damage. WhileGliding disables it while elytra fall-flying; WithMace disables it while holding a mace. Default none selected (NoFall always active otherwise).

modules.name: NoFOV
modules.summary: NoFOV overrides Minecraft's field of view value, letting you keep a fixed or custom FOV regardless of in-game effects such as sprinting or speed potions that normally widen the view. It exposes two modes: a Constant mode that locks the FOV to a chosen value, and a Custom mode that mathematically remaps the original FOV multiplier. This is useful for keeping a stable, distortion-free view during fast movement.
useCases: Lock your field of view to a single value so sprinting and speed effects never zoom the camera.
Fine-tune how much speed-based FOV changes are applied instead of fully disabling them, using Custom mode.
Set a wider or narrower fixed FOV for screenshots or a preferred visual feel.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which FOV-handling mode is active. Choices are Constant (default) and Custom. Constant locks the FOV to a fixed value; Custom remaps the dynamic FOV multiplier with a formula.

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Constant mode only. The exact field of view value to force, default 90, range 1 to 179. The game always renders at this FOV no matter what effects are active.

settings.name: BaseFOV
settings.description: Custom mode only. The base multiplier added in the FOV remap formula ((original - 1) * Multiplier + BaseFOV). Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.5. Higher values shift the resulting FOV upward.

settings.name: Limit
settings.description: Custom mode only. A float range (default 0.0..1.5, bounds 0.0 to 1.5) that clamps the final computed FOV multiplier, so the result is coerced between the lower and upper limit values.

settings.name: Multiplier
settings.description: Custom mode only. Scales how strongly the original FOV change is applied in the remap formula. Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 1.5. Lower values reduce the effect of dynamic FOV changes.

modules.name: NoHurtCam
modules.summary: NoHurtCam removes the camera tilt/shake effect that normally plays when you take damage. With it enabled, taking a hit no longer rotates or jolts your view, keeping the camera steady. This module has no configurable options; it is simply on or off.
useCases: Keep your aim stable during combat by eliminating the screen-tilt that occurs each time you are hurt.
Reduce visual distraction and motion when taking repeated damage.

modules.name: NoInterpolation
modules.summary: NoInterpolation reduces or removes the interpolation ticks the client uses to smooth out other entities' movement between position updates. Lowering interpolation makes entities snap closer to their true server positions, which can make their movement appear more abrupt but more accurate. It exposes a single setting controlling how many interpolation ticks are removed.
useCases: See entities at positions closer to their real server location for more accurate targeting in PvP.
Reduce the visual lag/smoothing of mobs and players when reacting to their movement.

settings.name: ReduceBy
settings.description: How many interpolation ticks to reduce entity movement smoothing by, 1-3, default 3. Higher values remove more interpolation, making entity movement snappier and closer to true positions.

modules.name: NoJumpDelay
modules.summary: Removes the small cooldown the game normally enforces between consecutive jumps. With it enabled you can jump again immediately upon landing instead of waiting for the vanilla jump-delay tick. The module has no configurable options; it simply toggles on or off.
useCases: Bunny-hopping or chaining jumps to keep momentum without the brief pause vanilla imposes.
Maintaining continuous jump-based movement in parkour or PvP situations.

modules.name: NoMissCooldown
modules.summary: NoMissCooldown removes the 10-tick attack cooldown that Minecraft normally applies after you miss an attack swing, letting you attack again immediately. It can also optionally cancel the attack entirely when you miss. This is useful for keeping attack speed high in fast combat.
useCases: Avoid the post-miss attack delay so you can keep attacking at full speed during PvP.
Optionally suppress missed swings to avoid wasting attacks on empty air.

settings.name: RemoveAttackCooldown
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, removes the 10-tick miss cooldown that normally prevents attacking right after a missed hit, so you can attack again immediately.

settings.name: CancelAttackOnMiss
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, cancels the attack action when a swing misses (no attack is performed on a miss).

modules.name: NoPitchLimit
modules.summary: NoPitchLimit removes the normal vertical look (pitch) clamp of -90 to +90 degrees, letting your head rotate beyond the usual up/down limits. With ServerSide enabled (default) the unclamped pitch is sent to the server; with ServerSide disabled the outgoing movement packet's pitch is coerced back into the legal -90..90 range so only your client view exceeds the limit. When the module is disabled, your pitch is immediately clamped back into the normal -90..90 range.
useCases: Achieving exaggerated over-the-top head rotations for visual or roleplay effect.
Sending out-of-range pitch values to the server (ServerSide on) to exploit servers or anticheats that mishandle them.
Keeping the extreme look client-side only (ServerSide off) while sending normal pitch to the server.

settings.name: ServerSide
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the over-limit pitch is also sent to the server in the move packet. When disabled, outgoing ServerboundMovePlayerPacket pitch is clamped back to -90..90 so the unlimited pitch stays client-side only.

modules.name: NoPose
modules.summary: NoPose prevents the player's pose (hitbox/visual posture) from changing in ways tied to lower server protocol versions, primarily by stopping the swimming pose and adjusting the sneaking hitbox height. With NoSwim enabled it cancels the swimming pose so you never enter the crawling/swimming body shape. The SneakHeight option overrides the dimensions used while sneaking to mimic the hitbox of older Minecraft versions (1.8, 1.9, or 1.15).
useCases: Avoid entering the crawling/swimming pose on servers that expect a standing hitbox, keeping a taller, easier-to-control body shape.
Restore the 1.8-style sneaking hitbox so movement and bridging feel like an older version.
Bypass crawl/swim animation requirements when playing against low-version protocol servers.

settings.name: NoSwim
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, cancels the SWIMMING pose for the player so the swimming/crawling body posture is never applied.

settings.name: SneakHeight
settings.description: Selects which version's sneak hitbox dimensions to apply while sneaking. Options: 1.8 (width 0.6, height 1.8, eye height 1.54), 1.9 (width 0.6, height 1.65, eye height 1.54), and 1.15 (width 0.6, height 1.5, eye height 1.27). Default is 1.15. Changing this alters your sneaking hitbox/eye height to match the chosen version.

modules.name: NoPush
modules.summary: NoPush prevents you from being shoved around by selected sources. Through the canPush check it blocks the chosen push sources (entities, blocks, fishing rods, liquids), and with the Sinking option it additionally zeros your downward velocity while in water or lava (unless you are holding jump or sneak) so you do not sink. Only the push types you select in the PushBy option are blocked.
useCases: Holding your position in PvP so other players cannot push you off blocks or out of place.
Staying still in flowing water/liquid currents instead of being carried away.
Preventing yourself from sinking in water or lava by enabling the Sinking option.

settings.name: PushBy
settings.description: Multi-select of which push sources to block. Options: Entities (pushing by other entities/players), Blocks (block-based pushing), FishingRod (knockback from fishing rod hooks), Liquids (flowing-water/lava currents), and Sinking (when selected, cancels your downward velocity in water or lava unless jump or sneak is held). Defaults to Entities and Liquids enabled.

modules.name: NoRotateSet
modules.summary: NoRotateSet prevents the server from forcibly rotating your head/camera. It offers two modes: SilentAccept, which accepts the server's rotation without visibly turning your view, and ResetRotation, which resets your rotation back using the rotation engine. The active mode determines how server-sent rotation packets are handled.
useCases: Stopping servers or anti-cheats from snapping your camera to a forced direction.
Using SilentAccept to invisibly comply with server rotation while keeping your own view.
Using ResetRotation to actively restore your intended rotation after a server rotate.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how server rotation is handled: SilentAccept (default; accept the rotation silently without turning the view) or ResetRotation (reset rotation back via the rotation engine).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Child of the ResetRotation mode. A nested rotation-engine value group controlling how the reset rotation is applied. Contains the sub-settings below.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Child of ResetRotation's Rotations. Selects the angle-smoothing algorithm (Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration) used when resetting the rotation.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Child of ResetRotation's Rotations. Controls how movement is corrected relative to the silent rotation. Default Silent.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Child of ResetRotation's Rotations. The angular difference (degrees) at which the rotation is considered close enough to begin resetting. Default 2, range 1 to 180.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Child of ResetRotation's Rotations. Number of ticks before the rotation is reset to normal. Default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks.

modules.name: NoSlotSet
modules.summary: NoSlotSet ignores the server's attempts to change which hotbar slot you have selected. When the server sends a held-slot packet (for example to force you onto a different slot), the module cancels it and instead tells the server you are still on your current (silent) serverside slot. This keeps your selected item under your own control regardless of server-side slot resets.
useCases: Prevent servers or plugins from forcibly switching your held item off the slot you intend to use.
Keep a chosen weapon or tool selected on servers that try to reset your hotbar slot.

modules.name: NoSlow
modules.summary: Cancels or reduces the various movement slowdowns Minecraft normally applies, both from using items and from special blocks/effects. It contains many independently toggleable groups: item-use slowdowns (Blocking, Consume, Bow, Bundle) each expose Forward/Sideways multipliers and anti-cheat-specific bypass modes, while block/effect groups (Sneaking, Soulsand, SlimeBlock, HoneyBlock, PowderSnow, Fluid, Slowness) let you tune how much speed those surfaces or effects take away. Each item-use group only acts while you are actually performing the matching action, and many bypass modes are tailored to specific anti-cheats like Grim, Intave and AAC.
useCases: Moving at full speed while eating, drinking, blocking with a shield/sword, charging a bow, or using a bundle.
Walking normally across soul sand, slime, honey or powder snow, or while sneaking, by raising their multipliers.
Bypassing a specific anti-cheat's item-use slowdown checks by picking the matching Grim/Intave/AAC mode.

settings.name: Blocking
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that removes the slowdown caused while blocking (shield/sword block, spyglass, horn, brush). Only active while you are blocking server-side or client-side.

settings.name: Forward (Blocking)
settings.description: Forward movement multiplier applied while blocking. Default 1.0 (no slowdown), range 0.0 to 1.0. Lower values reduce forward speed toward the vanilla slow.

settings.name: Sideways (Blocking)
settings.description: Sideways (strafe) movement multiplier applied while blocking. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: OnlySlowOnServerSide
settings.description: Blocking group (default false). When enabled, if you are detected as blocking server-side the original (slowed) movement is kept instead of applying the no-slow multipliers.

settings.name: Choice (Blocking)
settings.description: Selects the blocking bypass technique: None (default), Reuse, Switch, Blink, Interact, Grim2360, Grim2364-1.8, Grim2371, InvalidHand, or Intave14. Each manipulates packets/slot-switching differently to defeat a particular anti-cheat.

settings.name: Timing (Blocking Reuse)
settings.description: Reuse blocking mode: when the release/re-use packets are sent relative to the network tick. PreAndPost (default), Pre, or Post.

settings.name: Timing (Blocking Switch)
settings.description: Switch blocking mode: when the slot-switch packets are sent relative to the network tick. PreAndPost (default), Pre, or Post.

settings.name: Consume
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that removes slowdown while eating or drinking. Only active while using a consumable item.

settings.name: Forward (Consume)
settings.description: Forward movement multiplier applied while consuming. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Sideways (Consume)
settings.description: Sideways movement multiplier applied while consuming. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: NoBlockInteract (Consume)
settings.description: Consume group toggleable sub-feature (enabled by default). Cancels the block-interaction (use-item-on) packet when aiming at air while eating/drinking, helping bypass anti-cheats like Hypixel Watchdog.

settings.name: Mode (Consume)
settings.description: Consume bypass technique: None (default), Grim2360, Grim2364-1.8, InvalidHand, Grim2371, Jump, Intave14, or Release. Each uses a different packet trick to remove eating/drinking slowdown.

settings.name: Mode (Consume Intave14)
settings.description: Intave14 consume mode sub-option: Release (default) repeatedly sends release-use packets and releases at tick 3; New sends release packets only on the first ticks or when finishing.

settings.name: Bow
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that removes slowdown while charging a bow, crossbow or trident. Only active while using one of those.

settings.name: Forward (Bow)
settings.description: Forward movement multiplier applied while drawing a bow/crossbow/trident. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Sideways (Bow)
settings.description: Sideways movement multiplier applied while drawing a bow/crossbow/trident. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Choice (Bow)
settings.description: Bow bypass technique: None (default), Grim2360, Grim2364-1.8, Grim2371, or InvalidHand.

settings.name: NoBlockInteract (Bow)
settings.description: Bow group toggleable sub-feature (enabled by default). Cancels the use-item-on packet when aiming at air while using a bow/crossbow/trident to bypass certain anti-cheats.

settings.name: Bundle
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that removes slowdown while using a bundle.

settings.name: Forward (Bundle)
settings.description: Forward movement multiplier applied while using a bundle. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Sideways (Bundle)
settings.description: Sideways movement multiplier applied while using a bundle. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: Sneaking
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that reduces the movement penalty while sneaking. Only active while the sneak key is held.

settings.name: MinMultiplier
settings.description: Sneaking group: minimum movement multiplier enforced while sneaking. Default 1.0 (full speed), range 0.3 to 1.0. Lower values allow more vanilla-like sneak slowdown.

settings.name: Mode (Sneaking)
settings.description: Sneaking bypass technique: None (default), Switch, or AAC5. Switch and AAC5 send 1.21.5-style start/stop sneaking packets (require a pre-1.21.6 server via ViaFabricPlus).

settings.name: Timing (Sneaking Switch)
settings.description: Switch sneaking mode: when start/stop sneaking packets are sent. PreAndPost (default), Pre, or Post.

settings.name: Timing (Sneaking AAC5)
settings.description: AAC5 sneaking mode: when the start-sneaking packet is sent. PreAndPost (default), Pre, or Post.

settings.name: Soulsand
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that overrides the velocity multiplier applied when walking on soul sand.

settings.name: Multiplier (Soulsand)
settings.description: Velocity multiplier applied on soul sand. Default 1.0 (no slowdown), range 0.4 to 2.0. Above 1.0 makes you faster than vanilla; below 1.0 slows you.

settings.name: SlimeBlock
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that adjusts slime block behavior, forcing normal slipperiness and overriding the velocity multiplier.

settings.name: Multiplier (SlimeBlock)
settings.description: Velocity multiplier applied on slime blocks. Default 1.0, range 0.4 to 2.0.

settings.name: HoneyBlock
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that overrides the velocity multiplier applied when on honey blocks.

settings.name: Multiplier (HoneyBlock)
settings.description: Velocity multiplier applied on honey blocks. Default 1.0, range 0.4 to 2.0.

settings.name: PowderSnow
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that adjusts the slowdown caused by powder snow via its multiplier.

settings.name: Multiplier (PowderSnow)
settings.description: Movement multiplier applied in powder snow. Default 1.0, range 0.4 to 2.0.

settings.name: Fluid
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that cancels fluid push forces and optionally fluid collision, reducing how much water/lava slows or pushes you.

settings.name: Collision
settings.description: Fluid group (default true). When enabled, fluid collision checks remain active; when disabled, the player's fluid collision check is cancelled so fluids do not slow movement as much.

settings.name: Slowness
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that counteracts the Slowness potion effect by adding a positive movement-speed modifier scaled by the effect's amplifier.

settings.name: PerLevelMultiplier
settings.description: Slowness group: how much movement-speed reduction is removed per Slowness level. Default 0.0 (no compensation), range 0.0 to 0.15. At 0.15 it fully negates the vanilla per-level slowness. On disable it resets to 0.15.

modules.name: NoSlowBreak
modules.summary: NoSlowBreak automatically restores your block-breaking speed in situations that would normally slow it down. It does not change anything by itself; instead it flags specific negative conditions (mining fatigue, breaking while airborne, breaking underwater) so that the client's mining logic ignores the speed penalty for the conditions you select. Only the conditions enabled in the 'When' option are compensated for.
useCases: Keep mining at full speed while standing on a ladder, floating, or otherwise off the ground.
Negate the slowdown from a Mining Fatigue effect (e.g. from an Elder Guardian) while breaking blocks.
Break blocks underwater without the usual underwater mining penalty by enabling the Underwater option.

settings.name: When
settings.description: Selects which slowdown situations the module compensates for. Options are MiningFatigue (ignore the Mining Fatigue potion effect penalty), OnAir (ignore the penalty for breaking while not on the ground), and Underwater (ignore the underwater breaking penalty). By default MiningFatigue and OnAir are enabled and Underwater is disabled. Each enabled option independently removes the corresponding mining-speed penalty.

modules.name: NoSwing
modules.summary: NoSwing suppresses the arm/hand swing animation that normally plays when you attack, use an item, or break a block. It can hide the swing visually for you (the client side) and/or stop the swing from being shown to or sent for the server side, depending on which targets you select. With nothing selected it does nothing.
useCases: Hide your own distracting swing animation for a cleaner first-person view.
Prevent the server (and thus other players) from seeing your swing animation, which some anti-cheats or players use to read your attacks.

settings.name: HideFor
settings.description: Multi-select of where the swing animation is hidden. Options are Client (hides the swing locally on your own screen) and Server (suppresses the swing for the server side / what is sent). You may enable neither, one, or both; with neither selected the module has no effect. No options are enabled by default.

modules.name: Notebot
modules.summary: Notebot automatically plays note-block songs loaded from NBS (Note Block Studio) files by tuning and striking nearby note blocks in the correct sequence. On enable it loads the chosen song, scans surrounding note blocks within range, verifies that the required instruments/blocks are present, then progresses through Test, Tune and Play stages, rotating toward and interacting with blocks. It cannot run in creative mode, while PacketMine is enabled, or outside a game, and it disables itself when you quit. The matched blocks are highlighted with a fading box renderer whose colors change per stage.
useCases: Automatically performing a song on a wall or grid of note blocks from an NBS file.
Playing music in survival multiplayer by having the client tune and hit note blocks for you.
Reusing already-tuned note blocks across plays to avoid re-tuning every time.

settings.name: Song
settings.description: File picker for the NBS song file to load and play. The selected file is read on enable to provide the note sequence.

settings.name: PianoOnly
settings.description: When enabled (default false), every note is played using only the piano/harp instrument instead of the song's original instruments, so only harp note blocks are required.

settings.name: ReuseBlocks
settings.description: When enabled (default true), already-tuned note blocks are reused between playthroughs rather than re-tuned. Changing this setting forces the module to disable itself.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum reach distance (in blocks) for scanning and interacting with note blocks. Default 6, range 1 to 6.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the module keeps operating even while an inventory/GUI is open. Disable to pause interaction when an inventory is open.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Value group holding the per-stage start delays before each phase begins.

settings.name: Test
settings.description: Child of StartDelay. Ticks to wait before the Test stage starts. Default 0, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: Tune
settings.description: Child of StartDelay. Ticks to wait before the Tune stage starts. Default 0, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: Play
settings.description: Child of StartDelay. Ticks to wait before the Play stage starts. Default 2, range 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Shared rotation-engine configuration group used when aiming at note blocks. Contains AngleSmooth (rotation smoothing mode controlling how fast rotations turn toward the target), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1 to 180) and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks).

settings.name: Render
settings.description: Toggleable block-highlight renderer (enabled by default) that draws fading boxes around the note blocks involved in the song. Provides all the child settings below in addition to its own enable toggle.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: Child of Render. When enabled (default true), adjacent highlighted boxes are merged/culled together to reduce overhead and visual clutter.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: Child of Render. Starting scale of a box when it fades in. Default 1, range 0 to 2.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: Child of Render. Easing curve applied to the start-size animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: Child of Render. Final scale of a box. Default 0.8, range 0 to 2.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: Child of Render. Easing curve applied to the end-size animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: Child of Render. Easing curve used for the fade-in opacity animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: Child of Render. Easing curve used for the fade-out opacity animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: Child of Render. Duration of the fade-in animation in milliseconds. Default 500, range 0 to 5000 ms.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: Child of Render. Duration of the fade-out animation in milliseconds. Default 500, range 0 to 5000 ms.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of Render. Fill color of the highlight boxes during the Play stage. Default green with alpha 90.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Outline color of the highlight boxes during the Play stage. Default green at full alpha (255).

settings.name: TestColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Fill color of the highlight boxes during the Test stage. Default red with alpha 90.

settings.name: TestOutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Outline color of the highlight boxes during the Test stage. Default red.

settings.name: TuneColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Fill color of the highlight boxes during the Tune stage. Default yellow with alpha 90.

settings.name: TuneOutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Render. Outline color of the highlight boxes during the Tune stage. Default yellow.

modules.name: Notifier
modules.summary: Notifier reports a variety of player-related events to you, either as chat messages or pop-up notifications. It can announce when players join or leave, change game mode, consume (eat/drink) an item, hold specific tracked items, or pop a totem of undying. Each message uses a customizable format string with placeholders, and bot players (per AntiBot) and the local player are excluded from most tracking.
useCases: Getting alerts when players join or leave the server, or change game mode.
Tracking when nearby players eat/drink (e.g. golden apples) or pop totems during combat.
Watching when opponents pull out specific items like end crystals or enchanted golden apples.

settings.name: JoinMessages
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, announces when a player joins (their profile name added to the tab list, name length > 2).

settings.name: JoinMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for join announcements. Default '%s joined', where %s is the player's name.

settings.name: LeaveMessages
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, announces when a player leaves (removed from the player info list, name length >= 2).

settings.name: LeaveMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for leave announcements. Default '%s left', where %s is the player's name.

settings.name: GameModeMessages
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, announces when a tracked player's game mode actually changes (not during initial join).

settings.name: GameModeMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for game-mode-change announcements. Default '%s changed their game mode to %s' (name, new game mode).

settings.name: ItemConsumptionMessages
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, announces when a remote player finishes consuming an eatable/drinkable item; tracks usage per tick and reports on completion.

settings.name: ItemConsumptionMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for item-consumption announcements. Default '%1$s used %2$s' (player name, item name).

settings.name: HeldItemMessages
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, announces when a remote player holds one of the tracked HeldItems in either hand (or switches to it).

settings.name: HeldItemMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for held-item announcements. Default '%1$s holds %2$s x%3$s in %4$s' (player name, item name, stack count, hand).

settings.name: HeldItems
settings.description: Item selection list determining which held items trigger HeldItemMessages. Defaults to End Crystal and Enchanted Golden Apple. Only items in this set are reported when held.

settings.name: TotemPopMessages
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, announces when a (non-friend, non-local) player pops a Totem of Undying, including a running count of how many times that player has popped.

settings.name: TotemPopMessageFormat
settings.description: Format string for totem-pop announcements. Default '%1$s popped a totem %2$s times' (player name, pop count).

settings.name: UseNotification
settings.description: Default false. When false, all Notifier messages are printed to chat; when true, they are shown as pop-up notifications (INFO severity) instead.

modules.name: NoWeb
modules.summary: NoWeb removes or works around the movement slowdown caused by cobwebs. Depending on the selected mode it either fully cancels web collision in the air, breaks the web to bypass certain anticheats, applies strafe/jump boosts to push through, or places and picks up water buckets to destroy the webs. It is mutually exclusive with AvoidHazards' cobweb option: if AvoidHazards is enabled with cobwebs selected, NoWeb will disable AvoidHazards and show a compatibility error.
useCases: Maintaining normal movement speed when running through cobweb traps in PvP or on minigame maps.
Bypassing anticheats (Grim, Vulcan, Intave) that would otherwise flag attempts to ignore web slowdown.
Clearing cobwebs out of your path entirely by breaking them or flooding them with water.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how web slowdown is handled. Default is Air. Options: Air (cancels collision so webs never slow you), Grim2365 (breaks the web by sending dig packets to bypass Grim), Intave14 (applies periodic strafe and jump boosts to slip through webs, tuned for Intave 14), PlaceWater (places and retrieves water buckets to destroy webs), Strafe (applies a strafe boost, and optionally vertical motion, to push through webs).

settings.name: BreakOnWorld
settings.description: Grim2365 mode only. When enabled, also removes the web block locally in the world (needed to bypass BadPacketsX) in addition to sending the break packets. Default true.

settings.name: Strength
settings.description: Strafe mode only. Horizontal strafe strength applied each time you collide with a web, pushing you through it. Default 0.23, range 0.01 to 0.8.

settings.name: MotionY
settings.description: Strafe mode only. Toggleable sub-group; when enabled, overrides your vertical velocity while inside a web. Default disabled.

settings.name: MotionYStrength
settings.description: Strafe mode, inside the MotionY group. The vertical (Y) velocity applied to the player while moving through a web when the MotionY group is enabled. Default 0.6, range -2.00 to 2.00.

settings.name: OnlyOnGround
settings.description: Strafe mode only. When enabled, the strafe boost is only applied while you are on the ground; otherwise it is applied in the air too. Default false.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: PlaceWater mode only. Sub-group configuring the silent rotation engine used to aim at the web/water when placing or picking up the bucket. Contains AngleSmooth (rotation smoothing mode), MovementCorrection (movement correction relative to silent rotation, default Silent), ResetThreshold (degrees below which the rotation is reached, default 2, range 1 to 180) and TicksUntilReset (ticks before rotation resets, default 5, range 1 to 30).

settings.name: Pickup
settings.description: PlaceWater mode only. Toggleable sub-group controlling whether placed water is picked back up with a bucket after destroying the web. Default enabled.

settings.name: PickupSpan
settings.description: PlaceWater mode, inside the Pickup group. Float range (in seconds) defining the time window during which placed water remains eligible to be picked up; the lower bound is kept high enough for the water to spread at least one block. Default 0.8 to 3.0 s, allowed 0.5 to 20.0 s.

modules.name: Nuker
modules.summary: Nuker destroys blocks around you automatically. It picks a destruction Mode (Legit, which mines one valid block at a time with real rotations and respects normal break mechanics, or Instant, which sends many break packets per tick) and an AreaMode (Sphere of blocks within range, or Floor scanning a defined box layer by layer). A Filter/Blocks list controls which blocks are eligible, and target positions found within range are broken. The module auto-disables on quit and can render the block currently targeted.
useCases: Rapidly clear large amounts of terrain or structures around you using Instant mode with a high blocks-per-second setting.
Mine only specific block types (e.g. ores or a particular material) by setting the Filter to whitelist and listing those blocks.
Dig out a flat floor area within a defined region using the Floor area mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: The destruction strategy. Legit (default) mines one targeted block at a time with rotations and standard breaking; Instant sends rapid break packets to many blocks per tick.

settings.name: Mode > Legit > Range
settings.description: Reach for selecting/breaking blocks in Legit mode. Default 5, range 1..6.

settings.name: Mode > Legit > WallRange
settings.description: Through-wall reach in Legit mode. Default 0, range 0..6 (clamped to not exceed Range).

settings.name: Mode > Legit > ForceImmediateBreak
settings.description: If enabled, breaks the block immediately rather than respecting normal mining time. Default false.

settings.name: Mode > Legit > Rotations
settings.description: Dynamic rotation engine sub-group used to aim at the block being mined (AngleSmooth, MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold, TicksUntilReset).

settings.name: Mode > Legit > SwitchDelay
settings.description: Ticks to wait before switching to break a new target after the previous one. Default 0, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: Mode > Instant > Range
settings.description: Reach for selecting blocks in Instant mode. Default 5, range 1..50.

settings.name: Mode > Instant > BPS
settings.description: Blocks broken per server tick, randomized from this range. Default 40..50, range 1..200. Higher values destroy faster but are more detectable.

settings.name: Mode > Instant > DoNotStop
settings.description: If enabled, only START_DESTROY_BLOCK packets are sent without a matching STOP, leaving breaks open-ended. Default false.

settings.name: AreaMode
settings.description: Which region of blocks is scanned for targets. Sphere (default) scans all valid blocks within range; Floor scans a defined box region one Y-layer at a time.

settings.name: AreaMode > Floor > RelativeToPlayer
settings.description: If enabled, StartPosition/EndPosition are offsets relative to your block position; otherwise they are absolute world coordinates. Default true.

settings.name: AreaMode > Floor > StartPosition
settings.description: One corner of the box region to mine (a Vec3i, default 0,0,0). Combined with EndPosition to define the area.

settings.name: AreaMode > Floor > EndPosition
settings.description: The opposite corner of the box region to mine (a Vec3i, default 0,0,0).

settings.name: AreaMode > Floor > TopToBottom
settings.description: If enabled, Y layers are scanned from top to bottom; otherwise bottom to top. Default true. The first non-empty layer found is mined before moving on.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/Blacklist mode applied to the Blocks list to decide which blocks are valid targets. Default BLACKLIST (break everything except listed blocks).

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The block set used together with Filter to determine which blocks the Nuker is allowed to break.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: How the hand swing is shown when breaking blocks. Default DO_NOT_HIDE (visible swing).

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: If enabled, the Nuker keeps breaking even while a container/inventory screen is open. Default true.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable PlacementRenderer that highlights the last targeted block. Enabled by default (does not keep boxes), with sub-options for fade/size/color.

settings.name: TargetRendering > Clump
settings.description: Whether adjacent rendered boxes are merged/culled together. Enabled by default.

settings.name: TargetRendering > StartSize
settings.description: Starting box size for the fade-in animation. Default 1.0, range 0..2.

settings.name: TargetRendering > StartCurve
settings.description: Easing curve for the start-size animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: TargetRendering > EndSize
settings.description: Ending box size. Default 0.8, range 0..2.

settings.name: TargetRendering > EndCurve
settings.description: Easing curve for the end-size animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: TargetRendering > FadeInCurve
settings.description: Easing curve for the fade-in. Default LINEAR.
