settings.name: TargetRendering > FadeOutCurve
settings.description: Easing curve for the fade-out. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: TargetRendering > InTime
settings.description: Fade-in duration. Default 500 ms, range 0..5000.

settings.name: TargetRendering > OutTime
settings.description: Fade-out duration. Default 500 ms, range 0..5000.

settings.name: TargetRendering > Color
settings.description: Fill color of the rendered box. Default green with alpha 90.

settings.name: TargetRendering > OutlineColor
settings.description: Outline color of the rendered box. Default green at full alpha.

modules.name: Offhand
modules.summary: Offhand (also known as AutoTotem) manages what item is kept in your offhand slot, automatically swapping in the most relevant item for the current situation. It can keep a totem of undying equipped for survival, swap to crystals, gapples, strength potions or blocks depending on context (such as low health, holding a sword, KillAura/CrystalAura/Scaffold being active), and switch back to your previous item afterwards. Items can be triggered by health thresholds, predicted damage, bound keys, or a cycle key, and switching is performed using various packet strategies for compatibility across server versions.
useCases: Automatically keep a totem of undying in your offhand and re-equip it the instant your health drops below a danger threshold in crystal/anchor PvP.
Quickly toggle between offhand items (totem, gapple, crystal) on the fly using bound keys or a cycle key during combat.
Hold a gapple in your offhand only while holding a sword and KillAura is running, so you can eat without changing your main-hand weapon.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: Player inventory constraint sub-group (PlayerInventoryConstraints) that governs when and how inventory switch actions are allowed and timed. Contains StartDelay, ClickDelay, CloseDelay, MissChance and Requires.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Delay (in ticks) before beginning the inventory interaction. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Delay (in ticks) between inventory clicks. Default 2..4, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Delay (in ticks) before closing the inventory after interacting. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Percent chance to intentionally 'miss' an inventory action to look more human. Default 0..0, range 0..100%.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must be satisfied before inventory actions run. Options: NoMovement (not moving/jumping), NoRotation (rotation unchanged), NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat, and InventoryOpen (only act while the inventory is actually open). Default is none selected.

settings.name: SwitchMode
settings.description: How the offhand swap packets are performed. Smart uses SWAP_ITEM_WITH_OFFHAND where possible to send fewer packets (all versions); Switch performs a swap action (best on 1.16+ servers); PickUp performs 2-3 pickup clicks (all versions); Automatic chooses Switch or PickUp based on the protocol version (only works if ViaFabricPlus is installed). Default is Switch when ViaFabricPlus is not in use, otherwise Automatic.

settings.name: SwitchDelay
settings.description: Default delay in milliseconds before a non-totem item switch is performed. Default 0, range 0..500 ms.

settings.name: Cycle
settings.description: Keybind that cycles the statically held offhand mode to the next mode that can be cycled to. Default key H.

settings.name: Totem
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling automatic totem-of-undying offhand management. Enabled by default. Contains the totem switch delays, the Health sub-group, and SendDirectly.

settings.name: SwitchDelay
settings.description: Totem-specific switch delay in milliseconds (can be lower than the general switch delay). Default 0, range 0..500 ms. (Inside the Totem group.)

settings.name: SwitchBackDelay
settings.description: Delay in milliseconds before switching back from a totem to your previous item, allowing a separate/higher delay than other items. Default 40, range 0..500 ms. (Inside the Totem group.)

settings.name: Health
settings.description: Toggleable group that switches to a totem on low health and back when health recovers. Enabled by default. When disabled, the totem is kept statically in the offhand instead of health-gated.

settings.name: HealthThreshold
settings.description: Health value at or below which a totem is swapped into the offhand. Default 14, range 0..20. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: Safety
settings.description: Toggleable group for crystal PvP that lets you keep a useful offhand item longer when you are not exposed to the main damage source. Enabled by default. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: SafeHealthThreshold
settings.description: Health at or below which a totem is forced when you are burrowed or in a hole (i.e. exposed to explosions). Default 10, range 0..20. (Inside Totem > Health > Safety.)

settings.name: SubtractCalculatedDamage
settings.description: When enabled, subtracts the maximum predicted incoming damage from current health, leading to more aggressive (earlier) totem switching even when not strictly necessary. Default false. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: PredictExplosionDamageEntities
settings.description: Predicts explosion damage from entities such as creepers and end crystals to decide when to equip a totem. Default true. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: PredictExplosionDamageBlocks
settings.description: Predicts explosion damage from beds and respawn anchors in a 10-block sphere around you. Default false. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: PredictFallDamage
settings.description: Toggleable group that predicts fall damage and equips a totem if a lethal/relevant fall is incoming. Enabled by default. Ignores cases where NoFall is running, fall distance is small, or a fall-damage-blocking block is below. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: IgnoreElytra
settings.description: When enabled, fall-damage prediction is skipped while gliding with an elytra. Default false. (Inside Totem > Health > PredictFallDamage.)

settings.name: MissingArmor
settings.description: When enabled, forces a totem into the offhand whenever any armor slot is empty. Default true. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: SwitchBack
settings.description: When enabled, after a totem swap the original offhand item is restored once it is safe to do so. Default true. (Inside Totem > Health.)

settings.name: SendDirectly
settings.description: When enabled, ignores all active inventory requests and switch settings and sends the switch packets directly (immediately). Default false. (Inside the Totem group.)

settings.name: Crystal
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling end-crystal offhand management. Enabled by default. Lets you keep/swap a crystal in the offhand.

settings.name: OnlyWhileCrystalAura
settings.description: Restricts the crystal mode so it can only be cycled to/used while CrystalAura is running. Default false. (Inside the Crystal group.)

settings.name: WhenNoTotems
settings.description: When the totem mode finds no totem available, fall back to equipping a crystal in the offhand. Default true. (Inside the Crystal group.)

settings.name: CrystalBind
settings.description: Keybind to directly switch the static offhand mode to Crystal (and back). Unbound by default. (Inside the Crystal group.)

settings.name: Gapple
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling gapple (enchanted/regular golden apple) offhand management. Enabled by default. Contains WhileHoldingSword and GappleBind.

settings.name: WhileHoldingSword
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group: when enabled, a gapple is equipped to the offhand while holding a sword. Enabled by default. (Inside the Gapple group.)

settings.name: OnlyWhileKillAura
settings.description: When enabled, the gapple is only equipped while holding a sword if KillAura is also running. Default true. (Inside Gapple > WhileHoldingSword.)

settings.name: GappleBind
settings.description: Keybind to directly switch the static offhand mode to Gapple (and back). Unbound by default. (Inside the Gapple group.)

settings.name: StrengthPotion
settings.description: Toggleable group enabling automatic equipping of a strength potion to the offhand. Disabled by default. Equips a strength potion when you don't already have the Strength effect.

settings.name: OnlyWhileHoldingSword
settings.description: When enabled, the strength potion is only equipped while a sword is in your main hand. Default true. (Inside the StrengthPotion group.)

settings.name: OnlyWhileKillAura
settings.description: When enabled, the strength potion is only equipped while KillAura is running. Default true. (Inside the StrengthPotion group.)

settings.name: StrengthBind
settings.description: Keybind to directly trigger the Strength offhand mode. Unbound by default. (Inside the StrengthPotion group.)

settings.name: Block
settings.description: Toggleable group that equips a placeable block to the offhand. Disabled by default. Activates while Scaffold and/or Eagle are enabled.

settings.name: WhileScaffold
settings.description: When enabled, a block is equipped to the offhand while the Scaffold module is enabled. Default true. (Inside the Block group.)

settings.name: WhileEagle
settings.description: When enabled, a block is equipped to the offhand while the Eagle module is enabled. Default true. (Inside the Block group.)

modules.name: PacketLogger
modules.summary: PacketLogger is a debugging tool that prints every network packet (and its fields) that passes between the client and server. For each captured packet it shows the packet class name, its registry ID, whether it is a record, whether it was cancelled, and a list of its field names, types and values. Output can be sent to the in-game chat, written to a CSV file in the packet-logger config folder, or both. It is excluded from the auto-config because it is intended only for debugging.
useCases: Inspect exactly what data the client sends or receives to debug or reverse-engineer server behavior.
Record a session's packets to a CSV file for later analysis.
Filter to specific packet types (whitelist/blacklist) to watch only the packets you care about.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: How the C2SPackets and S2CPackets lists are applied. BLACKLIST (default) logs all packets except those listed; WHITELIST logs only the listed packets.

settings.name: C2SPackets
settings.description: The set of client-to-server (outgoing) packet types selected for the filter. Empty by default.

settings.name: S2CPackets
settings.description: The set of server-to-client (incoming) packet types selected for the filter. Empty by default.

settings.name: ShowFieldType
settings.description: When enabled (default true), each logged field includes its Java type in addition to its name and value (in chat output).

settings.name: OutputTarget
settings.description: Where logged packets are written. Options are Chat (default) and File; at least one must be selected (cannot be none). Selecting File creates a timestamped CSV file in the packet-logger config folder.

modules.name: PacketMine
modules.summary: PacketMine lets you mine a block by clicking it once, then automatically finishes breaking it for you using START/STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK packets, while you remain free to move or fight. It raytraces to make sure you can actually reach and look at the target (respecting Range/WallsRange), optionally rotates toward it, and can automatically switch to the best tool via AutoTool. It renders a shrinking/animated box showing breaking progress and supports several mining behaviors (Normal, Immediate, Civ) for different anticheat environments. Using it together with AutoTool is recommended.
useCases: Break a block in the background (e.g. while continuing to PvP or run) after a single click instead of holding left-click.
Bypass certain anticheats or mine on servers where a special packet pattern is needed, by choosing the matching mode (Normal/Immediate/Civ).
Quickly clear obstacles or mine ores hands-free while letting AutoTool pick the correct tool automatically.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the core mining behavior. Default Normal. Normal sends START then STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK once the block is broken and (optionally) waits for server confirmation. Immediate sends START and STOP immediately (cannot be manually changed mid-mine and cannot abort). Civ is tuned for Civ/anarchy-style servers (does not stop on block-state change and re-sends STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK to repeatedly break the same position).

settings.name: ClientSideSet
settings.description: (Normal mode) When enabled, also destroys the block client-side when finishing so it visually disappears immediately. Default false.

settings.name: WaitForConfirm
settings.description: (Normal mode) When enabled (default true), keeps the target after finishing until the server confirms the break and prevents switching targets in the meantime; when disabled, the target is reset immediately after the finish packet is sent.

settings.name: WaitForConfirm
settings.description: (Immediate mode) When enabled (default true), does not reset the target on finish, waiting for server confirmation; when disabled, marks the target finished and resets it right away.

settings.name: Switch
settings.description: (Civ mode) When enabled (default false), switches to a tool that can correctly mine blocks requiring a correct tool (using AutoTool if running, otherwise the best hotbar tool), then switches back. Lets you break blocks that only drop/break with the right tool.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum reach distance to a block when you have line of sight. Default 4.5, range 1.0 to 6.0. Targets farther than this cannot be mined.

settings.name: WallsRange
settings.description: Maximum reach distance to a block that is behind walls/obstructed. Default 4.5, range 0.0 to 6.0; it is clamped to never exceed Range. Set to 0 to refuse mining blocks you can't see.

settings.name: KeepRange
settings.description: Distance up to which an already-selected target is kept even if it leaves normal mining range. Default 25, range 0 to 200; clamped to never be below Range. Larger values let you walk farther from a block before the module drops the target.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Hand-swing animation used when starting/finishing a break. Default HIDE_CLIENT (swing is hidden from your own client). Other options control whether the swing is sent to the server and/or shown locally.

settings.name: Switch
settings.description: Tool-switching mode that decides when to switch to a mining tool and how breaking progress is calculated. Default OnStop. Always switches the whole time, PostStart switches after starting, OnStop switches only when finishing, Never never switches (progress is computed with the currently held item).

settings.name: AbortOnSwitch
settings.description: (Always tool mode) When enabled (default true), aborts the current mine if the held hotbar slot changes (server- or client-initiated) away from the mining tool, preventing mining with the wrong item.

settings.name: CancelAutomaticSwitching
settings.description: (Always tool mode) When enabled (default true), blocks other features from silently switching your hotbar slot while a mine is in progress (except PacketMine itself and AutoTool selecting the mining tool).

settings.name: SwitchMethod
settings.description: (OnStop tool mode) How the tool switch is performed. Default Normal (silent slot select, synced). Swap performs an inventory swap of the slots; Pick uses a pick-from-inventory packet and only works before 1.21.3 / requires ViaFabricPlus.

settings.name: Rotate
settings.description: When the module should rotate toward the target. Default Never. OnStart rotates only when starting, OnStop rotates only once progress reaches BreakDamage, Both rotates at start and stop, Always rotates continuously, Never disables rotations (relies on your aim).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Sub-group configuring the dynamic rotation engine used when Rotate is active. Contains AngleSmooth (mode selecting how the aim is interpolated), MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset (see child settings).

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: (Rotations) Algorithm used to smooth/spread the rotation over time toward the target. Available modes include Linear, Sigmoid and Acceleration, each with their own speed parameters. Default is the first (Linear).

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: (Rotations) How player movement is reconciled with the silent server rotation. Default Silent (rotation is sent to the server without turning your visible camera). Other options change movement to match the server rotation.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: (Rotations) Angular difference (degrees) below which the rotation is considered finished and may begin resetting back to normal. Default 2.0, range 1.0 to 180.0.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: (Rotations) Number of ticks without a new rotation target before the rotation resets back to the player's real view. Default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: When enabled (default true), rotations are still performed even while an inventory/GUI screen is open. When disabled, an open inventory blocks rotating.

settings.name: BreakDamage
settings.description: Progress threshold (0 to 1) at which the block is treated as broken / ready to finish. Default 1.0 (full break). Lowering it finishes earlier (e.g. for instant-mine setups), range 0.0 to 2.0.

settings.name: PostBreakDelay
settings.description: Extra delay (in ticks) after sending STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK before the next target may start. Default 6, range 0 to 10. Mimics vanilla's chained-break cooldown and helps avoid anticheat flags across different network conditions.

settings.name: AbortAlwaysDown
settings.description: When enabled, abort handling always uses the DOWN direction. Default false. Used by other features that mine through this module.

settings.name: SelectDelay
settings.description: Minimum time (ms) that must pass between clicks before you can select or unselect a target, so selecting/deselecting works reliably. Default 200, range 0 to 400 ms.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that renders an animated box around the mined block, shrinking/growing to visualize breaking progress. Contains the rendering sub-settings below.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: (TargetRendering) When enabled, merges adjacent rendered boxes/culls shared faces for cleaner rendering of multiple blocks. Default follows the module's clump=false here, so disabled by default for PacketMine.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Starting scale of the box during its appear animation. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 2.0.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Easing curve used for the start-size animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Final scale of the box. Default 0.8, range 0.0 to 2.0.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Easing curve used for the end-size animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Easing curve for the fade-in (appear) animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Easing curve for the fade-out (disappear) animation. Default Linear.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Duration of the fade-in animation in ms. Default 500, range 0 to 5000.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Duration of the fade-out animation in ms. Default 500, range 0 to 5000.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Fill color of the target box. Default yellow with alpha 90 (255,255,0,90).

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: (TargetRendering) Outline color of the target box. Defaults to the fill color with full opacity (alpha 255).

modules.name: Parkour
modules.summary: Parkour automatically jumps for you when you are about to walk off the edge of a block, letting you clear gaps without manually pressing jump. It uses a player movement simulation to detect that you would leave the ground on the next tick and triggers a jump only when you are moving on solid ground and are not sneaking or already holding jump/sneak.
useCases: Automatically jump across gaps and block edges while parkouring or traversing terrain.
Avoid accidentally walking off ledges by auto-jumping at the very edge.

modules.name: Particles
modules.summary: Particles spawns small decorative image-based particles in the world whenever you attack an entity, bursting out from the point of impact. The particles obey a simple physics simulation (gravity, drag and bouncing off blocks) and fade out after colliding or over time, and they are hidden when not in line of sight. It is purely cosmetic and provides a visual hit feedback effect.
useCases: Add a stylish hit-effect (stars, hearts, dollars, etc.) when fighting other players for visual flair.
Get clearer visual confirmation that your attacks are landing on a target.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Base size multiplier for each particle, from 0.5 to 2 (default 1). Particles also shrink over their lifetime regardless of this value.

settings.name: Count
settings.description: An integer range (default 2..10, allowed 2..30, unit 'particles') for how many particles spawn per attack; a random value in this range is chosen each hit.

settings.name: RandomParticleRotation
settings.description: When enabled (default true), each particle is rendered at a randomized rotation; when disabled all particles share a fixed orientation.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: horizontal speed multiplier applied to particle velocity, from 1 to 30 (default 15). Higher values make particles fly outward faster.

settings.name: BounceX
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: how much horizontal X velocity is retained (and reversed) when a particle hits a wall, 0.0..1.0 (default 0.8). 0 stops the particle, 1 bounces with no energy loss.

settings.name: BounceY
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: how much vertical Y velocity is retained (and reversed) on a floor/ceiling collision, 0.0..1.0 (default 0.6).

settings.name: BounceZ
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: how much Z velocity is retained (and reversed) on a Z-axis wall collision, 0.0..1.0 (default 0.8).

settings.name: Drag
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: horizontal velocity multiplier applied to X/Z when a particle lands on a surface, 0.0..1.0 (default 0.99). Lower values make particles slide to a stop faster.

settings.name: GravityFactor
settings.description: Child of the Physical group: multiplier for downward gravity (0.0..1f, default 0.8); the effective gravity is this value times 0.03125 per tick. Higher values make particles fall faster.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: The tint color (and alpha) applied to all particles (default red). The particle's alpha is further modulated by its fade-out over time.

settings.name: Particle
settings.description: Which built-in particle image(s) to use, chosen from Orbiz, Star, Dollar, Crown, Heart, Lightning, Line, Point, Rhombus, Snowflake and Spark (default Star; cannot be empty). When several are selected a random one is picked per spawned particle.

modules.name: Phase
modules.summary: Phase lets you move through solid blocks using one of several anticheat-specific methods selected via the Mode setting. The available modes target different servers/anticheats (Hypixel/Watchdog, Intave, a generic Blink-based method, and BlocksMC), each using a distinct packet or movement trick to slip through collisions. Only one mode is active at a time and the default is Hypixel.
useCases: Passing through walls or floors to reach otherwise blocked areas, such as before a round starts.
Choosing a mode that matches the target server's anticheat to maximize the chance of phasing successfully.
Escaping or entering enclosed spaces by clipping through blocks.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects which phase method/anticheat target to use. Options: Hypixel (default), Intave, Blink, BlocksMC. Only the chosen mode's behavior and sub-settings apply.

settings.name: Maximum
settings.description: Blink mode only: maximum number of ticks the player tick may be held/cancelled while blinking through blocks. Default 120, range 1 to 300 (unit: ticks). Limits how long the phase attempt is sustained before giving up.

modules.name: PingSpoof
modules.summary: Spoofs (artificially raises) your displayed ping by delaying incoming keep-alive and ping packets. Using the blink/packet-queue system, it holds back incoming server keep-alive and ping packets and only flushes them once the configured delay has elapsed, making the server measure a higher latency for you. It cannot be used in singleplayer and will automatically disable itself with an error message if you try. The module also disables while you are dead or dying.
useCases: Make yourself appear to have higher latency on a server, which can affect how some anticheats or players treat you.
Disguise your true connection quality by inflating your reported ping.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: The amount of artificial latency to add, in milliseconds. Incoming keep-alive/ping packets are queued and only released after this delay has passed since they arrived, so your displayed ping increases by roughly this amount. Defaults to 500 ms, range 0 to 25000 ms.

modules.name: Plugins
modules.summary: Plugins attempts to reveal the list of plugins running on the server using one or more techniques you select. It can run the '/plugins' command, the '/bukkit:plugins' command (which sometimes bypasses a blocked plugins command), and/or exploit command tab-completion to extract plugin names. It tries the selected methods in order, prints any plugins it finds in chat, and disables itself once done or when it times out; it also disables automatically when you leave the server.
useCases: Find out which plugins a server is running, for reconnaissance or to identify exploitable plugins.
Recover a partial plugin list via tab-completion on servers that have blocked the normal plugins commands.

settings.name: Try
settings.description: Selects which methods are attempted to obtain the plugin list. Options: Slash (run the '/plugins' command), ColonSlash (run '/bukkit:plugins', which may work when the plain plugins command is blocked), and TabComplete (exploit command tab-completion to extract some plugin names, with a 5-second timeout). Enabled methods are tried in order; if a command method gets a response the module stops, and TabComplete prints found plugins or an error message.

modules.name: PortalMenu
modules.summary: PortalMenu allows you to open and interact with menus (such as your inventory) while standing inside a nether portal, which the vanilla client normally blocks. It is a simple on/off module with no configurable options. Enable it to manage items or navigate GUIs during the portal transition delay.
useCases: Opening your inventory or other screens while inside a portal to swap gear or eat before teleporting.
Staying in a portal indefinitely while interacting with menus instead of being forced through.

modules.name: PotionSpoof
modules.summary: PotionSpoof lets you apply client-side potion (status) effects to yourself without actually drinking or holding the potion. It dynamically generates one toggleable group per status effect in the game registry, each named after the effect's localized English name. While a chosen effect's group is enabled, the module continuously re-applies that effect (and its attribute modifiers) to the player each tick; when disabled it cleans up the spoofed effect.
useCases: Granting yourself effects like Speed, Strength, or Jump Boost client-side to test or gain their attribute benefits without consuming potions.
Maintaining a desired effect indefinitely without it expiring, since it is re-applied every tick while enabled.
Selecting a specific amplifier level for an effect to control its strength.

settings.name: <per-effect toggle> (e.g. "Speed", "Strength", ...)
settings.description: For every status effect in the game registry, the module creates a toggleable group named after that effect's localized English name (disabled by default). Enabling a group spoofs that effect onto the player continuously; disabling it removes the spoofed effect.

settings.name: Level
settings.description: Child of each per-effect group. The amplifier level of the spoofed effect. Default 1, range 1 to 10. The applied amplifier is Level minus 1 (Level 1 = base effect, Level 2 = II, etc.).

modules.name: ProjectileAimbot
modules.summary: ProjectileAimbot automatically aims your held projectile weapon (such as a bow or other throwable) at the best enemy target by computing the correct launch angle for that item's primary-shot trajectory each game tick. It selects a target through a configurable Target value group and applies the resulting rotation through the rotation engine, but it does not fire on its own. It only adjusts your aim so that releasing the shot hits the chosen target.
useCases: Automatically aiming a bow or projectile weapon at the optimal enemy so your shots connect when you release.
Fine-tuning target selection (priority, FOV, hurt time) so the aimbot focuses the most relevant enemy.
Combining with a shooting/aura module that handles the actual release while ProjectileAimbot handles the angle.

settings.name: Target
settings.description: Target selection value group choosing which enemy to aim at. It exposes FOV, HurtTime and Priority described below (no distance range is configured for this module).

settings.name: FOV
settings.description: Target child (default 180, range 0-180 degrees). Maximum angle from your crosshair within which an entity is considered a valid target. Lower values restrict targeting to entities in front of you.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Target child (default 10, range 0-10). Maximum allowed hurtTime for a candidate target; only entities with hurtTime at or below this value are considered, letting you avoid or include recently-hit entities.

settings.name: Priority
settings.description: Target child (default Type + Health, cannot be empty). Ordered set of sorting criteria used to pick the best target. Options: Type (players first), Health (lowest health first), Distance (closest first), Direction (closest to crosshair first), HurtTime (lowest hurt time first), Age (oldest entity first).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine value group controlling how the computed projectile angle is applied. It contains the AngleSmooth mode selection plus MovementCorrection, ResetThreshold and TicksUntilReset described below.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Selects how rotations are smoothed toward the target angle (default Linear). Available modes are Linear, Sigmoid and Acceleration, each with its own sub-settings (see below).

settings.name: HorizontalTurnSpeed
settings.description: Linear/Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 180-180, bounds 0-180 degrees). Maximum yaw turn speed per tick; lower values slow horizontal aiming.

settings.name: VerticalTurnSpeed
settings.description: Linear/Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 180-180, bounds 0-180 degrees). Maximum pitch turn speed per tick; lower values slow vertical aiming.

settings.name: Steepness
settings.description: Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 10, range 0-20). Steepness of the sigmoid speed curve based on remaining angle difference.

settings.name: Midpoint
settings.description: Sigmoid AngleSmooth child (default 0.3, range 0-1). Midpoint of the sigmoid curve where turn speed reaches half its maximum.

settings.name: YawAcceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth child (default 20-25, bounds 1-180). Per-tick yaw acceleration range when turning.

settings.name: PitchAcceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth child (default 20-25, bounds 1-180). Per-tick pitch acceleration range when turning.

settings.name: DynamicAccel
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default disabled). When enabled, acceleration scales with target distance and uses separate crosshair acceleration values when on target.

settings.name: CoefDistance
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default -1.393, range -2 to 2). Coefficient multiplied by target distance to offset the acceleration range.

settings.name: YawCrosshairAccel
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default 17-20, bounds 1-180). Yaw acceleration used when DynamicAccel is on and the crosshair is on the target.

settings.name: PitchCrosshairAccel
settings.description: DynamicAccel child (default 17-20, bounds 1-180). Pitch acceleration used when DynamicAccel is on and the crosshair is on the target.

settings.name: AccelerationError
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default enabled). Adds randomized error proportional to acceleration to humanize rotations.

settings.name: YawAccelError
settings.description: AccelerationError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of yaw error proportional to acceleration.

settings.name: PitchAccelError
settings.description: AccelerationError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of pitch error proportional to acceleration.

settings.name: ConstantError
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default enabled). Adds a fixed randomized error to each turn.

settings.name: YawConstantError
settings.description: ConstantError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of constant yaw error per tick.

settings.name: PitchConstantError
settings.description: ConstantError child (default 0.1, range 0.01-1). Magnitude of constant pitch error per tick.

settings.name: SigmoidDeceleration
settings.description: Acceleration AngleSmooth toggleable sub-group (default disabled). Applies a sigmoid deceleration factor as the rotation approaches the target.

settings.name: Steepness
settings.description: SigmoidDeceleration child (default 10, range 0-20). Steepness of the deceleration sigmoid curve.

settings.name: Midpoint
settings.description: SigmoidDeceleration child (default 0.3, range 0-1). Midpoint of the deceleration sigmoid curve.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Rotations child (default Silent). Controls how the applied rotation interacts with movement input.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Rotations child (default 2, range 1-180 degrees). Angle threshold below which the rotation counts as reached and may reset.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Rotations child (default 5, range 1-30 ticks). Ticks after the target is reached before the rotation resets.

modules.name: ProjectilePuncher
modules.summary: Automatically attacks (punches) incoming projectiles such as ghast fireballs and shulker bullets to knock them back, acting as an AntiFireball defense. It scans nearby entities, predicts whether a fireball/bullet is actually heading toward you, silently aims at the closest threatening one, and attacks it when it is within range and your server-side rotation already faces it.
useCases: Deflecting ghast fireballs back at the ghast in the Nether or on minigame maps.
Knocking away shulker bullets to avoid the Levitation effect.
Auto-defending against incoming projectiles without manually timing your swings.

settings.name: CPS
settings.description: (Clicker) Attacks per second range used when punching projectiles; a value in this range is targeted. Default 5 to 8, max bound 60 clicks.

settings.name: Technique
settings.description: (Clicker) Click pattern used to distribute the attacks. Default Stabilized; options Stabilized, Efficient, Spamming, DoubleClick, Drag, Butterfly, NormalDistribution.

settings.name: AttackCooldown
settings.description: (Clicker, shown because it uses the attack key) When true (default), waits for Minecraft's miss/attack cooldown before attacking again, which is safer against anti-cheats that detect ignored cooldowns.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Maximum reach (in blocks) at which a projectile can be targeted and attacked. Default 3, range 3 to 6.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: How the hand swing is shown when attacking a projectile. Default DoNotHide.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: When true (default), the module keeps aiming/attacking even while an inventory screen is open (it does not consider the inventory state when rotating). Disabling it makes rotations respect an open inventory.

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Rotation engine value-group controlling the silent aim toward the projectile. Contains AngleSmooth (choices: Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1 to 180) and TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks).

modules.name: ProphuntESP
modules.summary: ProphuntESP highlights blocks that change or move in the world by drawing animated boxes around them. It can track falling-block entities, single block update packets, and bulk chunk section block-update packets, making sudden block changes easy to see. This is useful for Prophunt-style game modes (spotting disguised/moving blocks) and for visualizing server-side block changes in general. Boxes use the shared placement renderer with fade-in/out animations and are not kept once the block stops updating.
useCases: Playing Prophunt to spot props that move or update as blocks.
Detecting falling sand/gravel/anvils and other falling-block entities at a glance.
Visualizing server block updates (e.g. redstone, pistons, mined blocks) sent via block-update packets.

settings.name: Tracking
settings.description: Multi-select of which block-change sources to highlight (cannot be set to none). Options: FallingBlocks (highlight FallingBlockEntity positions each tick), BlockUpdates (highlight positions from single block-update packets), and ChunkDeltaUpdates (highlight all positions from section/chunk multi-block-update packets). Enabling more sources highlights more block changes.

settings.name: RenderBlockUpdates
settings.description: Toggle for the placement renderer group that draws the highlight boxes (enabled by default). When off, no boxes are rendered even though tracking still runs. Its child settings below control box appearance and animation.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. When enabled (default), adjacent highlighted blocks are merged/culled so shared faces between neighboring boxes are not drawn, producing cleaner combined outlines. When off, each block is rendered as its own full box.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The relative box size at the start of the fade-in animation (default 1.0, range 0.0-2.0). Controls how large the box is when a block first appears.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The easing curve used to interpolate the box size during the appear (start) animation. Default LINEAR; other easing functions change the acceleration of the size animation.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The relative box size at the end of the fade-out animation (default 0.8, range 0.0-2.0). Controls the box size as a block disappears.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The easing curve used to interpolate box size during the disappear (end) animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The easing curve applied to the opacity fade-in when a highlighted block appears. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The easing curve applied to the opacity fade-out when a highlighted block disappears. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. Duration in milliseconds of the fade-in/appear animation (default 500, range 0-5000). Higher values make boxes appear more slowly.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. Duration in milliseconds of the fade-out/disappear animation (default 500, range 0-5000). Higher values make boxes linger and fade out more slowly.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The fill color (RGBA) of the highlight boxes. Default is an orange tint (255,179,72) with alpha 90.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Child of RenderBlockUpdates. The outline color (RGBA) of the highlight boxes. Defaults to the same orange tint as Color but fully opaque (alpha 255).

modules.name: ProtectionZones
modules.summary: Visualizes the rectangular areas that would be protected by configured protection blocks (by default Emerald Blocks) and helps you plan optimal placement. It scans loaded chunks for the configured blocks, draws an outlined zone box around each one (plus a box on the block itself), highlights the zone you are standing closest to, and, when you are holding a protection block, shows a yellow placement indicator snapped to a grid so adjacent zones tile without gaps or overlaps.
useCases: Faction/anarchy servers where placing protection blocks (e.g. emerald blocks) creates claimed regions, letting you see exactly what area is covered.
Planning where to place your next protection block so coverage tiles seamlessly next to existing zones.
Spotting and avoiding entering areas already protected by other players' blocks.

settings.name: ProtectionBlocks
settings.description: The set of block types treated as protection blocks (block list). Defaults to a single entry, Emerald Block. Changing it restarts the chunk scan so the new block types are tracked and their zones rendered.

settings.name: RadiusX
settings.description: Half-width of a protection zone along the X axis, in blocks. Default 20, range 1..256. The full zone width is 2*RadiusX+1 blocks centered on the protection block.

settings.name: RadiusZ
settings.description: Half-width of a protection zone along the Z axis, in blocks. Default 20, range 1..256. The full zone depth is 2*RadiusZ+1 blocks centered on the protection block.

settings.name: RadiusY
settings.description: Half-height of a protection zone along the Y axis, in blocks. Default 383, range 1..383. The vertical extent is clamped to the world's min/max height.

settings.name: SnapToY
settings.description: Part of the PlacementIndicator group. When enabled, the placement indicator's Y level snaps to the reference zone's center Y instead of following your own Y position. Default false.

settings.name: RenderLimit
settings.description: Maximum number of zones to render, choosing the nearest ones to you. Default 16, range 3..50. Limits how many protection zones are drawn at once for performance/clarity.

settings.name: HoldBlockToRender
settings.description: When enabled, zones are only drawn while you are holding a protection block in your main or off hand; when disabled they are always drawn. Default false.

settings.name: ZoneFill
settings.description: Fill color of the highlighted zone box (the zone you are closest to, within 5 blocks and not already inside one). Default semi-transparent green (0,255,0,51).

settings.name: ZoneOutline
settings.description: Outline color drawn around every rendered protection zone box. Default opaque green (0,255,0,255).

settings.name: CenterZoneOutline
settings.description: Outline color of the small box drawn on the protection block itself (the zone's center). Default opaque cyan (0,255,207,255).

settings.name: IndicatorOutline
settings.description: Outline color of the grid-snapped placement indicator box shown while holding a protection block. Default opaque yellow (255,240,0,255).

settings.name: IndicatorFill
settings.description: Fill color of the grid-snapped placement indicator box shown while holding a protection block. Default semi-transparent yellow (255,240,0,51).

modules.name: QuickPerspectiveSwap
modules.summary: QuickPerspectiveSwap temporarily switches the camera perspective while its bind is held and reverts when released (it uses a hold bind action and disables itself on quit). It is intended as a quick way to peek in another view without permanently changing your perspective.
useCases: Hold a key to quickly peek behind or in third person, then automatically return to your normal view on release.

settings.name: RearView
settings.description: When enabled, the held perspective swap shows the rear/behind view rather than the front-facing third-person view. Default false.

modules.name: Radar
modules.summary: Radar draws directional pointer arrows around the center of your screen indicating the direction of rendered entities relative to where you are looking. The arrows rotate with your yaw so each one points toward the corresponding entity, and the radar can be tilted statically or based on your pitch for a pseudo-3D look. Pointer shape, size, color and distance-based opacity are all configurable. It is aliased as PointerESP.
useCases: Keep awareness of where players or mobs are around you, even outside your field of view.
Track only players (ignoring mobs) during PvP for a cleaner combat radar.
Color-code targets by distance or health to prioritize threats.

settings.name: Tilt
settings.description: How the radar plane is tilted: Static (default, a fixed angle) or ByPitch (tilt scales with your view pitch).

settings.name: Angle
settings.description: Child of the Static tilt mode: the fixed tilt angle in degrees, -90..90 (default 90). The vertical scale of the radar is the sine of this angle; 90 gives a flat top-down circle.

settings.name: Limitation
settings.description: Child of the ByPitch tilt mode: a degree range (default 45..90, allowed 0..90) clamping how far your pitch is allowed to tilt the radar in either direction (the negative bound is mirrored).

settings.name: Radius
settings.description: The radius from screen center at which the pointer arrows are placed, 2..200 (default 40). Larger values push the pointers further out from the middle.

settings.name: OnlyPlayers
settings.description: When enabled (default false), only player entities get a radar pointer; non-player entities are ignored.

settings.name: PointerMode
settings.description: The shape used for each pointer: Triangle (default, a drawn triangle), Image1 or Image2 (built-in triangle textures).

settings.name: Width
settings.description: Child of the Triangle pointer mode: the base width of the triangle, 1..100 (default 8).

settings.name: Height
settings.description: Child of the Triangle pointer mode: the length/height of the triangle, 1..100 (default 10).

settings.name: TailConcaveSize
settings.description: Child of the Triangle pointer mode: depth of the concave notch at the triangle's tail, 0..50 (default 2, capped at Height). 0 draws a solid triangle; larger values create an arrow-like notched tail.

settings.name: Size
settings.description: Child of the Image1/Image2 pointer modes: the rendered size of the pointer image, 1..100 (default 10).

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: How pointer color is chosen: DistanceHSB (default, hue by distance, fixed full alpha), EntityHealth (color by entity health), Static (a fixed color, default white with alpha 100) or Rainbow.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Child of the Static color mode: the fixed pointer color (default white with alpha 100).

settings.name: Alpha
settings.description: A distance-to-alpha curve controlling pointer opacity by camera distance. X axis Distance (0..200), Y axis Alpha (0..1); default keeps alpha at 1. Pointers whose computed alpha reaches 0 are not drawn.

modules.name: Reach
modules.summary: Extends how far you can interact with entities and blocks. The Entity sub-group increases your attack/interaction range against entities (and optionally allows reaching through walls), while BlockRangeIncrease extends your block-interaction distance. It works by modifying the game's attack-range and reach values.
useCases: Hitting enemies in PvP from slightly farther than the vanilla reach allows.
Interacting with or placing/breaking blocks at a greater distance than normal.

settings.name: RangeIncrease
settings.description: Entity sub-group: how many extra blocks are added to your entity attack/interaction range. Default 1, range 0..5 blocks.

settings.name: ThroughWallsRange
settings.description: Entity sub-group: the maximum range (in blocks) at which non-visible entities (behind walls) can be reached. Default 0 (cannot attack through walls), range 0..8 blocks; effectively capped at the interaction range.

settings.name: BlockRangeIncrease
settings.description: Extra blocks added to your block-interaction reach. Default 0.5, range 0..64 blocks.

modules.name: Replenish
modules.summary: Replenish (alias Refill) automatically tops up your hotbar stacks from matching items in your inventory whenever a stack drops to or below a threshold, so consumables and throwables never run out mid-fight. It tracks what was in each hotbar slot, can also refill slots that have gone completely empty, and supports faster refill methods (swap clicks and pickup-all/merge) as well as cleanup behavior. You can restrict when it operates relative to open inventory/chest screens.
useCases: Keep a full stack of blocks, snowballs, ender pearls or food in a hotbar slot during PvP without manual refilling.
Automatically restock a hotbar slot that was emptied (e.g. ran out of pearls) from spares elsewhere in your inventory.
Use UseSwap/UsePickupAll to refill with as few clicks as possible to stay quick against anticheat-sensitive servers.

settings.name: Constraints
settings.description: PlayerInventoryConstraints value group governing timing and conditions for the refill clicks. Contains StartDelay, ClickDelay, CloseDelay, MissChance and Requires (with the extra InventoryOpen requirement available since this targets the player inventory).

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Random delay (ticks) before the first refill action. Default 1..2, range 0..20.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Random delay (ticks) between refill clicks. Default 2..4, range 0..20.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Random delay (ticks) before closing the inventory if it was opened for the action. Default 1..2, range 0..20.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Percent chance to deliberately miss an action to mimic human error. Default 0..0, range 0..100%.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Conditions that must all be met before refilling. Options: NoMovement, NoRotation, NotUsingItem, NotBreaking, NotDuringCombat and InventoryOpen (require the player inventory to actually be open). Default: none selected.

settings.name: ItemThreshold
settings.description: The stack count at or below which a hotbar slot is refilled. Default 5, range 0..63. Slots whose item max stack size is at or below this threshold are not refilled. Raising it refills earlier (keeps stacks fuller).

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Minimum time (in milliseconds) between refill cycles. Default 40, range 0..1000. Lower values refill faster but more aggressively.

settings.name: ReplenishEmpty
settings.description: When enabled (default true), hotbar slots that have become completely empty are refilled using the item that was last tracked in that slot. When disabled, empty slots are forgotten and left empty.

settings.name: Features
settings.description: Optional refill behaviors. CleanUp (default enabled) refills from the smallest matching stacks first to consolidate clutter; UsePickupAll uses a pickup-all/merge-stack click to gather matching items at once; UseSwap uses a single swap click to move a larger inventory stack into the hotbar slot. Default: CleanUp only.

settings.name: InsideOf
settings.description: Controls in which open screens Replenish is allowed to run. Options: Chests (also run while a non-inventory container is open) and Inventories (also run while the player inventory screen is open). Default: none selected, meaning it runs normally but not while such screens are open unless the corresponding option is enabled.

modules.name: ReportHelper
modules.summary: ReportHelper (alias AutoReport) assists with reporting cheaters by automating two server-specific tasks. Its AutoReport sub-feature watches incoming chat for messages that mention you alongside another (non-friend) player and automatically runs a report command against that player. Its AutoConfirm sub-feature automatically clicks through the report confirmation/selection GUI on supported servers (Hypixel/Heypixel patterns). The module itself has no direct settings; everything is configured inside its two sub-groups.
useCases: Automatically report another player when their name appears in a chat message that also mentions you.
Automatically confirm a report through the server's in-game confirmation menu without manual clicking.
Speed up reporting suspected cheaters on supported servers like Hypixel.

settings.name: AutoReport
settings.description: Toggle for the AutoReport sub-feature (default disabled). When on, chat messages mentioning you and another non-friend player trigger an automatic report command against that player (each player reported only once per session/connection).

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: (AutoReport) Delay in ticks before sending the report command after detection. A random value within the range is used. Default 1..3, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: (AutoReport) Percentage probability that a detected target is actually reported. Default 100%, range 1..100%.

settings.name: CommandPattern
settings.description: (AutoReport) The command template used to report a player; '%s' is replaced with the target's name. Default 'report %s'.

settings.name: AutoConfirm
settings.description: Toggle for the AutoConfirm sub-feature (default disabled). When on, the configured server GUI pattern is detected and the report is confirmed automatically by clicking the appropriate slot and closing the menu.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: (AutoConfirm) The server GUI pattern to recognize. Hypixel (default, index 0) handles a 9x3 confirm screen with green/red terracotta and a player head; Heypixel handles a 9x1 selection screen, clicking the diamond sword (report as hack).

modules.name: ResetVL
modules.summary: ResetVL attempts to reset accumulated anticheat violation levels by repeatedly performing tiny up/down movements while on the ground, combined with a manipulated game timer. It runs a fixed number of repetitions and then automatically disables itself, showing a success notification. It only works against older or flawed anticheats that can be tricked into clearing violations this way.
useCases: Clear accumulated anticheat violations after using other cheats, to avoid being kicked or flagged, on servers with weak anticheats.
Quickly run a burst of movement spoofing to reset VL before performing a risky action.

settings.name: Times
settings.description: How many reset repetitions to perform before the module auto-disables and reports success. Default 10, range 1 to 50. Each repetition is one on-ground up/down movement cycle.

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: The game timer speed requested while ResetVL is active, which controls how fast the movement cycles are sent. Default 2.0, range 0.1 to 10.0. Higher values speed up the process; lower values slow it down.

modules.name: ReverseStep
modules.summary: ReverseStep lets you step down off blocks faster, snapping you to the ground below instead of slowly falling. It only activates when you are falling (not when you intentionally jump) and refuses to act if you are above unwanted blocks (water, cobweb, powder snow, hay block, slime block) or if the fall would exceed the configured maximum distance with no collision below. Three modes are available: Instant simulates the fall and teleports you down, Strict sets a fixed downward velocity, and Accelerator multiplies your downward velocity.
useCases: Quickly drop down from a ledge or block edge to gain a movement/timing advantage.
Descend stairs or terraced terrain faster than normal gravity allows.
Use Accelerator or Strict for a smoother, velocity-based descent that is less abrupt than Instant.

settings.name: MaximumFallDistance
settings.description: Maximum fall distance, in blocks, for which reverse stepping is allowed. Default 1.0, range 1.0 to 50.0. If your fall distance exceeds this, or there is no block collision within this distance below you, the reverse step is canceled to avoid falling too deep.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the reverse-step method. Default Instant. Options: Instant, Strict, Accelerator (each with its own settings below).

settings.name: Ticks
settings.description: (Instant mode) Number of simulation ticks used to predict the fall to the ground before snapping the player there. Default 20, range 1 to 40 ticks. Higher values allow snapping over longer/slower falls.

settings.name: SimulateFalling
settings.description: (Instant mode) Default false. When enabled, the simulated fall positions are sent to the server as movement packets while stepping down, making the descent appear gradual instead of an instant teleport.

settings.name: Factor
settings.description: (Accelerator mode) Multiplier applied to your downward (negative Y) velocity while falling. Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 5.0. Values above 1.0 accelerate your descent; lower values slow it.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: (Strict mode) Fixed downward velocity applied each tick while falling (player Y motion set to negative this value). Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 5.0. Higher values drop you faster.

modules.name: Rotations
modules.summary: Rotations makes your player model visually reflect the server-sided rotations used by other modules (such as aimbots), so your head and/or body turn to where the client is actually aiming on the server. It can optionally smooth these visual rotation changes and draw a line and/or dot showing the current rotation vector. This affects appearance and debugging only; it does not change the rotations sent to the server.
useCases: Make your character model turn toward targets that combat modules are silently aiming at, for a more legitimate appearance.
Debug or visualize where the client's rotation system is aiming using the vector line and dot.
Apply visual smoothing so server-sided rotation snaps look less robotic on your own model.

settings.name: BodyPart
settings.description: Selects which body parts of the player model adopt the server-sided rotation. Options are Head and Body. Only the selected parts are rotated to match the server rotation.

settings.name: Smooth
settings.description: Visually smooths the model rotation by interpolating toward the new rotation each tick. Default 0.0 (no smoothing), range 0.0 to 0.3. Higher values produce slower, smoother visual turning. This is purely visual and does not affect actual server rotations.

settings.name: VectorLine
settings.description: Color of a line drawn from your eyes outward along the current rotation direction. Default white with alpha 0, meaning the line is off; setting any alpha greater than 0 enables it.

settings.name: VectorDot
settings.description: Color of a small box (dot) drawn at the far end of the rotation vector. Default RGB (0, 128, 255) with alpha 0, meaning off; setting alpha greater than 0 enables it.

modules.name: SafeWalk
modules.summary: SafeWalk stops you from walking off ledges as if you were permanently sneaking, but without the visible sneak. It offers a simple Safe mode that simply flags the vanilla safe-walk behavior, and a more advanced OnEdge mode that detects when you are about to reach a block edge and actively manipulates your movement (stopping, inverting, or recentering you) for a configurable number of ticks. There is also a None option that disables the effect.
useCases: Building bridges or walking along narrow ledges without falling off and without the telltale sneaking animation.
Doing parkour or edge plays where you want fine control near drops via the OnEdge mode's stop/invert/center behaviors.
Safely traversing thin walkways in PvP while keeping full movement speed.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the safe-walk behavior. Default is Safe (index 1). Options: None (no effect), Safe (flags vanilla safe-walk so you never step off a block edge), OnEdge (predictive edge handling that rewrites your input near edges).

settings.name: Distance
settings.description: OnEdge mode only. Float range defining how close (in blocks) to an edge you must be before the module intervenes; a value is randomly picked within this range each activation. Default 0.1 to 0.15, allowed 0.05 to 0.5.

settings.name: Keep
settings.description: OnEdge mode only. Integer range for how many ticks the edge-correction behavior keeps overriding your input once triggered (a random value in this range is chosen). Default 1 to 2 ticks, allowed 1 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: OnEdge mode only. The edge-handling behavior: 'Stop' (default, cancels movement and jump near the edge), 'Invert' (reverses your directional input to back away), 'Center' (steers you toward the center of the last safe block). Note Stop falls back to Center if you are moving too fast to stop in time.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: OnEdge mode only. Integer range for how many ticks the player is forced to sneak when an edge is detected (random value within the range). Default 0 to 0 ticks (disabled), allowed 0 to 20 ticks.

settings.name: Jump
settings.description: OnEdge mode only. When enabled, forces a jump during the edge-correction window, allowing edge tricks. Default false.

modules.name: Scaffold
modules.summary: Automatically bridges by placing blocks under (or around) you as you move, picking the best block to use, aiming silently, and placing at a humanlike click rate. It supports multiple bridging techniques (Normal, Expand, GodBridge, Breezily), tower modes for going straight up while holding jump, movement prediction to place ahead of where you will be, and many anti-cheat oriented helpers (sprint control, strafe, speed limiter, blink/fake-lag, eagle/sneak, telly jumping). Block selection prefers solid, full-cube, walkable blocks and avoids unfavorable or disallowed blocks, and a placement renderer can visualize placed blocks.
useCases: Bridging quickly and safely across gaps in PvP/bedwars-style games without manually placing each block.
Towering straight upward while holding jump (e.g. for height advantage) using one of the tower modes.
Bypassing specific server anti-cheats by selecting a matching technique (GodBridge, Breezily, Telly) and tuning sprint/strafe/blink helpers.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Tick delay applied after a successful placement before the next placement. Default 0 to 0 (no delay), range 0 to 40 ticks; a random value in the range is chosen each time.

settings.name: MinDist
settings.description: Minimum horizontal distance from the player's eye to the targeted block face required before a placement is considered valid, on non-vertical faces. Default 0.0, range 0.0 to 0.25. Higher values reject placements that are too close.

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: Game-speed timer multiplier requested while scaffolding. Default 1.0 (no change), range 0.01 to 10. Values other than 1 speed up or slow down the client tick rate.

settings.name: BlockItemSelection
settings.description: Value-group controlling which blocks are usable. Contains Disallowed (multiEnum/block list, default TNT, Cobweb, Nether Portal) blocks that may never be placed and are not counted as blocks, and Unfavorable (block list, default Crafting Table, Jigsaw, Smithing Table, Fletching Table, Enchanting Table, Cauldron, Magma Block) blocks that are only used when no better option exists.

settings.name: AutoBlock
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that silently switches your hotbar to a valid block when needed. Child Always (boolean, default false) keeps a block held at all times; SlotResetDelay (int, default 5, range 0 to 40 ticks) controls how long before the silent slot resets; DoNotUseBelowCount (int, default 1, range 0 to 64) avoids consuming stacks at or below this count when alternatives exist.

settings.name: Prediction
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that predicts your future placement position so rotations/placements lead your movement. Child BootstrapBackoff (float, default 0.2, range 0.0 to 0.4) is how far the bootstrap prediction stays behind the detected edge before history exists; PredictionCutoffDistance (float, default 0.05, range 0.0 to 0.3) disables future-position prediction when this close to the edge; WarmupPlacements (int, default 2, range 0 to 4) is how many recorded placements are used to blend bootstrap into history-based prediction.

settings.name: Technique
settings.description: Selects the bridging technique. Options: Normal (default), Expand, GodBridge, Breezily. Each technique has its own sub-settings (documented below).

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: (Normal technique) How the target point on the block face is chosen. Options Center, Random, Stabilized (default), NearestRotation, ReverseYaw, DiagonalYaw, AngleYaw, EdgePoint.

settings.name: RequiresSight
settings.description: (Normal technique) When true, only places if a raycast from the player actually hits the intended block, requiring line of sight. Default false.

settings.name: Eagle
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default off) Sneaks near block edges so you do not fall off. Child BlocksToEagle (range, default 0..0, range 0 to 10) how many blocks between eagle resets; EdgeDistance (range, default 0.01..0.05, range 0.01 to 1.3) how close to the edge triggers sneaking; OnlyOnGround (boolean, default true) only eagle while grounded.

settings.name: Telly
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default off) Makes the player jump while moving for a faster telly-bridge. Child ResetMode (enum, default Reset; options Reverse, Reset) how rotation/jump is handled; Straight (int, default 0, range 0 to 5 ticks); Jump (range, default 0..0, range 0 to 10 ticks) ticks between jumps; AimOnTower (boolean, default true) keep aiming while towering.

settings.name: Down
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default off) Scaffolds downward, dropping you onto blocks placed below when you hold sneak. No child settings.

settings.name: StabilizeMovement
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default on) Nudges your movement input back toward the optimal bridging line to keep you centered while bridging. No child settings.

settings.name: Ceiling
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default off) Allows building a ceiling above you (placing blocks higher) when there is a solid block below. No child settings.

settings.name: HeadHitter
settings.description: (Normal technique sub-group, default off) Automatically jumps when there is a block two above you and you are moving on the ground, useful for head-hitter style upward bridging. No child settings.

settings.name: Length
settings.description: (Expand technique) How many blocks ahead in your facing direction the expand technique tries to place. Default 4, range 1 to 10 blocks.

settings.name: Modes
settings.description: (GodBridge technique) Which anti-fall ledge actions may be used: Jump (default), Sneak, StopInput, Backwards. At least one must be selected.

settings.name: ForceSneakBelowCount
settings.description: (GodBridge technique) When your block count is below this number, force the Sneak ledge action instead of a random mode for safety. Default 3, range 0 to 10.

settings.name: SneakTime
settings.description: (GodBridge technique) Number of ticks to sneak when the Sneak ledge action is used. Default 1 to 1, range 1 to 10.

settings.name: EdgeDistance
settings.description: (Breezily technique) Distance from the block edge used to decide when to strafe left/right while breezily bridging. Default 0.45 to 0.5 blocks, range 0.25 to 0.5; a random value in range is chosen as you move.

settings.name: SameY
settings.description: Controls keeping placed blocks at a fixed Y level. Options Off (default), On (place at player's level), Falling (same as On but only while not rising), Hypixel (Hypixel-specific behavior tied to jumps and a specific fall velocity).

settings.name: Tower
settings.description: Tower mode used to go straight up while holding jump. Options None (default), Motion, Pulldown, Karhu, Vulcan, Hypixel. Each mode has its own settings (below).

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: (Motion tower) Upward Y motion applied each tower step. Default 0.42, range 0.0 to 1.0.

settings.name: TriggerHeight
settings.description: (Motion tower) Height above the jump-off position at which the next upward motion step triggers. Default 0.78, range 0.76 to 1.0.

settings.name: Slow
settings.description: (Motion tower) Horizontal velocity multiplier applied during the tower step (values below 1 slow you down). Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 3.0.

settings.name: Trigger
settings.description: (Pulldown tower) Vertical velocity (Y per tick) threshold below which the pulldown forces you back down; default 0.1, range 0.0 to 0.2. Note: the Karhu tower also has a separate Trigger (default 0.06, range 0.0 to 0.2).

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: (Karhu tower) Client timer speed requested while towering. Default 5.0, range 0.1 to 10.

settings.name: Pulldown
settings.description: (Karhu tower) When true (default), pulls the player downward once the upward motion slows past the Trigger threshold to stack blocks faster.

settings.name: SafeWalk
settings.description: How safe-walk (edge protection) behaves while scaffolding, reusing the SafeWalk module's modes. Options None, Safe (default) which prevents walking off edges, and OnEdge which has child settings Distance (range, default 0.1..0.15) edge distance, Keep (range, default 1..2 ticks), Mode (enum, default Stop; options Stop, Invert, Center), Sneak (range, default 0..0 ticks), and Jump (boolean, default false).

settings.name: Rotations
settings.description: Scaffold rotation value-group. Contains AngleSmooth (choices: Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration), MovementCorrection (enum, default Silent), ResetThreshold (float, default 2, range 1 to 180), TicksUntilReset (int, default 5, range 1 to 30 ticks), plus Scaffold-specific ConsiderInventory (boolean, default false) which lets rotations continue while an inventory screen is open, and RotationTiming (enum, default Normal; options Normal=rotate before placing, OnTick=rotate on the placement tick, OnTickSnap=rotate on the tick and keep the rotation afterward).

settings.name: SprintControl
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) overriding sprint state. Child Client (enum, default DoNotChange) and Server (enum, default DoNotChange) each choose how client-side and server-side sprint is forced: DoNotChange, ForceSprint, ForceNoSprint, NoSprintOnPlace, NoSprintOnGround.

settings.name: SimulatePlacementAttempts
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) that fires extra simulated use/place attempts to mimic legitimate clicking. Contains a Clicker sub-group (CPS range default 5..8, Technique enum default Stabilized, AttackCooldown if attack key) and FailedAttemptsOnly (boolean, default true) which only simulates attempts that would fail to actually place a block.

settings.name: Acceleration
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) multiplying your horizontal velocity. Child SpeedMultiplier (float, default 0.6, range 0.1 to 3) and OnlyOnGround (boolean, default false) to apply only while grounded.

settings.name: Strafe
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) applying a custom strafe speed while bridging. Child Speed (float, default 0.247, range 0.0 to 5.0), Hypixel (boolean, default false) for Hypixel-tuned speed behavior, and OnlyOnGround (boolean, default false).

settings.name: StrafeOnJump
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) that applies a strafe speed burst right after jumping. Child StraightSpeed (range, default 0.48..0.49, range 0.1 to 1) used when moving straight and DiagonalSpeed (range, default 0.48..0.49) used when moving diagonally; values are randomized to avoid pattern detection.

settings.name: SpeedLimiter
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) that cancels movement input when your horizontal speed exceeds a limit. Child SpeedLimit (float, default 0.11, range 0.01 to 0.4).

settings.name: Blink
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off) that queues outgoing packets (fake lag) around placements. Child Time (range, default 50..250, range 0 to 3000 ms) for how long packets are held after a placement, and FlushOn (multiEnum) selecting conditions that immediately flush the queue: Place, Towering, Sneaking, NotSneaking, OnGround, InAir.

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Hand swing visibility mode when placing blocks. Default DoNotHide.

settings.name: AutoSpeed
settings.description: When true, temporarily enables the Speed module while Scaffold is active. Default false.

settings.name: Ledge
settings.description: Enables the ledge helper (auto-jump and auto-sneak at ledges) to avoid falling off while bridging. Default true.

settings.name: Render
settings.description: Toggleable PlacementRenderer group (enabled by default) that draws the blocks Scaffold places. Child settings: Clump (boolean) merges adjacent boxes; StartSize (float, default 1, range 0 to 2) and EndSize (float, default 0.8) box sizes; StartCurve/EndCurve/FadeInCurve/FadeOutCurve (enum easing, default Linear); InTime (int, default 500, range 0 to 5000 ms) and OutTime (int, default 500) fade durations; Color (color) fill color; OutlineColor (color) outline color.

modules.name: ServerCrasher
modules.summary: ServerCrasher attempts to crash, lag, or otherwise disrupt a multiplayer server by sending a chosen malicious exploit payload. You select one exploit from a list of version-, plugin-, and platform-specific attacks, and it fires when the module is enabled (most exploits disable the module automatically after firing). It refuses to run in singleplayer (it disables itself with an error message if you are on a local/integrated server) and turns itself off when you quit. It is excluded from auto-config since these exploits are rare edge cases.
useCases: Testing whether a specific server build or plugin is vulnerable to a known crash exploit during a security audit of your own server.
Demonstrating a particular CVE/exploit (e.g. Log4j, Paper completion overflow) against a server you control.
Choosing a targeted exploit for a known software stack (e.g. PaperMC version, WorldEdit/Essentials/PermissionsEx plugins).

settings.name: Exploit
settings.description: Selects which crash exploit to use; defaults to BundleExploit-1.21.4. Options: BundleExploit-1.21.4, PaperCompletion-1.20.2, PaperWindow-1.20.1, TranslationSign-1.8 (version-specific), InvalidPosition (generic), GrimConsoleSpammer, WorldEditCalc, PermissionsExPromote, EssentialsPayStar (plugin-specific), Log4jChat and Log4jTell (platform-specific). Only the chosen exploit's sub-settings (listed below) are active.

settings.name: AutoMode
settings.description: Sub-option of the PaperCompletion-1.20.2 exploit. Default true. When enabled, the exploit automatically cycles through all known working tab-completion commands (msg, tell, teammsg, etc.) sending oversized command-suggestion payloads each tick, then disables the module. When disabled, it sends only the single user-provided Message template once.

settings.name: Packets
settings.description: Sub-option of the PaperCompletion-1.20.2 exploit. Default 3, range 1..5. Number of malformed command-suggestion packets sent per attempt; higher values increase crash likelihood but also load.

settings.name: Length
settings.description: Sub-option of the PaperCompletion-1.20.2 exploit. Default 2032, range 1000..3000. Controls the nesting depth of the malformed JSON payload (number of opening brackets), used when AutoMode is off; larger values produce a bigger overflow payload.

settings.name: Message
settings.description: Sub-option of the PaperCompletion-1.20.2 exploit. Default "msg @a[nbt={PAYLOAD}]". The command template used (only when AutoMode is off); the literal {PAYLOAD} placeholder is replaced with the generated overflow string. Excluded from auto-config.

settings.name: Packets
settings.description: Sub-option of the PaperWindow-1.20.1 exploit. Default 6, range 2..12. Number of malformed container-click (inventory swap) packets sent each tick to trigger the crash.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Sub-option of the InvalidPosition exploit. Default NegativeInfinity. Selects which invalid coordinate value to send in movement packets: NegativeInfinity, PositiveInfinity, NaN, MaxValue, or MinValue.

settings.name: Times
settings.description: Sub-option of the InvalidPosition exploit. Default 1, range 1..100. How many invalid-position movement packets to send in a burst before the module disables itself.

settings.name: Packets
settings.description: Sub-option of the GrimConsoleSpammer exploit. Default 1, range 1..100. Number of malformed raw packets written directly to the network channel each tick (waits 1 tick between bundles to avoid being timed out).

modules.name: SilentHotbar
modules.summary: SilentHotbar hides the visual effect of items that are being silently selected by other modules. When another feature swaps your held slot in the background (a 'silent' hotbar selection), this module prevents that item from actually being rendered in your hand. This keeps your first-person view showing your normally held item even while the client is internally using a different slot.
useCases: Keep your hand showing your real item while modules silently switch to tools/weapons in the background.
Avoid the visual flicker or cooldown animation that a silent slot switch would otherwise cause.

settings.name: NoCooldownProgress
settings.description: When enabled (default true), suppresses the item cooldown progress overlay/animation for the silently selected item, so the hand view does not show the cooldown swing or progress associated with the background slot switch.

modules.name: SkinChanger
modules.summary: SkinChanger changes the skin shown for your own player, either by copying another account's skin by username (Online mode) or by loading a local image file (File mode).
