It can optionally upload the chosen skin to your real Mojang account so it shows for everyone (only works on official PROD authentication with a non-legacy account; uploads are debounced by 3 seconds). With ForceOverride enabled it also forcibly overrides the local client's skin lookup, which is more reliable on servers where the player list entry is unreliable. Skin changes/uploads are re-triggered on enable, on session changes, and when relevant settings change.
useCases: Display a custom appearance by mimicking another player's skin via their username.
Use a personal skin image file locally without changing your account.
Actually upload a skin to your Mojang account so other players see it (requires an official, non-legacy account).

settings.name: ForceOverride
settings.description: When enabled (default false), forcefully overrides the client's player skin lookup (AbstractClientPlayer.getSkin) so the custom skin applies locally even on servers where the normal player-list skin is unreliable.

settings.name: UploadSkin
settings.description: When enabled (default false), uploads the selected skin to your real Mojang/Microsoft account so it is visible to all players. Uploads are debounced by 3 seconds and only succeed on the official PROD session host with a non-legacy account; custom auth endpoints (e.g. The Altening) and legacy accounts are skipped.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the skin source. Default is the first option, Online. Choices: Online (fetch a skin by Minecraft username) and File (load a skin from a local image file). Each mode has its own sub-settings.

settings.name: Username
settings.description: Online mode setting: the Minecraft username whose skin and model will be copied. Default 'LiquidBounce'. Changing it resolves the account's UUID/profile and applies that player's skin (and model variant when uploading).

settings.name: Image
settings.description: File mode setting: a path to a local image file used as the skin texture. When a valid file is set it is read, registered as a texture, and applied as your skin.

settings.name: Model
settings.description: File mode setting: the player model arm type used for the file-based skin. Default Default (wide). Options: Slim (slim/Alex arms) and Default (wide/Steve arms).

modules.name: SkinDerp
modules.summary: SkinDerp toggles the visibility of selected skin overlay layers (such as hat, jacket, sleeves, pant legs and cape) to make your skin appear to blink or flicker. It requires a multi-layer skin to have any visible effect. Each tick it either randomly shows/hides each selected part, or, in Sync mode, toggles all selected parts together in unison. On disable it restores whatever skin layers you had enabled before activation.
useCases: Making your skin flicker or 'blink' for a comedic or attention-grabbing effect.
Synchronously flashing chosen skin layers on and off as a coordinated visual.
Randomly glitching specific parts (e.g. just the cape or jacket) of your skin.

settings.name: Sync
settings.description: When enabled, all selected parts are toggled together in sync (each toggle flips them from their current state). When disabled (default false), each selected part is independently set to a random on/off state each cycle, giving a chaotic flicker.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Number of ticks to wait between each blink/toggle cycle. Default 0, range 0 to 20 ticks. Higher values slow the flicker down.

settings.name: Parts
settings.description: Multi-select of which skin overlay layers are affected. Available parts are Hat, Jacket, LeftPants, RightPants, LeftSleeve, RightSleeve and Cape. Only the selected parts are toggled; others are left untouched.

modules.name: SleepWalker
modules.summary: Also known as BedGodMode, this module lets you move around while you are sleeping in a bed and shrinks your hitbox by forcing a standing pose. Each tick, if you are detected as sleeping, it resets your pose to STANDING, clears your sleeping position, and closes the sleep screen so you regain control. The net effect is that you can act and move freely despite being in a bed.
useCases: Stay mobile and keep a small hitbox while occupying a bed, useful for avoiding being locked into the sleep state.
Escape the sleep screen instantly while still benefiting from being in bed.

modules.name: SmartEat
modules.summary: SmartEat makes eating and healing easier and safer by intelligently selecting the best food/healing item based on your current health and hunger. It can silently eat from a virtual offhand-style slot while you keep a tool in your main hand (with an optional HUD indicator), and it can auto-eat when your hunger drops below a threshold. It prioritizes special items (gapples, notch apples, instant-health potions) at configurable health thresholds and can pause combat or refuse to eat during combat.
useCases: Eat while keeping a pickaxe/tool selected by using SilentOffhand, so you never have to manually switch to food.
Automatically refill hunger when it drops too low via AutoEat, without manually managing food.
Prioritize gapples, notch apples, or instant-health potions at low health for clutch survival in PvP.

settings.name: SwapBackDelay
settings.description: Delay (in ticks) before the silent hotbar slot is restored after eating. Default 5, range 1..20 (coerced to a minimum of 5 in some paths).

settings.name: PreferGappleHealthThreshold
settings.description: Health at or below which the module prefers gapples / instant-health potions over normal food. Default 9, range 0..20.

settings.name: PreferNotchAppleHealthThreshold
settings.description: Health at or below which the module prefers an enchanted golden apple (notch apple). Default 2, range 0..20.

settings.name: PreferHealthPotHealthThreshold
settings.description: Health at or below which the module prefers a health potion / golden apple. Default 12, range 0..20.

settings.name: CombatPauseTime
settings.description: How long (in ticks) combat is paused for when eating, to avoid being attacked mid-eat. Default 0, range 0..40 ticks.

settings.name: NotDuringCombat
settings.description: When enabled, the module will not eat (silent offhand or auto-eat) while you are in combat. Default false.

settings.name: SilentOffhand
settings.description: Toggleable group: when enabled, lets you eat the best food from a silent slot while keeping a mining tool in your main hand, without visibly switching items. Enabled by default.

settings.name: RenderSlot
settings.description: Toggleable sub-group: when enabled, renders an offhand-style HUD slot showing the currently selected best food item. Enabled by default. (Inside the SilentOffhand group.)

settings.name: Offset
settings.description: Horizontal offset (in pixels) for the rendered silent-offhand food slot on the HUD. Default 40, range 30..70. (Inside SilentOffhand > RenderSlot.)

settings.name: AutoEat
settings.description: Toggleable group: when enabled, automatically eats the best food when hunger falls below MinHunger. Enabled by default.

settings.name: MinHunger
settings.description: Hunger (food level) below which AutoEat triggers; it eats until hunger rises above this value. Default 15, range 0..20. (Inside the AutoEat group.)

modules.name: SmoothCamera
modules.summary: SmoothCamera smooths the movement of the camera so it eases toward the player position instead of snapping, producing a cinematic, glide-like camera motion. By default it only applies in third-person views (first person is left untouched because it looks odd), and it can optionally reset instantly when you switch perspectives to stay responsive. Separate horizontal and vertical smoothing factors let you tune how much the camera lags behind on each axis.
useCases: Get smoother, cinematic camera motion while recording or spectating in third person.
Optionally extend the smoothing into first person by enabling EnableFirstPOV.

settings.name: EnableFirstPOV
settings.description: When enabled, camera smoothing is also applied in first-person view; disabled by default because smoothing looks weird in first person, where the camera otherwise tracks the player exactly.

settings.name: ResetOnPerspectiveChange
settings.description: When enabled (default), the smoothed camera position is snapped to the real position immediately when you change perspective, giving better responsiveness right after switching views; when disabled it eases in gradually.

settings.name: HorizontalFactor
settings.description: Smoothing weight for the X and Z (horizontal) axes (default 0.9, range 0..1). Higher values keep more of the previous position, producing slower, smoother horizontal follow; 0 means no smoothing (instant).

settings.name: VerticalFactor
settings.description: Smoothing weight for the Y (vertical) axis (default 0.93, range 0..1). Higher values make vertical camera motion lag more and feel smoother; 0 means the camera follows vertical movement instantly.

modules.name: SnapTap
modules.summary: SnapTap (also known as NullMove or SOCD) makes opposing movement keys prioritize whichever was pressed most recently. When both left and right (or both forward and backward) are held at once, instead of cancelling out, it forces movement in the direction of the last-pressed key. This enables instant counter-strafing for sharper direction changes. It only works in-game (or in inventory if InventoryMove is enabled).
useCases: Counter-strafing in PvP so tapping the opposite key instantly reverses direction instead of stopping.
Removing the dead-zone where pressing both opposing keys would normally cancel movement.

modules.name: Sneak
modules.summary: Sneak keeps your character sneaking automatically at all times without holding the sneak key. It offers several implementation modes (client-side Legit, packet-based Vanilla, and a 1.21.5-and-older Switch mode) and can optionally stop sneaking while you are moving. The Legit mode can also be restricted to only sneak when standing on magma blocks.
useCases: Stay sneaking continuously to avoid fall-off edges or hide your name tag without holding the key.
Use OnMagmaBlocksOnly (Legit mode) to automatically sneak only when on magma blocks to avoid damage.
Use Vanilla or Switch mode to enforce server-side sneak state on specific protocol versions.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how sneaking is applied. Vanilla (default) forces the sneak flag on the player input packet. Legit overrides the local movement input to sneak (and supports the OnMagmaBlocksOnly sub-option). Switch sends explicit start/stop sneaking packets and is only valid on servers older than 1.21.6 (it warns if used otherwise).

settings.name: OnMagmaBlocksOnly
settings.description: Sub-setting of the Legit mode. When enabled, sneaking is only applied while the player is (or is about to be) on a magma block and is not immune to them, so you only crouch to avoid magma damage. Default false.

settings.name: NotDuringMove
settings.description: When enabled, the module stops sneaking while you are moving (and in Switch mode disables itself while moving). Default false.

modules.name: Spammer
modules.summary: Spammer automatically sends messages (or commands) to the chat at a configurable rate. It picks messages either from a built-in editable list or from lines of a chosen file, in random or linear order, then optionally transforms the text (leetspeak, random casing, random spacing, etc.) before sending. Messages starting with '/' are sent as commands; messages longer than 256 characters are skipped with a warning. The module automatically disables itself when you quit the world.
useCases: Advertising or repeatedly broadcasting a message in chat at a set interval.
Driving a list of custom messages or commands from a text file on a loop.
Bypassing simple anti-spam filters by applying text conversions (leet, random case/space) to each message.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Float range in seconds (default 2..4, allowed 0..300) for the pause between each batch of messages. A random value in this range is waited after each cycle; smaller values spam faster.

settings.name: MPS
settings.description: Integer range of messages per cycle (default 1..1, allowed 1..500, labelled 'messages'). A random count in this range is sent each cycle before waiting for the Delay; raising it sends bursts of multiple messages at once.

settings.name: MessageSource
settings.description: Selects where spam messages come from. Two modes: 'Setting' (use the editable Message list) and 'File' (read lines from a selected file). Default is the first mode, Setting.

settings.name: Message
settings.description: Editable list of messages used when MessageSource is 'Setting'. Defaults to four built-in LiquidBounce advertisement strings. Depending on Pattern, one is chosen randomly or cycled through in order.

settings.name: Source
settings.description: File picker used when MessageSource is 'File'. When a valid file is selected its lines are indexed; each spam message is read from a line, chosen randomly or sequentially based on Pattern. If the file is empty or not selected, sending fails with an error.

settings.name: Pattern
settings.description: Order in which messages are selected from the active source. 'Random' (default) picks a random entry/line each time; 'Linear' cycles through entries/lines sequentially and wraps around.

settings.name: MessageConverter
settings.description: Text transformation applied to each outgoing message. Options: None (no change), Leet (default; substitutes letters like o->0, l->1, e->3, a->4, t->7, s->Z), Random Case (randomizes upper/lower case of each character), Random Space (randomly inserts extra spaces between characters).

settings.name: CustomFormatter
settings.description: Default false. When false, each message is automatically prefixed with a short random alphabetic tag in brackets and has Random Case applied before the chosen MessageConverter. When true, the message is instead passed through a placeholder formatter that replaces %f with a random float, %i with a random int, %s with a random alphabetic string, and @a with a random online player's name (excluding yourself) before the MessageConverter is applied.

modules.name: Speed
modules.summary: Speed lets you move faster than normal by applying one of many anticheat-specific bypass modes (e.g. LegitHop, Custom, Hypixel BHop/LowHop, Spartan, Vulcan, NCP, Intave, Grim, Matrix, Hylex, BlocksMC, Verus, Sentinel, YPort, PiercingAttack, etc.). The active mode is chosen from the Mode list and drives how the speed boost is achieved. It supports conditional activation (only in combat, only on certain potion effects), can be suppressed under chosen 'Not' conditions, and integrates with Scaffold's auto-speed.
useCases: Move and bridge faster on a specific server by selecting the matching anticheat bypass mode.
Restrict the speed boost to combat or to when you have Speed/Slowness potion effects to look more legitimate.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: The active speed technique (default index 0 = LegitHop). Each mode is tuned for a particular anticheat/server and may expose its own sub-settings. Available modes include LegitHop, Custom, SpeedYPort, PiercingAttack, VerusB3882, HypixelBHop, HypixelLowHop, SpartanV4043, SpartanV4043FastFall, SentinelDamage, Vulcan286, Vulcan288, VulcanGround286, GrimCollide, NCP, Intave14, Intave14Fast, HylexLowHop, HylexGround, BlocksMC, and Matrix7.

settings.name: Not
settings.description: Conditions that disable Speed while active (default: DuringScaffold selected). Options: WhileUsingItem (while using an item), DuringScaffold (while Scaffold or Fly is running), WhileSneaking (while shift-sneaking), IsFallFlying (while elytra flying), and IsInLiquid (while in water/lava).

settings.name: AvoidEdgeBump
settings.description: Default on. When enabled, Speed delays jumps when about to bump into a block corner/edge (anti-corner-bump), preventing speed loss from clipping into edges.

settings.name: OnlyInCombat
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off). When enabled, the speed boost only applies while you are in combat (per CombatManager); outside combat Speed does nothing.

settings.name: Mode (OnlyInCombat)
settings.description: Child of OnlyInCombat. A separate speed mode selection (default index 0) used specifically when the in-combat condition is active, drawing from the same full list of speed modes.

settings.name: OnlyOnPotionEffect
settings.description: Toggleable group (default off). When enabled, the speed boost only applies based on your active potion effects as configured by its PotionEffect sub-setting.

settings.name: PotionEffect
settings.description: Child of OnlyOnPotionEffect (default SpeedPotionEffectMode). Selects which potion-effect condition gates activation: SpeedPotionEffectMode (active when you have Speed), SlownessPotionEffectMode (active when you have Slowness), or BothEffectsMode (checks both effects).

settings.name: Mode (OnlyOnPotionEffect)
settings.description: Child of OnlyOnPotionEffect. A separate speed mode selection (default index 0) used specifically when the potion-effect condition is active, drawing from the same full list of speed modes.

settings.name: SpeedYawOffset
settings.description: A shared sub-tree (SpeedYawOffset) added to the module that configures yaw/direction offset handling used by the speed modes when adjusting movement direction.

modules.name: Spider
modules.summary: Spider lets the player climb straight up walls by automatically applying upward motion whenever the player horizontally collides with a block. It provides several modes, including a generic Vanilla mode and bypasses for specific anti-cheats (Polar, Vulcan 2.8.8). The behavior and tuning depend on the selected mode.
useCases: Climbing vertical walls to reach high places without ladders or jumping.
Scaling walls on a Polar-protected server using the Polar bypass mode.
Climbing on Vulcan 2.8.8 servers using the Vulcan288 bypass mode.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the wall-climb algorithm. Default Vanilla. Choices: Vanilla (applies a configurable upward motion while horizontally colliding), Polar-29.03.2025 (shrinks block collision shapes and jumps to walk up them, tuned for the Polar anti-cheat), and Vulcan288 (timed high-velocity climb bursts tuned for Vulcan 2.8.8).

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Child of Vanilla mode. The upward velocity applied each tick while horizontally colliding with a wall. Default 0.3, range 0.05 to 0.8. Higher values climb faster.

settings.name: JumpHeight
settings.description: Child of Polar-29.03.2025 mode. The jump motion used to hit the shrunken block collision shape while climbing. Default 0.55, range 0.42 to 0.6. Note from the code: Polar allows up to 0.6 high, but 0.55 is faster for catching the collision shape.

modules.name: Sprint
modules.summary: Sprint makes your character sprint automatically whenever you are moving, removing the need to hold or double-tap the sprint key. Depending on the chosen mode it can also sprint while moving sideways or backwards (omnidirectional), or even rotate your in-game movement so that you always sprint toward your input direction (omnirotational). It can optionally keep sprinting through conditions that normally cancel it (blindness, low hunger, collisions) and can be told to stop sprinting under certain situations to look more legitimate.
useCases: Maintain constant sprint speed in PvP or bridging without manually managing the sprint key.
Use Omnidirectional mode to sprint and sprint-jump in any direction (including strafing/backwards) for better movement control.
Use the Ignore options to keep sprinting on servers where blindness, hunger, or collisions would otherwise stop you.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the sprint behavior. Legit (default) only sprints normally when moving forward. Omnidirectional lets you sprint in every direction and adjusts the jump yaw so sprint-jump boosts apply in any input direction. Omnirotational additionally rotates your movement yaw each tick toward your input direction so you always sprint where you are heading.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Choose conditions that should be ignored so sprinting continues anyway. Options: Blindness (keep sprinting while blinded), Hunger (keep sprinting even when food level is too low), and Collision (keep sprinting despite collisions). None are selected by default.

settings.name: StopOn
settings.description: Defines situations in which sprinting is suppressed (used to look more legitimate when no velocity fix is active and movement isn't actually carrying you forward). Options: Ground (stop while on the ground), Air (stop while airborne), Sneaking (stop while sneaking), and UsingItem (stop while slowed by using an item). None are selected by default; this prevention is bypassed when omnidirectional sprint is active.

modules.name: Step
modules.summary: Step lets you walk straight up blocks (up to 1-1.5 blocks high) without jumping, as if the steps were ramps. It offers several modes ranging from a simple legit auto-jump to packet-based instant stepping and anti-cheat-specific bypasses (Vulcan286, BlocksMC, Hypixel) that simulate realistic jump motion to avoid detection. Each mode tailors the step height, motion sequence, and packet behavior to a particular server/anti-cheat.
useCases: Move up single-block ledges and stairs smoothly without manually jumping.
Use the Instant mode to step instantly while still sending a legit-looking jump packet sequence to bypass anti-cheats like NoCheatPlus.
Use a server-specific mode (Vulcan286, BlocksMC, or Hypixel) to step on that anti-cheat without getting flagged.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the stepping method. Default Instant. Options: Instant, Legit, Vulcan286, BlocksMC, Hypixel.

settings.name: Height
settings.description: (Instant mode) Maximum height, in blocks, that you will step up. Default 1.0, range 0.6 to 5.0. Higher values let you step up taller obstacles.

settings.name: Trim
settings.description: (Instant mode) Default false. When enabled, the simulated jump-order packet heights are clamped to the actual step height so you do not appear to rise higher than the block you stepped onto, improving legitimacy.

settings.name: SimulateJumpOrder
settings.description: (Instant mode) Index range into the predefined natural jump-motion curve that determines which jump packets are sent after stepping. Default 0..2, range within the jump curve indices (0 to 8). 0..0 sends nothing; wider ranges send a more complete simulated jump arc to bypass anti-cheats.

settings.name: Wait
settings.description: (Instant mode) Random number of ticks to wait between consecutive steps, in ticks. Default 0..0 (no wait), range 0 to 60. A random value in this range is chosen after each step to throttle repeated stepping.

settings.name: PacketType
settings.description: (Instant mode) Type of movement packet used to simulate the step jump. Options: FULL (default) and POSITION_AND_ON_GROUND. Affects how much positional/rotation data is sent in the step packets.

settings.name: BaseTimer
settings.description: (BlocksMC mode) Game timer (tick speed) multiplier requested during the step motion. Default 3.0, range 0.1 to 5.0. Higher values speed up the client during the step sequence.

settings.name: RecoveryTimer
settings.description: (BlocksMC mode) Game timer (tick speed) multiplier requested after the step to recover/slow back down. Default 0.6, range 0.1 to 5.0. Lower values slow the client to compensate for the sped-up step.

settings.name: AlternateBypass
settings.description: (Hypixel mode) Default false. For steps taller than 1.25 blocks, when enabled it forces on-ground status instead of applying an extra upward velocity, providing an alternate way to complete tall steps without being flagged.

settings.name: Spoof
settings.description: (Hypixel mode) Default false. When enabled, spoofs the on-ground flag to true during the step (specifically when air ticks equal 8) to help bypass detection.

modules.name: StorageESP
modules.summary: StorageESP highlights storage blocks and storage entities (chests, barrels, ender chests, furnaces, brewing stands, dispensers/crafters, hoppers, shulker boxes, decorated pots, shelves, and storage minecarts/boats/chested horses) so you can see them through walls. It scans loaded chunks for storage block entities and draws each type in its own configurable color using either a glowing outline (Glow) or filled boxes with optional outlines (Box). Each storage type can be toggled individually and optionally given tracer lines, and rendering fades out with distance.
useCases: Quickly locate chests and other loot containers in dungeons, mineshafts, or bases through walls.
Color-code different container types so you can distinguish, for example, ender chests from regular chests at a glance.
Restrict the ESP to only show while ChestStealer is active to reduce on-screen clutter.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Rendering style for the highlights. Choices are Box and Glow (default Glow). Box draws filled translucent boxes (with optional outlines); Glow draws a glowing outline around the storage.

settings.name: Outline
settings.description: Box mode only. When enabled (default true), draws line outlines around the filled boxes in addition to the translucent faces.

settings.name: RequiresChestStealer
settings.description: When enabled (default false), StorageESP only renders while the ChestStealer module is running; otherwise it is suppressed even when toggled on.

settings.name: MergeAdjacent
settings.description: When enabled (default false), adjacent tracked block shapes of the same type are merged into combined shapes before rendering, producing cleaner outlines for grouped storage.

settings.name: Chest
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether chests (and chest minecarts, chest boats/rafts, and chested horses) are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Chest group. The highlight color for chests. Default RGB (0, 100, 255), a blue tone. A fully transparent color disables rendering for this type.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Chest group. When enabled (default false), draws a tracer line from your view to each chest of this type.

settings.name: Barrel
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether barrels are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Barrel group. The highlight color for barrels. Default RGB (246, 130, 31), an orange tone.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Barrel group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to barrels.

settings.name: EnderChest
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether ender chests are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: EnderChest group. The highlight color for ender chests. Default magenta.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: EnderChest group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to ender chests.

settings.name: Furnace
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether furnaces (including blast furnaces and smokers) are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Furnace group. The highlight color for furnaces. Default RGB (79, 79, 79), a dark gray.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Furnace group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to furnaces.

settings.name: BrewingStand
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether brewing stands are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: BrewingStand group. The highlight color for brewing stands. Default RGB (139, 69, 19), a brown tone.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: BrewingStand group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to brewing stands.

settings.name: Dispenser
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether dispensers (and droppers/crafters) are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Dispenser group. The highlight color for dispensers. Default light gray.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Dispenser group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to dispensers.

settings.name: Hopper
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether hoppers (including hopper minecarts) are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Hopper group. The highlight color for hoppers. Default gray.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Hopper group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to hoppers.

settings.name: ShulkerBox
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether shulker boxes are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: ShulkerBox group. The highlight color for shulker boxes. Default a brightened purple based on RGB (110, 77, 110).

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: ShulkerBox group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to shulker boxes.

settings.name: Pot
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether decorated pots are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Pot group. The highlight color for decorated pots. Default RGB (209, 134, 0), an amber tone.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Pot group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to decorated pots.

settings.name: Shelf
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) controlling whether shelves are highlighted. Contains Color and Tracers sub-settings.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Shelf group. The highlight color for shelves. Default RGB (160, 82, 45), a sienna brown.

settings.name: Tracers
settings.description: Shelf group. When enabled (default false), draws tracer lines to shelves.

settings.name: DistanceFade
settings.description: Value group controlling how the storage highlights fade in and out based on camera distance, defined by four float distances (all range 0 to 512). FarEnd also acts as the maximum render distance beyond which storage is not drawn.

settings.name: NearStart
settings.description: DistanceFade group. Distance (in blocks) at which the near fade begins. Default 0, range 0 to 512; clamped to not exceed NearEnd.

settings.name: NearEnd
settings.description: DistanceFade group. Distance at which the near fade ends (highlights fully visible). Default 0, range 0 to 512; coerced between NearStart and FarStart.

settings.name: FarStart
settings.description: DistanceFade group. Distance at which the far fade begins (highlights start fading out). Default 512, range 0 to 512; coerced between NearEnd and FarEnd.

settings.name: FarEnd
settings.description: DistanceFade group. Distance at which highlights become fully invisible; also serves as the effective maximum render distance. Default 512, range 0 to 512; not allowed below FarStart.

modules.name: Strafe
modules.summary: Strafe gives you greater directional control over your movement, including while airborne, by redirecting your velocity toward your input direction. The strength of this correction can be set separately for when you are in the air versus on the ground, and an optional strict mode zeroes out horizontal momentum when you are not actively moving. It only acts on self-driven (player-controlled) movement.
useCases: Steering more sharply in midair, e.g. while jumping or falling, to reach platforms or dodge.
Eliminating momentum/slide when you stop pressing movement keys by enabling StrictMovement.
Fine-tuning ground vs. air maneuverability independently for combat or parkour.

settings.name: StrengthInAir
settings.description: How strongly your velocity is redirected toward your input direction while airborne. Default 1.0, range 0.0..1. 1.0 gives full strafe control in the air; 0.0 disables air strafing entirely (no effect while not on ground).

settings.name: StrengthOnGround
settings.description: How strongly your velocity is redirected toward your input direction while on the ground. Default 1.0, range 0.0..1. 1.0 gives full strafe control on the ground; 0.0 disables ground strafing.

settings.name: StrictMovement
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, if you are not actively moving (no input) your horizontal velocity (X and Z) is forced to zero, instantly killing slide/momentum so you stop dead instead of drifting.

modules.name: StrongholdFinder
modules.summary: Automatically tracks your Eye of Ender throws and uses a Bayesian estimator (similar to Ninjabrain-Bot triangulation) to predict the chunk that most likely contains a stronghold. Each time you throw an eye it samples the eye's flight angle, recomputes a posterior over candidate chunks, and shows the best guesses as colored planes in the world plus an on-screen overlay with the best chunk coordinates and a ready-to-use /tp command. It only operates in the Overworld and, once it detects actual end-portal blocks nearby, switches to highlighting those portal/frame blocks and drawing a guidance line to the closest one.
useCases: Speedrunning or locating a stronghold by throwing two or more Eyes of Ender and reading off the predicted chunk instead of manually triangulating.
Confirming and walking to the exact end-portal room once portal frame blocks come into render distance.
Tuning the estimator (sigma, hypothesis count) when playing on a server whose eye-throw mechanics differ slightly from vanilla.

settings.name: Sigma
settings.description: Assumed standard deviation (in degrees) of the measurement error on each eye-throw angle, used by the Bayesian estimator. Default 0.03, range 0.005 to 0.20. Larger values make the estimator more forgiving of noisy throws; changing it triggers a recompute of the posterior.

settings.name: HypothesisCount
settings.description: Number of candidate stronghold hypotheses generated and evaluated by the estimator. Default 20000, range 2000 to 100000. Higher values give more accurate predictions at the cost of more computation; changing it rebuilds the hypothesis cache and recomputes the posterior.

settings.name: RequireSameStrongholdAcrossThrows
settings.description: When true (default), the estimator only considers solutions where all sampled throws point to the same stronghold, improving accuracy with multiple throws. Disabling it allows mixing throws aimed at different strongholds.

settings.name: SampleDelayTicks
settings.description: Number of ticks to wait after an Eye of Ender spawns before measuring its angle, letting it settle into its flight direction. Default 2, range 0 to 10.

settings.name: MinEyeHorizontalSpeed
settings.description: Minimum horizontal speed an eye must have before its angle is sampled, so stationary or barely-moving eyes are ignored. Default 0.02, range 0.001 to 0.2.

settings.name: MaxSampleAgeTicks
settings.description: Maximum age (in ticks) of a pending throw record that can still be matched to a newly spawned eye entity. Default 20, range 5 to 100. Older pending throws are discarded.

settings.name: ShowTopCandidates
settings.description: How many of the highest-probability candidate chunks are kept and rendered. Default 3, range 1 to 10. Changing it recomputes the posterior with the new candidate count.

settings.name: RenderRays
settings.description: When true (default), draws long white lines in the world along each recorded eye-throw direction so you can visualize the triangulation rays.

settings.name: RenderBestChunk
settings.description: When true (default), renders the most likely candidate chunk as a blue 16x16 plane at the player's Y level.

settings.name: RenderTopChunks
settings.description: When true (default), renders the additional (non-best) top candidate chunks as orange 16x16 planes.

settings.name: AnnouncePrediction
settings.description: When true (default), shows a notification with the best chunk coordinates and probability each time a new best chunk is predicted.

settings.name: ResetOnWorldChange
settings.description: When true (default), clears all collected measurements, tracked eyes and predictions whenever the world changes (e.g. dimension change or rejoin).

modules.name: SuperKnockback
modules.summary: SuperKnockback increases the knockback you deal to other entities by exploiting how sprint-resetting affects vanilla knockback. It works by manipulating your sprint or movement state around the moment you attack so the game registers extra knockback. It only acts on living targets whose hurt time is low enough, respects a configurable chance, and skips attacks that would already be critical hits. It is also known by the alias WTap.
useCases: Knock opponents back further in PvP to gain distance or combo control without manually w-tapping.
Automate sprint-reset (W-tap) mechanics so every qualifying hit applies maximum knockback.
Restrict knockback boosting to specific situations (e.g. only while moving forward on the ground and out of water) to look more legitimate.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the knockback technique. Options: Packet (default) toggles sprint via sprint start/stop packets at the moment of attack; SprintTap temporarily disallows sprinting after a hit and re-enables it after a delay; WTap temporarily blocks forward movement input after a hit. Changing the mode changes how the sprint reset is performed and exposes that mode's own sub-settings.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Maximum target hurt-time (invulnerability ticks) at which the module will still trigger. Default 10, range 0..10. With 10 it always acts; lowering it only boosts knockback on targets that are not currently in their hurt cooldown.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Percent probability (0..100, default 100, unit %) that the knockback boost is applied on a given qualifying hit. Lowering it makes the effect trigger only some of the time.

settings.name: Conditions
settings.description: Additional conditions that must ALL be met for the module to operate. Options: OnlyFacing (target must not be looking toward you / you are behind it), OnlyOnGround (you must be on the ground), NotInWater (you must not be in water or a bubble column). Default selection is NotInWater.

settings.name: OnlyOnMove
settings.description: Toggleable group (enabled by default) that restricts the module to only act while you are moving. When enabled, the module does nothing if you are standing still.

settings.name: OnlyForward
settings.description: Child of OnlyOnMove (default true). When enabled, the module only operates while moving straight forward and is suppressed if you are strafing sideways.

settings.name: ReSprint
settings.description: SprintTap mode only. Number of ticks to wait after sprinting has been blocked before allowing sprint again, chosen randomly within the range. Default 0..1 ticks, range 0..10.

settings.name: UntilMovementBlock
settings.description: WTap mode only. Number of ticks to wait after a hit before forward movement input is blocked, chosen randomly within the range. Default 0..1 ticks, range 0..10.

settings.name: UntilAllowedMovement
settings.description: WTap mode only. Number of ticks to keep movement blocked (after forward impulse stops) before re-allowing movement, chosen randomly within the range. Default 0..1 ticks, range 0..10.

modules.name: Surround
modules.summary: Surround automatically builds a protective ring of blocks (by default obsidian, ender chest or crying obsidian) around your feet so you stand in a safe hole, mainly to defend against Crystal PvP. It uses a shared block placer to place the four blocks around the hole, can extend the build to cover blocking entities, place blocks below you, and instantly replace blocks the moment they are broken. It can also actively protect the surround from being blown open by destroying enemy end crystals and pre-placing an extra layer of obsidian. The module is configured to disable itself when you leave the hole (it disables on quit and, by default, when your Y coordinate changes).
useCases: Stay protected in Crystal PvP by instantly walling yourself into a 1x1 obsidian hole.
Automatically re-place blocks that opponents mine or blow out, optionally destroying the crystals they use to block your replacements.
Defend against fall/face placements by adding an extra obsidian layer and placing a block beneath you so enemies cannot mine you down.

settings.name: Features
settings.description: Multi-select of optional behaviors. Center: runs the Center command on enable to snap you to block center. Extend: when entities block placement spots, extends the surround to also wall those entities. NoWaste: if you are already in a completed 1x1 hole, do not build wider 2x1/2x2 holes even if you block replacements (recommended only with no wall placements or much lower ping). Down: places blocks below the surround so enemies cannot mine the block under you and drop you. Defaults to Extend and Down enabled.

settings.name: DisableOn
settings.description: Multi-select of conditions that auto-disable the module. YChange: disable when your Y coordinate changes from the start. XZMove: disable when you move more than 0.5 blocks horizontally from the original center. XZSpeed: disable when your speed reaches 5 m/s or more. Defaults to YChange only.

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: When true (default), replaces broken surround blocks instantly on block-update packets instead of waiting for the next tick. Requires the placer's rotation mode 'None' to take effect.

settings.name: Protect
settings.description: Toggle for the crystal-protection sub-group (enabled by default). When enabled, the module watches your surround blocks for enemy mining progress and reacts to protect them. Contains MinDestroyProgress and the ExtraLayer sub-group.

settings.name: MinDestroyProgress
settings.description: Child of Protect. The block destroy stage (0-9, unit 'stage', default 4) at which protective actions are taken. Lower values react earlier to enemy mining; higher values wait until the block is nearly broken.

settings.name: ExtraLayer
settings.description: Child toggle of Protect (enabled by default). When a protected block is being broken, places an extra slice of obsidian around the surround to keep you walled even after a block is lost.

settings.name: Corners
settings.description: Child of ExtraLayer (default false). When enabled, the extra layer also fills the diagonal corner positions, producing a full 3x3 ring of blocks around you instead of only the cardinal sides.

settings.name: AddExtraLayer
settings.description: A bindable key. While held/toggled it manually forces the ExtraLayer protection blocks to be placed regardless of enemy mining state.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Whitelist/Blacklist mode (default Whitelist) controlling how the Blocks list selects which hotbar item is used for the surround.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The set of blocks the surround is allowed to place. Defaults to obsidian, ender chest and crying obsidian. Combined with Filter to choose the hotbar slot.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Placer sub-tree (Placing). Maximum reach distance for placements, 1.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Reach distance for placing through walls / against faces pointing away, 0.0-6.0, default 4.5. 0 disables facing-away faces.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Tick range to wait between placement actions, 0-40 ticks, default 1..2 (a random value in the range is used each time).

settings.name: Swing
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Swing/animation mode used when placing (default DoNotHide), controlling whether the arm swing is shown or hidden.

settings.name: ConstructFailResult
settings.description: Placer (Placing), default true. When a raytrace fails, construct a center hit result so placements still go through. Makes placing more reliable but rotations can be slightly off and placements can go slightly outside range.

settings.name: Sneak
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Number of ticks to sneak when placing on an interactable block, 0-10 ticks, default 1..1, to avoid triggering the block's interaction.

settings.name: Ignore
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Conditions to ignore so placing continues: OpenInventory (place even with a container screen open) and UsingItem (place even while using an item). Default none selected.

settings.name: SlotResetDelay
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Ticks before the silently-selected hotbar slot is reset back, 0-40 ticks, default 4..6.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: Placer (Placing). Choice of how to rotate for placements: Normal (uses the rotation engine) or None (no rotation). Default Normal. Note Surround's Instant feature requires None.

settings.name: PostMove
settings.description: Placer RotationMode child (default false). Sends the action packet on post-move for a slight timing advantage; not legit and may flag post-rotation anti-cheat checks.

settings.name: Instant
settings.description: Placer RotationMode child (default false). Instantly sends the action when possible, ignoring packet ordering; may flag some anti-cheats and can make PostMove irrelevant.

settings.name: IgnoreOpenInventory
settings.description: Placer Normal rotation mode child (default true). Allows rotating/placing even when an inventory screen is open.

settings.name: SendRotationPacket
settings.description: Placer None rotation mode child (default false). When in None mode, sends a standalone rotation packet to the server before the placement.

settings.name: AngleSmooth
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations, under Normal mode). Selects how rotations are smoothed (e.g. Linear, Sigmoid, Acceleration). Controls how naturally the aim moves toward the placement target.

settings.name: MovementCorrection
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). How player movement is corrected relative to the server rotation, default Silent.

settings.name: ResetThreshold
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). Angle difference (1-180, default 2) below which the rotation is considered reached/can reset.

settings.name: TicksUntilReset
settings.description: Placer rotation engine (Rotations). Ticks the rotation is held before resetting to the player's own aim, 1-30 ticks, default 5.

settings.name: Support
settings.description: Placer Support sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Places extra helper blocks so otherwise-unsupported surround positions become placeable. For Surround its block list is pre-filled with obsidian.

settings.name: Depth
settings.description: Support child. Maximum search depth (Manhattan distance) for building a support path, 1-12, default 4.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Support child. Minimum time between support-path searches, 0-1000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Support child. Whitelist/Blacklist (default Blacklist) controlling which blocks may be used as support/helper blocks.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: Support child. The block list used with the Support Filter to pick support blocks (Surround additionally pre-adds obsidian).

settings.name: DestroyCrystals
settings.description: Placer crystal-destroyer sub-group toggle (enabled by default). Attacks end crystals that would block your placements; required for Surround's Protect crystal destruction to function.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Reach for attacking crystals, 1.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: WallRange
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Through-wall reach for attacking crystals, 0.0-6.0, default 4.5.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Minimum time between crystal attacks, 0-1000 ms, default 0.

settings.name: SwingMode
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Swing/animation mode used when attacking crystals, default DoNotHide.

settings.name: RotationMode
settings.description: DestroyCrystals child. Normal vs None rotation mode (default Normal) for aiming at crystals, with the same PostMove/Instant (and Normal's Rotations/IgnoreOpenInventory, None's SendRotationPacket) sub-options as the main placer rotation mode.

settings.name: TargetRendering
settings.description: Placer PlacementRenderer sub-group (disabled by default). Renders boxes at all positions queued to be placed. Contains the rendering settings below.

settings.name: PlacedRendering
settings.description: Placer PlacementRenderer sub-group (enabled by default). Renders boxes at positions that were just placed (boxes are not kept). Contains the same rendering settings as TargetRendering.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child (default true). Clumps/culls adjacent placement boxes together for cleaner rendering.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Box size at the start of the animation, 0.0-2.0, default 1.0.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing curve for the start-size animation, default Linear.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Box size at the end of the animation, 0.0-2.0, default 0.8.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing curve for the end-size animation, default Linear.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing curve for the fade-in, default Linear.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Easing curve for the fade-out, default Linear.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fade-in duration, 0-5000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fade-out duration, 0-5000 ms, default 500.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Fill color of the placement boxes, default green with low alpha.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: PlacementRenderer child. Outline color of the placement boxes, default green fully opaque.

modules.name: SwordBlock
modules.summary: SwordBlock restores classic 1.8-style blocking with swords on modern combat versions, primarily intended for servers running ViaVersion. When you use/right-click while holding a sword, it triggers an off-hand shield use so the server registers a block, and it can also display the old sword-blocking animation. On protocols that already support blocking with swords it does nothing functional. Aliased as OldBlocking.
useCases: Blocking with a sword (old-style) on ViaVersion servers that translate modern clients down to 1.8 combat.
Showing the nostalgic sword-block animation while actually blocking with a hidden off-hand shield.
Using OnlyVisual to merely render the sword-block animation without sending any blocking packets.

settings.name: OnlyVisual
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, the module only shows the sword-block animation and does not send any packets to actually block (the packet-handling logic is skipped).

settings.name: FakeOnPressing
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, the sword-block animation is shown on your own player whenever the Use key is pressed, regardless of whether real blocking is occurring.

settings.name: HideShieldSlot
settings.description: Default false. Controls whether the off-hand shield slot used for blocking is hidden in the HUD/inventory display so the shield trick is less visible.

settings.name: ApplyToThirdPersonView
settings.description: Default true. When enabled, the sword-block animation is also applied in third-person view, not just first-person.

settings.name: AlwaysHideShield
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, an off-hand shield is hidden even when you are not holding a sword in your main hand (otherwise the shield is only hidden while a sword is held).

modules.name: TargetLock
modules.summary: TargetLock restricts which players combat/targeting modules are allowed to focus on, either by temporarily locking onto whoever you attack or by filtering by username. In Temporary mode, attacking a player locks that player for a configurable duration and other players are ignored until they go out of range or the timer expires. In Filter mode, a whitelist or blacklist of usernames determines who may be targeted. It can be limited to combat modules only, otherwise non-locked players are fully ignored by targeting.
useCases: Lock onto the player you are currently fighting so KillAura never switches to bystanders mid-fight (Temporary mode).
Only ever target a specific list of players, or never target friends, using a username whitelist or blacklist (Filter mode).
Restrict the lock so it affects only combat modules while leaving other targeting (like render ESP) unaffected.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the locking strategy. 'Temporary' (default) locks onto players you attack for a set time; 'Filter' locks based on a username whitelist/blacklist.

settings.name: Combat
settings.description: When enabled (default false), non-locked players are only excluded from combat module targeting; when disabled, non-locked players are entirely ignored by all targeting (the tag is set to ignore).

settings.name: Usernames
settings.description: Filter mode: the list of usernames used by the whitelist/blacklist. Defaults to a single entry 'Notch'. Comparison is case-insensitive.

settings.name: FilterType
settings.description: Filter mode: whether the Usernames list is a 'Whitelist' (only listed players may be targeted) or a 'Blacklist' (listed players are never targeted). Defaults to Whitelist.

settings.name: MaximumTime
settings.description: Temporary mode: how many seconds a locked target remains locked after the last attack before being released. Default 30, range 0..120 (seconds).

settings.name: MaximumRange
settings.description: Temporary mode: the maximum distance a locked target may be from you before the lock is dropped for being out of range. Default 20, range 8..40 (blocks).

settings.name: WhenNoLock
settings.description: Temporary mode: behavior when no target is currently locked. 'AllowAll' (default) lets all players be targeted normally until you lock one; 'AllowNone' blocks targeting of every player until you have locked someone by attacking them.

modules.name: TargetStrafe
modules.summary: TargetStrafe automatically strafes (circle-strafes) the player around a locked combat target, keeping a chosen orbit distance while staying on safe ground. It picks a target from KillAura, Aimbot, or its own target selector, then steers movement either by altering motion directly (Motion mode) or by rewriting directional input (Input mode). A Planner validates each candidate strafe point against edges and the void, optionally shrinking the orbit radius to find a safe spot, and visuals can render the orbit circle and the next strafe point.
useCases: Automatically orbiting an opponent during combat with KillAura/Aimbot to dodge while staying in range.
Circle-strafing without manually walking, while EdgeCheck/VoidCheck stop you from walking off ledges or into the void.
Restricting strafing to certain conditions (e.g. only while sprinting via Speed, only on ground, only while jumping, or only with KillAura active) using Requirements.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects how strafing is applied. Default Motion. Motion mode directly modifies the player's movement vector around the target; Input mode instead rewrites the directional (WASD) input to steer toward the strafe direction.

settings.name: Hypixel
settings.description: Child of Motion mode (default false). When on and the Speed module is running, uses Hypixel-tuned strafe handling: enforces a minimum speed (0.48 on ground, 0.281 in air) and coordinates with the Speed module's low-hop strafe timing.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: The desired orbit radius / target-selection range around the target. Default 2.95, range 0 to 8. Increasing it widens the circle; it also drives FollowRange to never be smaller than Range.

settings.name: FollowRange
settings.description: Maximum horizontal distance to the target at which strafing still operates. Default 4, range 0 to 10. If the player is farther than this from the target, strafing stops. Coerced to be at least the target selector's max range and at least Range.

settings.name: Requirements
settings.description: Multi-select conditions that must all be met for strafing to activate. Options: Space (jump key held), Speed (Speed module running), KillAura (KillAura module running), Ground (player on ground). With none selected there are no extra conditions.

settings.name: Planner
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that plans and validates the next strafe point and handles direction control and adaptive range.

settings.name: ControlDirection
settings.description: Child of Planner (default true). When on, your A/D (left/right) input chooses the strafe direction (left = counter-clockwise, right = clockwise); otherwise direction is automatic and only flips on collision/invalid points.

settings.name: Validation
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of Planner, default enabled) that checks whether a candidate strafe point is safe before moving there.

settings.name: EdgeCheck
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of Validation, default enabled). When enabled, rejects strafe points that would put the player too close to a drop-off (edge).

settings.name: MaxFallHeight
settings.description: Child of EdgeCheck. The maximum fall height tolerated below a strafe point before it is considered an unsafe edge. Default 1.2, range 0.1 to 4. Lower values keep you farther from ledges.

settings.name: VoidCheck
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of Validation, default enabled). When enabled, rejects strafe points where the player would fall into the void.

settings.name: SafetyExpand
settings.description: Child of VoidCheck. Extra safety margin (block expansion) used when testing whether a point would fall into the void. Default 0.1, range 0 to 5. Higher values are more cautious.

settings.name: AdaptiveRange
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of Planner, default disabled). When enabled and the ideal orbit point is unsafe, it progressively tries smaller orbit radii (in RangeStep increments up to MaxRange) to find a valid point instead of just reversing direction.

settings.name: MaxRange
settings.description: Child of AdaptiveRange. The largest orbit radius tried while searching for a valid strafe point. Default 4, range 1 to 5.

settings.name: RangeStep
settings.description: Child of AdaptiveRange. The increment by which the search radius grows each attempt when looking for a valid point. Default 0.5, range 0.1 to 1.

settings.name: Visuals
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that renders the strafe orbit circle and the next strafe point in the world.

settings.name: Width
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Thickness of the rendered orbit ring. Default 0.12, range 0.01 to 1.

settings.name: HeightOffset
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Vertical offset of the rendered orbit and point markers relative to the target/player position. Default 0.05, range -1 to 1.

settings.name: OuterColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Outer gradient color of the orbit circle. Default LiquidBounce color at alpha 100.

settings.name: InnerColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Inner gradient color of the orbit circle. Default LiquidBounce color at alpha 20.

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Color of the orbit circle's outline. Default LiquidBounce color at alpha 180.

settings.name: ShowNextPoint
settings.description: Child of Visuals (default true). When on, renders a marker at the next computed strafe point.

settings.name: PointRadius
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Radius of the next-point marker circle. Default 0.18, range 0.05 to 1.

settings.name: PointColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Fill color of the next-point marker when the point is valid. Default LiquidBounce color at alpha 90.

settings.name: PointOutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Outline color of the next-point marker when the point is valid. Default LiquidBounce color at alpha 180.

settings.name: InvalidPointColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Fill color of the next-point marker when the point is invalid/unsafe. Default red (255,90,90) at alpha 90.

settings.name: InvalidPointOutlineColor
settings.description: Child of Visuals. Outline color of the next-point marker when the point is invalid/unsafe. Default red (255,90,90) at alpha 180.

modules.name: Teams
modules.summary: Teams identifies your teammates and prevents combat modules like KillAura from attacking them. It determines team membership using configurable criteria such as shared scoreboard team, matching name color, matching name prefix, and matching dyed armor color. Entities recognized as teammates are excluded from targeting, and it can also colorize entity tags based on team or armor color sources.
useCases: Avoid accidentally attacking your own teammates in team-based modes like BedWars or team Skywars while using KillAura.
Use prefix-based detection to recognize teammates on servers that color names by team (e.g. Hypixel BedWars, GommeHD Skywars).
Tint entity tags by team or armor color to visually distinguish allies.

settings.name: Matches
settings.description: The criteria used to decide whether another player is on your team. Options: 'ScoreboardTeam' (allied via scoreboard), 'NameColor' (your and their display-name colors are equal), and 'Prefix' (the first space-separated token of both display names matches, useful for prefix-tagged servers). Defaults to ScoreboardTeam and NameColor enabled.

settings.name: ArmorColor
settings.description: Which armor equipment slots are compared by dyed color to detect teammates (and also used as the Armor color source). Choices are the humanoid armor slots Feet, Legs, Chest, and Head. Defaults to Head. A player is treated as a teammate if any selected slot's dyeable armor color matches yours.

settings.name: ColorSources
settings.description: Sources used to color an entity's tag, applied in order with the first non-null result winning. 'Team' uses the entity's scoreboard team color; 'Armor' uses the dyed color of the first matching ArmorColor slot. Can be set to none. By default all sources are enabled.

modules.name: Teleport
modules.summary: Teleport is the configuration backend for the client's teleport commands (.vclip, .tp, .tphere). It does not teleport on its own when toggled; instead it must be invoked via those commands, and enabling it without a queued teleport simply shows a warning and turns itself back off. It snaps the player (or their vehicle) to the requested position, optionally distributing the move across multiple packets to bypass anti-cheat, and can wait for a number of server-sent position resets before completing the teleport.
useCases: Instantly move to coordinates or to another player using the teleport commands while controlling how the move is packaged.
Enable PaperBypass to split a long teleport into many small move packets to evade Paper-style movement checks.
Use FunctionAfterTeleports (optionally with WithDisablerOnWait) to defer the teleport until after the server has sent a set number of position corrections.

settings.name: AllFullPacket
settings.description: When PaperBypass is active, sends full move packets (position, rotation and on-ground) instead of position+on-ground packets for the incremental steps. Default false.

settings.name: PaperBypass
settings.description: Enables the Paper exploit: instead of a single snap, the teleport distance is broken into multiple sequential move packets (one per ~10 blocks) to slip past movement validation before the final position packet. Default false.

settings.name: HighTP
settings.description: Enables high/long-distance teleport behavior used by the teleport commands. Default false.

settings.name: HighTPAmount
settings.description: The distance amount used for high teleports. Default 200.0, range 0.0 to 500.0.

settings.name: GroundMode
settings.description: Controls the onGround flag sent in the move packets during a PaperBypass teleport. True always reports on-ground, False always reports airborne, and Correct (default) reports the player's actual on-ground state.

settings.name: ResetMotion
settings.description: When enabled (default true), zeroes the player's (or vehicle's) velocity after teleporting so you don't carry momentum into the destination.

settings.name: FunctionAfterTeleports
settings.description: Number of server position-reset (teleport) packets to wait for before actually performing the queued teleport. Default 0 (teleport immediately), range 0 to 5.

settings.name: WithDisablerOnWait
settings.description: When waiting on server teleports, automatically enables the Disabler module on the last pending teleport and disables it again once the teleport completes. Default false.

modules.name: TerrainSpeed
modules.summary: TerrainSpeed lets the player move faster on or through specific surface types. It bundles three independent sub-features: FastClimb (climbing ladders/vines faster), IceSpeed (manipulating slipperiness and motion on ice blocks), and WaterSpeed (faster swimming). Each sub-feature is a toggleable group with its own settings so you can enable only the surfaces you care about.
useCases: Climbing ladders and vines much faster than vanilla allows.
Moving faster across ice without sliding uncontrollably by tuning slipperiness.
Swimming through water quickly with automatic surfacing and configurable horizontal/vertical speed.

settings.name: FastClimb
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that speeds up climbing ladders, vines and other climbable blocks.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Child of FastClimb. Selects how fast climbing is done. Default Motion. Choices: Motion (anti-cheat-friendly upward motion while colliding with a climbable block) and Clip (vanilla-like instant teleport up the ladder, does not bypass anti-cheats).

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Child of FastClimb's Motion mode. The upward velocity applied each tick while horizontally colliding with a climbable block. Default 0.2872, range 0.1 to 0.5. Higher values climb faster.

settings.name: IceSpeed
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that manipulates movement physics on ice blocks (ice, blue ice, frosted ice, packed ice).

settings.name: Slipperiness
settings.description: Child of IceSpeed. Overrides the slipperiness multiplier applied to ice blocks. Default 0.6, range 0.3 to 1. Lower values reduce sliding (more control); higher values increase slide.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of IceSpeed, default disabled). When enabled, additionally multiplies the player's horizontal delta movement on ice by its Motion value to boost speed.

settings.name: Motion
settings.description: Child of IceSpeed's Motion group. The horizontal velocity multiplier applied on ice when the Motion group is enabled. Default 0.5, range 0.2 to 1.5. Higher values move faster across ice.

settings.name: WaterSpeed
settings.description: Toggleable group (default enabled) that increases swimming speed in water.

settings.name: AutoSwim
settings.description: Child of WaterSpeed (default true). When on, automatically holds jump while in water (unless sneaking) to keep the player swimming/surfacing without manual input.

settings.name: BaseSpeed
settings.description: Non-toggleable value group (child of WaterSpeed) holding the default swimming speeds used when not sprinting.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Child of WaterSpeed BaseSpeed. Horizontal swim speed while moving in water (non-sprint). Default 0.44, range 0.1 to 10.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Child of WaterSpeed BaseSpeed. Vertical swim speed applied when holding jump (up) or sneak (down) in water (non-sprint). Default 0.44, range 0.1 to 10.

settings.name: SprintSpeed
settings.description: Toggleable group (child of WaterSpeed, default enabled). When enabled and the sprint key is held, uses its faster horizontal/vertical speeds instead of BaseSpeed.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Child of WaterSpeed SprintSpeed. Horizontal swim speed while sprinting in water. Default 1, range 0.1 to 10.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Child of WaterSpeed SprintSpeed. Vertical swim speed while sprinting in water (jump up / sneak down). Default 1, range 0.1 to 10.

modules.name: TextFieldProtect
modules.summary: TextFieldProtect hides the visible text inside text-field widgets (such as the chat input) when the typed content matches certain patterns, masking it with asterisks so sensitive information isn't shown on screen. It is intended to keep credentials private, for example when typing login or registration commands while streaming or screen-sharing. The actual sent text is unaffected; only the on-screen rendering of matching input is masked.
useCases: Hide passwords/emails on screen when typing /login, /register, or /email commands while streaming or recording.
Add your own command prefixes to the pattern list to mask any other sensitive text-field input.

settings.name: Patterns
settings.description: List of regular expressions; if the text-field content matches any of them, its rendered characters are replaced with '*'. Defaults to patterns matching commands starting with /register, /login and /email. Add or edit regexes to control which inputs get masked.

modules.name: TickBase
modules.summary: TickBase manipulates the player's tick timing to gain a reach/timing advantage, simulating future player movement and 'spending' banked ticks to teleport-step toward an enemy at the right moment (preferring ticks that would land a critical hit). It maintains a tick balance that recovers over time and is capped, and it can run extra ticks either in the past or future. It conflicts with vehicles and Blink (and pauses then) and can pause when the server flags you with a position correction.
useCases: Close distance and land hits faster against a nearby enemy in PvP by spending banked ticks.
Prioritize critical hits by stepping into a position with fall distance before attacking.
Combine with KillAura so tick stepping only happens when an attack is about to register.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Whether extra ticks are processed as Past (skip ticks first, then run them; default) or Future (run ticks immediately then skip an equal amount). Determines the ordering of the tick manipulation relative to the wait.

settings.name: Call
settings.description: What each extra tick runs: Game (a full game tick via mc.tick(), default; updates rotations and full game state) or Player (only the player tick, the previous default, which does not update the rotation manager). Game is more complete; Player is kept for compatibility.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Distance window (in blocks) for tick-stepping. The start is the minimum range you can tick into and the end is the range beyond which tickbase will not act. Default 2.5 to 4.0, configurable within 0.0 to 8.0.

settings.name: BalanceRecoverIncrement
settings.description: How much tick balance is regained each movement input tick. Default 1.0, range 0.0 to 2.0. Higher values let you bank ticks faster.

settings.name: BalanceMaxValue
settings.description: Maximum tick balance that can be accumulated, limiting how many ticks can be spent in a burst. Default 20, range 0 to 200.

settings.name: MaxTicksAtATime
settings.description: Maximum number of ticks that may be processed in a single burst. Default 4 ticks, range 1 to 20.

settings.name: PauseOfFlag
settings.description: When enabled (default on), the tick balance is reset to zero whenever the server sends a position-correction packet (a flag), effectively pausing the module after being flagged.

settings.name: Pause
settings.description: Number of extra ticks to wait/skip after a tick-step burst before resuming. Default 0 ticks, range 0 to 20.

settings.name: Cooldown
settings.description: Number of ticks to wait after a tick-step burst completes before another can occur. Default 0 ticks, range 0 to 100.

settings.name: ForceGround
settings.description: When enabled, only candidate ticks where the player is on the ground are considered for stepping. Default off.

settings.name: Line
settings.description: Color of the line rendered to visualize the simulated tick path. Default white. If alpha is zero the line is not drawn. (Not always included in configs.)

settings.name: RequiresKillAura
settings.description: When enabled (default on), tick-stepping only occurs if KillAura is running and would click at the chosen tick, ensuring ticks are spent only when an attack will land.

modules.name: Timer
modules.summary: Timer changes the speed of the entire game clock, effectively speeding up or slowing down everything (movement, ticks, etc.). It offers three modes: Classic sets one constant speed multiplier; Pulse alternates between a normal and a boost speed for set tick durations; and Boost builds up a 'balance' of timer time while standing still and spends it to speed up while moving, optionally normalizing during combat. The module auto-disables on quit and resets the timer to normal speed when turned off.
useCases: Use Classic mode with a speed above 1 to move and react faster than normal (e.g. to escape or chase).
Use Pulse mode to alternate fast/slow bursts so an anticheat sees a balanced average tick rate while still gaining speed.
Use Boost mode to bank timer time while idle and burn it for short speed bursts when moving, with auto-normalization during combat to avoid detection.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the timer behavior: Classic (default), Pulse, or Boost.

settings.name: Mode > Classic > Speed
settings.description: Constant game-speed multiplier applied while enabled. Default 2.0, range 0.1..20. Values above 1 speed the game up; below 1 slow it down.

settings.name: Mode > Pulse > NormalSpeed
settings.description: The timer speed used during the normal phase of the pulse. Default 0.5, range 0.1..20.

settings.name: Mode > Pulse > NormalSpeedTicks
settings.description: How many ticks the normal-speed phase lasts. Default 20, range 1..500 ticks.

settings.name: Mode > Pulse > BoostSpeed
settings.description: The timer speed used during the boost phase of the pulse. Default 2.0, range 0.1..20.

settings.name: Mode > Pulse > BoostSpeedTicks
settings.description: How many ticks the boost-speed phase lasts. Default 20, range 1..500 ticks.

settings.name: Mode > Pulse > OnMove
settings.description: If enabled, the pulsing only runs while the player is moving. Default false.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > BoostSpeed
settings.description: The speed used while spending banked timer time (moving). Default 1.3, range 0.1..20.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > SlowSpeed
settings.description: The speed used while banking timer time (standing still) or paying back negative balance. Default 0.6, range 0.1..20.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > TimeBoostTicks
settings.description: Maximum amount of banked timer ticks that can be accumulated/spent. Default 12, range 1..60 ticks.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > AccountTimerValues
settings.description: If enabled, the bank/spend calculations scale by the actual timer speed values (a balance accounting), so faster/slower speeds consume the budget proportionally. Default true.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > NormalizeDuringCombat
settings.description: If enabled, the timer is forced to normal speed (1.0) while in combat to avoid suspicious behavior. Default true.

settings.name: Mode > Boost > AllowNegative
settings.description: If enabled, you may boost into a negative balance (overdraw) while in combat or while Scaffold is running, which is later repaid by slowing down. Default false.

modules.name: TimerRange
modules.summary: TimerRange automatically speeds up the game timer when an enemy is within a certain distance, giving a timing advantage as you approach, then slows back to normal when very close so you do not overshoot. It uses a recovering balance system to limit how long the speed-up can last, and it can pause when you get flagged by a server position correction. It can be restricted to only operate while on ground and only while KillAura is active.
useCases: Gain a timing edge when closing in on an enemy in PvP without manually toggling timer hacks.
Automatically normalize timer speed when very close to a target to avoid desync/overshoot.
Restrict the speed-up to ground combat and only when KillAura is engaged for safer use.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Percentage chance that the speed-up is applied when conditions are met. Default 100%, range 0 to 100. Below 100, the module randomly skips speeding up some ticks.

settings.name: TimerBalanceLimit
settings.description: The balance threshold governing how long the boosted timer can be sustained before falling back to the balance-limit speed; balance recovers up to twice this value. Default 20.0, range 0.0 to 50.0.

settings.name: NormalSpeed
settings.description: Timer speed used when an enemy is within working range but not yet within speed-up range. Default 0.9, range 0.1 to 10.0.

settings.name: InRangeSpeed
settings.description: Timer speed used once the balance limit is reached while an enemy is within speed-up range. Default 0.95, range 0.1 to 10.0.

settings.name: BalanceLimitSpeed
settings.description: Timer speed requested when the balance timer drops to or below the balance limit, used to let balance recover. Default 0.99, range 0.1 to 1.0.

settings.name: BoostTimer
settings.description: The boosted timer speed applied while an enemy is within speed-up range and balance is still available. Default 2.0, range 0.1 to 10.0. This is the main speed-up value.

settings.name: BalanceRecoveryIncrement
settings.description: Divisor controlling how the balance timer changes based on current timer speed; affects how quickly balance is consumed or recovered. Default 1.0, range 1.0 to 10.0.

settings.name: DistanceToSpeedUp
settings.description: Enemy distance (in blocks) at or below which the boosted/in-range speed is applied. Default 3.5, range 0.0 to 10.0.

settings.name: DistanceToPause
settings.description: Enemy distance (in blocks) at or below which the timer is set back to normal (1.0) to avoid overshooting a very close target. Default 3.0, range 0.0 to 10.0.

settings.name: DistanceToStartWorking
settings.description: Maximum enemy distance (in blocks) at which the module begins operating at all; beyond this no timer change is requested. Default 100.0, range 0.0 to 500.0.

settings.name: PauseOnFlag
