settings.description: When enabled (default on), the balance timer is set to its maximum (limit times two) when the server sends a position-correction packet, stopping the speed-up after being flagged.

settings.name: OnlyOnGround
settings.description: When enabled, the module only adjusts the timer while the player is on the ground. Default off.

settings.name: RequiresKillAura
settings.description: When enabled (default on), the module only operates while KillAura is running and has a current target. Otherwise it does nothing.

modules.name: TimeShift
modules.summary: Abuses legacy (1.8-style) client-sided timing mechanics, formerly known as Regen or Zoot, to rapidly send movement packets and speed up the client tick when certain conditions are met, effectively accelerating regeneration-like behavior. It computes a tick speed based on your current health, fire status, and harmful effects, then slows the game timer and sends that many extra move packets to fast-forward time. It is intended for servers behaving like Minecraft 1.8 (it warns you if the target is not 1.8 or older) and disables itself when you quit. It skips activity while in creative mode or dead, and respects user-selected exemption conditions.
useCases: Regain health faster on a legacy/1.8 server by triggering rapid client ticks when your health is low.
Speed up burning off fire damage or running out harmful effect durations.
Replace the older Regen/Zoot modules with a single combined timer-abuse tool on compatible servers.

settings.name: Health
settings.description: Toggle for the Health-based speed group (enabled by default). When on, the module increases tick speed when your health is below the trigger value; the speed scales with how far below the trigger you are. When off, health-based time shifting is disabled.

settings.name: Health
settings.description: Child of the Health group. The health threshold that triggers the speed boost. Tick speed is computed as (this value minus your current health) times Increment. Defaults to 16, range 0 to 20 (half-hearts).

settings.name: Increment
settings.description: Child of the Health group. Multiplier applied to the health deficit when computing tick speed; higher values produce a faster time shift for the same amount of missing health. Defaults to 20, range 0 to 60.

settings.name: BadEffects
settings.description: When enabled, the module time-shifts to burn through harmful (non-infinite) status effects, basing tick speed on the longest harmful effect's remaining duration (capped by MaximumSpeed). Defaults to false.

settings.name: Fire
settings.description: When enabled, the module applies a tick speed of 9 while you are on fire and not in water or rain, helping you burn off fire faster. Defaults to false.

settings.name: MaximumSpeed
settings.description: Upper cap on the tick speed used by the BadEffects logic (limits how many extra ticks/packets are sent for harmful effects). Defaults to 100, range 5 to 200.

settings.name: Timer
settings.description: The game timer speed requested while time shifting is active. Values above 1.0 speed up the client clock and below 1.0 slow it down. Defaults to 1.0, range 0.1 to 10.0.

settings.name: Conditions
settings.description: A set of exemption conditions that, if any are met, pause time shifting that tick. Options: NotInTheAir (skip while not on ground), NotDuringMove (skip while moving), NotDuringRegeneration (skip while you already have the Regeneration effect), and DoNotCauseHunger (skip while your food level is below 20 to avoid creating hunger). Defaults to NotInTheAir selected.

settings.name: PacketType
settings.description: The type of movement packet sent to advance time. Options come from MovePacketType (e.g. FULL, position/rotation variants). FULL is the default and is most likely to bypass anticheats, since vanilla 1.17+ clients send full move packets when using items and many anticheats exempt those from timer checks.

modules.name: TNTTimer
modules.summary: TNTTimer highlights active primed TNT entities in the world and can display their remaining fuse time. It can apply a glow/ESP highlight (with a color that shifts from yellow toward red and pulses faster as the fuse runs down) and optionally render a floating text label above each TNT showing the time left, in either ticks or seconds, plus the placer's name. Only TNT entities with a fuse greater than zero are tracked, and tracking is cleared when the module is disabled.
useCases: Track when nearby TNT will explode so you can flee or take cover in time during PvP or raids.
Identify who placed each piece of TNT via the owner name label.
Visually locate all active TNT through walls using the glow highlight.

settings.name: ESP
settings.description: When enabled (default true), applies a glowing highlight/ESP to active TNT entities so they stand out (including through obstructions). The glow color is red and pulses faster the closer the TNT is to detonating.

settings.name: ShowTimer
settings.description: Toggle for the ShowTimer sub-group (default off). When enabled, renders a floating text label above each active TNT showing its remaining fuse time. The child settings below only take effect when this is on.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: Scale of the floating timer text label. Default 1.5, range 0.25 to 4. Higher values make the label larger. Part of the ShowTimer group.

settings.name: RenderY
settings.description: Vertical offset (in blocks) of the timer label relative to the TNT's center. Default 1.0, range -2.0 to 2.0. Increasing it moves the label up, decreasing moves it down. Part of the ShowTimer group.

settings.name: OwnerName
settings.description: When enabled (default true), appends the name of the entity that placed/owns the TNT in parentheses after the time on the label. Part of the ShowTimer group.

settings.name: TimeUnit
settings.description: Unit used to display the remaining fuse on the label. Default Ticks. Options: Ticks (shows the raw tick count) or Seconds (shows the time as seconds, formatted like '0.00s', i.e. ticks multiplied by 0.05). Part of the ShowTimer group.

modules.name: TpAura
modules.summary: TpAura attacks enemies that would normally be out of reach by briefly teleporting (desyncing) the client toward a target, swinging, and then teleporting back. It keeps your real (visual) position desynced from the position the server thinks you are at, while a click scheduler drives the actual attacks. Two travel strategies are offered: AStar (path-finding around blocks) and Immediate (a direct teleport). The module disables itself automatically when you quit the world.
useCases: Hit players or mobs that are far away on servers that don't validate teleport distance, without walking to them.
Reach and damage a fleeing target by pathing to it and snapping back to your original spot.
Combine a high CPS clicker with long-range teleport attacks for aggressive aura-style combat.

settings.name: AttackRange
settings.description: Maximum boxed distance (in blocks) from the desynced position at which a target may be attacked. Default 4.2, range 3.0 to 5.0. Higher values let you hit targets slightly farther away.

settings.name: CPS
settings.description: Clicks-per-second range used by the attack click scheduler (part of the Clicker sub-group). Default 5..8, configurable 1..maxCps (60). A random value within this range governs how many attacks are scheduled per second.

settings.name: Technique
settings.description: Click pattern used to distribute clicks over time. Options: Stabilized (default), Efficient, Spamming, DoubleClick, Drag, Butterfly, NormalDistribution. Affects the human-likeness and timing distribution of the generated clicks.

settings.name: AttackCooldown
settings.description: Part of the Clicker. Default true. When enabled, respects Minecraft's miss cooldown (won't click while mc.missTime > 0). Useful against anti-cheats that detect ignoring the post-miss cooldown. Only present because the clicker is bound to the attack key.

settings.name: Minimum
settings.description: Part of the ItemCooldown sub-group of the Clicker. Float range, default 1.0..1.0, range 0.0..2.0. Minimum attack-strength cooldown progress required before a click is allowed; 1.0 means waiting for a fully charged attack. A random value in the range is picked per click.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the teleport/travel strategy. AStar (default) path-finds around blocks toward the target; Immediate teleports directly in a straight line. Each mode exposes its own sub-settings.

settings.name: MaximumDistance
settings.description: AStar mode only. Maximum straight-line distance (blocks) to a target that AStar will attempt to path to. Default 95, range 50..250.

settings.name: MaximumCost
settings.description: AStar mode only. Maximum path-finding cost (node budget) before giving up on a path. Default 250, range 50..500. Higher values allow longer/more complex paths at greater computation cost.

settings.name: TickDistance
settings.description: AStar mode only. Number of path nodes grouped into one teleport chunk when the way is clear, to use fewer packets. Default 3, range 1..7.

settings.name: AllowDiagonal
settings.description: AStar mode only. Default false. When enabled, the path-finder may move diagonally between blocks instead of only cardinal directions.

settings.name: TpBack
settings.description: AStar mode only. Default true. When enabled, after attacking the client travels the path back in reverse to return to the starting position; when disabled it stays at the desynced position and continues from there.

settings.name: Stick
settings.description: AStar mode only. Number of ticks to remain at the target position after teleporting before returning. Default 5, range 1..10 (ticks).

modules.name: Tracers
modules.summary: Tracers draws a line from your view toward every rendered entity within a configurable range, making it easy to locate players and mobs around you. Lines are colored by the selected color mode, with friends always shown in blue and entity tags overriding the color when present. Each tracer runs from the entity's feet up to the top of its hitbox.
useCases: Quickly locate nearby players and mobs even through obstacles by following the tracer lines.
Distinguish friends (blue) from other entities at a glance during combat.
Gauge entity distance/health using the distance or health color modes.

settings.name: ColorMode
settings.description: Selects how tracer lines are colored. Options: distance-based HSB (default), entity health based, static color (default static color RGBA 0,160,255,255), and rainbow. The active mode's color is used unless the entity is a friend or has a tag color.

settings.name: LineWidth
settings.description: Thickness of the tracer lines. Default 1.0, range 1..16. At exactly 1.0 thin lines are drawn; higher values draw thicker lines.

settings.name: MaximumDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance (in blocks) at which entities will have a tracer drawn to them. Default 128, range 1..512. Entities farther than this are skipped.

modules.name: Trajectories
modules.summary: Trajectories predicts and draws the flight path of projectiles, showing where thrown or fired items will land. It renders simulated arcs for projectiles already in the world (such as arrows, snowballs, and fishing bobbers) as well as a hypothetical trajectory for the item currently held by you and optionally other players, including bows when drawn and multishot spreads. It can display detailed info labels (item icon, owner name, distance, flight duration) at the projectile's owner, current, or landing position.
useCases: Aim throws of ender pearls, snowballs, or potions accurately by seeing the predicted landing point.
Preview a bow or crossbow shot's arc, including multishot spread, before firing.
Track and visualize projectiles fired by other players to anticipate incoming hits.

settings.name: MaxSimulatedTicks
settings.description: Maximum number of ticks the projectile flight is simulated for, default 240, range 1 to 1000. Higher values trace longer/farther arcs at greater compute cost.

settings.name: MaxRenderDistance
settings.description: Maximum distance in meters from your view within which trajectories are drawn, default 96, range 16 to 512. Projectiles and players farther than this are skipped.

settings.name: CullBehindPlayer
settings.description: When enabled (default false), skips drawing trajectories for entities/players that are behind your view direction (and more than 3 blocks away), reducing clutter.

settings.name: ShowMultiShot
settings.description: When enabled (default true), also renders the additional spread arrows of a multishot (e.g. crossbow with Multishot) hypothetical shot.

settings.name: TrajectoryTypes
settings.description: Selects which projectile trajectory types are shown (the available TrajectoryType entries). Cannot be set to none. Only trajectories of the selected types are simulated and drawn.

settings.name: Show
settings.description: Selects which trajectory sources to display. Options: AlwaysShowBow (show a bow's trajectory even when not drawn), OtherPlayers (show held-item trajectories for other players, default on), ActiveTrajectoryArrow (show already-flying arrow trajectories, default on), and ActiveTrajectoryOther (show already-flying non-arrow projectile trajectories).

settings.name: ShowDetailedInfo
settings.description: Toggleable group (default disabled) that draws on-screen text labels with details about each trajectory. Contains ShowAt, Item, OwnerName, Distance, DurationUnit, Color, Scale, and RenderOffset sub-settings.

settings.name: ShowAt
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. Where the info label is anchored: Owner (at the projectile owner's position), Entity (at the projectile's current position, default), or Landing (at the predicted landing position).

settings.name: Item
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. When enabled (default true), draws the projectile/item icon next to the info label.

settings.name: OwnerName
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. When enabled (default true), shows the owner's name in the label (omitted when the owner is yourself).

settings.name: Distance
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. When enabled (default true), shows the distance in meters from you to the projectile's landing position.

settings.name: DurationUnit
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. Unit used to display flight duration: Ticks (raw tick count, default) or Seconds (ticks converted to seconds, e.g. '1.2s').

settings.name: Color
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. Text color of the info labels. Default white.

settings.name: Scale
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. Scale factor for the info label rendering. Default 1.0, range 0.25 to 4.0. Higher values make the labels larger.

settings.name: RenderOffset
settings.description: ShowDetailedInfo group. A 3D world-space offset added to the anchor position before projecting the info label to the screen, letting you nudge where labels appear. The in-GUI locate button is disabled.

modules.name: TrueSight
modules.summary: TrueSight reveals things that are normally hidden from view, specifically invisible entities and barrier blocks. When Entities sight is enabled, invisible living entities are still rendered (tinted with the configured colors) instead of being fully hidden. It also cooperates with the ESP module: invisible entities that ESP wants to highlight will be rendered even if you have not explicitly enabled Entities sight in TrueSight.
useCases: Spotting players or mobs that have an invisibility effect during combat.
Revealing barrier blocks placed by a server (e.g. invisible walls or map borders) so you can see map boundaries.

settings.name: Sight
settings.description: Multi-select choosing what categories of hidden objects to reveal. Options are Barriers (show invisible barrier blocks) and Entities (render invisible living entities). Both are off by default; enable either or both. Barriers controls barrier-block visibility; Entities controls whether invisible living entities are drawn.

settings.name: EntityColor
settings.description: The tint color (RGBA) applied to the body of revealed invisible entities. Default is white with alpha 100 (semi-transparent), so revealed entities appear as a faint outline; raising the alpha makes them more solid/visible.

settings.name: EntityFeatureLayerColor
settings.description: The tint color (RGBA) applied to the feature/overlay layers of revealed invisible entities (e.g. armor, held items, secondary model layers). Default is white with alpha 120. Adjusting it changes how visible those extra layers appear on revealed entities.

modules.name: Twerk
modules.summary: Twerk repeatedly and automatically toggles the sneak (crouch) state, making your character bob up and down. It works by alternating between sneaking and standing each fixed interval based on your tick count. The handler runs at a high priority so more important modules can override the sneak input when needed. It is purely cosmetic and provides no combat or movement advantage.
useCases: Taunting or messing around with other players for fun.
Adding a visual idle animation to your character while AFK or posing.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Length in game ticks of each sneak period and each stand period. With the default of 2 (range 1-20), the client sneaks for 2 ticks then stands for 2 ticks and repeats. Lower values make the twerking faster; higher values make it slower.

modules.name: VehicleBoost
modules.summary: VehicleBoost gives you a burst of momentum the moment you dismount a vehicle. Each tick it tracks whether you are a passenger, and the instant you stop riding (transition from in-vehicle to not), it overwrites your movement vector with a launch in the direction you are facing plus an upward kick. This effectively flings you off boats, minecarts, horses, etc.
useCases: Gaining sudden forward distance by mounting and quickly dismounting a vehicle.
Launching yourself upward and forward off a boat or minecart to cross gaps or escape.
Chaining vehicle entry/exit to repeatedly boost across terrain.

settings.name: HorizontalSpeed
settings.description: Horizontal launch strength applied in the direction you are looking when you leave the vehicle. Sets the X/Z components of your delta movement (scaled by the sine/cosine of your yaw). Default 2.0, range 0.1 to 10.0. Higher values throw you farther forward.

settings.name: VerticalSpeed
settings.description: Upward launch strength applied when you leave the vehicle. Sets the Y component of your delta movement. Default 1.0, range 0.1 to 5.0. Higher values send you higher into the air.

modules.name: VehicleControl
modules.summary: VehicleControl (alias BoatFly) lets you freely fly and steer any vehicle you are riding, such as a boat. It applies custom horizontal and vertical speeds using your movement keys (jump to go up, sneak to go down), with an optional faster speed profile while sprinting and a configurable downward glide when not ascending. A Rehook sub-feature periodically dismounts and re-mounts the vehicle to bypass BoatFly anti-cheat checks (e.g. Vulcan 2.9.1). On enable it warns you how to quit the vehicle safely, and it prevents you from sneaking out of the vehicle while in the air (only allowing dismount when the vehicle is on ground or in water).
useCases: Flying across the map in a boat instead of being limited to ground/water travel.
Quickly gaining or losing altitude in a vehicle using jump and sneak keys.
Bypassing server anti-cheats that detect boat flying by enabling Rehook to periodically re-enter the vehicle.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Base horizontal speed of the vehicle while moving (part of the BaseSpeed group). Default 0.5, range 0.1..10. Higher values make the vehicle move forward/sideways faster when not sprinting.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Base vertical speed of the vehicle (part of the BaseSpeed group). Default 0.35, range 0.1..10. Determines how fast you ascend (jump key) or descend (sneak key) when not sprinting.

settings.name: SprintSpeed
settings.description: Toggle for the SprintSpeed group. Default enabled (true). When on and the sprint key is held, the vehicle uses the faster Horizontal/Vertical values below instead of the base speeds.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Horizontal speed used while sprinting (child of SprintSpeed). Default 5, range 0.1..10. Applied instead of the base horizontal speed when SprintSpeed is enabled and the sprint key is held.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Vertical speed used while sprinting (child of SprintSpeed). Default 2, range 0.1..10. Applied instead of the base vertical speed when SprintSpeed is enabled and the sprint key is held.

settings.name: Glide
settings.description: Vertical velocity applied when neither jump nor sneak is held (passive glide). Default -0.15, range -0.3..0.3. Negative values sink slowly, positive values rise. Not applied while the vehicle is in water (to avoid drowning the vehicle), nor when sprinting if NoGlideOnSpring is enabled.

settings.name: MouseControl
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, the vehicle's yaw (facing direction) is synced to your camera/player yaw, letting you steer the vehicle by moving the mouse instead of relying solely on movement keys.

settings.name: NoGlideOnSpring
settings.description: Default false. When enabled, the passive Glide is disabled while sprinting (with SprintSpeed active), so releasing jump/sneak while sprinting holds altitude instead of sinking. (Display name is literally "NoGlideOnSpring".)

settings.name: Rehook
settings.description: Toggle for the Rehook group. Default disabled (false). When enabled, the module periodically dismounts and re-mounts the vehicle to bypass anti-cheats (such as Vulcan 2.9.1) that detect boat flying; it warns if the vehicle becomes too far away or is gone.

settings.name: UnhookAfter
settings.description: Child of Rehook. Default 4, range 1..10. Number of ticks to stay mounted before triggering a dismount in the rehook cycle.

settings.name: HookAfter
settings.description: Child of Rehook. Default 2, range 1..10. Number of ticks to wait before re-mounting the vehicle after dismounting in the rehook cycle.

modules.name: VehicleOneHit
modules.summary: VehicleOneHit lets you destroy boats and minecarts in a single interaction by spamming the attack packets needed to break them all at once. When you attack a boat or minecart, the module automatically fires the full burst of swings and attack packets required by the current protocol (3 on 1.8 or older, 19 on newer versions, which need more because of the lower attack strength). This makes vehicles break instantly instead of needing many manual hits.
useCases: Instantly clearing boats or minecarts that other players have placed to block or trap you.
Quickly removing vehicle entities used as obstacles on minigame or PvP servers.

modules.name: Velocity
modules.summary: Velocity modifies how much knockback/velocity you take from hits and explosions, ranging from reducing or fully cancelling knockback to advanced anti-cheat-specific bypasses. You pick a mode that determines the exact technique, and each mode exposes its own settings. Two shared top-level options let you delay incoming velocity packets and pause the module briefly after the server corrects your position. It is also known by the alias AntiKnockBack.
useCases: Reduce or remove the knockback you take in PvP so opponents cannot push you around.
Use a server- or anti-cheat-specific mode (e.g. Hypixel, Grim, Intave) to bypass that server's knockback checks.
Apply jump-reset or strafe techniques automatically to minimize knockback while staying mobile.

settings.name: Mode
settings.description: Selects the velocity technique. Default Modify. Generic options: Modify, Reversal, Strafe, JumpReset, Lag, Reduce. Server options: Hypixel, Dexland, Hylex, BlocksMC. Anti-cheat options: Grim2371, Grim2344-117, AAC4.4.2, Intave. Each mode applies knockback differently and exposes its own child settings.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Top-level. Delays incoming local-player velocity packets by a random number of ticks within the range before they are applied (default 0..0 = disabled, range 0..40 ticks). When the upper bound is above 0, velocity packets are held and re-applied after the chosen delay.

settings.name: PauseOnFlag
settings.description: Top-level. Number of ticks to pause the entire module after the server sends a position correction (a flag/setback). Default 0, range 0..20 ticks. Helps avoid getting flagged repeatedly after a setback.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Modify mode. Multiplier applied to incoming horizontal knockback (X and Z). Default 0, range -1..1. 0 means horizontal velocity is taken from your own motion (see MotionHorizontal) rather than the server packet; if both Horizontal and Vertical are 0 the velocity packet is fully cancelled. Negative values reverse direction.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Modify mode. Multiplier applied to incoming vertical knockback (Y). Default 0, range -1..1. 0 means vertical velocity is taken from your own motion (see MotionVertical) instead of the server packet.

settings.name: MotionHorizontal
settings.description: Modify mode. When Horizontal is 0, the horizontal velocity is set to your current motion multiplied by this factor, preventing horizontal slowdown. Default 0, range 0..1.

settings.name: MotionVertical
settings.description: Modify mode. When Vertical is 0, the vertical velocity is set to your current motion multiplied by this factor, preventing vertical slowdown. Default 0, range 0..1.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Modify mode. Percent chance (0..100, default 100, unit %) that the velocity modification is applied to a given knockback/explosion packet.

settings.name: Filter
settings.description: Modify mode. Condition under which the modification applies. Options: Always (default), OnGround (only when on ground), InAir (only when off ground).

settings.name: OnlyMove
settings.description: Modify mode, default false. When enabled, the modification only applies while you are pressing a horizontal movement key.

settings.name: TransactionBuffer
settings.description: Modify mode. Number of outgoing pong/transaction packets to buffer (cancel) per modified velocity, default 0, range 0..3. Used to desync transactions for certain anti-cheats.

settings.name: ConsiderExplosion
settings.description: Modify mode, default true. When enabled, explosion knockback packets are also modified the same way as regular velocity (relevant because some servers send explosion packets to trick cheats).

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Reversal mode. Number of ticks after taking velocity before your motion is reversed. Default 2, range 1..5 ticks.

settings.name: XModifier
settings.description: Reversal mode. Factor applied to the reversed X motion (motion becomes -X * XModifier). Default 0.5, range 0.0..1.0.

settings.name: ZModifier
settings.description: Reversal mode. Factor applied to the reversed Z motion (motion becomes -Z * ZModifier). Default 0.5, range 0.0..1.0.

settings.name: OnlyMoving
settings.description: Reversal mode, default false. When enabled, the reversal only triggers while you are moving.

settings.name: Delay
settings.description: Strafe mode. Number of ticks to wait after taking knockback before applying the strafe. Default 2, range 0..10 ticks.

settings.name: Strength
settings.description: Strafe mode. Multiplier applied to your horizontal speed when strafing to counteract knockback. Default 1, range 0.1..2.

settings.name: OnlyFacing
settings.description: Strafe mode. Toggleable group (disabled by default). When enabled, the strafe only applies when you are looking at a nearby enemy within Range.

settings.name: Range
settings.description: Strafe mode, child of OnlyFacing. Range used to detect and require facing the enemy for the strafe to apply. Default 3.5, range 0.1..6.

settings.name: UntilGround
settings.description: Strafe mode, default false. When enabled, the strafe correction keeps being applied to your movement every tick until you land back on the ground.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: JumpReset mode. Percent chance (0..100, default 100, unit %) that a jump-reset is performed when knockback is received while eligible.

settings.name: JumpByReceivedHits
settings.description: JumpReset mode. Toggleable group (disabled by default). When enabled, the jump-reset triggers after a number of received hits rather than purely automatically.

settings.name: HitsUntilJump
settings.description: JumpReset mode, child of JumpByReceivedHits. Number of received hits (chosen randomly in the range) to wait before performing the jump-reset. Default 2..2, range 0..10.

settings.name: JumpByDelay
settings.description: JumpReset mode. Toggleable group (enabled by default). When enabled, the jump-reset triggers after a tick delay.

settings.name: UntilJump
settings.description: JumpReset mode, child of JumpByDelay. Number of ticks (chosen randomly in the range) to wait before performing the jump-reset. Default 2..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: LagTime
settings.description: Lag mode. Number of ticks (chosen randomly in the range) to delay/queue incoming knockback packets before they are applied. Default 5..5, range 1..20 ticks.

settings.name: JumpReset
settings.description: Lag mode, default false. When enabled, a jump is forced when the queued lag is released (while sprinting and on ground) to combine lag with a jump-reset.

settings.name: ConsiderExplosion
settings.description: Lag mode, default true. When enabled, explosion-based knockback is also lagged/queued, not just regular velocity packets.

settings.name: AttackCount
settings.description: Reduce mode. Number of automatic attacks (chosen randomly in the range) performed against the target while reducing velocity. Default 3..3, range 0..20.

settings.name: LagTargetRange
settings.description: Reduce mode. Distance range (blocks) used to find/keep a target for the lag-and-reduce behavior; the start is the engage distance and the end is the maximum tracking distance. Default 2..6, range 0..20.

settings.name: LagMaxDelay
settings.description: Reduce mode. Maximum number of ticks to lag (queue) incoming packets while closing on the target before releasing. Default 10, range 1..1000 ticks.

settings.name: LagRequireKillAura
settings.description: Reduce mode, default false. When enabled, the lag behavior only runs while the KillAura module is active.

settings.name: Horizontal
settings.description: Reduce mode. Multiplier applied to your horizontal motion (X and Z) on each reduce attack. Default 0.6, range 0..1.

settings.name: Vertical
settings.description: Reduce mode. Multiplier applied to your vertical motion (Y) on each reduce attack. Default 1.0, range 0..1.

settings.name: Debug
settings.description: Reduce mode. Toggleable group (disabled by default) for diagnostic output of the reduce/lag state.

settings.name: ChatMessage
settings.description: Reduce mode, child of Debug, default false. When enabled (and Debug is on), debug status messages are printed to chat.

settings.name: Notification
settings.description: Reduce mode, child of Debug, default false. When enabled (and Debug is on), debug status is shown as on-screen notifications.

settings.name: BlinkEsp
settings.description: Reduce mode. ESP rendering style for the lagged/tracked target position. Options: Box, Model, Wireframe, None (default index points to Wireframe). Visualizes where the real target is while packets are queued.

settings.name: AlternativeBypass
settings.description: Grim2344-117 mode, default true. When enabled, sends the position packet 4 times (instead of once) as an alternative duplicate-exempt bypass technique against Grim.

settings.name: Reduce
settings.description: AAC4.4.2 mode. Multiplier applied to your horizontal motion each tick while hurt and airborne to reduce knockback. Default 0.62, range 0..1.

settings.name: ReduceOnAttack
settings.description: Intave mode. Toggleable group (enabled by default). When enabled, your motion is reduced when you attack shortly after being hit.

settings.name: Factor
settings.description: Intave mode, child of ReduceOnAttack. Multiplier applied to horizontal motion when reducing. Default 0.6, range 0.6..1.

settings.name: HurtTime
settings.description: Intave mode, child of ReduceOnAttack. Hurt-time window (ticks) during which the reduce-on-attack applies. Default 5..7, range 1..10.

settings.name: LastAttackTimeToReduce
settings.description: Intave mode, child of ReduceOnAttack. Maximum time in milliseconds since your last attack for the reduction to still apply. Default 2000, range 1..10000.

settings.name: JumpReset
settings.description: Intave mode. Toggleable group (enabled by default). When enabled, performs a jump-reset against knockback based on hurt time and chance.

settings.name: Chance
settings.description: Intave mode, child of JumpReset. Percent chance (0..100, default 50, unit %) of performing the jump-reset on a given eligible tick.

settings.name: Randomize
settings.description: Intave mode, child of JumpReset. Toggleable group (disabled by default). When enabled, the jump-reset is spaced out by a random tick delay instead of firing immediately.

settings.name: DelayTicks
settings.description: Intave mode, child of Randomize. Random tick delay range between jump-resets when Randomize is enabled. Default 0..5, range 0..10.

modules.name: VoidESP
modules.summary: VoidESP highlights nearby ground positions where there is no solid block below within a threshold, effectively marking void or pit edges around you. It scans a rectangular area in front of and to the sides of where you are standing, searching downward at each cell, and renders colored boxes on positions that drop into the void. The highlighted positions update every tick as you move and look around.
useCases: Avoid falling into the void on maps with holes, bridges, or sky islands.
See void/edge hazards highlighted while bridging or running across gaps.
Get a visual warning of unsafe positions in front of you in bedwars/skywars-style scenarios.

settings.name: YThreshold
settings.description: How many blocks downward to search for solid ground before treating a column as void. Default 16, range 3 to 32. Higher values require a deeper drop before a position is flagged.

settings.name: RangeSide
settings.description: How far to the left and right of your standing position the scan extends, in blocks. Default 3, range 0 to 32.

settings.name: RangeFacing
settings.description: How far forward and backward (along your facing direction) the scan extends, in blocks. Default 8, range 1 to 32.

settings.name: Render
settings.description: Toggleable group (PlacementRenderer) controlling how the highlighted void positions are drawn, including fade and color. Enabled by default.

settings.name: Clump
settings.description: Render: whether to clump/merge culling data for rendered boxes to reduce overhead. Default true.

settings.name: StartSize
settings.description: Render: the box's size at the start of its appear animation. Default 1.0, range 0 to 2.

settings.name: StartCurve
settings.description: Render: easing curve for the start-size animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: EndSize
settings.description: Render: the box's size at the end of its animation. Default 0.8, range 0 to 2.

settings.name: EndCurve
settings.description: Render: easing curve for the end-size animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: FadeInCurve
settings.description: Render: easing curve for the fade-in (appear) animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: FadeOutCurve
settings.description: Render: easing curve for the fade-out (disappear) animation. Default LINEAR.

settings.name: InTime
settings.description: Render: duration of the appear animation, in milliseconds. Default 500, range 0 to 5000.

settings.name: OutTime
settings.description: Render: duration of the disappear animation, in milliseconds. Default 500, range 0 to 5000.

settings.name: Color
settings.description: Render: fill color of the highlighted void boxes. Default red with alpha 90 (RGBA 255,0,0,90).

settings.name: OutlineColor
settings.description: Render: outline color of the highlighted void boxes. Default the fill color at full alpha (red, alpha 255).

modules.name: Vomit
modules.summary: Vomit drops items out of your inventory in a random order so it looks like your character is vomiting. In survival it throws random non-empty storage slots from your inventory (or from an open container if your inventory is empty), while in creative it generates random block-item stacks and throws them, filling empty slots first to bypass the creative drop limit. All actions are scheduled through the shared inventory constraints, which control timing and the conditions under which dropping is allowed.
useCases: Spam-drop your items for fun or trolling, simulating a vomiting animation.
In creative mode, rapidly throw random block items into the world.

settings.name: StartDelay
settings.description: Inventory constraint: range of ticks to wait before starting an inventory interaction. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: ClickDelay
settings.description: Inventory constraint: range of ticks to wait between inventory clicks/throws. Default 2..4, range 0..20 ticks. In creative, if the lower bound is 0 or less the module batch-fills and throws all empty slots at once instead of one slot per action.

settings.name: CloseDelay
settings.description: Inventory constraint: range of ticks to wait before closing the inventory after interacting. Default 1..2, range 0..20 ticks.

settings.name: MissChance
settings.description: Inventory constraint: percentage chance to deliberately miss/skip an inventory action to appear more human. Default 0..0 (no misses), range 0..100%.

settings.name: Requires
settings.description: Inventory constraint: conditions that must be met before any drop action is performed. Options: NoMovement (not moving or jumping), NoRotation (rotation unchanged from previous), NotUsingItem, NotBreaking (not breaking a block), NotDuringCombat, and InventoryOpen (only act while the inventory is open). None selected by default.

modules.name: XRay
modules.summary: XRay hides most ordinary terrain and only renders a configurable set of valuable blocks (ores, mineral blocks, chests, utility blocks, liquids, portals, etc.), letting you spot ores and structures through walls. The block list is fully customizable and can be reset to defaults via the XRay command. Optional FullBright lights the visible blocks even underground, and ExposedOnly limits rendering to blocks that touch a non-solid neighbor. Changing any of its options triggers a world re-render so the effect applies immediately.
useCases: Mining efficiently by seeing ore veins (diamonds, ancient debris, etc.) through stone.
Locating chests, spawners, or other structures hidden inside walls and terrain.
Customizing the rendered block set via the /xray command to target only specific blocks you care about.

settings.name: FullBright
settings.description: When enabled (default true), the blocks still shown through walls are lit fully bright so they are visible even in dark or underground areas. Changing it reloads the world renderer.

settings.name: ExposedOnly
settings.description: When enabled (default false), only renders listed blocks that have at least one non-solid (non-redstone-conductor) neighbor, i.e. blocks exposed to air/caves, hiding fully buried ones. Changing it reloads the world renderer.

settings.name: Blocks
settings.description: The customizable set of blocks that remain visible while everything else is hidden. Defaults to a large list of ores, mineral and raw-mineral blocks, storage blocks (chests, shulker boxes, copper chests), utility/job blocks, cauldrons, liquids (lava, water), portals, command blocks, and others. Add or remove blocks (or reset to defaults) to control exactly what XRay shows; changes reload the world renderer.

modules.name: YggdrasilSignatureFix
modules.summary: YggdrasilSignatureFix addresses issues with Mojang's Yggdrasil profile/skin signature handling. It includes an option to force player skins to be rendered using the slim (Alex) arm model.
useCases: Fix skin rendering or signature-related problems for player profiles.
Force all players to display with the slim arm model regardless of their actual skin model setting.

settings.name: ForceSlimModel
settings.description: When enabled (default true), forces affected player skins to use the slim (Alex/3-pixel arm) model. Disable it to keep the default/classic model behavior.

modules.name: Zoom
modules.summary: Zoom is a HOLD-bound render module that narrows your field of view to magnify distant targets while you hold its keybind. The zoom transition is animated using an easing curve, and the mouse is slowed down (via mixin) while zoomed so aiming feels natural at high magnification. Optionally, scrolling the mouse wheel while holding the bind adjusts the zoom level on the fly.
useCases: Hold the bind to scope in on far-away players or terrain like a spyglass.
Improve long-range aim by zooming in and benefiting from the reduced mouse sensitivity.
Scroll to dynamically fine-tune zoom level for spotting distant entities or details.

settings.name: Zoom
settings.description: Target field of view (in degrees) to zoom to when the bind is held. Default 30, range 10..150. Lower values produce stronger magnification.

settings.name: Scroll
settings.description: Toggle for the Scroll value group (enabled by default). When enabled, scrolling the mouse wheel in the hotbar while zoomed adjusts the target FOV (clamped between 1 and 179) and cancels the normal hotbar scroll.

settings.name: Speed
settings.description: Child of the Scroll group. Multiplier applied to each scroll step when adjusting zoom via the mouse wheel. Default 2.0, range 0.5..8.0. Higher values change the zoom more per scroll notch.

settings.name: Transition
settings.description: Easing function used to animate the FOV change when zooming in and out. Default QUAD_IN. Changing it alters the feel/shape of the zoom animation.

settings.name: DurationFactor
settings.description: Multiplier (suffix 'x') that scales the animation duration relative to the size of the FOV change. Default 2.0, range 0..10. Higher values make the zoom transition slower; 0 makes it effectively instant.
